item:99-year-old-port.text: 99-Year-Old Port. The 99-Year-Old Port is an exceptionally rare bottle of vintage liquor shipped from Booty Bay as a personal gift for Gazlowe. After a cargo accident on the Ratchet docks, it was snatched away by a lunatic named Mad Magglish, who fled into the twisting tunnels outside the Wailing Caverns. Transporting precious freight across the Great Sea always carries risks, but Crane Operator Bigglefuzz made things far worse during a routine morning unloading in Ratchet. Attempting to clear an overwhelming shipment from Booty Bay, the goblin overloaded his crane and brought a mountain of crates crashing down onto the docks. In the chaos, the town eccentric—a troublesome figure known as Mad Magglish—snatched an extraordinarily aged bottle of 99-Year-Old Port and bolted into the hills toward the Wailing Caverns.

item:a-bloodstained-journal-page.text: A Bloodstained Journal Page. A torn, bloodstained parchment examined during the investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle. A few words remain legible through the thick blood, and Commander Althea Ebonlocke asks that its handwriting be checked. Commander Althea Ebonlocke keeps a vigilant watch over Darkshire and asks for the handwriting on this torn, blood-spattered page to be examined. Despite the thick blood, a few words remain legible enough for Clerk Daltry to compare with the Town Registry.

item:a-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: A Clue to Sanders' Treasure. A Clue to Sanders' Treasure is a weathered parchment left behind by the notorious pirate Captain Sanders. It serves as the second step in a treasure hunt scattered across the bluffs and coastlines of Westfall. Discovered after following Captain Sanders' initial treasure map, this parchment provides directions further inland into Westfall. The scrawled note directs the finder due east from the coast, urging them to climb up the bluffs toward the main road. Sanders hid his next marker inside an old barrel resting near the crumbling stone ruins of an abandoned chimney, leading seekers deeper into the troubled farmlands.

item:a-dusty-unsent-letter.text: A Dusty Unsent Letter. A Dusty Unsent Letter is a forgotten parchment recovered from an old footlocker in Westfall. It offers vital proof that the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle lived in Moonbrook before his disappearance. While searching for the past of the mysterious Stalvan Mistmantle, investigators discover this unsent letter tucked away inside an old footlocker in Moonbrook. Darkshire's town registry still listed his last address as the Moonbrook Schoolhouse, and Clerk Daltry wanted word on whether he had truly lived there. This unmailed correspondence provides the missing link, confirming that Stalvan resided in the Westfall township for a time. Yet its presence also raises ominous questions, as retrieving it disturbs a vengeful Forlorn Spirit that guards the remnants of Stalvan's past with bitter malice.

item:a-faded-journal-page.text: A Faded Journal Page. A Faded Journal Page is an old parchment retrieved from an upstairs chest in Marshal Haggard's secluded home in Elwynn Forest. It serves as a vital clue in unraveling the dark history surrounding Stalvan Mistmantle. Left behind inside an old trunk when retired Marshal Haggard took residence near the eastern border of Elwynn Forest, this weathered parchment sat undisturbed for years. With Haggard's failing eyesight preventing him from deciphering it, the page remained neglected until adventurers digging into the legend of Stalvan Mistmantle retrieved it.

item:a-letter-to-grelin-whitebeard.text: A Letter to Grelin Whitebeard. This sealed correspondence is addressed to Grelin Whitebeard, an experienced dwarf stationed out in the snowy wilderness of Coldridge Valley. Sent from the mountain capital of Ironforge, it serves as a rare dispatch of news and instructions reaching the remote frontier. Life in the snowy basin of Coldridge Valley can be isolated, especially for those stationed beyond the safety of Anvilmar. Letters like this represent the crucial link connecting scouts and scholars in the field to the halls of Ironforge. Carried southward along the mountain paths, the missive brings word from the capital to Grelin Whitebeard's wilderness campsite.

item:a-mysterious-message.text: A Mysterious Message. A Mysterious Message is a piece of correspondence intercepted from a courier traveling across Westfall. Addressed among conspirators, the dispatch provides the People's Militia with concrete evidence linking Edwin VanCleef directly to the leadership of the Defias Brotherhood. Carried by a courier journeying between the Defias operations at Moonbrook, the Gold Coast Quarry, and the Jangolode Mine, this message represents a crucial break in Gryan Stoutmantle's investigation. For weeks, the People's Militia suspected organized direction behind the bandit uprising, but lacked irrefutable proof. Intercepting this missive confirms beyond doubt that Edwin VanCleef commands the brotherhood's efforts across the region, directing his network through coded ranks and intermediaries.

item:a-simple-compass.text: A Simple Compass. A Simple Compass is an old personal keepsake belonging to the City Architect of Stormwind, Baros Alexston. Stored away inside a small chest at his family's burned-down homestead in Westfall, it serves as a cherished memento of his youth before he rose to prominence in the capital. Long before Baros Alexston became a master architect directing major works in Cathedral Square, he grew up laboring on his family's farm in Westfall. The simple compass was his very first navigational instrument, likely sparking his early interest in geometry, drafting, and exploration. When the Alexston Farmstead fell victim to the Defias Brotherhood's raids and burned, the compass was left behind inside a sturdy chest amidst the ruins, preserved even as the surrounding farmland was overrun by bandits. Baros's father managed to escape the farmstead's destruction but could not carry the family's possessions with him to safety. While the instrument possesses little practical utility to a master builder working within the stone walls of Stormwind City, its emotional significance remains immense. Returning it to Baros offers him a rare, intact link to his humble beginnings and the peaceful countryside of his childhood.

item:a-stack-of-letters.text: A Stack of Letters. A Stack of Letters is a small bundle of correspondence brought through the mountain pass into Coldridge Valley. Though initially believed to belong entirely to Talin Keeneye, the bundle holds communications meant for multiple scouts stationed in the freezing wilderness. Reaching remote camps within Dun Morogh's rugged mountains is grueling work, and postal runners often rely on passing travelers to carry mail out of Anvilmar. This bundle of letters arrived through the pass destined for scouts stationed deeper in Coldridge Valley. While thought to be solely for Talin Keeneye at his lakeside camp, sorting through the parcel reveals missives meant for other outposts across the snows, including mountaineer Grelin Whitebeard.

item:a-torn-journal-page.text: A Torn Journal Page. A Torn Journal Page is a tattered piece of parchment recovered from an old shipping crate along the Stormwind City canals. It serves as an essential physical clue into the identity and dark history of Stalvan Mistmantle, connecting the grim happenings in Duskwood to records preserved in Elwynn Forest. Discovered hidden near the bottom of a sealed storage crate beside Stormwind City's canals—tucked beneath old books, family heirlooms, and a ceramic vase—this fragment was left behind among forgotten personal effects. Though damaged and worn, the handwriting upon the page carries a distinct script that points directly to Stalvan Mistmantle's past, prompting investigators to seek out those who might still recognize the hand that penned it.

item:abercrombie-s-crate.text: Abercrombie's Crate. Abercrombie's Crate is a lost container of delicate tools and collected herbs belonging to the eccentric hermit Abercrombie. It rests abandoned near the entrance of the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in southern Duskwood after the old man was chased off by marauding ogres. While wandering far from his shack in western Duskwood to gather vegetation, Abercrombie crossed paths with a hostile gang of ogres. Fleeing for his life, the old hermit dropped his crate of precious instruments and harvested botanicals. The ogres hauled his belongings back to their stronghold at the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound, leaving the heavy chest sitting carelessly near their cave mouth.

item:admiral-proudmoore-s-orders.text: Admiral Proudmoore's Orders. Admiral Proudmoore's Orders are written battle plans recovered from Kul Tiras forces entrenching themselves along the coastline of Durotar. Penned before the Grand Admiral's defeat at Theramore, the documents outline persistent military strategies that continue to threaten the nascent orc homeland. Even after the death of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore at Theramore, his expeditionary forces refuse to yield. Recovered from Lieutenant Benedict's garrison at Tiragarde Keep, these tactical directives detail long-term maneuvers and fortifications designed to undermine the Horde. The orders prove that the Grand Admiral's offensive in Durotar was no hasty raid, but an organized campaign structured to endure long past his own demise. For the Horde, the recovered documents offer vital insight into Kul Tiras operations and potential reinforcements threatening their borders.

item:ados-fragment.text: Ados Fragment. The Ados Fragment is an inscribed piece of stone recovered from the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands. Together with three companion shards, it forms the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic bearing enigmatic Titan inscriptions. Unearthed in the muddy trenches of Whelgar's Excavation, the Ados Fragment is one of four missing pieces required to reconstruct the Goaz Stone. Prior to raptors overrunning the dig site, Prospector Whelgar began translating the primary tablet, only to discover that the inscriptions broke off at crucial moments. The scattered pieces—named Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru—were lost across the ruins, concealed within ancient containers and dirt mounds amidst prowling beasts.

item:agamand-family-axe.text: Agamand Family Axe. The Agamand Family Axe is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand family crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a martial symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by Coleman Farthing to strip the undead family of their remaining dignity. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty reigned as prosperous landowners across the northern hills of Tirisfal Glades, maintaining vast mills and a private family crypt. The Agamand Family Axe rested among the ancestral arms entombed alongside deceased patriarchs and warriors, kept intact on underground weapon racks even as the Scourge overran the estate and slaughtered its inhabitants. When the Scourge raised the fallen Agamands as mindless thralls to the Lich King, their former servant Coleman Farthing survived—in undeath—with bitter hatred for his old masters. Farthing blames the family for his own demise and commissions Forsaken wanderers to enter the crypt, strip the weapon racks of the axe, sword, mace, and dagger, and erase the final vestiges of the Agamand heritage.

item:agamand-family-dagger.text: Agamand Family Dagger. The Agamand Family Dagger is an ancestral heirloom of the fallen Agamand dynasty, resting on weapon racks within their ancestral crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Coleman Farthing seeks this blade alongside the rest of their family arsenal to strip his former masters of their remaining legacy and honor. Before the Third War, the Agamand family maintained vast estates and grain mills across the rolling meadows of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of their lineage's armaments, the Agamand Family Dagger survived the devastation wrought by the Scourge, locked within the family crypt north of Agamand Mills. Protected by the restless, undead remnants of the household and mindless minions of the Lich King, the dagger represents the prestige and martial heritage that once elevated the family above their servants and tenants. For Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken residing at Brill who died in the Agamands' service, the blade represents bitter resentment rather than noble lineage. Holding the family directly responsible for his death, Farthing directs adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt to recover the dagger along with the family sword, axe, and mace. In stripping these ancestral armaments from their tomb, Farthing aims to rob the now-Scourge patriarchs of their last vestiges of dignity and ensure the Agamand memory is utterly extinguished.

item:agamand-family-mace.text: Agamand Family Mace. The Agamand Family Mace is an ancestral heirloom preserved within the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a symbol of pride for a wealthy dynasty of northern Lordaeron, it has become an object of spiteful retribution sought by their former servant Coleman Farthing. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held extensive farmlands and windmills in the northern reaches of Tirisfal Glades. Like the rest of the regional aristocracy, they fell before the plague of undeath. The Agamands were reanimated as mindless thralls in service to the Lich King, wandering their ruined estate while their ancient family treasures remained locked within the depths of the family crypt. The Agamand Family Mace is stored among these weapons, an emblem of a forgotten lineage now reduced to shambling Scourge.

item:agamand-family-sword.text: Agamand Family Sword. The Agamand Family Sword is a tarnished ancestral blade kept inside the Agamand Family Crypt in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a proud symbol of the wealthy mill-owning dynasty, it is sought by the Forsaken Coleman Farthing to erase the final vestiges of his former masters' legacy. Before the Third War, the Agamand dynasty held immense wealth and influence across the rolling mills of northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end, their bodies raised into mindless thralls of the Lich King. Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial family sword, were sealed away in the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Stripping these blades from their burial racks serves not merely as looting, but as a deliberate act to break whatever memory and noble standing remains of the fallen household.

item:ahanu-s-leather-goods.text: Ahanu's Leather Goods. Ahanu's Leather Goods is a bundled consignment of finished leather armor and supplies crafted atop the mesas of Thunder Bluff. Prepared by the leatherworker Ahanu, the parcel is bound for the Crossroads in the Barrens to supply wandering hunters and adventurers. The supply lines of the Horde depend on practical trade between established strongholds and frontier outposts. In Thunder Bluff, the artisan Ahanu works raw hides into finished apparel and gear, preparing this consignment specifically for trade beyond Mulgore. The bundle is destined for Jahan Hawkwing, a merchant operating in the bustling heart of the Barrens at the Crossroads. Because overland travel across the plains is slow, transporting the bundle introduces messengers to the aerial courier network maintained by the tauren, relying on Tal and Devrak's trained wind riders to ferry goods swiftly across long distances.

item:alaric-s-remains.text: Alaric's Remains. Alaric's Remains are the recovered bones of an individual once interred in a shallow grave along Silverpine Forest. His lingering spirit bids travelers to carry what is left of him past the Rot Hide gnolls into the towers of Fenris Keep. Unearthed from an unremarkable shallow grave in Silverpine Forest, the remains belong to Alaric, a former resident of Fenris Isle. Rather than linger in an exposed pit, his spirit yearns for the place he cherished in life. He asks whoever unearths his bones to leave his ill-fitting boots behind and bring his skeletal remains directly into the keep, seeking quiet sanctuary far away from the scavengers prowling the mainland.

item:alien-egg.text: Alien Egg. The Alien Egg is an unusual and mysterious clutch found guarded by local wind serpents across the canyons of Thousand Needles. Despite its unfamiliar appearance, the native serpents protect the egg fiercely as if it were their own. Its presence has aroused the curiosity and concern of the tauren scouts stationed atop Freewind Post. Discovered resting at the base of the towering spires south and northeast of Freewind Post, the Alien Egg stands out dramatically from the typical fauna of the canyon floor. Rather than abandoning or destroying the odd clutch, the native serpents of the needles fiercely guard it alongside their own nests. Hagar Lightninghoof, a tauren brave keeping watch from the heights of Freewind Post, sought to retrieve the specimen to determine whether it represented a threat to the mesa settlements or merely an unusual variation of local reptilian life.

item:alterac-granite.text: Alterac Granite. Alterac Granite is a prized, durable stone quarried from the mountainous terrain of northern Lordaeron, specifically around Darrow Hill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Revered by master stonecutters for its exceptional resilience and grain, it is chosen by King Magni Bronzebeard's royal mason to carve an enduring tribute for fallen soldiers. When King Magni Bronzebeard ordered a monument to commemorate Sully Balloo—a brave dwarven defender who perished in the tragedy at the Thandol Span—ordinary quarry stone would not do. Grand Mason Marblesten, tasked with sculpting the memorial in Ironforge, insisted on obtaining Alterac Granite. Renowned as one of the finest stones available across the Eastern Kingdoms, its legendary durability ensures that the likeness and memory of a fallen hero can endure untarnished for generations. Harvesting Alterac Granite is far from a simple errand. The stone rests around Darrow Hill in the northern reaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills, close to the ruined territories of Alterac. With the region rife with hostile wildlife, lurking syndicate brigands, and lingering strife, retrieving unblemished slabs of this pristine stone requires bold adventurers willing to venture deep into contested lands to secure it for Ironforge's artisans.

item:altered-snapjaw-shell.text: Altered Snapjaw Shell. An Altered Snapjaw Shell is the carapace of a freshwater turtle inhabiting the lush oases of the Barrens. Druids studying the region examine these mutated shells to understand how strange subterranean fissures are warping the local wildlife. The freshwater turtles dwelling within the Lushwater and Stagnant Oases have undergone noticeable, unnatural changes. Believed to be drinking from springs fed by mysterious underground fissures, the oasis snapjaws exhibit altered carapaces that intrigue researchers at the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem, a tauren druid seeking to divine the health of the land, gathers these shells to determine whether the energies welling up from the deep earth are an unnatural blight or something far stranger.

item:ambercorn.text: Ambercorn. Ambercorn is a sacred nut that falls from the tall, ancient trees scattered across Mulgore. Infused with natural magic, it serves as a vital reagent in tauren shamanic brews, most notably used to induce spiritual visions during youth trials. Gathered from beneath the sturdy boughs of Mulgore's great trees, ambercorns are more than ordinary nuts to the tauren. Rich with the spiritual vitality of the land, they hold latent magical properties that tauren mystics have understood and utilized for generations. Young hunters and wanderers learn early to keep their eyes on the grass beneath the canopy, honoring the Earth Mother's gifts that fall freely from above. In Bloodhoof Village, the seer Zarlman Two-Moons relies on ambercorn when preparing young tauren for the Rite of Vision. Combined with stones gathered from the plains' pristine water wells, ambercorn is steeped into the potent Water of the Seers. Consuming this ceremonial elixir before the ancestral flames allows an initiate's senses to shift, revealing a guiding spirit animal meant to lead them to their next destination.

item:amethyst-phial.text: Amethyst Phial. The Amethyst Phial is a delicate ceremonial vessel entrusted to young night elf adventurers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It is crafted specifically to gather and preserve sacred waters from the premier moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree. Entrusted to initiates on Teldrassil, the Amethyst Phial is the final vessel used in the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage. Corithras Moonrage tasks travelers with carrying it to the far northwestern reaches of the boughs, nestled within the Oracle Glade. There, beneath the ancient canopy of the Oracle Tree, lies the island's first and most potent moonwell. The phial is carefully dipped into these radiant waters to draw out the essence of Elune's grace, allowing druids and priestesses to study and tend to the unpredictable growth of the World Tree.

item:an-undelivered-letter.text: An Undelivered Letter. An Undelivered Letter is a piece of long-forgotten mail left behind in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn. Penned years ago by the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle, it serves as a critical clue in unraveling the dark tale of his past. Years ago, a storm drove a traveling courier into the Lion's Pride Inn looking for dry lodging. Near midnight, the terrified messenger fled down the stairs in his sleeping clothes and vanished into the pouring rain, never to return. He abandoned a chest full of belongings on the second floor, including a letter written by Stalvan Mistmantle addressed to an estate in Stormwind City's Canal District.

item:anaya-s-pendant.text: Anaya's Pendant. Anaya's Pendant is a keepsake carried by the restless ghost of Anaya Dawnrunner among the ruins of Ameth'Aran. It serves as a tragic token of remembrance for her lover, Cerellean Whiteclaw, who survived the Sundering only to find her spirit still tormented millennia later. Ten thousand years ago, during the cataclysmic destruction of the Well of Eternity, the ancient kaldorei city of Ameth'Aran fell in ruin. Believing his beloved Anaya had perished, Cerellean Whiteclaw carried his profound grief into the long slumber alongside Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage. When he at last awakened, he wandered Darkshore only to discover that Anaya's tormented apparition still drifted through Ameth'Aran, bearing this very pendant. Unable to bear raising a hand against her himself, Cerellean asks passing travelers to release her spirit and recover the heirloom.

item:ancient-moonstone-seal.text: Ancient Moonstone Seal. The Ancient Moonstone Seal is a powerful relic of Highborne sorcery forged long before the Sundering. Imbued with potent arcane binding magic, it served as the anchor holding the spirit of Asterion captive within the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Forged by Asterion's former master, the powerful Highborne sorcerer Athrikus Narassin, the Ancient Moonstone Seal was crafted to serve as an unbreakable metaphysical anchor. While the Well of Eternity still stood and Queen Azshara reigned, Athrikus used the artifact to bind Asterion's soul to the pillars of Bashal'Aran. Over ten millennia later, Asterion remained an incorporeal prisoner to its magic, unable to break the ward with any strength or spell he possessed.

item:ancient-statuette.text: Ancient Statuette. The Ancient Statuette is a sunken relic recovered from the shores of the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Sought by the night elf Talen, the small effigy originates from the submerged ruins of the ancient city of Zoram. The waters off northwestern Ashenvale conceal the sunken remains of Zoram, a pre-Sundering night elven city lost beneath the waves ten thousand years ago. In recent days, the explorer Talen surveyed the submerged ruins from a small craft, seeking lost historical relics. When a vicious assault by naga drove him ashore, Talen abandoned most of his belongings in his flight, dropping the ancient statuette he had dredged up onto the tideline sand near his scuttled skiff. Talen considers the statuette his most prized possession and the entire justification for braving the monster-infested coast. Rather than merely being a piece of decorative stonework, he believes the effigy serves as an essential key to deciphering the architecture, history, and arcane secrets locked away beneath the surf of Zoram Strand.

item:andron-s-ledger.text: Andron's Ledger. Andron's Ledger is an intelligence document obtained from Andron Gant in the Undercity. The Deathstalkers seek it as part of an operative's early work gathering information for the Forsaken.

item:another-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Another Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Another Clue to Sanders' Treasure is a weathered parchment slip left behind by the notorious pirate Captain Sanders. Retrieved from an old barrel, it contains directional verse pointing fortune hunters toward a lonely landmark on the bluffs of Westfall. Captain Sanders was careful never to keep his stolen riches in plain sight. Instead of drawing a single map that could be seized at once, he split his instructions into a succession of riddles and buried markers. This scrap of parchment continues the trail, directing whoever holds it to turn north from the previous hiding place and seek out a discarded jug sitting near an isolated windmill towering over the sea cliffs.

item:arikara-serpent-skin.text: Arikara Serpent Skin. The Arikara Serpent Skin is the scaled hide taken from the mythical wind serpent Arikara atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Carried back to Whitereach Post, it serves as tangible proof that the vengeance-seeking beast was summoned and slain. Arikara is a formidable wind serpent tied to ancient tauren legend, rumored to seek retribution against Cairne Bloodhoof amid shifting cultural ways. Using enchanted Incendia Powder prepared under the direction of Elder Magatha Grimtotem, champions light the sacred fire atop the burial bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle to force the spirit-beast into the physical realm. Stripping the serpent's hide yields the Arikara Serpent Skin—an unmistakable relic of the beast's demise.

item:arnak-s-hoof.text: Arnak's Hoof. Arnak's Hoof is the macabre proof of death taken from the criminal Arnak Grimtotem. Hunted down on the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle, Arnak was marked for execution by the defenders of Freewind Post after murdering a fellow tauren and kidnapping his sister. Arnak Grimtotem earned notoriety throughout Thousand Needles as an outlaw whose brutality crossed even the contentious lines of tauren clan politics. After murdering another tauren and abducting the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong, a formal bounty was posted for his death. Arnak holed up on the heights of Darkcloud Pinnacle, surrounded by Grimtotem guards. Slaying him and claiming his severed hoof serves as undeniable confirmation for Cliffwatcher Longhorn at Freewind Post that the murderer has finally answered for his crimes.

item:astor-s-letter-of-introduction.text: Astor's Letter of Introduction. Astor's Letter of Introduction is a document carried by Astor Hadren, a courier traveling between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. Taken by aspiring Deathstalkers, the letter serves as cover to infiltrate a suspected conspiracy involving the shopkeeper Andron Gant. Astor Hadren served as a discreet courier moving between Silverpine Forest and the capital. His personal letter of introduction establishes the bearer's bona fides to illicit contacts in the city. When Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad needed to investigate suspicious leaks within the Undercity, Astor's travels made him an immediate target. By eliminating or robbing Hadren of his papers, an operative can assume his identity and intercept covert communications meant for Astor's eyes alone.

item:ataeric-s-staff.text: Ataeric's Staff. Ataeric's Staff is a powerful magical conduit wielded by Archmage Ataeric, a senior Dalaran wizard in Silverpine Forest. It serves as both a focus for manipulating local ley lines and physical proof of the archmage's defeat for the Forsaken at the Sepulcher. Carried by Archmage Ataeric, this staff was used to direct and harness ley energies in southern Silverpine Forest. Under Dalaran's direction, Ataeric attempted to reactivate an ancient ley energy node near the borders of the magocracy's territory. The staff acted as a vital tool for weaving these immense ambient currents, rendering the archmage a formidable threat to nearby Forsaken settlements. Alarmed by Dalaran's magical expansion, Shadow Priest Allister ordered Ataeric's assassination and demanded the recovery of the staff. With Ataeric slain and his staff recovered, the concentrated ley energies collapsed back into dormancy. Bringing the staff to the Sepulcher marked a decisive victory against Dalaran's ambitions, though the Forsaken remain watchful of the latent power remaining in the earth.

item:athrikus-narassin-s-head.text: Athrikus Narassin's Head. This severed head is proof of the death of Athrikus Narassin, an ancient warlock who directed dark rituals in northern Darkshore. Taken from the heights of the ruined spire, it serves to confirm the disruption of demonic activity centered around the Tower of Althalaxx. Perched at the pinnacle of the Tower of Althalaxx, Athrikus Narassin commanded a coven of dark sorcerers practicing fel magic along the Darkshore coast. Ancient and entrenched, Narassin coordinated demonic summonings that threatened the surrounding wilderness. Claiming his head shatters the coven's leadership, driving back their immediate foothold in the region, even if the lingering corruption promises future vigilance will be needed.

item:bag-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Bag of Empty Ooze Containers. The Bag of Empty Ooze Containers is a set of sterile glassware supplied by the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. Prepared for delicate field collection, it holds empty sample jars intended to capture pristine, uncorrupted slime specimens across Azeroth. While investigating the bizarre biology of Azeroth's oozes, Laris Geardawdle realized that slime creatures rapidly absorb and mirror the corruption of their surroundings. Having studied tainted residues from places like Felwood, the gnome scientist commissioned these robust sample jars to withstand acidic specimens while preserving their natural state. The satchel holds enough jars for an explorer to gather clean, unpolluted slime from wild, untouched regions—most notably the primordial wilderness of Un'Goro Crater, where ancient glutinous oozes thrive free from demonic taint.

item:balnir-snapdragons.text: Balnir Snapdragons. Balnir Snapdragons are vibrant flowers cultivated at the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. Naturally receptive to magical currents, they serve the Forsaken as delicate indicators for detecting the creep of Scourge corruption from the bordering Plaguelands. These colorful blooms still grow in the garden of the Balnir Farmstead, a homestead in eastern Tirisfal Glades left in ruin by the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Scourge. Lying so close to the Plaguelands to the east, the garden sits right where the Lich King's blight presses against Tirisfal, which makes its flowers a telling place to look for the spread of that corruption. Because snapdragons are unusually sensitive to atmospheric magic, they act as living barometers for magical blights. Anastasia Hartwell and the Forsaken mages in the Undercity seek fresh specimens from the farmstead's window boxes. By turning the plants over to the Royal Apothecary Society, the Undercity hopes to analyze the flora and measure how deeply the Lich King's plague has seeped across the border into Tirisfal's soil.

item:baron-longshore-s-head.text: Baron Longshore's Head. This severed head is proof of the death of Baron Longshore, captain of the Southsea Freebooter vessel Heedless. Gazlowe posted a public bounty for the pirate's identifiable remains to protect Ratchet's commercial shipping along the Merchant Coast. Operating out of camps along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Baron Longshore directed raids against regional merchant vessels on behalf of the Southsea Freebooters. His flagship, the Heedless, posed a direct threat to the goblin trade lanes linking Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Gazlowe, Chief Engineer of Ratchet, placed a bounty on Longshore requiring identifiable proof of demise. Delivering the pirate's head satisfies the contract and secures a monetary reward from the port authority.

item:barrel-of-barleybrew-scalder.text: Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder. The Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder is a cask of stout ale crafted by the Barleybrew family to prove their brewing prowess against their chief competitors. It is entrusted to covert couriers tasked with infiltrating the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos to stage a sly taste-test sabotage. Brewing is serious business among the dwarves of Dun Morogh, and few rivalries burn hotter than the feud between the Thunderbrews and the Barleybrews. While the Thunderbrews enjoy vast renown and pride of place from their busy distillery in Kharanos, Marleth Barleybrew refuses to sit in their shadow. Rather than relying solely on open taverns, Marleth brews the fiery 'Scalder' to prove his recipes are second to none—hoping that unsuspecting patrons who taste it will realize the Thunderbrews do not hold a monopoly on fine dwarven drink.

item:barrel-of-shimmer-stout.text: Barrel of Shimmer Stout. A freshly brewed cask of Rejold Barleybrew's experimental dwarven ale, crafted in the cold reaches of Dun Morogh. Known for giving drinkers a potent jolt that supposedly brightens their vision, it is intended as a gift for guards keeping watch on the high mountain passes. Crafted by Rejold Barleybrew after gathering rare ingredients across Dun Morogh, Shimmer Stout represents the latest triumph of the storied Barleybrew family. Dwarven brewers take their craft with deadly seriousness, constantly competing to produce hearty concoctions capable of staving off the freezing mountain chill. Rejold's latest recipe is designed not only to warm the gut, but to sharpen the senses of those stationed out in the freezing winds. This particular barrel is earmarked for Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew, who stands guard at the southern tower along the pass leading into Loch Modan. Out on the lonely frontier, mountaineers endure bone-chilling cold and prolonged watches between skirmishes with troggs and wildlife. A fresh cask of family ale serves as both a welcome taste of home and an energizing tonic potent enough to make a tired sentry swear he can see clearly through the dark.

item:barrel-of-thunder-ale.text: Barrel of Thunder Ale. The Barrel of Thunder Ale is a prized keg of Kharanos's signature brew, smuggled straight out of the Thunderbrew Distillery's cellar. Swapped out for a cask of Marleth's Barleybrew Scalder, it serves as undeniable proof of foul play in an escalating brewing rivalry. In Dun Morogh, competition between rival master brewers runs deep, and few disputes are fiercer than the feud between the Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village. Marleth Barleybrew sought to slip a barrel of his own Barleybrew Scalder into his rivals' cellar, so that the Thunderbrews' patrons would taste his brew over theirs. This heavy barrel of Thunder Ale was seized in the exchange, dragged out under the noses of the local guards as physical evidence that the switch succeeded.

item:barrow-key.text: Barrow Key. The Barrow Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. It is kept locked inside a barrow cache to guard the ancient treasures sealed within the den's hoard. Within the subterranean barrows of the Talon Den, night elf druids established elaborate wards to protect their relics from interlopers. The Barrow Key is one piece of this multi-layered lock, concealed inside a specialized cache hidden among the subterranean passages. Accessing it requires the Gatekeeper's Key, ensuring that only those with knowledge of the druids' defensive network can ever hope to claim it.

item:bartleby-s-mug.text: Bartleby's Mug. Bartleby's Mug is the personal drinking vessel of the stubborn brawler Bartleby in Stormwind. Surrendered only after a tavern brawl and emptied down to the last drop, it serves as proof of a warrior's ability to forcefully persuade an uncooperative opponent. To the casual tavern regular, Bartleby's Mug is nothing more than ordinary drinkware clutched tight by a notoriously stubborn drinker. For a novice warrior training in Stormwind, however, wrestling the vessel away from Bartleby is a test of sheer physical dominance. Bartleby will not relinquish his beloved mug until knocked into submission—and even then, he insists on draining every last drop before handing it over as a trophy.

item:bathran-s-hair.text: Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is a rare, delicate herb found among the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale. Celebrated in night elf lore for its potent restorative qualities, the plant is believed to mend afflictions of the spirit as well as the flesh. Grown in the shadows of the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, Bathran's Hair has long been valued by night elf healers. Unlike common medicinal flora that soothe simple physical wounds, this herb possesses restorative properties said to cure deep ailments of the spirit. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls victim to an insidious, unyielding sickness, the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks strands of this rare plant to brew a vital remedy.

item:battleboar-flank.text: Battleboar Flank. Battleboar Flanks are hearty cuts of meat harvested from the vicious battleboars trained by Bristleback quilboar in Mulgore. Collected by young hunters around Camp Narache, they serve both as proof of culled threats and as nourishing sustenance for the tauren tribe. The Bristleback quilboar lurking in Brambleblade Ravine have trained vicious battleboars to encroach on tauren hunting grounds. While these aggressive beasts pose a direct hazard to the young tauren coming of age at Camp Narache, nothing taken from nature is wasted. Grull Hawkwind directs novice hunters to harvest the flanks of these felled beasts alongside their snouts. The cuts of flank provide rich, sustaining meat that is cooked down into hearty stew for the tribe's youth, turning a quilboar weapon of war into vital tribal nourishment.

item:battleboar-snout.text: Battleboar Snout. Battleboar Snouts are harvested from the aggressive boars trained by the Bristleback quilboar in Mulgore. Collected by young tauren hunters, they serve both as proof of thinning an invasive threat and as hearty ingredients for tribal cooking in Camp Narache. In the shadow of Red Cloud Mesa, the Bristleback quilboar train malicious battleboars within Brambleblade Ravine to probe tauren hunting grounds. When young braves are sent out by Grull Hawkwind to push back against this encroachment, the snout serves as undeniable proof of a beast brought down. Rather than wasting any part of the kill, the tauren use these snouts alongside cuts of flank to prepare rich, sustaining stews to feed their young.

item:battleworn-axe.text: Battleworn Axe. Battleworn Axes are crude, notch-scarred weapons carried by the Blackrock orcs invading the Redridge Mountains. Marshal Marris accepts these recovered blades in Lakeshire as physical proof of dead invaders threatening the local populace. These heavy, nicked axes serve as standard gear for the Blackrock reavers pushing south from the Burning Steppes into Redridge. For Marshal Marris and the beleaguered town watch of Lakeshire, collecting them serves two purposes: ensuring another marauding orc has fallen, and gathering physical evidence of how heavily armed the encroaching warband truly is. Blackrock invaders have fortified Stonewatch Keep and established footholds in the southeastern pockets of Redridge, effectively trapping townspeople within Lakeshire. Stripping the raiders of their battleworn weapons directly diminishes the arms available to the warband while clearing the roads for Alliance travel.

item:berard-s-journal.text: Berard's Journal. Berard's Journal is a collection of research notes penned by Apothecary Berard before he fell victim to Archmage Arugal's curse. Left behind in Pyrewood Village, the book documents Berard's study of an ancient plague that once wiped out the aquatic life of Lake Lordamere, making it highly valuable to the Royal Apothecary Society. Before Archmage Arugal unleashed his shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was considered one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising minds. Stationed in Pyrewood Village, he focused his work on an ancient, virulent blight that had eradicated all aquatic life within Lake Lordamere centuries prior. When Arugal's curse gripped the settlement, Berard's mind was shattered, turning him into another mindless thrall. His detailed field notes remained behind on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

item:bernice-s-necklace.text: Bernice's Necklace. Bernice's Necklace is a sentimental heirloom belonging to "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield of the Stonefield Farm in Elwynn Forest. Originally worn as a lucky charm by her late husband during his military service, the trinket was lost near the Fargodeep Mine and snatched by an opportunistic kobold. Though known locally as Bernice's necklace, the piece originally belonged to Auntie Bernice Stonefield's late husband. A veteran of Stormwind's military campaigns, he carried the charm as a token of good fortune into battle. According to Bernice, the only time tragedy struck was during his final campaign—the one expedition where he forgot to bring his lucky necklace along. Following his death, the keepsake remained one of Bernice's most cherished possessions on the Stonefield Farm.

item:besseleth-s-fang.text: Besseleth's Fang. Besseleth's Fang is the massive venomous tooth harvested from the giant spider Besseleth in Sishir Canyon. Carried as proof of her demise, it represents the removal of a deadly threat stalking the trails of Stonetalon Mountains. Sishir Canyon has long been infested by aggressive arachnids, but none strike more terror into travelers than Besseleth. Growing to monstrous proportions, she and her brood turned the gorge into a death trap for wanderers navigating the Webwinder Path at night. The fang itself measures nearly two feet in length and drips with potent venom, making it an unmistakable signature of the broodmother's slaughter. Presenting this grisly trophy brings relief to local defenders who have suffered her venomous strikes.

item:bethor-s-scroll.text: Bethor's Scroll. Bethor's Scroll contains magical incantations scribed by Bethor Iceshard to counter the dark sorcery of his former colleague, Thule Ravenclaw. Created to aid Apothecary Renferrel in brewing a protective draught, the scroll is vital for surviving the Scourge necromancy guarding Fenris Isle. Upon examining tainted ichor recovered from Rot Hide gnolls, Bethor Iceshard recognized the handiwork of Thule Ravenclaw. Once a promising young mage of the Kirin Tor, Thule betrayed his brethren to serve the Lich King when the Scourge rose to power. Learning that Thule had survived and was directing Rot Hide attacks across Silverpine Forest from Fenris Isle, Bethor drew upon his intimate knowledge of his former colleague's spellcraft to author this scroll.

item:bingles-blastencapper.text: Bingles' Blastencapper. Bingles' Blastencapper is a specialized explosive device designed by the gnome pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when his gyrocopter plunged into the Loch, it was stolen by local troggs, endangering Bingles' plans to support the liberation of Gnomeregan. Bingles' Blastencapper represents the peak of pilot Bingles Blastenheimer's personal ordnance. Built to deliver decisive aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes overruning Gnomeregan, the explosive was aboard his gyrocopter when mechanical failure sent him plummeting into the waters of the Loch. While Bingles survived, troggs infesting the lake's northern islands pillaged his wreckage and dragged the volatile weapon back to their camps. To Bingles, the Blastencapper is far more than simple salvage. The exiled gnomes are actively preparing to take back their radioactive home, and Bingles considers his gyrocopter and signature munitions vital components of the impending air assault. Recovering this ordnance prevents the indigenous troggs of Loch Modan from accidentally triggering a catastrophe and preserves a valuable weapon for the gnomish resistance.

item:bingles-hammer.text: Bingles' Hammer. Bingles' Hammer is an engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, an eccentric gnome aviator stranded in Loch Modan. After crashing his flying machine into the Loch, hostile troggs scavenged the hammer along with his other specialized gear. Bingles needs it recovered so he can repair his aircraft and aid the war effort to liberate Gnomeregan. When pilot Bingles Blastenheimer plunged into the waters of the Loch, his survival was only the first of his troubles. Troggs inhabiting the freshwater islands quickly raided the crash site, looting his specialized toolkit and high-potency explosives. Among the pilfered gear was his hammer, an indispensable implement for repairing the dented airframe and recalibrating the gyrocopter's mechanical assemblies. Without this essential tool and the rest of his equipment, Bingles remains thoroughly grounded, unable to fly support runs for the gnome liberation forces struggling to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:bingles-screwdriver.text: Bingles' Screwdriver. Bingles' Screwdriver is an essential engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, a gnome pilot who crashed his gyrocopter into the waters of Loch Modan. Following the crash, native troggs plundered the wreckage, scattering Bingles' tool buckets and specialized gear across the loch's northern islands. When Bingles Blastenheimer plummeted into the Loch, he lost more than his flying machine—he lost the specialized equipment needed to repair it. Among the scattered gear was his trusty screwdriver, packed away inside one of several tool buckets snatched up by opportunistic troggs inhabiting the nearby isles. For an engineer stranded in the wilderness, fine adjustment tools like this screwdriver are irreplaceable, especially when assembling delicate gyrocopter mechanisms or handling volatile armaments. Bingles is not merely a recreational aviator; he serves a larger cause dedicated to liberating the fallen city of Gnomeregan from troggs and leper gnomes. His mission relies on combining flight mechanics with his volatile Blastencapper munitions to deliver an aerial assault against the subterranean menace. Recovering this screwdriver alongside his wrench and hammer is crucial for putting his gyrocopter back together and keeping the gnomish airborne counteroffensive alive.

item:bingles-wrench.text: Bingles' Wrench. Bingles' Wrench is a vital piece of gnomish engineering gear belonging to the pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when Bingles crash-landed his flying machine into the Loch, it was hauled off by the local troggs alongside the rest of his toolkit. After Bingles Blastenheimer crashed his gyrocopter into the placid waters of the Loch, his survival quickly turned into an ordeal. Troggs inhabiting the small northern islands raided the crash site, looting his specialized supplies and scattering his tools into various buckets across their camps. Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools needed alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without it, Bingles has no hope of repairing his downed gyrocopter, stalling his planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

item:black-claw-stout.text: Black Claw Stout. Black Claw Stout is a special drink prepared by Zardeth of the Black Claw beneath the streets of Stormwind. Concocted for a meddlesome nobleman, it is delivered under the guise of an ordinary tavern beverage.

item:black-feather-quill.text: Black Feather Quill. The Black Feather Quill is a sacred night elf relic used by the Druids of the Talon during their rites of hibernation and awakening. Stored within a dedicated chest in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, it is one of several vital focuses needed to safely call slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druidism relies on deeply attuned sacred items to navigate the threshold between the waking world and the Emerald Dream. The Black Feather Quill, along with the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting, forms the core set of ritual items required to break the delicate hibernation of the Druids of the Talon. Without these focuses, a slumbering druid risks remaining trapped within the Dream indefinitely, unable to rejoin their waking body. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the sacred chests housing these treasures fell into danger. Left unguarded in the winding depths, the relics had to be recovered swiftly by order of Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the captive druids were lost forever to the Dream.

item:blackened-skull.text: Blackened Skull. A blackened skull is the darkened cranial remnant of a Darkeye Bonecaster animating in the Agamand Mills. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill demands these grisly trophies as proof of thinning the mindless Scourge forces threatening Tirisfal Glades. These blackened skulls are salvaged from the Darkeye Bonecasters haunting the Agamand Mills. These skeletal spellcasters direct necromantic malice against the living and the Forsaken alike, attempting to entrench a forward base for the Lich King's armies in northern Tirisfal. Presenting their ruined skulls to Deathguard Dillinger serves as tangible evidence that the Scourge's mystical vanguard is being crushed.

item:bloodfeather-belt.text: Bloodfeather Belt. A Bloodfeather Belt is a crude leather strap worn by the Bloodfeather harpies infesting northern Teldrassil. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak collects these belts as proof that local nests encroaching on the Oracle Glade have been cleared. The Bloodfeather harpies have nested aggressively in the boughs around the Oracle Glade, threatening the ancient Oracle Tree and choking travel through northern Teldrassil. When a runner carrying reports to Darnassus was ambushed and slain by the flock, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak called on travelers to strike back directly at their nests. Taking the belts from fallen harpies serves as tangible proof that their numbers are being culled, securing the paths so communication with the capital can resume.

item:bloodfury-ripper-s-remains.text: Bloodfury Ripper's Remains. Bloodfury Ripper's Remains are the physical proof recovered from the matriarch of the Bloodfury harpies in the Charred Vale. Sought by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat, this trophy confirms the death of the brood's ferocious leader, dealing a decisive blow to the harpy presence threatening the local tauren settlement. The Bloodfury harpies nesting within the scorched ruins of the Charred Vale have long posed a savage threat to the travelers and shamans of the Stonetalon Mountains. While culling their numbers thins the immediate danger, Maggran Earthbinder of Sun Rock Retreat recognizes that true reprieve requires eliminating their leadership. Bloodfury Ripper rules her flock almost as a queen, guiding their territorial aggression. Taking her remains is essential proof of her demise, scattering the remaining harpies into disarray and granting peace of mind to the tauren striving to heal and secure their rugged lands.

item:bloodstone-choker.text: Bloodstone Choker. The Bloodstone Choker is a dark magical talisman crafted from bloodstone, originally held by the warlock mentor Gakin the Darkbinder. Stolen by a treacherous apprentice who fled to the Defias Brotherhood, it serves as a powerful ritual focus capable of piercing the void to draw forth and bind a Voidwalker. Carved from bloodstone, the choker possesses the latent mystical authority required to bridge the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. Once returned to Gakin, it is immediately put to the test in the crypts beneath the tavern. A warlock must channel the choker's magic at the underground summoning circle to rip a hostile Voidwalker from the void. Only by subduing the furious entity in direct combat while wielding the talisman can a practitioner prove the willpower necessary to command such a guardian.

item:blueleaf-tuber.text: Blueleaf Tuber. Blueleaf Tubers are exceptionally rare root vegetables that grow concealed beneath the thorny terrain of Razorfen Kraul. Prized across the world as an exotic culinary delicacy, they are almost impossible to locate with the naked eye. Though native to the Barrens, Blueleaf Tubers grow only in the subterranean depths beneath Razorfen Kraul. Concealed beneath the dense root systems and quilboar briars, they remain hidden to casual foragers. Despite their harsh growing conditions, they fetch an exorbitant price among wealthy gourmands and traders worldwide who savor their unique flavor. Because the roots cannot be easily spotted by surface dwellers, the enterprising goblin Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet devised an unusual harvesting method. By training native snufflenose gophers to detect the tubers by scent from fifty paces away, adventurers guided by specialized command sticks can unearth the roots from the soil before quilboar patrols catch wind of the intrusion.

item:book-from-sven-s-farm.text: Book from Sven's Farm. The Book from Sven's Farm is a dirt-stained, untitled journal unearthed from the ruins of Sven Yorgen's ransacked homestead in Duskwood. Its fragmented entries reveal that an unknown onlooker witnessed the massacre of Sven's family, sparking a relentless hunt across the shadowed woods. Buried in a loose dirt mound amid the charred remains of Sven's farm in southern Duskwood, this unassuming, weather-damaged volume contains the frantic notes of an anonymous wanderer. The entries offer incomplete glimpses into the tragedy that struck the farmstead, confirming Sven Yorgen's darkest suspicion: someone lurked in the shadows while his family was slain. Because the narrative cuts off abruptly, the book raises more questions than answers, prompting investigators to carry it back to Darkshire in search of anyone who recognizes the handwriting or its enigmatic author.

item:book-stresses-of-iron.text: Book: Stresses of Iron. The Stresses of Iron is a scholarly metallurgical text authored by Margulf Blaggon. Originally kept in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep, it became the focus of an errand between monks after being loaned out to Northshire Abbey for transcribing. Written by Margulf Blaggon, The Stresses of Iron covers the practical and theoretical properties of metallurgy. Kept within the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep under the care of Milton Sheaf, the book was loaned to Northshire Abbey so that Brother Paxton could copy its contents by hand for his own collection. Paxton's transcription took far longer than anticipated, leaving Brother Kristoff in Cathedral Square waiting anxiously for the text to return to the city.

item:bottle-of-disease.text: Bottle of Disease. A Bottle of Disease is a vial of virulent concoctions brewed by the Forsaken operating in Ashenvale. Found at an encampment near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, these vials represent an ominous attempt by the undead to introduce blighted plagues into the pristine night elven wilderness. Deep within the ancient canopy of eastern Ashenvale, the Forsaken have crept far past the front lines of the Warsong Outriders. Establishing an outpost near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, undead alchemists brew foul contagions and seal them within glass bottles. To the night elves guarding Forest Song, these vials are clear evidence of a quiet, insidious offensive aimed at sickening the woodland soil and wildlife rather than engaging in open combat.

item:bottle-of-moonshine.text: Bottle of Moonshine. A Bottle of Moonshine is a potent alcoholic spirit sold in the gloomy settlement of Darkshire. Barkeep Daniels of Lakeshire urgently seeks a bottle to help restock the town tavern as Blackrock orc incursions cut off regular supply shipments. Lakeshire stands besieged by the Blackrock clan, leaving its local innkeeper, Barkeep Daniels, in dire straits as regular supply caravans fail to arrive. To keep up morale among the town guards and beleaguered townsfolk, Daniels sends couriers across the southern kingdoms to gather regional specialties. Among these is a potent bottle of moonshine brewed and sold at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in neighboring Duskwood, where locals favor stiff drinks to ward off the encroaching dread of the woods.

item:bottle-of-zombie-juice.text: Bottle of Zombie Juice. A Bottle of Zombie Juice is a potent, foul liquor brewed from the pungent rot blossom found in Duskwood. Procured from the tavern in Darkshire, it is supposedly requested by the reclusive hermit Abercrombie to ward off the chill of the gloomy woods. Brewed from rot blossoms gathered among the shadowed soils of Duskwood, Zombie Juice is a remarkably harsh brew. The bartender who provides it warns that the drink is potent enough to raise the dead. While ordinary folk steer clear of such vile distillations, the eccentric hermit Abercrombie claims it is the only thing capable of keeping him warm on the damp, cold nights out by his lonely shack.

item:bottom-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. The Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered mechanical winding key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel foundered off Darkshore, the piece was scavenged by the shoreline's native reef crawlers. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was sunk by threshadons off the coast of Darkshore, the gnome was thrown ashore along with his belongings. Among his most prized possessions was the winding key used to activate his mechanical first mate. The key shattered on the coastal rocks into three distinct pieces, and local scavengers immediately descended upon the debris. The bottom piece of the key was snatched up by the aggressive crustaceans wandering the surf—specifically the reef and tide crawlers that pick through the detritus along the tideline.

item:branch-of-cenarius.text: Branch of Cenarius. The Branch of Cenarius is a sacred dryad relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis in eastern Ashenvale. Recovering this heirloom was the dying wish of the dryad Anilia, who perished defending it from the woods' corruptors. Revered by the daughters of Cenarius, the Branch of Cenarius represents both the blessing of the Forest Lord and the deep connection his dryads maintain with Ashenvale. The branch was held in high regard by the dryad sisters Anilia and Illiyana until a band of corrupt satyrs ambushed them. The satyr leader, Geltharis, seized the relic and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. With her dying breaths, Anilia pointed northward toward the arch where Geltharis lurks, pleading for a champion to wrest the sacred bough from his claws and restore it to dryad hands at Forest Song.

item:brass-collar.text: Brass Collar. The Brass Collar is a sturdy neckpiece worn by Princess, a prize-winning sow owned by the Brackwell family. It serves as tangible proof for Ma Stonefield that the gluttonous beast has been put down before ruining her farm's crops. Princess is no ordinary swine; she is an enormous, ribbon-worthy pig belonging to the Brackwell family who roams around their pumpkin patch east of the Maclure homestead. Unfortunately for her neighbors, her prize-winning size is fueled by a ravenous appetite for the crops at the Stonefield Farm. Tired of losing her valuable vegetables to the wandering glutton, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay the massive sow. Because Princess wears a prominent brass band around her neck, her collar serves as undeniable proof that the marauding pig will never raid the Stonefield fields again.

item:bristleback-attack-plans.text: Bristleback Attack Plans. The Bristleback Attack Plans are crude maps and tactical notes drafted by the quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine. They outline a coordinated siege aimed directly at overrunning the tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Hidden deep within a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine, these scribbled tactical sketches reveal that the Bristleback quilboar are no longer just skirmishing on the borders of the Red Cloud Mesa. Instead, their leadership planned an organized, sustained assault to push into Camp Narache and wipe out the young tauren training there. Delivering this map to Chief Hawkwind allows the tribe to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements, blunting the impending invasion before it can begin.

item:bristleback-belt.text: Bristleback Belt. A Bristleback Belt is a piece of crudely crafted gear worn by the quilboar infesting Brambleblade Ravine. For young tauren coming of age in Camp Narache, collecting these belts serves as physical proof of valor during the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests every youth who aspires to earn respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. The first trial, the Rite of Strength, requires the initiate to protect the tribe from active threats. Because the hostile Bristleback quilboar repeatedly raid tribal food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind demands the belts of these intruders. Returning twelve belts to the chieftain proves that an initiate can confront danger directly and strike a blow for the tribe's defense. Stripped from Bristleback quilboar warriors and shamans throughout Brambleblade Ravine, these belts are fashioned from rough hide, twine, and scrap. While worthless as apparel to a tauren warrior, they are distinctly quilboar make and serve as unmistakable evidence of a slain enemy. Bringing them back to the camp circle fulfills the proof required by the rite.

item:bristleback-quilboar-tusk.text: Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are harvested from the slain Bristleback quilboar across the northern and central Barrens. Collected as proof of slaughter, they serve as gruesome tokens of vengeance for the grieving orc warrior Mankrik. Bristleback quilboar inhabit thickets and bramble dens throughout the Barrens, fiercely defending their territory against Horde expansion. Their tusks are prominent, jagged ivory used as natural weapons in close quarters. For Mankrik, a veteran warrior stationed at the Crossroads whose wife was lost during a vicious quilboar ambush, these tusks represent more than simple hunter trophies. Collecting dozens of them is a measure of pure retribution, a bloody tally meant to ensure the Bristlebacks suffer as deeply as he has.

item:brock-s-list.text: Brock's List. Brock's List is a dispatch compiled by the mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. It contains the names of top mining pupils who have earned honorary picks from the guild halls in Ironforge. Mining is the lifeblood of dwarven civilization, and apprentice diggers must prove their skill before they are entrusted with serious work in Khaz Modan's veins. In Thelsamar, the local mining trainer compiles this parchment to reward students who excel in their lessons. The document records those who have earned honorary picks—coveted symbols of competence forged in the capital. Because the honorary tools must be etched and distributed from the capital, the parchment is entrusted to travelers bound for Ironforge. Carried aboard a gryphon from Thelsamar's roost, Brock's List makes its way directly to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Deep Mountain Mining Guild in the Great Forge, where the honored students' names are engraved into stone and steel.

item:broken-and-battered-samophlange.text: Broken and Battered Samophlange. The Broken and Battered Samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical device recovered from Venture Company operations in the Barrens. After a botched tinkering attempt pushed its structural integrity to critical lows, it must be carried to goblin experts in Orgrimmar who might actually understand how it functions. A samophlange is an obscure piece of proprietary machinery designed by the Venture Company for their resource operations in the northern Barrens. When Wenikee Boltbucket attempted to inspect and modify one, she affixed extraneous gauges, levers, and dials to measure its stability. Instead of stabilizing the mechanism, her amateur meddling devastated its structural integrity, leaving it battered and teetering on the verge of ruin. Realizing more gadgets would only cause total failure, she packed off the fragile assembly to someone with real factory experience. Salvaging the broken device requires the insight of someone who has worked directly on Venture Company production lines. This leads travelers to Rilli Greasygob, a former Venture employee now operating out of Nogg's Machine Shop in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. Handing over such a battered apparatus immediately catches the engineer's eye, marking anyone daring enough to scavenge from goblin operations as either remarkably daring or foolhardy.

item:broken-samophlange.text: Broken Samophlange. The Broken Samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical device recovered from the northern Barrens. Despite its damaged state, its internal gears and shifting parts captivate engineers curious enough to uncover its true function. The samophlange remains one of the stranger contraptions found throughout the northern Barrens. Even when broken, the mechanism exhibits remarkable internal craftsmanship, filled with moving assemblies and fine gears. The Ratchet goblin Sputtervalve accidentally damaged the delicate apparatus before its full operation could be documented. Eager to deliver working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, the finder sought someone skilled enough to restore it, turning to Wenikee Boltbucket—a clever tinkerer stationed near the border outpost of Mor'shan Rampart. Upon examining the ruined apparatus, even an inquisitive mind like Wenikee's cannot immediately deduce what a samophlange is actually designed to do. However, the tantalizing sounds of internal clockwork and its dynamic motion immediately draw her interest. Rather than discarding the ruined junk, the mystery of its design inspires an attempt to repair it and witness its mechanisms working at full capacity.

item:broken-tools.text: Broken Tools. Broken Tools are the shattered remnants of dwarven prospector picks, intentionally destroyed at an anvil. They serve as physical proof to Baine Bloodhoof that the invasive dwarven excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been disrupted. To the northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators have set up operations to delve into the hills of Mulgore. While the dwarves seek buried ancient history, the tauren view their aggressive excavation as a direct defilement of the Earth Mother. The noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, particularly the roaming kodo herds. Rather than merely driving the excavators away, young Baine Bloodhoof instructs defenders to confiscate the prospectors' iron picks and shatter them upon a forge, rendering the expedition unable to gouge further into the earth.

item:bundle-of-crocolisk-skins.text: Bundle of Crocolisk Skins. The Bundle of Crocolisk Skins is a prepared package of cured reptilian hides harvested from the dangerous marshes of the Wetlands. Destined for the leatherworkers of Menethil Harbor, it serves as valuable trade stock for crafting sturdy boots and tough harbor gear. The vast waterways of the Wetlands are teeming with crocolisks, whose tough, water-resistant hides are an essential commodity for the coastal settlement of Menethil Harbor. Hunters braving the bogs collect and cure these skins before sending them westward to local artisans like James Halloran. However, this particular bundle took an unusual detour into an adventurer's hands: the hunter Einar sought a courier purely to avoid returning to town and facing the temper of his frustrated wife, Sida.

item:bundle-of-hides.text: Bundle of Hides. A Bundle of Hides consists of cured skins collected from the beasts of the Barrens, bundled together for transport across central Kalimdor. Bound for the leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff, it serves as a straightforward courier shipment that introduces travelers to the Horde's wind rider flight network. The untamed plains of the Barrens are home to vast herds of kodo, prowling lions, and roving raptors. Hunters along the trade paths skin these creatures not only for meat and survival, but to supply city artisans. Without raw pelts from the wilds, settlements like Thunder Bluff would struggle to sustain their local leathercrafters, who transform dried skins into essential gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde. Transporting heavy goods overland through the Barrens and up into Mulgore is dangerous and slow, constantly threatened by roaming quilboar and centaur raiders. To speed delivery between the Crossroads and the tauren capital, couriers rely on Devrak's trained wyverns. Handing a bundle of hides to a wind rider courier demonstrates the sheer efficiency of air travel across Kalimdor's fractured terrain.

item:bundle-of-wood.text: Bundle of Wood. Bundles of Wood are tied timber stacks harvested by laborers near the Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. Recently abandoned due to prowling wildlife, they represent critical shipments needed to fulfill local lumber contracts. The Eastvale Logging Camp serves as a primary source of lumber for the Kingdom of Stormwind, sending freshly chopped wood westward to sustain town infrastructure and construction projects. Recently, aggressive local wildlife—specifically forest bears and prowling wolves—pushed into the groves northwest of the camp. Terrified loggers fled for their lives, abandoning freshly gathered Bundles of Wood where they lay among the trees. Facing tight delivery deadlines, camp overseers rely on brave travelers to slip past the predators and retrieve the cut lumber before contracts are breached.

item:burning-blade-medallion.text: Burning Blade Medallion. The Burning Blade Medallion is a dark talisman carried by cultists lurking within the Valley of Trials. Guarded by dark magic in the depths of the Burning Blade Coven, it serves as direct proof of demonic corruption attempting to subvert the young warriors of Durotar. Discovered deep inside the winding caverns of the Burning Blade Coven, the medallion is held by Yarrog Baneshadow, an agent of the sinister Burning Blade cult. Identified through the divinations of Zureetha Fargaze, the trinket channels dark power amidst the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Striking down its bearer and seizing the medallion cuts short an insidious attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar itself.

item:burning-blood-quest-item.text: Burning Blood (quest item). Burning Blood is an unnatural fluid harvested from the ferocious Nightbane worgen prowling Duskwood. The Stormwind armorer Grimand Elmore requires twenty vials of this fiery essence to experiment with advanced smithing techniques. The cursed Nightbane worgen infesting Duskwood run hot with a strange, unnatural fury, and their blood burns with literal heat. This searing fluid can be drawn from the beasts haunting the haunted timberlands and the abandoned dig site of Roland's Doom. While grotesque to harvest, the fiery substance holds rare metallurgical properties coveted by master armorers seeking to quench and temper resilient plate. Grimand Elmore, a veteran craftsman working in the Dwarven District of Stormwind, seeks to test novel smithing methods pioneered by his former student Furen Longbeard. To see if these radical forging techniques hold merit, Elmore requires burning blood alongside a dense burning rock held by the worgen chieftain Gutspill. Those willing to face the predatory pack and return with the bubbling fluid are promised sturdy warrior armor forged in the heat of his forge.

item:burning-rock.text: Burning Rock. The Burning Rock is an unusual, smoldering mineral recovered from the Nightbane worgen leader Gutspill deep within Roland's Doom in Duskwood. Master blacksmith Grimand Elmore in Stormwind requires this rare curiosity, alongside fiery worgen blood, to forge specialized enchanted armor for promising warriors. Carried by Gutspill, a savage Nightbane worgen lurking in the decrepit shafts of Roland's Doom, the Burning Rock is an anomaly among Duskwood's subterranean horrors. Emitting an unyielding supernatural heat, it caught the attention of Grimand Elmore in Stormwind City. Seeking to test experimental smithing techniques originated by his peer Furen Longbeard, Grimand uses the rock's intrinsic heat and the boiling blood of the local worgen to temper tough armor plate for veteran fighters.

item:cache-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. The Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture is a stockpile of potent poison secured inside a locked chest at the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Named for the jungle troll witch doctor Zanzil, it serves as a critical target for the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company keeps a tower outpost. A cache of an altered mixture bearing the name of the infamous troll witch doctor Zanzil sits locked inside Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix's private strongbox at the summit of the tower. A poison has weakened everything in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to any intruder bold enough to strike.

item:cactus-apple.text: Cactus Apple. Cactus Apples are tough, moisture-rich fruits harvested from the rugged flora of Durotar's Valley of Trials. Flourishing in the arid desert heat, they are prized by local orcs as a rare, refreshing source of sustenance. The sun-scorched earth of Durotar offers little luxury, forcing its inhabitants to make use of whatever hardy plants survive the elements. Cactus apples grow in clusters around the thick cactuses dotting the Valley of Trials. While difficult to gather without catching a few thorns, the fruit provides vital hydration in the sweltering canyon. A local orc named Galgar gathers these fruits to prepare his signature Cactus Apple Surprise, a cooling confection that brings welcome relief to recruits enduring their harsh initial training.

item:calor-s-note.text: Calor's Note. Calor's Note is a scrap of faded parchment written by the woodsman Calor to recommend a tested adventurer to Master Jonathan Carevin. It serves as an introduction into a shadowy cadre operating alongside, yet distinct from, Darkshire's formal town militia. Duskwood offers very little warmth to strangers, and Calor is notoriously hard to impress. Surviving encounters with the bloodthirsty worgen stalking the woods earns his respect, prompting him to draft this brief message. Carried to Darkshire, the faded note acts as a badge of credibility, introducing an outsider directly to Jonathan Carevin. While Darkshire relies on the Night Watch for public defense, Calor and Carevin pursue a grimmer, more clandestine fight. Calor openly laments being outnumbered by the town guard, hoping for enough capable fighters to advance their private war. Delivery of the note grants entry into Carevin's campaign against demons, undead, and the hidden sympathizers abetting Duskwood's decline.

item:candle-of-beckoning.text: Candle of Beckoning. The Candle of Beckoning is an enchanted ritual taper kept by the reclusive necromancer Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. Placing and lighting the candle upon an altar on a nearby islet summons forth a restless spirit known as Lillith Nefara. Found stored in a crate beside the solitary mage Gunther Arcanus on his island in Brightwater Lake, the Candle of Beckoning serves as an instrument in a dark ritual of summoning. Gunther is a fiercely independent undead sorcerer who broke free of the Lich King's command on his own, remaining wary of the Scourge and the Forsaken alike. To prove your loyalty is not to the Lich King, Gunther directs you to take one of these candles southwest to a smaller islet. There, set upon an old, bloodstained table, the candle's flame pierces the veil between worlds to awaken and beckon the dormant shade of Lillith Nefara, a powerful Scourge agent, so she may be destroyed.

item:cantation-of-manifestation.text: Cantation of Manifestation. The Cantation of Manifestation is a specialized arcane incantation written on a parchment scroll, used by mages to reveal unseen magical anomalies. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell provides it to apprentices investigating invisible magical entities haunting Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. The Cantation of Manifestation holds a focused spell designed to pierce magical veils and force incorporeal, invisible beings into the visible spectrum. Kept in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity near Anastasia Hartwell, the scroll is entrusted to capable mages tasked with containing rogue magical anomalies. When read aloud in an area suffering from arcane instability—such as Algernon's alchemical workshop in the Apothecarium—the words force stray rift spawns to materialize, allowing the caster to subdue and trap them within containment coffers for further study.

item:canvas-scraps.text: Canvas Scraps. Canvas Scraps are remnants of tough woven fabric carried by human invaders and centaur tribes encroaching upon Durotar. In Razor Hill, aging veteran Furl Scornbrow collects these salvaged swatches to stitch useful travel sacks for fresh Horde recruits. Canvas is not a fabric native to the rough hide-working traditions of the Orcs, but it is abundant among Durotar's enemies. The Kul Tiras marines and sailors entrenched along the eastern shoreline carry heavy canvas gear and sailcloth remnants from their naval excursions. Further inland, the roaming Kolkar centaur repurpose scraps of coarse cloth looted from supply caravans and past conflicts. Defeating these hostiles yields durable remnants that can be salvaged from their camps and gear. Perched atop the Razor Hill watchtower, veteran Furl Scornbrow keeps an eye out for invaders while turning his hands to useful labor. Though past his fighting prime, the old warrior repurposes salvaged enemy fabric into sturdy carrying bags for younger soldiers. By turning the materials of Kul Tiras and the Kolkar against them, Furl equips the new generation of defenders fighting to secure the Horde's borders.

item:cask-of-merlot.text: Cask of Merlot. A Cask of Merlot is a barrel of fine red wine produced and sold in Stormwind City. It serves as one of several regional specialty liquors needed by the Lakeshire innkeeper during the supply shortages caused by the Blackrock orc invasion. Harvested and fermented in the heart of the kingdom, this Cask of Merlot comes straight from the cellars of the Galina Winery, nestled along the canals bordering Stormwind's Trade District. Winemaker Roberto Pupellyverbos manages the vintages there, catering to the capital's more refined palates.
