Provided by the hermit Brine in the Barrens, it is carried north into ancient night elf lands to secure a sacred, untainted liquid necessary to fashion the Water Totem. Communing with the spirit of water requires tangible communion with pure, undisturbed sources across Kalimdor. Handed down by the recluse Brine from her hilltop hut in the southern Barrens, the Empty Blue Waterskin represents the final and most perilous gathering task of a shaman's early training. It is destined to hold pristine water taken directly from a secluded fountain deep within the ancient Ruins of Stardust, nestled along the contested borderlands of Ashenvale. Filling this simple container demands that the initiate journey beyond the safety of Horde territory into the ancient groves guarded by nature beasts and night elves. Once dipped into the waters of the ruined sanctuary, the vessel becomes a Filled Blue Waterskin. Combined with samples from the Barrens and Tarren Mill, its contents allow Brine to brew the draught needed to summon and appease the elemental spirit of water.

item:empty-brown-waterskin.text: Empty Brown Waterskin. The Empty Brown Waterskin is an elemental vessel provided by Brine during a shaman's trials in the Barrens. Used to gather water from a nearby oasis, it serves as the first physical tool in learning the delicate, contested nature of water in an arid land. In the sun-baked plains of the Barrens, water is far more than a resource; it is life itself and a constant spark for war. The hermit Brine entrusts an initiate with this simple leather skin as the opening trial of the Call of Water. The task seems modest—carry the empty vessel down to the watering hole beneath her dwelling and bring it back full. Yet in drawing from that solitary pool, the bearer immediately confronts the harsh truth of the land: every drop of liquid is jealously guarded by local quilboar who view the oasis as an invaluable hoard, forcing the initiate to understand how water both sustains life and drives mortals to violence.

item:empty-cleansing-bowl.text: Empty Cleansing Bowl. The Empty Cleansing Bowl is a ritual vessel given by Thundris Windweaver to aid in investigating the corruption of the Blackwood furbolgs. When filled at the Auberdine moonwell and combined with food samples, it creates a mixture capable of temporarily breaking a satyr's demonic sway. Entrusted to adventurers by Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the Empty Cleansing Bowl is crafted to carry sacred waters from the local moonwell. The night elves discovered that the northern Blackwood furbolgs fell under demonic madness orchestrated by satyrs, who exert their will through enchanted talismans. By drawing pure lunar water into the bowl and blending it with the furbolgs' harvested nuts, grains, and fruits, the vessel produces a blessed meal that temporarily restores sanity to the afflicted creatures, exposing the satyr overseer responsible.

item:empty-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler. The Empty Cliffspring Falls Sampler is a specialized flask entrusted to novice night elf druids by the Cenarion Circle. It is used to collect a water specimen from the mouth of Cliffspring River cave in Darkshore to help diagnose a foul poison corrupting the local wildlife. Cliffspring Falls provides the principal freshwater source for northern Darkshore, making any disturbance to its headwaters a mortal danger to the local ecosystem. When the native deer population began succumbing to a virulent wasting poison, Dendrite Starblaze of the Cenarion Circle provided these empty samplers to young druids sent out from Moonglade. Druids must venture deep into the cliffs near the falls, right to the entrance of a cave now overrun by hostile naga, to scoop up a viable water sample.

item:empty-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Empty Dreadmist Peak Sampler. The Empty Dreadmist Peak Sampler is a specialized Cenarion vessel entrusted to Horde druids to gather tainted water from the summit of Dreadmist Peak. Studying the foul liquid collected in this vial is vital for diagnosing and curing the spreading blight affecting wildlife in the northern Barrens. When a foul affliction began sickening gazelles and destabilizing the fragile ecology of the northern Barrens, druid Dendrite Starblaze suspected that the weather-influencing pools atop Dreadmist Peak were acting as the epicenter. He dispatched druid initiates with empty sampling vessels to brave the mountain's heights—now infested by the demon-worshipping Burning Blade—and extract raw water directly from the pool at the peak.

item:empty-leaden-collection-phial.text: Empty Leaden Collection Phial. The Empty Leaden Collection Phial is a shielded container designed by gnome tinkerers to harvest radioactive fallout from the ruins of Gnomeregan. Crafted from lead to protect the bearer from lethal contamination, it is used by adventurers assisting Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. Ozzie hopes the captured glow might yield a cure for their afflicted kin—or at least an extraordinarily potent beverage. When the vents of Gnomeregan flooded the subterranean city with toxic radiation to purge the trogg menace, it instead warped the surviving defenders into leper gnomes and irradiated the invading beasts. Seeking to study and reverse the fallout, Ozzie Togglevolt crafted the Empty Leaden Collection Phial. Made of heavy lead to shield handlers from the ambient danger, the specialized vial draws in the noxious green glow lingering on the bodies of Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers that prowl the ruins. Once sealed, the resulting Full Leaden Collection Phial provides the raw, dangerous matter needed for experimental remedies.

item:empty-red-waterskin.text: Empty Red Waterskin. The Empty Red Waterskin is a leather vessel entrusted to fledgling shaman during their elemental trials. It is used to collect fresh, untainted water from a surprising source in the plagued town of Tarren Mill. Given by the hermit Brine in the Barrens, this plain red skin serves a vital spiritual purpose in the Call of Water trials. Initiates are tasked with carrying it far across the sea to the Hillsbrad Foothills, seeking out the town of Tarren Mill. Though the town is occupied by the Forsaken and steeped in undeath, a lone well in its center continues to draw sweet, pristine spring water. Filling the red waterskin captures a vital sample of life persevering amidst blight, which Brine blends into a vial of purest water for the initiate's trial.

item:empty-sampling-tube.text: Empty Sampling Tube. The Empty Sampling Tube is a glass phial provided by Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. It is intended to collect corrupted water from the Cliffspring River so night elf scholars can study the encroaching taint threatening Darkshore. As the wilderness of Darkshore succumbs to creeping blight, the natural waterways have begun to turn foul. Thundris Windweaver, an investigator stationed in Auberdine, provides this empty glass tube to gather concrete evidence from the Cliffspring River. Drawn from the pool beneath the first waterfall north of town, the resulting sample allows night elf naturalists to examine the nature of the corruption washing toward Mist's Edge.

item:empty-water-tube.text: Empty Water Tube. The Empty Water Tube is a simple glass vessel provided in Auberdine to collect sacred moonwell water. It is meant to carry the blessed liquid up to the strange red crystal perched on the eastern cliffs of Darkshore. Sentinels and scholars studying the mysterious red crystal along Darkshore's eastern ridge require pure lunar essence to test its nature. Because mundane glass or flasks can easily contaminate consecrated water, this sealed vial is specifically entrusted to investigators visiting the moonwell in Auberdine. Once filled, its contents are carried up the mountain slopes to see how the alien mineral responds to Elune's magic.

item:enchanted-resonite-crystal.text: Enchanted Resonite Crystal. The Enchanted Resonite Crystal is an alchemically altered mineral infused with shamanic magic by Mor'rogal in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is crafted specifically to shatter the Resonite cask binding a slumbering, ancient Earthen named Goggeroc. Raw resonite crystals gathered from the deep caverns of the Stonetalon Mountains possess unusual harmonic and earthen properties. Recognizing the danger slumbering within a sealed subterranean cask, the shaman Mor'rogal altered the raw minerals using his elemental powers. The resulting Enchanted Resonite Crystal serves as a precise tool: when struck against the reinforced Resonite cask, it disrupts the housing and forcibly rouses the giant Earthen Goggeroc while he is still disoriented from his long sleep.

item:encrypted-memorandum.text: Encrypted Memorandum. The Encrypted Memorandum is a coded missive handed to novice rogues starting out in Coldridge Valley. Though disguised as official communication, it is actually a clandestine invitation from the local rogue trainer, Solm Hargrin, calling for solidarity among scoundrels in exile. In the bustling dwarven refuge of Anvilmar, rogues must maintain a low profile. Rather than approaching recruits in plain view, the trainer Solm Hargrin uses the Encrypted Memorandum to establish contact. Masked as an official directive from distant superiors, the coded parchment ensures that fledgling rogues know where to find mentorship without drawing unwanted attention from the local guards or suspicious townsfolk.

item:encrypted-parchment.text: Encrypted Parchment. The Encrypted Parchment is a ciphered missive delivered to aspiring orc rogues training in the Valley of Trials. Handed over by Gornek, it discreetly directs promising recruits into the shadows of the Den to meet the covert trainer Rwag. Young orcs seeking to prove their martial prowess in the Valley of Trials typically fight out in the open sun. However, those showing an aptitude for stealth, deception, and bladecraft draw a very different kind of attention. The Encrypted Parchment is handed to promising orc rogues by Gornek once they have cut their teeth against the local wildlife. Rather than an open announcement, the message is coded to ensure that only someone with an eye for subterfuge heeds the call. Deciphering the parchment directs the novice deep into the cave known as the Den, past the watchful eye of other clan trainers to find Rwag. There, the recruit learns that the summons was arranged on behalf of the Shattered Hand—an order operating within the Horde's covert network. By answering the parchment, the rogue takes their first step into a world of espionage, shadowcraft, and guarded secrets.

item:encrypted-rune.text: Encrypted Rune. An Encrypted Rune is a coded summoning message handed to promising new rogues in Coldridge Valley. Delivered covertly, it bids the bearer to decipher its contents and seek out the rogue trainer Solm Hargrin inside Anvilmar. In the sheltered snowy basin of Coldridge Valley, overt recruitment is rarely the style of the local scoundrels and scouts. Instead, novitiates showing a knack for stealth and cunning are slipped an Encrypted Rune. Marked with subtle ciphers, the inscribed stone carries a discreet invitation from Solm Hargrin, the rogue mentor quartered in Anvilmar. It serves as both a private test of literacy in thieves' cant and an introduction to the shadowy craft needed to survive Dun Morogh's harsh wilderness. Deciphering the rune directs new rogues to Solm, who looks to bolster the valley's covert ranks amidst rising local tensions. Beyond basic bladecraft and stealth techniques, Solm emphasizes vigilance and camaraderie, reminding incoming rogues that in this time of strained peace it is all the more important for their kind to stick together.

item:encrypted-scroll.text: Encrypted Scroll. The Encrypted Scroll is a discreet parchment delivered to promising newly risen rogues in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of David Trias, it directs the recipient to introduce themselves for formal training among the Forsaken's covert operatives. When a freshly awakened Forsaken shows an aptitude for stealth and subterfuge, they do not remain unnoticed for long. The Encrypted Scroll is handed over in Deathknell once a scout proves capable against the mindless Scourge roaming the nearby graveyard. Bearing the personal seal of the rogue trainer David Trias, the scroll instructs the bearer to seek him out in the local inn. It serves as an initial vetting process, pointing fledgling operatives toward the discipline required to serve the Dark Lady rather than wasting their second chance at life as mere pickpockets. The message itself is brief, directing the rogue to establish contact within Deathknell before venturing deeper into Tirisfal Glades. Trias keeps tabs on up-and-coming talent on behalf of the Shadowstalkers, the covert arm of the Forsaken. To survive in Lordaeron, the Forsaken rely heavily on silent blades and cunning scouts to counter the Scarlet Crusade, surviving Alliance enclaves, and leftover Scourge filth. Answering this ciphered summons is the first step toward joining that covert network.

item:encrypted-sigil.text: Encrypted Sigil. The Encrypted Sigil is a coded token delivered to newly awakened night elf rogues in Shadowglen. Bearing hidden instructions from the trainer Frahun Shadewhisper, it directs fledgling operatives to initiate their training amidst growing threats to Teldrassil. Within the sheltered hollow of Shadowglen, emerging night elf scouts and infiltrators are contacted through discreet means. The Encrypted Sigil is passed directly into an initiate's hands by a quiet messenger on behalf of Frahun Shadewhisper. Concealing its contents in a manner fitting the profession, the sigil instructs the recipient to report to Frahun near Aldrassil. To Shadewhisper, reading and delivering the token proves an initiate can follow subtle directives and handle covert missives. Frahun uses the summons to stress the necessity of rogues in an unsettled world. With tensions simmering between the night elves and the distant Horde, Shadewhisper reminds his recruits that open warfare is not the only peril facing their people. Rogues must serve as the early eyes and unseen blades of the Kaldorei, gathering intelligence across Teldrassil and learning to strike before threats can take root in the boughs of the World Tree.

item:encrypted-tablet.text: Encrypted Tablet. The Encrypted Tablet is a coded message delivered to novice Darkspear troll rogues training in the Valley of Trials. Inscribed by the rogue trainer Rwag, it summons promising cutpurses and scouts to his post inside the Den. Novice troll rogues arriving in the Valley of Trials are handed the Encrypted Tablet as their initial directive. Inscribed with ciphered instructions, the slate directs them directly to Rwag, an orc trainer residing within the shaded caves of the Den. Rather than openly broadcasting guild business, the local shadow operatives use these encrypted slates to test comprehension and discreetly draw new talent under official tutelage. Deciphering the tablet introduces recruits to the larger shadow network of the Horde. Upon reporting to Rwag, scouts learn that their progression is scrutinized by shadowy syndicates like the Shattered Hand, who look to valley trainers to ensure prospective cutpurses, spies, and assassins are sharp enough to serve the new nation.

item:essence-of-nightlash.text: Essence of Nightlash. The Essence of Nightlash is the lingering magical remnant collected from the defeated banshee Nightlash at the Dead Fields. It serves as irrefutable proof for High Executor Hadrec that the Scourge force bolstering the local rot hide gnolls has been broken. At an abandoned farmstead in northern Silverpine known as the Dead Fields, packs of undead rot hide gnolls have entrenched themselves under Scourge command. Initial Forsaken assaults were repeatedly broken not by the feral gnolls, but by their spectral commander: the banshee Nightlash. Calling upon wailing magics, she reinforced the gnoll lines and routed the forces sent from the Sepulcher. Slaying her dissolves her incorporeal form into dust, leaving behind a crystalline, magical essence that represents her permanent dissolution. Because banshees leave behind no corporeal corpse, the Essence of Nightlash is the only physical evidence that the malevolent spirit has been destroyed. High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher requires this essence to verify that the Scourge's local foothold has collapsed, allowing the Forsaken to finally secure their northern perimeter and suppress the rot hide threat.

item:essential-artificial.text: Essential Artificial. An Essential Artificial is a versatile, standardized mechanical component vital to gnomish tinkers and engineers. Left behind in stockpiles during the frantic evacuation of Gnomeregan, these parts are highly sought after by gnomes seeking to rebuild their technological efforts from exile in Ironforge. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the essential artificial served as a cornerstone of day-to-day gnomish engineering. Described by tinkers as a nigh-universal component, it was integrated into countless contraptions, clockwork wonders, and heavy machinery throughout the subterranean halls. Its standardized nature made it indispensable to smiths and machinists seeking reliable, interchangeable modular parts. When the trogg invasion and subsequent radiation disaster forced the gnomes into a desperate, panicked exodus, massive reserves of these components were abandoned where they sat. They remain stored inside heavy, steam-powered dispensers known as artificial extrapolators scattered across the deeper passages of Gnomeregan. In Tinker Town, master craftsman Klockmort Spannerspan actively recruits daring adventurers to venture back into the contaminated ruins and salvage these parts so research and invention can continue.

item:etched-note.text: Etched Note. The Etched Note is a formal summons delivered to promising young tauren hunters resting at Camp Narache. Penned by the camp's hunter trainer, Lanka Farshot, the message welcomes the novice into the traditions of the hunt and calls them forward for their initial instruction. Within the safe confines of Camp Narache, young shu'halo are recognized early for their natural inclinations and family lineages. The Etched Note is delivered by a runner on behalf of Lanka Farshot, the resident hunter mentor. It names the hunter as the heart of the tribe while serving as a stern reminder that raw instinct must be tempered through rigorous instruction and a deep reverence for the wilderness of Mulgore. For the tauren, hunting is far more than a practical method of survival—it is an honored, sacred discipline woven into tribal society. The note reminds the reader that hunters blend the roles of warriors, shamans and druids, and that the tribe will look to them for guidance and protection. By presenting the letter to Lanka, the student takes their first official steps into learning weaponcraft, understanding beasts, and fulfilling their duty to defend and sustain the tribes.

item:etched-parchment.text: Etched Parchment. The Etched Parchment is a written summons delivered to novice hunters training within Durotar's Valley of Trials. Handed over by Gornek, it directs aspiring wilderness stalkers to seek instruction from the troll trainer Jen'shan. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls seeking their place among the Horde begin their rites in the arid basin of the Valley of Trials. While they prove themselves against the local vermin, Gornek serves as a watchful overseer who guides recruits toward their calling. For those destined to wield bow, gun, and fang, Gornek passes along this etched parchment. It bears a direct message from Jen'shan, a skilled hunter trainer seeking fresh eyes and steady hands. Carrying the parchment to Jen'shan marks the true beginning of a hunter's training in Durotar. Jen'shan emphasizes that walking the wild path is no easy task, requiring just as much dedication to master the beasts of the desert as an arcanist devotes to magic or a shaman gives to the spirits. Reading the parchment and answering her call introduces novitiates to proper marksmanship and wilderness survival.

item:etched-rune.text: Etched Rune. The Etched Rune is a carved stone tablet given to aspiring dwarven hunters in Coldridge Valley. It serves as an invitation from the hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson, directing fledglings to seek him out within Anvilmar to begin their formal wilderness instruction. Carved with specific dwarven runes, this small stone tablet is passed along to novices who demonstrate potential out in the snowdrifts of Coldridge Valley. Sent by the mountaineer and hunter trainer Thorgas Grimson, the rune encourages fledgling trackers to pause their outdoor tasks and report to Anvilmar. Reading the stone marks a hunter's first step away from basic survival and toward understanding the deeper craft of the wild—learning to respect the beasts of Dun Morogh, track mountain predators, care for ranged weaponry, and endure the brutal elements.

item:etched-sigil.text: Etched Sigil. An inscribed token delivered to aspiring night elf hunters awakening in Shadowglen. Carried by a woodland runner, it bears a summons from the hunter trainer Ayanna Everstride atop the great bough of Aldrassil. Carved with the marks of the hunt, the Etched Sigil is handed to newly awakened night elf hunters as they step into Shadowglen. The token serves as an official notice and welcome from Ayanna Everstride, the local hunter trainer residing high within the hollowed boughs of Aldrassil. Instructing the novice to seek her out, the sigil begins a lifelong tutelage in archery, wilderness tracking, and the ancient night elven bond between stalker and beast.

item:explosive-stick-of-gann.text: Explosive Stick of Gann. The Explosive Stick of Gann is a customized blasting charge assembled by Gann Stonespire using stolen dwarven schematics. It was designed specifically to sabotage the dwarven flying machine stationed at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. When the dwarven Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build the fortress-dig of Bael Modan. Driven by vengeance and a desire to honor his displaced and fallen kin, Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm's blueprints to turn dwarven engineering against the invaders. By studying the recovered plans, Gann assembled this specialized charge with enough concussive force to wreck heavy machinery.

item:faded-shadowhide-pendant.text: Faded Shadowhide Pendant. A tarnished talisman once worn by the Shadowhide gnolls of Redridge, enchanted to serve as a conduit for dark orders. To the astonishment of whoever holds it, the pendant also carries a delayed magical message cast by the wizard Theocritus. The Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains answer to a sinister master named Morganth, coordinating their movements through enchanted pendants. While investigating these talismans from his sanctuary at Tower Azora, the High Mage Theocritus devised an experimental spell to breach their mystical frequency. Though his magical broadcast took weeks to manifest, this faded pendant proved that the gnolls' communication line can be hijacked, opening a path to disrupt their dark master's reach.

item:fallen-moonstone.text: Fallen Moonstone. A Fallen Moonstone is a luminous, magically charged stone gathered from the tranquil waters of Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale. Imbued with sacred lunar energy, these stones possess potent restorative properties capable of renewing vitality and curing severe frailty. Fallen Moonstones were once gathered in abundance along the shores and shallows of Fallen Sky Lake, southeast of Astranaar. Highly treasured by the night elves for their restorative magic and lunar blessing, they were often sought out to aid in recovery when ordinary remedies proved insufficient. However, harvesting them became treacherous when corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake. Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, hoarded every stone it could find on a small central island, cutting off the local Kaldorei from a vital source of healing.

item:fandral-s-message.text: Fandral's Message. Fandral's Message is a missive penned by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. It is entrusted to an adventurer to carry across the sea to the Ancient of Lore, Onu, in Darkshore. Written by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in the Cenarion Enclave, this sealed dispatch serves as direct correspondence between the acting leader of the night elven druids and Onu, the venerable Ancient of Lore dwelling within the Grove of the Ancients. After receiving reports regarding the state of Teldrassil's Oracle Glade, Staghelm wastes no time pressing couriers into service to send word south of Auberdine. The delivery requires travelers to journey across the waters to Darkshore, bridging the heart of the new World Tree with the older, shadowed mainland.

item:fang-of-vagash.text: Fang of Vagash. The Fang of Vagash is a massive predator tooth taken from the notorious beast Vagash in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. It serves as tangible proof for local breeders that the marauding monster threatening their prized rams has finally been slain. Dun Morogh's high crags are home to bitter cold and ferocious predators, but none have plagued the local ranches quite like Vagash. Looming in the ridges above the Amberstill Ranch, this savage beast frequently stalks downhill under cover of darkness to slaughter prized rams. With Ironforge's troops already stretched thin, the local herdsmen cannot count on the city guard for protection. Slaying the beast and carving away one of its vicious fangs offers indisputable evidence that the pasturelands are safe once more.

item:fangore-s-paw.text: Fangore's Paw. Fangore's Paw is the severed hand of Lieutenant Fangore, a commanding officer among the Shadowhide gnolls in the Redridge Mountains. It serves as gruesome proof of the gnoll chieftain's demise for Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire. The grim bounty was placed to dismantle the warlord's threat against the besieged township. Lieutenant Fangore acts as a primary field commander for the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching across the Redridge Mountains. Operating in direct service to the renegade mage Morganth, Fangore directs violent assaults against trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. Because gnoll raiders do not leave traditional uniforms, official seals, or banners to confirm their casualties, the township authorities rely on grim physical evidence. Magistrate Solomon specifically demanded Fangore's paw as unmistakable proof of his execution, allowing the town of Lakeshire to breathe slightly easier amid mounting surrounding perils.

item:farren-s-report.text: Farren's Report. Farren's Report is an official dispatch drafted by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore detailing his investigations into the local naga. Farren uses this document to appeal to his former mentor, Major Samuelson in Stormwind Keep, hoping to secure a reassignment back to the capital. Stationed on the embattled coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew weary of local leadership and the remote frontier. After tasking adventurers with hunting the Daggerspine naga to gather proof of their threat, Orinelle compiled his findings into a formal report. Rather than submitting it to his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Farren aimed to send it directly to Major Samuelson, the captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep. Having trained under Samuelson, Farren hoped the document would demonstrate his competence and justify an immediate transfer back to the comforts of Stormwind City.

item:fathom-core.text: Fathom Core. The Fathom Core is a specialized relic recovered from a submerged fathom stone in the depths of Blackfathom Deeps. When deciphered, it provides a comprehensive record of elemental activity in the surrounding region. The Earthen Ring seeks this artifact to discern what dark rituals the Twilight's Hammer cult is conducting beneath Ashenvale. Resting within an ancient fathom stone submerged among the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core serves as a historical record for elemental phenomena. It registers and preserves shifts, disruptions, and surges in the elements over time. For the shaman of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost, acquiring the core is essential for understanding how the Twilight's Hammer cultists are manipulating the regional elements to serve their own ends.

item:feather-charm.text: Feather Charm. Feather Charms are crude magical trinkets carried by Frostmane troll novices in the snow-swept valleys of Coldridge Valley. Though fashioned from simple materials, they harbor an innate sorcerous resonance that catches the eye of local warlock mentors. The Frostmane trolls inhabiting the snowy caverns southwest of Anvilmar are known mostly for territorial savagery, but their novices dabble in primitive spellcraft. The feather charms carried by these young trolls hold a faint yet unmistakable magical power. In Anvilmar, warlock instructor Alamar Grimm considers them an intriguing subject of study—surprising for crude trollcraft—and uses them as a proving ground for fledgling warlocks seeking to master the binding of their first imp.

item:fel-cone.text: Fel Cone. Fel Cones are corrupted seed pods that drop from the boughs of Teldrassil, easily spotted by the noxious green fumes drifting from their hulls. Though foul and tainted by dark energies, local night elf defenders find clever uses for them against nearby tricksters. Teldrassil is young, but corruption has already seeped into its living wood. Fel Cones are the visible evidence of this insidious rot—gnarled, fallen pine cones that billow with foul green smoke. Scattered beneath the boughs just east of Dolanaar, these pods are steeped in tainted magic that warps natural flora and makes them dangerous to touch or consume without caution.

item:fel-moss.text: Fel Moss. Fel Moss is a tainted vegetative substance spreading through the forests of Teldrassil. Carrying demonic and corruptive energies, it is carried by hostile grell and grellkin and poses an insidious threat to the wildlife and native furbolg tribes of the World Tree. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' immortality and heal the natural world, but corruption has already crept into its pristine boughs. Fel Moss is one of the most visible signs of this degradation. Found clinging to and carried by the impish grells and grellkin infesting Shadowglen, this malevolent growth radiates an unnatural, wicked magic. Forest protectors like the dryad Tarindrella have begun gathering samples to measure just how deeply this rot has infiltrated the sacred woodland canopy.

item:felix-s-box.text: Felix's Box. Felix's Box is a small container of personal belongings belonging to Felix Whindlebolt, a refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. Lost during the frantic evacuation into Dun Morogh, the box was looted by local Frostmane trolls and carried off to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace, Felix Whindlebolt joined the frantic exodus of gnomes into Coldridge Valley. In his desperation to escape the radioactive fumes, Felix dropped his most prized personal possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road. Before he could recover them, indigenous Frostmane trolls plundered the roadside remnants and dragged his box, along with his chest and bucket of bolts, back to their crude settlements southwest of Anvilmar. Unaccustomed to physical violence and ill-suited for the harsh wilderness of Dun Morogh, Felix was forced to seek the help of passing adventurers in Anvilmar to recover his belongings. Retrieving Felix's Box represents more than just returning a modest container; it restores a piece of normalcy and livelihood to a displaced artisan who lost everything in the catastrophe that consumed his underground homeland.

item:felix-s-bucket-of-bolts.text: Felix's Bucket of Bolts. Felix's Bucket of Bolts is a container of spare hardware and tools owned by Felix Whindlebolt, a gnome refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. During his escape into Dun Morogh, the bucket was snatched by local Frostmane trolls and dragged into their nearby camps. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan following the disaster against the troggs, thousands of gnomes fled into the freezing wilds of Dun Morogh with whatever they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape with his vital equipment, but in the chaos of his flight toward Anvilmar, he was ambushed by the Frostmane trolls who inhabit the crags southwest of town. The trolls plundered his belongings, including this bucket full of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan stranded without the essential materials needed to ply his craft in exile.

item:felix-s-chest.text: Felix's Chest. Felix's Chest is a container of personal belongings lost by the exiled gnome Felix Whindlebolt during the flight from Gnomeregan. Carried away by Frostmane trolls lurking near Coldridge Valley, it sits abandoned within one of their primitive mountain camps. When the subterranean techno-city of Gnomeregan fell to trogg incursions and toxic radioactive fallout, thousands of gnomes fled toward the snowy surface of Dun Morogh with whatever possessions they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape the irradiated ruins, but amidst the panic of the evacuation, native Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook the scattered survivors. Felix lost his primary toolkits and belongings, with his sturdy chest hauled off to the crude camps the trolls maintain in the crags southwest of Anvilmar.

item:felstalker-hoof.text: Felstalker Hoof. A Felstalker Hoof is a physical token taken from demonic beasts infesting the Burning Blade Coven in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Young shaman must retrieve these hooves as a trial of readiness before learning to commune with the elemental spirits of the earth. Within the sun-baked Valley of Trials, the trainer Canaga Earthcaller tasks budding shaman with facing the demonic taint threatening Durotar. The Burning Blade Coven to the north harbors vile familiars and demonic felstalkers. Taking the hooves of these fiends is not merely an act of culling pests, but a rigorous test of endurance, resolve, and spirit. Only by subduing these chaotic beasts can an aspiring shaman prove worthy of receiving the secrets of the earth and preparing the ceremonial sapta needed to commune directly with elemental spirits.

item:fenwick-s-head.text: Fenwick's Head. Fenwick's Head is the grisly proof of execution taken from Fenwick Thatros on the shores of Lordamere Lake. It is claimed by Forsaken rogues operating on direct orders passed down through Lord Varimathras. Within the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity, Mennet Carkad acts on urgent intelligence routed directly from dreadlord Varimathras. A hostile undead leader named Fenwick Thatros has established a foothold near the decaying docks along Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. To prevent this threat from rallying hostile undead against the Forsaken, Carkad dispatches promising Deathstalkers to locate Thatros, eliminate him, and sever his head as undeniable proof of the kill. Returning Fenwick's Head to Carkad is more than a simple bounty collection; it serves as a crucial trial for Deathstalker operatives. Presenting the severed trophy validates the rogue's competence in infiltration and assassination, opening the door to deeper, more specialized instruction in the shadow arts from the Forsaken masters.

item:fey-dragon-scale.text: Fey Dragon Scale. A Fey Dragon Scale is a shimmering woodland relic harvested from the elusive faerie dragons living around Stonetalon Peak. It is sought after by the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses it as an exotic reagent in an alchemical brew mocking night elven nature magic. Faerie dragons are mysterious, elusive creatures tied closely to the wild groves of Kalimdor, particularly the untouched forests around Stonetalon Peak. Their scales carry a natural magical luster reminiscent of the deep woods they guard. While revered by the night elves as harmless woodland spirits and allies, outsiders view them as an untamed source of rare magical ingredients.

item:filled-amethyst-phial.text: Filled Amethyst Phial. The Filled Amethyst Phial contains sacred water taken from the ancient moonwell beneath the boughs of the Oracle Tree. Gathered on behalf of Corithras Moonrage, this purified water is used by the Cenarion druids to study the troubled, imperfect growth of Teldrassil. Far to the northwest in Teldrassil lies the Oracle Glade, where the oldest and most potent of the island's moonwells rests beneath the great Oracle Tree. While the lesser moonwells across the boughs serve the day-to-day needs of the night elves, this well's waters are saturated with the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids tasked with monitoring the health of the World Tree use specialized amethyst phials to collect and preserve this powerful liquid for testing and ritual cleansing.

item:filled-blue-waterskin.text: Filled Blue Waterskin. The Filled Blue Waterskin holds pristine water gathered from a fountain at the ancient Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. Shaman seeking communion with the water spirits collect this sample as a vital reagent for their trial of passage. Initiates undertaking the Call of Water are directed northward across the border from the Barrens into the dense forests of Ashenvale. Nestled against the mountains dividing Ashenvale from Stonetalon, beyond Lake Mystral, lie the Ruins of Stardust—a secluded elven sanctuary guarded by fierce forest beasts. At the center of this sacred lake stands an untouched fountain. Drawing from its basin into a blue waterskin yields water untainted by corruption or drought, prized by shaman masters for ritual attunement. The water collected within this vessel serves as the final sample required by Brine, a hermit water expert dwelling on a hill in the southern Barrens. Combined with waters gathered from other contrasting wells and springs, this pure essence is distilled into an offering potent enough to manifest and soothe the elemental spirits of water, completing the initiate's trial.

item:filled-brown-waterskin.text: Filled Brown Waterskin. The Filled Brown Waterskin contains fresh water drawn from a rare pond near Brine's hut in the Barrens. Collected by aspiring shaman, it forms the first fundamental step in brewing the sapta needed to commune with the spirits of water. In the parched expanse of the Barrens, surface water is both a blessing and a battleground. The pond nestled beneath Brine's hut offers precious hydration that draws the desperate and defensive quilboar who dwell nearby. For an initiate walking the path of the shaman, filling this simple leather waterskin is not merely an errand of gathering supplies; it is an elemental lesson. By approaching the pool and witnessing the fierce territorial struggle surrounding it, the novice observes firsthand how the very substance that sustains life in the desert can drive mortal creatures to violence.

item:filled-cliffspring-falls-sampler.text: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. The Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler contains murky water drawn from the headwaters near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore. Gathered on behalf of the Cenarion Circle, it serves as crucial evidence in uncovering what is poisoning the local deer population. Cliffspring Falls provides the principal drinking water for much of Darkshore, cascading down from the eastern highlands toward the sea. Recently, however, the wildlife relying on these waters—specifically the local deer—have fallen prey to a debilitating, unnatural malady. At the behest of Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, druidic initiates retrieve this sample directly from the mouth of a cave infested by hostile naga. The vial holds visibly putrid liquid, confirming that the region's primary fresh water supply is actively corrupted.

item:filled-containment-coffer.text: Filled Containment Coffer. A Filled Containment Coffer is an enchanted receptacle used by Forsaken spellcasters to trap erratic magical entities. By deploying a Cantation of Manifestation to reveal and weaken rift spawn in the Apothecarium, mages can trap the anomalies inside these reinforced boxes for safe examination. When unexplained magical disturbances manifested within Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium, the Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell commissioned practitioners of the arcane to capture the entities responsible. Because the rift creatures exist purely as living magical energy and wander unseen, ordinary cages are useless. Instead, spellcasters reveal the entities with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, and snap these specially prepared containment coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes shield the carrier from volatile magical backlashes while keeping the specimens intact for magical dissection. The presence of living mana creatures in the Undercity poses a serious threat. Once sealed into containment coffers, the captive beasts are transported back to Anastasia Hartwell and the city's scholars. The primary concern among the Forsaken mages is determining whether these intrusions are natural rifts in Azeroth's magical fabric or the preliminary probes of a calculated magical assault aimed at the kingdom.

item:filled-crystal-phial.text: Filled Crystal Phial. A Filled Crystal Phial contains sacred waters drawn from the moonwell just north of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Gathered at the instruction of Tenaron Stormgrip, this water serves as a novice's introduction to the sacred and volatile power coursing through Teldrassil. To prepare young night elves before they venture into the wider world, Tenaron Stormgrip sends them to gather water from the moonwell nestled in Shadowglen. The phial holds more than simple spring water; moonwells are infused with residual energies traced back to the ancient Well of Eternity. While the Sentinels honor these sites as blessed shrines of Elune and druids channel their restorative qualities into tending nature, the arcane sorcery of old remains strictly forbidden. Drawing this water is the first step in understanding the sacrifices of Mount Hyjal and the delicate balance required to nurture Teldrassil.

item:filled-cursed-ooze-jar.text: Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. A Filled Cursed Ooze Jar contains the noxious remains of a cursed ooze collected from the corrupted forests of Felwood. It is gathered on behalf of Laris Geardawdle, a gnome scholar in Ironforge seeking to uncover the primordial origins of slimes across Azeroth. While most adventurers avoid the vile puddles and caustic slimes crawling across Kalimdor, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle sees them as a biological mystery. Noticing that slimes appear in diverse environments and observing Forsaken apothecaries diligently harvesting them, Geardawdle developed a controversial theory: oozes might be primordial secretions tied directly to Azeroth's creation. Gathering a sample requires braving Felwood's blighted woods, defeating a cursed ooze, and scooping the acidic matter into an empty jar before it completely dissolves. Securing these pungent samples serves a dual purpose for Geardawdle. Beyond the pursuit of natural science, he hopes a major discovery will cement his reputation within the dwarven-led Explorers' League. In the wake of Gnomeregan's devastating fall, many gnome refugees in Ironforge feel an intense pressure to prove their worth to their dwarven hosts, and Geardawdle believes that unlocking the ancient secrets of ooze will show everyone that welcoming gnomes was no mistake.

item:filled-dreadmist-peak-sampler.text: Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. The Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler is a vial containing corrupted water drawn from the elevated pools atop Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens. Gathered by fledgling druids of the Horde, it provides the physical evidence needed by the Cenarion Circle to study a vile affliction poisoning the region's wildlife. The high crags of Dreadmist Peak house natural pools whose mists historically shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. When the demon-worshipping Burning Blade established their coven atop the summit, the water quickly soured. Suspecting that demonic rituals poisoned the vapors feeding the surrounding savanna, Cenarion druids dispatch initiates to capture a specimen using a specialized sampler. The foul liquid inside confirms their worst fears, reeking of corruption potent enough to sicken the herds wandering below.

item:filled-etched-phial.text: Filled Etched Phial. A Filled Etched Phial is an ornate dryad vessel laden with consecrated water drawn directly from a night elf moonwell in Ashenvale. Requested by the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this sanctified water possesses the rare spiritual potency required to quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. Obtaining this phial demands infiltrating night elf territory deep within Ashenvale. The empty vessel must first be claimed from the dryads around Raynewood Retreat, whose delicate containers are crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. Filled subsequently at a sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River, the phial captures water brimming with celestial, nature-bound power. To the night elves, taking this water uninvited is an act of blatant desecration, but the tauren see it as a vital necessity for addressing a regional threat further south.

item:filled-jade-phial.text: Filled Jade Phial. The Filled Jade Phial holds sacred waters drawn from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Carried back to Dolanaar, it serves as part of an ongoing ritual to replenish the capital's central waters while young night elves learn the history of their people. The druids of Darnassus rely on sacred moonwell waters drawn from across the boughs of Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. Specially crafted vessels, such as the jade phial entrusted to young adventurers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, are attuned to contain these pure waters safely. By venturing eastward to the moonwell outside Starbreeze Village, initiates collect the vital water while proving their devotion to the maintenance of the World Tree. Returning the Filled Jade Phial to Dolanaar is more than a simple errand; each replenished vessel earns another chapter in the oral history of the kaldorei. Upon receiving the full phial, Corithras Moonrage speaks of the desperate era following the Third War—the burning of Nordrassil, the loss of night elf immortality, the release of the Betrayer, and the sudden disappearance of Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage.

item:filled-pure-sample-jar.text: Filled Pure Sample Jar. A Filled Pure Sample Jar contains an uncorrupted specimen of primordial ooze gathered from the remote wilds. It serves as crucial baseline data for the gnome scholar Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge, who is studying how environmental corruption alters living matter. In his study of oozes across Azeroth, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle discovered a troubling phenomenon: these amorphous creatures absorb and reflect the magical and environmental corruption of their habitats. After cataloging the tainted slimes of Felwood, Laris determined that deciphering the nature of the rot required a control group. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds ooze harvested from pristine, untainted wilderness—such as the primordial ecology of Un'Goro Crater—offering scholars an unaltered specimen to compare against diseased and corrupted strains. Because oozes are extraordinarily malleable organisms, true 'pure' samples cannot be collected near modern civilization, demonic blights, or necromantic fallout. The glutinous oozes inhabiting the untamed basin of Un'Goro Crater remain relatively isolated from outside corruption, making them an ideal scientific standard for Ironforge's inquiring minds.

item:filled-red-waterskin.text: Filled Red Waterskin. The Filled Red Waterskin contains pristine spring water drawn from the village well in Tarren Mill. Gathering this pure water amidst the blighted ruins held by the Forsaken serves as a vital trial for young shaman seeking communion with the water spirits. While training shaman in the ways of water, the hermit Brine in the Barrens dispatches initiates on a lengthy journey to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Amidst the decay and the dead, the town's central well miraculously draws clear, untainted spring water. Brine regards this holy vestige in an unhallowed land as an emblem of enduring spirit—drawing a parallel between the uncorrupted spring and Warchief Thrall's enduring resolve despite profound hardship. Gathering this sample proves an initiate's reverence for water's purity regardless of hostile surroundings.

item:filled-tainted-ooze-jar.text: Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. A Filled Tainted Ooze Jar contains viscous, tainted ooze scooped directly from the remains of oozes wandering the corrupted forests of Felwood. Secured in specialized containment jars, these samples are brought to Ironforge to support radical theories regarding the origin of life on Azeroth. The tainted oozes roaming northern Kalimdor carry the deep, lingering corruption of Felwood. Harvesting them requires careful containment using jars provided by gnomish researchers. While most travelers avoid the noxious creatures entirely, collecting these samples provides rare material for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted forests. The samples are gathered on behalf of Laris Geardawdle, an ambitious gnome scholar stationed with the Explorers' League in Ironforge. Geardawdle is fascinated by the ubiquitous nature of slimes and noticed that the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society has also been taking an active interest in them. Defying popular academic skepticism, he theorizes that slimes and oozes may be primal secretions tied to the very creation of Azeroth itself. Securing these samples is his attempt to prove his standing among dwarven scholars following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan.

item:filled-tourmaline-phial.text: Filled Tourmaline Phial. The Filled Tourmaline Phial holds enchanted waters drawn from the moonwell bordering the Pools of Arlithrien in southern Teldrassil. Collected at the request of Corithras Moonrage, the water serves as part of an effort to monitor the health and balance of the growing World Tree. The Tourmaline Phial is prepared specifically to draw water from the moonwell located southeast of the road to Darnassus, on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. Gathering water from this shrine has become fraught with peril due to the sudden aggression of the Gnarlpine furbolgs, peaceful neighbors who have rapidly deteriorated into violent madness. Corithras Moonrage tasks travelers with braving the hostile groves to secure this water, aiming to diagnose the deepening corruption unsettling the land.

item:filled-vessel.text: Filled Vessel. The Filled Vessel contains purified waters drawn from the various sacred moonwells across Teldrassil. Entrusted to couriers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, it is delivered to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus to aid his study of the World Tree's ailments. Teldrassil was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its immense boughs vulnerable to unexpected corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. In an attempt to monitor and cleanse the burgeoning boughs, night elf acolytes are dispatched to gather water samples from moonwells situated across the boughs. Corithras Moonrage consolidates these gathered phials into a single Filled Vessel, sending it onward to the capital. The mixture serves as a vital sample of Teldrassil's vitality for Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, who works tirelessly in the Cenarion Enclave to uncover a remedy for the Great Tree's pervasive flaws.

item:final-clue-to-sanders-treasure.text: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. The Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure is a whiskey-stained note found stuffed inside an old jug on the Westfall coast. It provides the concluding directions left behind by the deceased pirate Captain Sanders, guiding scavengers straight into the open sea to recover his buried booty. Reeling from a heavy stench of spirits, this smudged parchment marks the end of Captain Sanders' convoluted paper trail across Westfall. The late buccaneer, known for leaving cryptic directions across the shoreline, hid his final note deep inside an old whiskey jug along the coast. The instructions are crude yet straightforward: head due west into the ocean waves from the location of the bottle, braving the cold surf until reaching a lonely offshore rock where his ironbound sea chest lies waiting.

item:fine-crab-chunks.text: Fine Crab Chunks. Fine Crab Chunks are prime cuts of meat gathered from the coastal crustaceans roaming the beaches of Darkshore. Highly prized for their culinary versatility, they are sought after by local shore-dwellers and hungry fishermen looking to prepare an endless variety of seafood dishes. The misty, jagged shores of Darkshore are thick with skittering crustaceans, specifically Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers. While many travelers view these armored shore-prowlers as pests or aggressive hazards along the waterline, enterprising gourmands consider their meat among the finest bounty of the coast. Prized cuts harvested from these creatures yield rich, tender morsels that lend themselves to practically any cooking method imaginable, from boiling and broiling to deep frying and savory stews.

item:fine-moonstalker-pelt.text: Fine Moonstalker Pelt. A Fine Moonstalker Pelt is the thick, pristine hide taken from the most mature predatory moonstalkers roaming southern Darkshore. Terenthis of Auberdine uses these prized furs to weave an enchanted cloak that allows searchers to slip past the woods' hostile beasts unnoticed. While common moonstalkers prowl throughout the mist-laden forests of Darkshore, only the older moonstalker sires and matriarchs possess coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. These powerful wildcats establish territories along the Wildbend River and further south toward the borders of Ashenvale, where they hunt with lethal patience.

item:fire-tar.text: Fire Tar. Fire Tar is a volatile substance gathered by Razormane quilboar spellcasters across the eastern Barrens. To Horde shamans, it serves as a crucial ritual component used to brew the Fire Sapta, which grants spiritual communion with the element of fire. Carried almost exclusively by spellcasting Razormane quilboar—including their geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers—fire tar is an alchemical substance tuned closely to flame. While the bristled tribes of the Barrens use it for their own harsh magic and rituals, shamanic instructors recognize it as an essential worldly reagent capable of bridging the gap between mortal senses and raw elemental fury. When young orc and troll shamans are sent to Telf Joolam perched high in Durotar's crags, they are charged with forging their fire totem. Telf requires two key elements tied to heat and flame to brew a fire sapta: a reagent pouch stolen from Burning Blade cultists, and fire tar harvested from the Razormane. Drinking the resulting brew allows the shaman to pierce the veil and perceive the elemental spirits of flame awaiting them atop the nearby peaks.

item:fizzle-s-claw.text: Fizzle's Claw. Fizzle's Claw is the severed hand of the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm. Taken from his encampment in Thunder Ridge, it serves as physical proof to the Horde commanders in Razor Hill that a dangerous Burning Blade conspirator has been slain. Orgnil Soulscar, tasked with uprooting shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland, identified Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. Demand for Fizzle's claw was not merely out of savagery, but practical necessity: the Horde requires indisputable evidence when a covert warlock operating under the banner of the Burning Blade is eliminated. Thunder Ridge lies just northwest of Razor Hill, making Fizzle's cultist presence an imminent peril to the surrounding territories. By severing the goblin's claw and returning it to Razor Hill, Horde scouts confirmed that the warlock's rituals and his attempts to establish a Burning Blade foothold had been thwarted.

item:flagongut-s-fossil.text: Flagongut's Fossil. Flagongut's Fossil is an ancient specimen recovered from the dig sites of the Wetlands. Entrusted to the dwarven Explorers' League, it holds latent secrets that Archaeologist Flagongut seeks to decipher using a mysterious relic known as the Stone of Relu. Unearthed as part of the dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan, this ancient fossil represents more than just petrified stone. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it holds forgotten powers tied to the deep antiquity of the world, comparable to artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore. For safekeeping during regional studies, the fossil was held by Prospector Whelgar at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands.

item:flatland-cougar-femur.text: Flatland Cougar Femur. A Flatland Cougar Femur is a dense thigh bone taken from the predatory cougars that prowl the golden grasses of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional tauren folk remedy used to counter lethal, venomous infections. The flatland cougar is one of Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers, blending seamlessly with the dry brush until it springs upon unsuspecting prey. While hunters often harvest cougar pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, their heavy marrow-rich bones possess practical value in regional medicine. When Maur Raincaller, a tauren of Bloodhoof Village, suffered a venomous wound from the monstrous pink strider Mazzranache, he urgently requested a cougar femur alongside parts from other local beasts. The bone is crushed or boiled to extract its potent properties, forming an antitoxin poultice capable of drawing fever and necrotic venom out of a festering bite.

item:flatland-prowler-claw.text: Flatland Prowler Claw. A Flatland Prowler Claw is taken from the dangerous feline predators that stalk the grassy plains of Mulgore. For aspiring hunters, gathering these claws serves as a traditional rite of passage, demonstrating cunning and martial resolve to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers are among the most cunning and territorial predators roaming the wind-swept plains of Mulgore. Quick on their feet and adept at ambushing prey in the tall grass, they present a genuine threat to travelers and a worthy test for young hunters. Collecting their sharp claws is not merely a task of survival, but a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud advises promising wanderers to harvest these trophies to present to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise, proving they possess the resolve and fieldcraft necessary to pursue the hunter's way.

item:foreman-s-blackjack.text: Foreman's Blackjack. The Foreman's Blackjack is a heavy leather-wrapped cosh loaned out to fresh Horde recruits in the Valley of Trials. Taskmasters hand it down as an everyday disciplinary tool to wake slumbering peons and enforce the grueling pace of Durotar's early construction. Building a new home in the rugged desert of Durotar requires massive stockpiles of lumber, and the labor falls squarely on the shoulders of the Horde's peons. In the Valley of Trials, Foreman Thazz'ril relies on the Foreman's Blackjack to keep work crews moving. Rather than dealing lethal blows, this weighted bludgeon is designed to deliver a jarring wake-up call to laborers caught napping beneath the valley's shade trees. It serves as a stark reminder of peon life in the new Horde: grueling, unglamorous, and supervised with an iron fist.

item:forged-steel-bars.text: Forged Steel Bars. Forged Steel Bars are refined metal ingots belonging to the orc blacksmith Thun'grim Firegaze. Stolen by opportunistic Razormane quilboar during a night raid, they serve as proof of a warrior's resolve to recover stolen property in the Barrens. Forged Steel Bars represent high-quality smithing stock belonging to the visually impaired orc smith Thun'grim Firegaze, who maintains a camp in the northern Barrens. Taking advantage of Thun'grim's failing eyesight, local Razormane quilboar distracted the smith with grunts and snorts while thieves slipped away with an iron chest containing the ingots. Unskilled in metalcrafting fine steel, the quilboar abandoned the unopened container near a ruined wagon in their encampment to the northwest, leaving the bars intact for recovering warriors to reclaim.

item:fragments-of-rok-alim.text: Fragments of Rok'Alim. Fragments of Rok'Alim are the shattered stone remains of a primeval earth elemental roaming the canyons of Thousand Needles. Brought to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, they serve as undeniable physical proof that a warrior has bested an ancient terror in single combat. While most elementals faded from Azeroth following the banishment of the Old Gods, a handful possessed enough raw power to endure on the surface without being summoned by mortal magic. Rok'Alim the Pounder is one such survivor, wandering the canyon flats south of the main thoroughfare. Local centaur know him by the thunderous crashes of his stony fists pulverizing anything foolish enough to wander into his path. Striking down this living remnant of the primordial world yields jagged pieces of dense, animated rock—a trophy fit to prove unmatched physical prowess. For the tauren hermit Dorn Plainstalker, recovering the fragments is the decisive component of the Test of Strength. As part of a series of spiritual and martial rites conducted high within the Weathered Nook, the trial demands that an initiate face an entity of unyielding brute force. Delivering the battered rubble of Rok'Alim proves that an adventurer possesses the bravery and physical might required to survive the harshest perils of Kalimdor.

item:frostwolf-banner.text: Frostwolf Banner. The Frostwolf Banner is a tribal standard cached deep within Wildpaw Cavern in Alterac Valley. Horde initiates are sent to recover it as an ancestral rite of passage to awaken their battle spirit and earn their first clan insignia. For warriors of the Horde arriving in Alterac Valley, claiming true standing among the Frostwolf clan begins with a trial of grit. Warmaster Laggrond sends new recruits south into the damp, hostile corridors of Wildpaw Cavern, a den swarming with territorial gnolls. Reaching the banner hidden within their depths and returning it unbroken demonstrates courage, proving the warrior's battle rage has awakened and earning them the Frostwolf initiate's insignia.

item:full-leaden-collection-phial.text: Full Leaden Collection Phial. A heavy, lead-lined flask filled with irradiated radioactive fallout gathered from the troggs infesting Gnomeregan. The inventor Ozzie Togglevolt requested this hazardous sample in hopes of synthesizing a cure for irradiated leper gnomes—or perhaps concocting a dangerously potent rum. The lead lining of this collection phial is essential to shield the carrier from the volatile green fallout saturating Gnomeregan. The fallout originated when High Tinker Mekkatorque's advisors flooded the lower corridors with toxic radiation to halt the invading troggs, a catastrophe that instead corrupted both troggs and surviving gnomes into maddened, irradiated horrors. By collecting fluid residue directly from Irradiated Invaders and Pillagers, daring adventurers furnish refugee tinkerers like Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos with raw materials needed to experiment on remedies.

item:fungal-spores.text: Fungal Spores. Fungal Spores are harvested from laden mushrooms growing around the strange oases of the Barrens. Imbued with the mysterious vital energies of these waters, they are prized by Royal Apothecary Society researchers seeking potent reagents for their chemical concoctions. Across the arid plains of the Barrens, emerald oases such as the Forgotten Pools, the Lushwater Oasis, and the Stagnant Oasis pulse with an unusual vitality. The water does more than merely quench thirst; it actively accelerates, alters, and invigorates surrounding flora and wildlife. Mushrooms growing along the damp shores become swollen and heavy with spores that carry this concentrated, volatile growth potential. To naturalists, it is an ecological curiosity; to the Royal Apothecary Society, it is a prime botanical specimen awaiting weaponization or refinement. Apothecaries stationed abroad, such as Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads, constantly harvest exotic local reagents to send back to their laboratories or share with distant colleagues like Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff. The spores' altered physiology makes them particularly valuable for concocting potent chemical solutions. The Forsaken value these specimens precisely because their natural properties have already been shifted by the mysterious forces surging beneath the Kalimdor soil.

item:furen-s-instructions.text: Furen's Instructions. Furen's Instructions is a handwritten parchment given by the master armorer Furen Longbeard in Stormwind. It details the rare and perilous reagents required to forge fire-hardened mail armor for promising Alliance warriors. Furen Longbeard does not hand out exceptional armor lightly. Having already tested a warrior's resolve with simpler smithing tasks, the dwarven craftsman offers to hammer out an extraordinarily resilient suit of mail, provided the adventurer fetches the rare components himself. To ensure nothing is forgotten, Furen provides this detailed checklist, sending his charge across continents on an arduous scavenger hunt. The instructions outline a dangerous journey spanning both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Crafting the hardened links requires dozens of scorched spider fangs from the damp caves of the Wetlands, horns harvested from fire-breathing chimaeras in the crags of Stonetalon Mountains, and a prized galvanized horn from the chimaera matriarch herself. The final, alchemical catalyst is a vial of volatile phlogiston, held deep within the quilboar bastion of Razorfen Kraul.

item:furen-s-notes.text: Furen's Notes. Furen's Notes are written folios containing the metallurgical and armorsmithing insights discovered by Furen Longbeard in Stormwind. Penned after forging resilient protective gear for veteran warriors, they are dispatched across the Alliance to refine the techniques of fellow craftsmen. When Furen Longbeard completes the rigorous forging of specialized warrior armaments in Stormwind's Dwarven District, he compiles the methods and breakthroughs he discovered along the way into written notes. Dwarven metallurgy is ever-evolving, and Furen makes multiple copies of these treatises so his peers can replicate and expand upon his findings. The documents capture practical advancements in tempering, reinforcing, and shaping armor against lethal combat blows. Furen distributes his notes to trusted contacts within the Alliance's crafting networks. While local masters like Grimand Elmore might scoff at being schooled by a peer they claim to have tutored, the value of the insights cannot be ignored. Copies are even carried overseas across the Great Sea to night elven craftsmen such as Mathiel on the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, bridging the gaps between distinct ancestral traditions through shared martial necessity.

item:furlbrow-s-deed.text: Furlbrow's Deed. Furlbrow's Deed is the legal property title belonging to Farmer Theodore Furlbrow and his wife Verna for their land in Westfall. Snatched by Defias bandits to serve as a template for forging land claims, it represents the precarious state of honest folk driven from their homes across the kingdom. Signed by Theodore Furlbrow and co-signed by his wife Verna, this paper establishes ownership over their family farm in Westfall. When the Defias Brotherhood overran the region, brigands muscled the couple out and took the document with them into Elwynn Forest. Scrawled notes on the back reveal that the thieves intended to use the official parchment as a template to forge legal deeds for other properties. Stripped of their home and livelihood, the Furlbrows were forced onto the road, left stranded near the border when their wagon broke down.

item:furlbrow-s-pocket-watch.text: Furlbrow's Pocket Watch. Furlbrow's Pocket Watch is a cherished family heirloom belonging to Farmer Furlbrow of Westfall. Given to him by his wife Verna's father on their wedding day, the timepiece was abandoned in haste when Defias bandits seized their pumpkin farm. When Defias hooligans swarmed the Furlbrow Pumpkin Patch, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were forced to abandon their homestead in the middle of the night. In the frantic rush to escape, the farmer left behind a prized pocket watch, given to him as a wedding gift by his father-in-law. The heirloom remained tucked away inside a wardrobe in the overrun farmhouse, guarded by cutthroats led by Benny Blaanco. For the displaced couple camping along the road, recovering the watch represents preserving one of the few pieces of their former life that the outlaws have not ruined.

item:gaea-seed.text: Gaea Seed. Gaea Seeds are hardy plant kernels found along the water's edge of Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Treasured by tauren shamans, they are imbued with elemental blessings to help replenish areas ravaged by war and industry. Gaea Seeds are native to Stonetalon Mountains, naturally washing up or growing around the shores of Mirkfallon Lake. While modest in appearance—resembling small, fibrous coconuts—they carry an inherent resilience. As industrial exploitation and conflict scar Stonetalon, shamanic practitioners view these seeds as vital conduits for healing the wounded earth.

item:gaffer-jack.text: Gaffer Jack. A Gaffer Jack is a specialized engineering component used for intricate mechanical adjustments, such as tuning stintle pegs. A crate of them was carelessly lost beneath the waves off the coast of Auberdine by the eccentric gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle during his voyage across the sea. Seeking peace and quiet away from the clattering forge-works and noisy taverns of Ironforge, gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle booked passage aboard a ship bound for Auberdine. Having indulged in a bit too much drink during the ocean voyage, Wizbang managed to fumble and drop an entire container of gaffer jacks over the railing. These small mechanical fasteners sank into the misty coastal waters of Darkshore, leaving him stranded without the vital parts required to tune his stintle pegs. Because gaffer jacks were spilled into the surf along the shoreline, they occasionally snag on the hooks of patient fishermen casting into the coastal waters of Darkshore. Recovering these lost components allows Wizbang to assemble his bizarre contraptions, though dredging tiny metal hardware out of the open sea remains a testament to both extraordinary patience and pure luck.

item:gallywix-s-head.text: Gallywix's Head. Gallywix's Head is a severed trophy taken from Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, an overseer of the Venture Company operating at the Sludge Fen in the Barrens. It serves as gruesome proof of execution demanded by the Shattered Hand, the covert rogue syndicate based in Orgrimmar. Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix directed operations out of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen. After word came that the Venture Co. were planning something on a grand scale, the Shattered Hand dispatched operatives to dismantle the facility entirely. Claiming Puzik Gallywix's head serves as absolute proof to Shenthul in Orgrimmar that the overseer was executed, securing the rogue's standing within the guild.

item:galvanized-horn.text: Galvanized Horn. A Galvanized Horn is a hardened biological growth harvested from the formidable chimaera matriarchs haunting the scorched crags of Kalimdor. Highly sought after by master armorers across both factions, this resilient specimen serves as a core material for specialized warrior armor. Chimaeras are savage, twin-headed beasts known for their ferocity, but the elder matriarchs that prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains bear horns forged unusually hard by ash, flame, and survival. While standard fledglings yield brittle, blackened horns, the matriarch's horn possesses a naturally tempered strength akin to treated metal. Both the dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff covet the horn, requiring it as a test of martial valor and as a critical ingredient in crafting exceptional mail armor.

item:gargantuan-tumor.text: Gargantuan Tumor. The Gargantuan Tumor is a massive, diseased growth torn from the corrupted timberling Oakenscowl in Teldrassil. It serves as glaring proof of the unnatural sickness spreading through the creatures inhabiting Lake Al'Ameth. Near the southern bank of Lake Al'Ameth, a cavern shelters Oakenscowl, once a noble timberling elder who has fallen prey to vile affliction. The creature was visibly poisoned by an enormous growth that warped its behavior and seeped taint into surrounding wildlife. Severing this grotesque tumor is crucial not only to end the beast's tormented rampage, but to allow local researchers to inspect the blight and understand how such a foul malady took root in the boughs of the newly grown World Tree.

item:garrick-s-head.text: Garrick's Head. Garrick's Head is the severed head of Garrick Padfoot, a notorious cutthroat operating near the vineyards of Northshire Valley. It serves as gruesome proof of death to claim a bounty issued by the authorities at Northshire Abbey. For weeks, Garrick Padfoot and his gang of thugs harassed local farmers and merchants across Northshire Valley. Taking advantage of the Kingdom of Stormwind's stretched defenses, Garrick holed up in a shack near the Northshire vineyards, raiding passing trade. With local guards pinned down by encroaching kobolds and Defias bandits, Deputy Willem placed a bounty on Padfoot's head, seeking an enterprising adventurer to eliminate the outlaw and present undeniable proof of his demise.

item:gazlowe-s-ledger.text: Gazlowe's Ledger. Gazlowe's Ledger is a detailed record of trade goods and inventories kept by the goblin boss of Ratchet. It serves as an accounting book to cross-check cargo shipments arriving from Booty Bay against the harbor manifest. Overseeing a bustling trade port like Ratchet requires meticulous accounting. Gazlowe maintains this personal ledger to track imported crates, outbound cargo, and warehouse stores. When a long-awaited shipment from Booty Bay goes unaccounted for, Gazlowe uses the book to cross-reference his projected inventory against the maritime records kept down at the docks by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

item:gem-of-anacondra.text: Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

item:gem-of-cobrahn.text: Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

item:gem-of-pythas.text: Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

item:gem-of-serpentis.text: Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

item:gerenzo-s-mechanical-arm.text: Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm is the grafted prosthetic limb taken from the rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as unmistakable proof of his demise for goblin operatives seeking to clear out competition. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took self-modification to a grotesque extreme, grafting whirring gears and metal directly onto his failing body. Perched above Cragpool Lake, the renegade gnome replaced natural limbs with intricate machinery. When the goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks seeks Gerenzo's elimination to impress his superiors, this distinctive mechanical arm is the only trophy unique enough to serve as indisputable evidence of the engineer's death.

item:ghost-hair-comb.text: Ghost Hair Comb. The Ghost Hair Comb is an eerie grooming tool entangled with the spectral strands of the spirit Blind Mary. Sent to the ghost by Madame Eva, the comb becomes an instrument of tragic realization before its gathered hair is spun into uncanny thread. Madame Eva of Darkshire sends the comb to the haunted spirit Blind Mary, who resides in a lonely dilapidated dwelling on the outskirts of Duskwood.
