When presented with the comb, the ghost recoils in sheer horror, suddenly confronted with the harrowing reality that she is no longer the lovely living woman she once was. In her grief and distress, Mary thrusts the comb away, leaving it tangled with strands of her own ghostly hair.

item:ghost-hair-thread.text: Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is a rare, supernatural material spun by Madame Eva in Darkshire. Infused with potent occult properties, it is said to bind spiritual energies and even sew life into inanimate things. The hermit Abercrombie requests it to ward his dilapidated shack against restless ghosts. Spun by the fortune teller Madame Eva in Darkshire, Ghost Hair Thread is far more than an ordinary tailoring supply. According to Eva, the spectral thread possesses versatile occult properties, ranging from binding malevolent spirits to stitching vitality into inanimate objects. Its ethereal nature makes it a valuable asset for rituals and wards in the cursed realm of Duskwood.

item:ghoul-fang.text: Ghoul Fang. Ghoul Fangs are gruesome trophies harvested from the undead prowling the blighted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. In Darkshire, the seer Madame Eva uses them as essential components in crafting defensive talismans for travelers facing the encroaching darkness. The shadowed forest of Duskwood crawls with ravenous undead, from flesh eaters lurking near the graves to rotted corpses roaming the woods. Taking a fang from these monstrous creatures is both grim work and proof of survival against the ravenous dead that threaten Darkshire's borders. Madame Eva, the resident fortune teller and mystic in Darkshire, sees terrible omens swirling around travelers who dare step through Duskwood. She binds the latent necrotic essence of ghoul fangs alongside skeletal fingers and arachnid venom to enchant the Totem of Infliction, turning the dark forces of the forest into a protective charm against violent assault.

item:ghoul-rib.text: Ghoul Rib. Ghoul Ribs are harvested from the undead prowling the haunted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. The hermit Abercrombie claims to need them as materials to construct a grotesque effigy to ward off the flesh-eating horrors near his shack. The cursed forest of Duskwood crawls with violent undead, including ravenous ghouls such as Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones, and Plague Spreaders. Abercrombie, an eccentric recluse living isolated in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery, requests these sturdy, rotted bones from passing travelers. He claims that living outside the protection of the Night Watch in Darkshire leaves him vulnerable, and that assembling a terrifying effigy from ghoul ribs will serve as a scarecrow to frighten off prowling packs of the dead.

item:giant-crocolisk-skin.text: Giant Crocolisk Skin. Giant Crocolisk Skins are thick hides taken from the massive reptiles native to the marshes of the Wetlands. Prized by Menethil Harbor tradesmen for leatherworking, harvesting them is perilous work that has maimed more than one unwary hunter. The bogs and waterways of the Wetlands are home to enormous crocolisks whose hides are dense enough to resist the damp rot of the marshes. In Menethil Harbor, artisans like James Halloran rely on steady shipments of skins to craft rugged leather goods. However, taking a hide from a fully grown giant crocolisk requires braving deep waters and outmatching ferocious swamp predators, making every gathered pelt hard-won.

item:gloom-weed.text: Gloom Weed. Gloom Weed is a sickly plant native to the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades, commonly growing in the fields between Deathknell and Brill. It is best known as the wrong plant collected by Gordo, a lumbering Forsaken abomination who confuses it with the alchemy reagent doom weed. Sprouting amid the gloom and decay of Tirisfal Glades, Gloom Weed thrives in the fallow earth west of Brill and east of the Solliden Farmstead. Despite its morbid name, the plant is relatively harmless and lacks the potent alchemical kick prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. Its primary notoriety stems from the abomination Gordo, who wanders the roadway attempting to pull weeds with his massive, clumsy hands. Having misunderstood his master's commands, Gordo constantly gathers Gloom Weed and enlists gullible travelers to carry bunches of it back to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard, much to the apothecary's supreme annoyance.

item:glowing-ember.text: Glowing Ember. A Glowing Ember is the lingering, elemental core recovered from a defeated Minor Manifestation of Fire atop the crags of Durotar. It serves as a vital ceremonial reagent in a shaman's trials, used to ignite the brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame. When a rising shaman drinks the fire sapta and faces the fiery spirits atop the ridge near Telf Joolam, they confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire. Upon the elemental's defeat, this smoldering remnant is all that remains of its physical form. Still pulsing with raw elemental heat, the ember carries the living spark of fire necessary to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

item:glowing-fruit.text: Glowing Fruit. The Glowing Fruit is an exotic, luminescent specimen found growing amid strange fronds on the boughs of Teldrassil. Its unnatural radiance and bizarre interaction with the World Tree's soil make it an object of urgent botanical study for naturalists. Discovered hanging beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, this large, round fruit radiates an unmistakable light. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth recognizes it as non-native to the World Tree, speculating its seeds arrived from distant lands across the sea. Whatever its origin, the fruit reacts strangely to the rich, enchanted soil of Teldrassil, demonstrating how vulnerable the nascent world bough is to foreign and unpredictable flora.

item:glowing-gem.text: Glowing Gem. The Glowing Gem is an enchanted stone recovered from the murloc camps along the waters of Ashenvale. Originally sought by the fallen scout Teronis, the stone is a vital component needed to reconstruct the magical rod crafted by Dartol. Discovered in the possession of the aggressive murlocs dwelling near Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem is imbued with latent magical energy. The young night elf Teronis ventured out from Astranaar to track it down, aiming to piece together a tool capable of driving back the corruption seeping through Ashenvale's forests. Though Teronis met an untimely end at the lake, the stone itself survived intact among the shoreline scavengers.

item:glowing-soul-gem.text: Glowing Soul Gem. A Glowing Soul Gem is a dark ritual artifact carried by operatives of the Cult of the Dark Strand in northern Ashenvale. Imbued with shadowy sorcery, the stone traps the spirit of an unwitting victim to fuel the cult's sinister operations. Northeast of Maestra's Post, in the shadowed ruins of Ordil'Aran, members of the Cult of the Dark Strand wield dark sorcery under the watchful eyes of their shadowy masters. Among their ranks, operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems—vessels enchanted to trap and torment the souls of the dead. Rather than mere decorative trinkets, these stones act as conduits of magical energy, anchoring bound spirits to serve the cult's shadowy ends.

item:glutton-shackle.text: Glutton Shackle. Glutton Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by Moonrage Glutton worgen in Silverpine Forest. Crafted by the mad archmage Arugal, these bands channel magic to bolster his otherwise flawed sorcery and sustain his cursed lupine creations. To the trained mages of the Forsaken, the feral worgen infesting Silverpine are not merely savage monstrosities—they are evidence of gross arcane ineptitude. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds nothing but contempt for Archmage Arugal, deeming him an incompetent hack unworthy of the Kirin Tor. Dawnweaver discovered that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to compensate for his fragile spells. The Glutton Shackles, worn by the heavy Moonrage Gluttons wandering northern Silverpine, act as magical anchors that reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

item:glyph-of-azora.text: Glyph of Azora. A Glyph of Azora is an arcane tracking device crafted by the wizard Theocritus at the Tower of Azora. Bound to the scrying power of the Eye of Azora, these inscribed stones allow the mage to peer across distances and delve into the thoughts of his enemies. From his tower in Elwynn Forest, the wizard Theocritus works tirelessly to monitor hostile powers threatening the realm. While his crystal relic, the Eye of Azora, enables long-range visual scrying, it lacks the reach to pierce deeper into the minds and plans of adversaries. To overcome this limitation, Theocritus embeds miniature focuses known as Glyphs of Azora. Once affixed to a surface in a remote location, a glyph acts as an anchor for his magic, allowing him not only to read enemy intentions but also to project his voice across miles to communicate directly with field agents.

item:glyphic-letter.text: Glyphic Letter. The Glyphic Letter is an official missive bearing the arcane sigil of Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer in Northshire Abbey. Delivered to promising novitiates after early service to the garrison, it bids aspiring mages to report upstairs and face the rigorous realities of arcane study. Sealed with the personal insignia of the mage trainer Khelden Bremen, the Glyphic Letter is handed to apprentice spellcasters once they have proven their discipline in Northshire Valley. The letter acts as a formal invitation to step away from basic field duties and begin dedicated magical instruction within the abbey. Bremen uses the summons to gauge the student's resolve, ensuring anyone meddling with the arcane is fully prepared to confront dangerous forces, unyielding scrutiny, and the burdens that come with wielding raw magical power.

item:glyphic-memorandum.text: Glyphic Memorandum. The Glyphic Memorandum is a written notice delivered to novice mages arriving in Coldridge Valley. Penned on behalf of the mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, it directs fledgling spellcasters indoors to begin their formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters setting out into the bitter frost of Coldridge Valley receive this brief missive after completing their initial tasks. Authored by the local mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, the memorandum summons young practitioners into the warmth of Anvilmar. Rather than stern academic dogma, Marryk's guidance is informal and blunt: learn your incantations, set aside coin for training and tavern ale, and steer well clear of the irradiated ruin of Gnomeregan.

item:glyphic-scroll.text: Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is a summons delivered to newly raised Forsaken magi in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of Isabella, the local arcane trainer, it calls fledgling spellcasters to the desecrated church to refine their craft in undeath. When a freshly awakened Forsaken mage returns from culling mindless Scourge in the graveyard of Deathknell, this sealed missive awaits them. Written under the mark of Isabella, the settlement's resident mage trainer, the scroll calls the recipient into the ruined parish sanctuary. For newly risen magi, it serves as an initial orientation into the discipline of the arcane under the Forsaken banner—reminding them that while death may have unburdened them of mortal weakness, the corrupting temptations of magical power remain as persistent as ever.

item:glyphic-tablet.text: Glyphic Tablet. The Glyphic Tablet is an inscribed slate handed to novice Darkspear troll mages upon beginning their trials in Durotar. Delivered through the overseer Gornek, it directs fledgling spellcasters to seek tutelage from the troll mage trainer, Mai'ah. In the Valley of Trials, new Darkspear troll initiates exhibiting an affinity for arcane power are presented with the Glyphic Tablet. Passed along by Gornek while young recruits handle early tasks around the red canyons, the tablet contains an invitation from Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage posted outside the Den. For the Darkspear, whose arcane traditions diverge from the scholarly academies of humans or high elves, the tablet serves as a formal call to discipline. Mai'ah uses the meeting to offer both arcane instruction and a solemn warning: raw magic is corruptive, deceptive, and far more hazardous to a practitioner's mind than any enemy soldier.

item:glyphs-of-summoning.text: Glyphs of Summoning. The Glyphs of Summoning are ritual inscriptions used by apprentice warlocks in Orgrimmar. Transcribed from the ancient Tablet of Verga, they allow a practitioner to draw a voidwalker from the Nether into a summoning circle and bind it to their service. In the subterranean depths of the Cleft of Shadow, the dark arts are studied far from the prying eyes of the Warchief's guards. For an aspiring warlock under the tutelage of Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks a vital step in their craft. The Glyphs of Summoning, derived from the esoteric knowledge inscribed upon the Tablet of Verga, bridge the boundary between Azeroth and the Nether. Laid down within the summoning circle in Neeru Fireblade's tent, the glyphs tear open a threshold, pulling a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. The ritual demands that the warlock conquer the summoned entity in combat before Gan'rul imparts the final methods of binding.

item:gnoam-sprecklesprocket.text: Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket is a sophisticated power supply salvaged from Sneed's shredder deep within the Deadmines. Gnomish engineers seek this component to supercharge specialized drilling machines in an ambitious bid to reclaim their fallen home of Gnomeregan. Found in a goblin shredder operated within the Defias stronghold, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket represents an exceptional feat of compact mechanical energy. Operating deep in the lumbering machine piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this specialized core delivers enough sustained energy to drive heavy industrial logging and cutting blades. Its stability and potent output make it an invaluable piece of salvage amidst the subterranean tunnels of Westfall. In Stormwind City, the gnomish inventor Shoni the Shilent singled out the Deadmines shredder as the key to a larger offensive. Gnomish forces seek to reclaim Gnomeregan from the trogg hordes that overran it, but the sealed underground approaches present a formidable barrier. By harnessing the Sprecklesprocket, Shoni intends to power heavy gyrodrillmatic excavationators capable of boring directly through the solid bedrock surrounding the lost techno-city, establishing an unexpected underground assault route.

item:gnoll-paw.text: Gnoll Paw. Gnoll Paws are crude physical trophies harvested from Riverpaw gnolls roaming the grasslands of Westfall. Collected by The People's Militia, they serve as proof of a patrol's success in thinning the packs that threaten the local farmsteads. With the royal army absent and the crown seemingly blind to the plight of rural settlements, the defense of Westfall has fallen to ordinary citizens and volunteer forces. The People's Militia, operating out of Sentinel Hill, struggles constantly against outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and aggressive hyena-headed gnolls. To curb the gnoll menace, Captain Danuvin instituted bounties requiring physical evidence of slain beasts. Collecting severed paws is a grim necessity, ensuring that contracted adventurers truly scour the scrublands rather than loaf in the shadow of the watchtower. The Riverpaw gnolls in Westfall are more than just feral wild beasts foraging on the plains. Observers among the militia have noted troubling signs that these gnolls operate in close coordination with the Defias thieves based around the Deadmines. By terrorizing outlying farmsteads and preying on traveling supply wagons, the gnoll packs effectively screen the bandits from local resistance. Suppressing them by bringing in their paws helps keep the precarious overland routes between Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest open.

item:gnomeregan-gumdrop.text: Gnomeregan Gumdrop. A Gnomeregan Gumdrop is a specialty seasonal sweet distributed during Hallow's End on behalf of the displaced gnomes. Adventurers fetch this confection to help the sick child Jesper in Stormwind's orphanage celebrate the holiday. While innkeepers across the Alliance dispense regional treats during Hallow's End, the exiled gnomes of Gnomeregan do not have a full capital inn of their own to operate. Instead, the inventive gnome Talvash del Kissel, residing in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, hands out Gnomeregan Gumdrops to travelers willing to play along with his festive tricks. Despite the radioactive disaster that drove his people from their subterranean kingdom, gnomes still proudly share their distinct confectionery with the wider Alliance. Because Jesper is sick and confined to the Stormwind orphanage in Cathedral Square, he cannot travel the continents to go trick-or-treating himself. A Gnomeregan Gumdrop is one of the four essential regional confections—alongside treats from Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus—that kind-hearted travelers gather across the Alliance capitals to bring the festivities to him.

item:gnomish-tools.text: Gnomish Tools. Gnomish Tools are intricate mechanical implements recovered from the sunken warships of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet off the coast of Durotar. The Horde seeks these salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and turn their enemies' technological advantages to their own benefit. When Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to the shores of Durotar, his fleet carried vast supplies of modern equipment, including sophisticated gear manufactured by their gnomish allies. Following the destruction of Proudmoore's fleet along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, these delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Today, waterproof toolboxes remain scattered among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows. Gar'Thok, overseer of Razor Hill, tasked Horde scouts with securing these tools from the watery grave of Proudmoore's navy. The orcs recognize that humans and gnomes possess advanced technical craftsmanship, particularly in siege engines, shipwrighting, and clockwork mechanics. By collecting and dispatching these kits by caravan to the craftsmen and scholars in Orgrimmar, the Horde intends to dissect Alliance contraptions, learn how to counter their war machines, and adapt foreign innovations for their own survival.

item:gold-dust.text: Gold Dust. Gold Dust consists of fine flecks of precious metal sifted and hoarded by the kobolds infesting the mines of Elwynn Forest. While ordinary miners seek intact ore veins, local opportunists pay good coin to anyone willing to pry these gathered particles from the vermin. Beneath the soil of Elwynn Forest, kobolds scratch away at the subterranean tunnels of the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines. Rather than properly refining the ore they uncover, the rat-like creatures often hoard coarse gold dust directly in their pockets and pouches. These small, glittering shavings represent the tedious labor of subterranean scavenging, easily overlooked by proper mining syndicates but intensely coveted by local peddlers and fences looking to turn a quiet profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

item:golm-fragment.text: Golm Fragment. The Golm Fragment is one of four missing pieces chipped from the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic uncovered at the Wetlands excavation site. Recovered by adventurers dodging ferocious raptors, it helps dwarven archaeologists piece together mysterious Titan inscriptions. Discovered at the excavation site in the southern Wetlands, the Golm Fragment is part of a monumental slab known as the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar discovered the stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back, but found its inscription severed in four critical places. The Golm Fragment was abandoned amid the dirt and overturned crates when the dig was overrun, hidden away inside an ancient relic box until brave explorers could retrieve it.

item:gordon-s-crate.text: Gordon's Crate. Gordon's Crate is a heavy shipment of weapons packed in the Undercity for the Forsaken forces stationed in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an essential supply consignment meant to be ferried directly to the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. Maintaining the Forsaken grip on Silverpine Forest requires a steady logistical flow from the Undercity. Gordon's Crate holds armaments intended to bolster Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher, ensuring outpost sentries are not caught off guard by the worgen, wild beasts, or human remnants lurking in the woods. Because overland roads out of the capital are dangerous and slow, valuable shipments rely on the Undercity's bat handlers. The crate is handed to Michael Garrett, the bat master perched above the city's trade quarter, who secures passage atop a trained flying bat back to Karos Razok's roost in the Sepulcher.

item:grape-manifest.text: Grape Manifest. The Grape Manifest is a handwritten ledger tracking the harvest from Milly Osworth's vineyard in Northshire Valley. It documents the recovery of fresh fruit after local brigands overran the fields, destined for the cellars of Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey has long sustained itself on regional agriculture, including the lush vineyards tended by local farmers like Milly Osworth. When Defias bandits moved into the valley and seized the harvest, the abbey's stock of fresh fruit and fermentables was thrown into jeopardy. The Grape Manifest serves as official confirmation that the crates have been reclaimed from the fields. It details the quantity of saved grapes so the abbey's quartermasters can balance their stores and prepare barrels for fermentation. Brother Neals oversees Northshire's food and drink, maintaining a particular fondness for testing the abbey's vintage in the high quiet of the bell tower. For him, receiving the manifest is not merely administrative paperwork; it ensures that the monks and visiting recruits will not go thirsty. To the devout brothers of the abbey, every saved bushel is celebrated as both a logistical victory and a quiet blessing from the Holy Light.

item:gray-bear-tongue.text: Gray Bear Tongue. A gray bear tongue is a raw reagent harvested from the wild bears roaming the Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill to serve as a biological component in their experimental toxins. The untamed wilderness surrounding Tarren Mill is rich in native fauna, including several varieties of sturdy gray bears. While natural predators pose a constant threat to travelers, the Forsaken see them as a harvestable source of raw alchemy components. Apothecary Lydon studies local wildlife to isolate potent organic agents, using the heavy muscular tissue and fluids of gray bear tongues as a base ingredient for concocting lethal solutions such as the Elixir of Suffering.

item:gregor-s-remains.text: Gregor's Remains. Gregor's Remains are the physical bones recovered from the Scourge-enslaved Gregor Agamand. Once part of the wealthiest dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, his remains are sought by a former mill worker eager to settle an old score from beyond the grave. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held immense wealth and vast tracts of land across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the patriarchs chose pride over flight, fortifying their family mills and persuading their loyal laborers to make a desperate stand against the undead. The defense failed entirely. The estate was overrun, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became another mindless thrall in the service of the Lich King, haunting the very mills his family once ruled. For survivors who broke free from the Lich King's grip to join the Forsaken, the memory of that fateful defense remains a bitter wound. Coleman Farthing, a former mill worker stationed in Brill, blames the hubris of the Agamands for trapping his soul in eternal rot. Collecting Gregor's remains offers Farthing a measure of personal retribution, closing the chapter on a master who led his household straight into damnation.

item:grelin-s-report.text: Grelin's Report. Grelin's Report is a dispatch written by Grelin Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll situation in Coldridge Valley. Entrusted to an adventurer rather than a novice apprentice, it serves as the official link between the scouts guarding Anvilmar and Senir Whitebeard stationed in Kharanos. Written after observing the Frostmane trolls in Coldridge Valley, Grelin's Report concludes that they pose no large threat and can be dealt with by the Mountaineers already stationed there and mercenaries paid from Senate funds. Rather than trusting his fumbling apprentice with such vital intelligence, Grelin enlists a capable traveler to carry the document through the trogg-infested Coldridge Pass. The paper acts as an official pass through Mountaineer Thalos's blockade, proving the bearer travels on urgent business to the wider snowy expanse of Dun Morogh. When delivered to Senir Whitebeard at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, the report provides critical field updates intended for Ironforge. Senir notes with amused resignation that his brother invoked King Magni Bronzebeard's name liberally throughout the text. Grelin claims the King's sanction for the action, and Senir expects that appeal to royal authority to ruffle some feathers in the Ironforge Senate.

item:grelin-whitebeard-s-journal.text: Grelin Whitebeard's Journal. Grelin Whitebeard's Journal is a personal field notebook kept by the dwarf scout Grelin Whitebeard in Coldridge Valley. Containing critical notes on local Frostmane troll activity, the journal was stolen by the Frostmane brute Grik'nir the Cold and dragged into the troll cave in Coldridge Valley. While observing the aggressive movements of the Frostmane trolls near Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard diligently recorded his findings in this leatherbound notebook. The document contains his raw field observations regarding the strength, organization, and threat level posed by the indigenous winter trolls. However, during a confrontation or ambush, the journal was snatched away by Grik'nir the Cold—a heavily marked troll brute—forcing Grelin to recruit passing adventurers to delve into the troll cave and wrest it back before his report could be finalized.

item:grell-earring.text: Grell Earring. Grell Earrings are crude baubles scavenged and worn by the feral creatures infesting the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Though unremarkable at a glance, their proximity to ancient relics allows sensitive spirits to trace the lingering magical seals holding them in torment. The Wild Grells and Vile Sprites lurking around the collapsed marble of Bashal'Aran hoard assorted trinkets, frequently fashioning earrings from scraps they scavenge among the ruins. To most mortals, these items are worthless refuse. However, to Asterion, an ancient night elf bound as a tormented phantom within the ruins, they serve as dowsing implements. By scrutinizing the resonant magical traces absorbed by these earrings, Asterion attempts to locate the ancient seal that imprisons his spectral form.

item:grenka-s-claw.text: Grenka's Claw. Grenka's Claw is a physical trophy taken from the formidable harpy Grenka Bloodscreech in the depths of Roguefeather Den. Presented to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, it serves as undeniable proof that an aspiring adventurer has endured a grueling physical trial in the canyon heights. Within the winding caverns of Roguefeather Den, west of Freewind Post, harpies cache food and violently defend their territory against outsiders. To test the physical resilience of young champions, Dorn Plainstalker tasks them with invading the deep roosts and destroying the flock's food reserves. Such brazen provocation inevitably draws the fury of Grenka Bloodscreech. Severing and returning her wicked talon proves that a warrior can withstand wave after wave of enraged harpies and survive the vicious onslaught of their matriarch.

item:grimtotem-satchel.text: Grimtotem Satchel. The Grimtotem Satchel is a leather pouch clutched by the fallen tauren Maur Grimtotem deep inside Ragefire Chasm. Even as troggs overwhelmed him in the subterranean cavern beneath Orgrimmar, Maur shielded this pack with his dying breath. Recovering it and returning it to Thunder Bluff reveals that Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem had an active interest in whatever her clansman carried. Discovered beneath the broken body of Maur Grimtotem in the depths of Ragefire Chasm, this simple pack was held in a fierce, vice-like embrace. Maur fought desperately to protect whatever it contains while surrounded and slain by savage troggs. The sheer determination required to shield a satchel above one's own life suggests its contents are far more significant than ordinary trail rations or supplies.

item:grizzled-bear-heart.text: Grizzled Bear Heart. A Grizzled Bear Heart is a biological reagent harvested from the sturdy bears roaming Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital component in the Royal Apothecary Society's grim research into the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works ceaselessly to develop an engineered blight capable of exterminating both the Scourge and living humanity. In the woodlands of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel discovered that a unique toxin derived from the heart of a grizzled bear, when combined with arachnid ichor, yields a remarkably lethal concoction. Couriers and Forsaken loyalists hunt down ferocious grizzled bears, giant grizzled bears, and the infamous beast Old Vicejaw to carve out these organs and deliver them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity.

item:grizzled-scalp.text: Grizzled Scalp. A Grizzled Scalp is the thick, furred hide taken from grizzled thistle bears roaming the southern forests of Darkshore. While seemingly an odd trophy, these pelts are sought by the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle to supply his hidden wilderness machinery.

item:gryshka-s-letter.text: Gryshka's Letter. Gryshka's Letter is a personal note of thanks written by Innkeeper Gryshka of Orgrimmar and addressed to the butcher Zargh at the Crossroads. Sent after receiving a delivery of fresh meat, the letter serves as both a sign of gratitude and an excuse to teach young Horde couriers how to navigate the wind rider flight network. When Zargh ships a bundle of prepared steaks from the arid expanses of the Barrens to Orgrimmar's central tavern, Innkeeper Gryshka pens this note in return. Beyond expressing her satisfaction with the butcher's cuts, the letter reveals a fond—if rugged—appreciation for Zargh, recalling humorous misadventures such as the time he lost a finger while preparing meat. Gryshka concludes with affectionate amusement, remarking that he looks handsome even when bloodied by his trade. Carrying Gryshka's Letter provides travelers with a practical lesson in Horde logistics. To return the parchment to the Crossroads, adventurers are instructed to report to Doras, the wind rider master roosted atop Orgrimmar's plateau. By demonstrating that a traveler has already checked in with Devrak at the Crossroads, Doras introduces fledgling couriers to the wyvern flight paths that bind the settlements of Durotar and the Barrens together.

item:gunther-s-spellbook.text: Gunther's Spellbook. Gunther's Spellbook is a personal arcane tome belonging to Gunther Arcanus, a former Kirin Tor wizard dwelling in Tirisfal Glades. Imbued with an enchantment by Bethor Iceshard, the book serves as proof to Gunther that other mages have successfully broken free of the Lich King's control.

item:gyromechanic-gear.text: Gyromechanic Gear. A Gyromechanic Gear is a salvaged piece of precision engineering recovered from the fallout outside Gnomeregan. Gnomish inventors in Kharanos seek these specific gears to construct an experimental device capable of reversing leper gnome mutations. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg invasion, it corrupted a vast portion of the surviving gnome population into mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Refusing to abandon their twisted kin, inventors Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket set to work drafting schematics for the Recombobulator—an ambitious contraption designed to undo the radiation's horrific effects. Building the prototype requires precision mechanisms capable of enduring volatile internal pressures, particularly Gyromechanic Gears and complementary Restabilization Cogs. Because local manufacturing collapsed with the fall of their capital, researchers are forced to scavenge these delicate parts directly from the hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-letter.text: Hallowed Letter. The Hallowed Letter is a formal summons bearing the insignia of Priestess Anetta, delivered to promising young priests in Northshire Valley. It calls the bearer to Northshire Abbey to begin formal study and training in the Holy Light. Sealed with the personal mark of Priestess Anetta, the Hallowed Letter is presented to fledgling priests after their first trials against the kobold camps of Northshire Valley. Anetta recognizes the inner spark of the Holy Light within the novice and urges them not to linger, but to step inside the abbey walls to formally dedicate themselves. With dark forces still lingering across Azeroth in the wake of the Third War, the priesthood actively gathers those capable of healing, protecting, and offering spiritual guidance to an empire struggling to maintain order.

item:hallowed-rune.text: Hallowed Rune. The Hallowed Rune is an inscribed stone passed to novice priests beginning their training in Coldridge Valley. Sent by the dwarven priest trainer Branstock Khalder, it calls aspiring wielders of the Holy Light into Anvilmar to begin their formal tutelage. When a fledgling priest demonstrates their resolve aiding the mountaineers and defenders of Coldridge Valley, Branstock Khalder sends forth the Hallowed Rune. Inscribed with teachings of the Holy Light, the stone serves as both an introduction and an invitation. Dwarven novices are directed to step away from minor skirmishes in the snow and report to Anvilmar, where Branstock prepares them to mend wounds and harness holy power against the trogg infestation threatening Dun Morogh.

item:hallowed-scroll.text: Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is a formal summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Bearing the personal seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, it directs fledglings to the ruined chapel to begin their re-education in faith, willpower, and shadow. Newly risen Forsaken priests find that their connection to the world has violently shifted. Delivered amidst the ongoing chaos of Deathknell's reclamation, the Hallowed Scroll directs nascent spellcasters to seek guidance within the settlement's ruined chapel. Marked with the seal of Dark Cleric Duesten, the parchment serves as both an introduction and an order to report for formal instruction, initiating the priest into the pragmatic philosophy that defines Forsaken priesthood. Upon answering the scroll's summons, priests are immediately disabused of old dogmas. Duesten makes it clear that traditional crutches—the veneration of the Holy Light, ancestral spirits, or demonic pacts—no longer serve the undead. Instead, the scroll marks the start of an inward discipline rooted strictly in individual willpower. The teachings initiated by this parchment emphasize surviving and ruling through sheer conviction, turning religious devotion into an instrument of self-determination and mastery.

item:hallowed-sigil.text: Hallowed Sigil. The Hallowed Sigil is an inscribed night elf token carried by young initiates within Shadowglen. Sent by the priest trainer Shanda, it serves as a formal summons directing prospective servants of Elune to the ancient boughs of Aldrassil. Novice night elf priests stepping into the sacred canopy of Shadowglen often receive the Hallowed Sigil from a woodland messenger. Engraved with holy markings, the token acts as a personal writ from Shanda, the resident priest trainer at Aldrassil. Carrying and reading the sigil directs an acolyte upward to the towering hollow of Aldrassil, formally introducing them to the Sisterhood of Elune and initiating their spiritual service to the Kaldorei as new travelers arrive across Teldrassil.

item:hallowed-tablet.text: Hallowed Tablet. The Hallowed Tablet is an inscribed message delivered to young Darkspear troll priests training in the Valley of Trials. Sent by the spiritual elder Ken'jai, it bids novices to seek him out and begin learning how to commune with the spirits. When a promising troll priest takes their first steps in the harsh crimson canyons of the Valley of Trials, Gornek hands them the Hallowed Tablet. Rather than a formal bureaucratic writ, it serves as a personal invitation from Ken'jai, the resident priest trainer residing outside the Den. Ken'jai interprets the signs and whisperings of the spirits, sensing when young Darkspear with spiritual potential arrive in Durotar. The tablet instructs the initiate to read its words and present themselves for guidance on properly channeling spiritual authority.

item:hand-of-dextren-ward.text: Hand of Dextren Ward. The Hand of Dextren Ward is a severed trophy taken from a condemned grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Delivered to Darkshire, it serves as proof that frontier justice has finally been carried out against a man who desecrated the town's dead. Dextren Ward earned a death sentence from Lord Ebonlocke after he was caught digging up bodies in the Duskwood cemeteries and selling them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Before the town could execute him, Stormwind intervened, hauling the criminal away to the Stockade. For the grieving families of Darkshire, the Hand of Dextren Ward is physical proof that the defiler has met the execution he deserved, bypassing the House of Nobles' unwanted leniency.

item:handful-of-oats-classic.text: Handful of Oats (Classic). Handfuls of Oats are simple grains salvaged from the abandoned farmsteads of Westfall. They serve as essential feed for working livestock like Old Blanchy, who struggle under the weight of refugee travel. Once the breadbasket of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Westfall's vast agrarian plots now lie overgrown or overrun by Defias bandits and rogue harvest golems. Despite the collapse of order, sacks of cultivated grain and oats remain abandoned near outbuildings, barns, and overgrown plots. For travelers and refugees stranded by broken wagons along the dusty roads, recovering handfuls of these leftover oats is one of the few ways to nourish weary draft horses.

item:handful-of-stardust.text: Handful of Stardust. Handfuls of Stardust are shimmering, frosted coatings gathered from sparkling bushes in the southern wilderness of Ashenvale. Sourced from the ancient Ruins of Stardust, this powder possesses cooling natural properties prized by night elven healers treating intense fevers. Found clinging to the leafy shrubs within the ancient Ruins of Stardust south of Astranaar, stardust appears as a fine, luminous frost. While the ruins themselves are haunted by lingering elemental spirits, the vegetation that thrives among the broken stones absorbs a rare ambient luminescence. Traditional night elven medicine makes use of this frosted residue, processing it into poultices to draw out persistent, dangerous fevers when ordinary salves and moonwell waters fail to bring complete relief.

item:hardened-tortoise-shell.text: Hardened Tortoise Shell. Hardened Tortoise Shells are remarkably durable carapaces harvested from the sparkleshell tortoises wandering the Shimmering Flats. Coveted by gnomish racers at the Mirage Raceway, these rugged organic plates offer unmatched resistance against volatile and corrosive experimental fuels. The sun-scorched expanse of the Shimmering Flats is home to various breeds of sparkleshell tortoises, including snappers and borers, whose carapaces have evolved into exceptionally tough defenses against the harsh desert salt and wandering predators. Out on the salt flats, standard metal alloy fuel tanks frequently corrode or rupture under the strain of gnomish experimental chemistry. Mechanics like Wizzle Brassbolts prize these shells not for armor or shields, but as organic raw material tough enough to be retrofitted into makeshift, acid-resistant fuel tanks capable of containing volatile rocket propellants.

item:hardened-tumor.text: Hardened Tumor. A Hardened Tumor is a rare biological anomaly harvested from the Vile Fin murlocs dwelling around Lake Lordamere. Noted originally in the research of Apothecary Berard, now a mindless servant of Arugal, this calcified growth serves as an unusual reagent in the Royal Apothecary Society's efforts to brew the New Plague. While studying the indigenous wildlife along the eastern borders of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard cataloged an abnormal, calcified growth developing within the Vile Fin murlocs of Lake Lordamere. Such growths are exceedingly rare, appearing only in mature specimens along the shoreline and the Dawning Isles. What causes the Vile Fin murlocs to produce these hardened masses remains uncertain, but their dense, morbid tissue caught the immediate attention of the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:harpy-lieutenant-ring.text: Harpy Lieutenant Ring. Harpy Lieutenant Rings are crude ornaments worn by the Witchwing Slayers in the Dry Hills of the northern Barrens. Carried as emblems of command among the flock, they serve as proof of death for Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads. Within the matriarchal hierarchy of the Witchwing harpies, rank is ruthlessly maintained. While the rank-and-file raiders harrying the Barrens fight with little coordination, the Witchwing Slayers serve as field lieutenants directing assaults against Horde travelers. To distinguish themselves and assert authority over their underlings, these veteran slayers carry distinctive rings. For Darsok Swiftdagger and the defenders stationed at the Crossroads, severing these rings from fallen harpies is the only sure way to confirm that the flock's middle leadership has been broken.

item:head-of-arugal.text: Head of Arugal. The Head of Arugal is the grisly trophy taken from the mad archmage atop Shadowfang Keep. Brought to the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, it serves as undeniable proof that the master of the local worgen has fallen. Archmage Arugal has long cast a dark shadow across Silverpine Forest, commanding the lupine horrors from the ramparts of Shadowfang Keep. Claiming his severed head is the ultimate mandate given by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher. To the Forsaken, the head is far more than a gruesome token; it signifies the removal of a potent spellcaster whose feral beasts impeded Lady Sylvanas's complete dominion over Silverpine. Presenting it to Dawnweaver confirms that the rogue archmage's foul sorcery has finally been severed from the land.

item:head-of-bazil-thredd.text: Head of Bazil Thredd. The severed head of Bazil Thredd serves as definitive proof that the leader behind the Stockade uprising has been eliminated. Demanded by Warden Thelwater, this grim trophy marks an end to the Defias Brotherhood's organized control over Stormwind's subterranean prison. When riots erupted throughout the Stockade beneath Stormwind City, Bazil Thredd quickly established himself as the rebellion's mastermind. Entrenched in his cell block among loyal Defias inmates, Thredd directed the chaos from deep within the dungeon walls. Distrustful of outsiders and struggling to maintain order, Warden Thelwater demanded Thredd's head as unambiguous evidence of his demise and as a test of the adventurer's true allegiance to Stormwind.

item:head-of-deepfury.text: Head of Deepfury. The severed head of Kam Deepfury serves as grim proof that the Dark Iron conspirator behind the sabotaged Thandol Span has met his end. Slain within the riots of the Stormwind Stockade, his death fulfills a personal vendetta for the dwarven defenders of Dun Modr. Kam Deepfury was arrested and locked away in the Stormwind Stockade for political reasons, spared from immediate execution by human diplomatic bureaucracy. To the Ironforge mountaineers stationed at Dun Modr, this restraint was unacceptable. Intelligence uncovered by Roggo revealed that Deepfury orchestrated the devastating attack on the Thandol Span—an assault that cost the lives of King Magni's soldiers and the kin of Longbraid the Grim. Bound by duty to remain at his post, Motley Garmason commissioned Alliance champions to infiltrate the rioting prison and claim Deepfury's head, ensuring true dwarven vengeance was delivered where human diplomacy faltered.

item:head-of-gath-ilzogg.text: Head of Gath'Ilzogg. The severed head of Gath'Ilzogg serves as indisputable proof that the Blackrock warlord has been slain. Claiming it breaks the leadership behind the siege of Stonewatch Keep and brings desperate relief to the town of Lakeshire. Gath'Ilzogg orchestrated the brutal Blackrock assault that overran Stonewatch Keep, driving out its defenders and subjecting the surrounding valley to relentless raiding. With Lakeshire on the verge of ruin and Stormwind offering virtually no military reinforcements, Magistrate Solomon posted a bounty upon the warlord's head. Slaying Gath'Ilzogg within the fortified upper levels of Stonewatch and claiming his head shatters the local Blackrock leadership, marking the first real step toward reclaiming the keep for the kingdom.

item:head-of-grimson.text: Head of Grimson. The Head of Grimson is the severed trophy taken from Grimson the Pale, the corrupted overseer of the Deep Elem Mine in Silverpine Forest. Brought to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, it serves as physical proof that the mine's leadership has been eliminated. Securing the mine allows the Forsaken to seize valuable mineral wealth to fuel Varimathras's military campaigns. While Dalar Dawnweaver studies Archmage Arugal's shadowy enchantments from the safety of the Sepulcher, Forsaken scouts known as Darkstalkers identified a strategic threat brewing in the southeastern hills. Arugal's dark magic had seeped into the Deep Elem Mine, corrupting its workers and driving its overseer, Grimson the Pale, into madness. To secure the subterranean riches for Varimathras's forces, Dawnweaver dispatched champions to cut down Grimson and return with his severed head as undeniable confirmation of the mine's liberation from rogue magics.

item:head-of-kelris.text: Head of Kelris. The severed head of Twilight Lord Kelris serves as undeniable proof that the leader of the Twilight's Hammer within Blackfathom Deeps has fallen. Carried out from the corrupted temple ruins, it is sought by representatives of the Argent Dawn to confirm the end of his profane ritual sacrifices. Within the submerged depths of the sunken Temple of Elune, Twilight Lord Kelris orchestrated dark sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God. Claiming his head marks the end of his tyrannical leadership over the Twilight's Hammer cultists and their naga allies in the cavern. The grisly trophy must be carried back to surface civilizations to assure leaders that Kelris's bloody ceremonies have finally ceased. For months, Kelris was presumed dead or lost by the Argent Dawn, only for his sinister influence to resurface alongside Kalimdor's encroaching shadows. When presented to agents in Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, the head settles lingering bounties and confirms that his attempts to plunge the world back into primeval chaos have been thwarted.

item:head-of-targorr.text: Head of Targorr. The Head of Targorr is the grim proof demanded by Guard Berton in Lakeshire to confirm the death of Targorr the Dread. Once the supreme executioner for the Blackrock warlord Gath'Ilzogg in the Redridge Mountains, the captured orc was sentenced to death in the Stormwind Stockade before suspicious political meddling halted his execution. Targorr the Dread gained infamy across Redridge as the brutal executioner serving under the Blackrock clan warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Responsible for torturing and slaughtering defenders of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Targorr was eventually captured and condemned to death within the Stormwind Stockade. However, bureaucratic intervention from Stormwind nobles mysteriously suspended the sentence, leading local guardsmen like Berton to suspect foul play and corruption in the capital. Fearing that Targorr might be used as a political pawn or somehow orchestrate an escape, Guard Berton commissioned an outside champion to breach the volatile prison and finish what the courts delayed. Severing Targorr's head bypassed the paralyzed legal system entirely, delivering closure to the grieving families and besieged defenders of Lakeshire who suffered under the executioner's blades.

item:head-of-vancleef.text: Head of VanCleef. The severed head of Edwin VanCleef serves as grim, irrefutable proof that the leader of the Defias Brotherhood has fallen. Brought back from the depths of the Deadmines to Sentinel Hill, it represents the hard-won vengeance of the People's Militia. For months, Edwin VanCleef directed the Defias Brotherhood's terror from the deepest sanctum of the Deadmines, shielded by heavily armed outlaws, goblin engineers, and a massive war juggernaut. Words alone could never convince the battered settlers of Westfall that their nightmare was over. Gryan Stoutmantle, leader of the People's Militia, demanded undeniable physical proof before declaring the countryside safe. Severing the ringleader's head and bringing it out into the daylight offers the exhausted defenders tangible assurance that the grand architect of their ruin will never threaten Westfall again.

item:heart-of-isha-awak.text: Heart of Isha Awak. The Heart of Isha Awak is taken from the mighty thresher known as Isha Awak, the Deep Doom of the Merchant Coast. Sought by the tauren seer Mahren Skyseer, it serves as proof of overcoming one of the ocean's most formidable predators. Off the sun-drenched shores of the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet dwells Isha Awak, a massive sea beast revered and feared by sailors and coastal inhabitants alike. Known as the Deep Doom, the creature has claimed the lives of numerous human trespassers along the shoreline. For the mystic Mahren Skyseer, however, the beast represents an honorable predator rather than a mindless menace. She believes Isha Awak's fierce spirit resides directly within its heart, charging brave hunters to plunge into the waves, best the beast in its domain, and claim the pulsating organ as both trophy and spiritual offering.

item:heartswood.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is timber harvested from a sacred tree rooted within the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. Born from the final resting place of two ancient lovers, its resonance with undying devotion makes it an essential lure for summoning a succubus. The Heartswood grows among the elven stones of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran in northwestern Ashenvale. According to legend, two lovers named Anathera and Latherion fell side by side during the catastrophic War of the Ancients thousands of years ago. On the very earth where they breathed their last, a peculiar tree took root, blossoming as an eternal testament to their devotion. Even millennia later, the wood cut from this tree hums with the memory of undying passion, making it an object of great curiosity for those who study emotional and spiritual bonds.

item:heartswood-core.text: Heartswood Core. The Heartswood Core is an enchanted ritual focus crafted from the wood of an ancient tree. Provided by Gakin the Darkbinder in Stormwind City, it channels the magic required to pierce the Twisting Nether and summon a succubus into an arcane summoning circle. Within the dark crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb tavern in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, warlocks conduct rites far away from the prying eyes of the city watch. The Heartswood Core serves as an essential arcane conduit for initiating the ritual of binding. Fashioned from harvested heartswood, the core contains sufficient lingering magical resonance to pierce the veil between worlds. By focusing their dark arts through the wood at a consecrated summoning circle, an initiate can tear open a passage to the Twisting Nether, compelling a succubus across the planar barrier.

item:heavy-leaden-collection-phial.text: Heavy Leaden Collection Phial. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a shielded sampling vessel provided by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. It is designed to safely siphon and contain highly unstable irradiated discharge from the mutants deep inside Gnomeregan for ongoing decontamination research. The Heavy Leaden Collection Phial is a sampling vessel used to draw volatile residues from living, irradiated creatures in Gnomeregan. Containing this fallout is difficult, and collecting a suitable sample may take several attempts. Ozzie Togglevolt provides the phial as part of his research to reverse the horrific mutations afflicting leper gnomes. Earlier samples taken from surface troggs lacked the potency needed for effective chemical analysis. By using the leaden phial on virulent beasts like irradiated slimes and lurkers in the Hall of Gears, researchers hope to isolate the active elements of the city's toxic fallout and formulate an effective antidote.

item:hezrul-s-head.text: Hezrul's Head. Hezrul's Head is the grisly trophy taken from Hezrul Bloodmark, chieftain of the Kolkar centaur dwelling in the Barrens. Brought to Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads, it serves as undeniable proof that the central leadership of the local marauders has fallen. The Kolkar centaur maintain an aggressive hold on the crucial oases throughout the arid Barrens, constantly threatening Horde supply routes and fledgling settlements. Hezrul Bloodmark directs his clan from the Lushwater Oasis to the south. Regthar Deathgate, an orc veteran tasked with securing the territory west of the Crossroads, recognizes that while the Kolkar possess fierce rage, they lack formal discipline. By demanding Hezrul's severed head, Regthar seeks to fracture the clan's command structure, plunging their surviving fighters into disarray and blunting their coordinated assaults against the Horde.

item:high-potency-radioactive-fallout.text: High Potency Radioactive Fallout. High Potency Radioactive Fallout is a concentrated, volatile sample of the irradiated sludge poisoning the lower depths of Gnomeregan. Gathered in heavy leaden containers by order of gnome researchers, it is sought in the hope of reverse-engineering a cure for the afflicted leper gnomes. While minor radiation samples can be scraped from contaminated surface scavengers outside, the true heart of Gnomeregan's catastrophe demands something far more concentrated. Researchers stationed outside the fallen capital require raw, unadulterated radioactive fallout taken directly from living irradiated horrors, lurkers, and slimes creeping across the lowest tiers of the Hall of Gears. Because this viscous sludge is constantly decaying, it must be contained in a specialized leaden phial and returned quickly before the sample destabilizes entirely. The desperate pursuit of such lethal materials serves an urgent purpose. Ozzie Togglevolt and his colleagues believe that unlocking the secrets of the irradiated sludge is the only viable path toward developing a cure for the leper gnomes. Driven mad and deformed by the toxic venting ordered during the trogg invasion, these tragic survivors remain trapped in a living nightmare, making even the most dangerous gathering expeditions inside the ruins worth the hazard.

item:highborne-relic-classic.text: Highborne Relic (Classic). Highborne Relics are ancient magical implements recovered from the restless spirits haunting the ruins of Ameth'Aran in Darkshore. Imbued with the arcane dabblings that shattered ancient Kalimdor, they are sought by night elf scholars who wish to see them destroyed before their dormant powers can cause further harm. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne caste practiced reckless arcane magic, ultimately bringing ruin upon ancient Kalimdor. Today, their former estates lie in shattered ruin across Darkshore. Within the crumbling columns of Ameth'Aran, wailing and writhing apparitions wander the forest floor, endlessly clinging to the physical implements of their bygone sorcery. These relics remain persistent tether-points of arcane taint, clutched by ghosts who refuse to release the instruments of their own undoing. For modern night elf society, which largely renounced arcane magic after the Great Sundering, such artifacts represent a grave hazard. Scholars like Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, acting upon scouting reports from the Sentinels, actively commission travelers to wrest these relics from the spectral hands of the cursed spirits. Once gathered, the relics are systematically destroyed to ensure that the ancient evils and catastrophic mistakes of the Highborne cannot be repeated.

item:highperch-venom-sac.text: Highperch Venom Sac. Highperch Venom Sacs are harvested from the wild wyverns nesting upon the towering spires of Highperch in Thousand Needles. While orcs prize wyverns as aerial mounts, select apothecaries and traders value their potent stingers even more than the living beasts. The high spires of Thousand Needles house thriving prides of wild wyverns, particularly around the elevated crags of Highperch. These winged predators rely on powerful venom delivered through their barbed tails to paralyze and kill prey. While the Horde often domesticates these creatures as loyal wind riders, their venom sacs command a remarkably high price among alchemists, hunters, and opportunistic merchants across Kalimdor. Though native to the deep canyons of central Kalimdor, this venom draws interest far beyond them. In the port town of Theramore, the high elf Fiora Longears pays handsomely for fresh sacs collected from Highperch's broods. She seeks samples swollen with venom—typically found only on young wyverns or fertile females—fueling trade in dangerous reagents far from the beasts' natural desert habitat.

item:highperch-wyvern-egg.text: Highperch Wyvern Egg. Highperch Wyvern Eggs are clutch eggs gathered from the nesting grounds atop the high mesas of Thousand Needles. They are sought after by aspiring Horde wind riders to raise and train new aerial mounts. The high plateau of Highperch in Thousand Needles provides a natural sanctuary for native wyverns to roost and raise their young. Accessible only via steep winding paths up the canyon walls, these nesting grounds are fiercely guarded by adult beasts. The eggs laid among these roosts are sturdy and warm, holding developing hatchlings capable of adapting to the harsh skies of Kalimdor. Across Kalimdor, the demand for trained wyverns continually outstrips supply as the Horde expands its courier and scouting networks. At Freewind Post, trainees like the tauren Elu seek out intact eggs directly from wild aeries. By raising the hatchlings from their shells, handlers hope to forge the deep bonds required to train trustworthy winged mounts for the Horde's wind riders.

item:hildelve-s-journal.text: Hildelve's Journal. Hildelve's Journal is the final record of dwarven pilot Hildelve, recovered from his remains in the frigid wilderness of Dun Morogh. Its bloodstained pages recount his fatal encounter with a ferocious bear and convey his dying wish for vengeance. When his steam tank broke down, dwarven pilot Hildelve left his partner Hammerfoot with the tanks and set out alone into the snow-swept crags of Dun Morogh in search of rumored chiron ore. According to the entries scrawled in his journal, he was stalked for days and then ambushed by a monstrous ice claw bear known as Mangeclaw. Though Hildelve fought bravely and managed to drive the beast off, he was left gravely mauled and stranded in the bitter cold. The journal details his agonizing final hours, concluding with a single, clear plea before the predator returned to finish him: that whoever discovered his body avenge his death by hunting down Mangeclaw.

item:hillsbrad-human-skull.text: Hillsbrad Human Skull. A gruesome war trophy harvested from slain human defenders and townsfolk across the Hillsbrad Foothills. These skulls are collected by Forsaken stationed at Tarren Mill as grim mementos of the relentless assault against the local human settlements. As conflict rages between the Forsaken of Tarren Mill and the human inhabitants of Southshore and surrounding settlements, severed skulls serve as physical proof of the slaughter. While Deathstalkers and soldiers carry out the systematic purge ordered by Darthalia during the Battle of Hillsbrad, other guards stuck on watch duty crave a piece of the carnage. Deathguard Samsa eagerly solicits these trophies from frontline fighters, taking twisted pleasure in amassing the remains of the very people the Forsaken once lived among in life.

item:hillsbrad-town-registry.text: Hillsbrad Town Registry. The Hillsbrad Town Registry is an official municipal ledger kept inside the town hall of the Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as an accounting of the settlement's surviving citizens, landowners, and civic records, making it a key strategic target during the Forsaken offensive against the human stronghold. Resting in the town hall near the podium of Magistrate Burnside, the Hillsbrad Town Registry documents the population, households, and administrative rights of Hillsbrad. As the Forsaken from Tarren Mill push to break human resistance in the foothills, Darthalia commands Horde champions to infiltrate the town hall, eliminate the council, and seize this ledger. Confiscating the registry strips Hillsbrad of its civic order and provides the Undercity with valuable intelligence on the surviving population and their assets.

item:hollow-vulture-bone.text: Hollow Vulture Bone. Hollow Vulture Bones are lightweight, durable skeletal remains harvested from the scavengers of the Shimmering Flats. At the Mirage Raceway, goblin mechanics prize them as specialized building materials to lighten their rocket cars without sacrificing structural integrity. Speed is everything out on the salt, and weight is the enemy of speed. While standard engineering leans heavily on iron and copper, the goblin pit crews at the Mirage Raceway turn to whatever the desert provides to gain an edge. Vulture bones are naturally hollow yet remarkably sturdy, providing the perfect strength-to-weight ratio for internal brackets, steering rigs, and minor structural supports. For chief tinkerers like Pozzik, harvesting bones from local scavengers is a practical and cheap shortcut to shaved seconds on the track.

item:honorary-picks.text: Honorary Picks. The Honorary Picks are a bundle of ceremonial tools crafted in Ironforge for young dwarven mining apprentices. Entrusted to travelers by way of the gryphon network, they are delivered to Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar to mark his students' readiness to work the rich ore veins of Loch Modan. In dwarven society, mining is far more than a trade; it is a cultural cornerstone that keeps the great forges burning and the kingdom supplied with iron and stone. The Honorary Picks represent formal recognition for novice prospectors learning under Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. Sourced directly from Ironforge, these picks are presented to students who have proven their dedication and are ready to tackle the open ore deposits across Loch Modan. Transporting the picks serves a secondary purpose for the mountaineers and merchants of the Alliance: introducing couriers to the kingdom's gryphon network. Ferried from Ironforge's Great Forge directly to Gryth Thurden and flown across the mountains to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar, the shipment illustrates how closely tied the capital remains to its outlying outposts through swift aerial passage.

item:horn-of-arra-chea.text: Horn of Arra'chea. The Horn of Arra'chea is a hunting trophy taken from the legendary kodo Arra'chea, who wanders the plains of Mulgore. Claimed at the behest of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the horn serves as definitive proof that an aspiring hunter has the discipline and tracking prowess to provide for the Shu'halo. Though passing the initial Rites of the Earthmother grants a youth their rightful place atop Thunder Bluff, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof expects his people to continually prove their worth. For the tauren, identity is bound directly to the hunt and their enduring harmony with the land. Cairne tests young hunters by tasking them with tracking down Arra'chea, a massive, lone kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking Arra'chea's horn proves mastery over the fundamental art of tracking prey across vast distances. Bringing the horn to the high rise of Thunder Bluff is more than a display of martial strength; it serves the survival of the entire community. In tauren culture, nothing of a slain beast is allowed to go to waste. Presenting the trophy alerts the High Chieftain to the fallen beast's location, allowing gathering parties to quickly depart down into the plains to harvest Arra'chea's thick hide and rich meat for the fledgling capital.

item:horn-of-awakening.text: Horn of Awakening. The Horn of Awakening is a sounding instrument kept in a chest by Kerlonian Evershade in southern Darkshore. It is used to rouse the drowsy druid whenever he collapses into a slumber on the road to Ashenvale. Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw recently awoken from centuries inside the Emerald Dream, finds himself persistently lethargic in the waking realm. Journeying south toward Maestra's Post, he entrusts this horn to travelers willing to escort him. Whenever exhaustion overtakes him along the perilous wilderness trail, a clear blast from the instrument jolts his senses, prodding him back to his feet before wild beasts or cultists can seize upon his slumber.

item:horn-of-echeyakee.text: Horn of Echeyakee. The Horn of Echeyakee is a hunting instrument provided by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. Sounding it among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement calls forth Whitemist, the legendary white predator of the Barrens. Given to initiates testing their prowess in the hunt, the horn's call echoes across the savannah to summon Echeyakee, whose name translates from Taur-ahe as 'Whitemist.' Known as the king of the savannah cats, Echeyakee is revered by tauren hunters as both mercy and death, striking so swiftly that his quarry feels neither terror nor suffering. The horn is meant to be sounded only at the great predator's lair, a sun-bleached nest of giant kodo bones tucked behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

item:huge-gnoll-claw.text: Huge Gnoll Claw. The Huge Gnoll Claw is an unmistakable trophy taken from Hogger, the massive gnoll prowling southwestern Elwynn Forest. Sized far beyond any normal gnoll talon, it serves as the official proof of demise required by the Stormwind authorities in Goldshire. For months, the brute Hogger has terrorized the southern woodlands of Forest's Edge, shrugging off patrols and overwhelming every effort by the local garrison to corral or subdue him. Outmatched and stretched thin across Elwynn, the Stormwind Army posted an open bounty on the beast's head. Marshal Dughan at Goldshire demands undeniable evidence before disbursing the reward funds, and the brute's oversized claw offers undisputed confirmation that the terror of the woods has finally fallen.

item:humbert-s-sword.text: Humbert's Sword. Humbert's Sword is the personal sidearm belonging to Deathguard Humbert of Tarren Mill. The weapon was looted from his camp by dwarven soldiers while he was scouting their stronghold at Dun Garok. Deathguard Humbert was dispatched by High Executor Darthalia to monitor the dwarven presence at Dun Garok from a concealed position. While he left his post unattended one morning to collect firewood to boil water, dwarven patrols stumbled across his campsite and plundered all of his gear, including his personal blade. With so many dwarves to search, Humbert relies on Horde agents to infiltrate the fortress and retrieve his lost weapon. Following the theft, Humbert's belongings were carried back behind the fortified barricades of Dun Garok. Because dwarven riflemen, mountaineers, and priests circulate supplies throughout the garrison, locating the specific thief requires searching among the defenders stationed within the stronghold's trenches and redoubts.

item:hyacinth-mushroom.text: Hyacinth Mushroom. Hyacinth Mushrooms are distinctive fungi found sprouting at the roots of trees throughout Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Prized by local night elf herbalists for their medicinal properties, they also happen to be favored food and forage for the mischievous grell and grellkin. Hyacinth Mushrooms grow abundantly across Shadowglen, flourishing in the damp shadows at the bases of trees, mossy stones, and the sprawling roots of Aldrassil. While useful in woodland remedies, they have also caught the attention of the corrupted grell, who frequently hoard them. When young night elf sentinels or trainees are afflicted by local venomous fauna—such as the spiders of Shadowthread Cave—these mushrooms serve as a core component in soothing draughts and antivenoms concocted by forest healers.

item:hypercapacitor-gizmo.text: Hypercapacitor Gizmo. The Hypercapacitor Gizmo is an eccentric piece of engineering recovered from the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. Once dangling from the neck of a caged beast in a ruined caravan, its true purpose remains a mystery even to the tinkerer who claims to own it. When centaur marauders ambushed a goblin caravan traveling through Thousand Needles, they plundered nearly everything in sight. The sole survivor, Wizlo Bearingshiner, managed to crawl his way to safety at Whitereach Post, leaving behind his best gizmo: the Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Strangely, the gadget wound up secured around the neck of a ferocious, enraged panther locked inside a transport cage. The raiding centaur feared the beast enough to leave the cage entirely alone amidst the burning wreckage, unwittingly preserving Wizlo's odd machine. While Wizlo proudly calls the device his best gizmo, he admits upon its recovery that he has no real idea what it actually does. Like many goblin contraptions, the Hypercapacitor Gizmo is a tangled mass of ambition and volatile parts, destined to keep its owner occupied with endless tinkering rather than serving any practical, understood function.

item:ignition-key.text: Ignition Key. The Ignition Key is an essential control key carried by Supervisor Lugwizzle at the Venture Company's drilling operation in Sludge Fen. It is required to unlock the steering column and activate the controls of an advanced Venture Company shredder. When Sputtervalve of Ratchet dispatched an operative to steal a proprietary Venture Company shredder from Sludge Fen, things did not go smoothly. The undercover pilot, Wizzlecrank, managed to slip into the machine's cockpit only to find its movement column completely locked down. To keep suspicious foremen from catching on, he feigned mechanical troubles while awaiting an adventurer to retrieve the necessary Ignition Key. The key remains held under lock and key by Supervisor Lugwizzle high atop the central oil derrick, controlling access to the machine's state-of-the-art arm, speed, and rotation mechanisms.

item:ilkrud-magthrull-s-tome.text: Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome is a grimoire recovered from a dangerous orc warlock residing within the corrupted depths of Ashenvale. Brought to Delgren the Purifier, its foul contents reveal the broader dark dealings surrounding the cultists operating out of the Tower of Althalaxx. Ilkrud Magthrull is a formidable orc warlock entrenched at the Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, a site poisoned by lingering demonic influence. Surrounded by summoned minions, Magthrull recorded his foul rituals and shadowy communications within this personal tome. While the Argent Dawn paladin Delgren the Purifier had long known of the warlock's presence, the uncovered links between Magthrull and the dark cultists gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx made recovering the book an urgent priority.

item:incantations-from-the-nether.text: Incantations from the Nether. Incantations from the Nether is a grimoire of demonic magic held by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar. Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to claim the tome to harness its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. Beneath the red stone streets of Orgrimmar, the Searing Blade—a subterranean sect tied to the Shadow Council—operates in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. Among their darkest treasures is the Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook laden with demonic rites bestowed by agents of the Burning Legion. While the cultists use its vile secrets to plot treason within the Orcish capital, word of the text reached far across the sea to the royal quarters of Undercity.

item:incendia-agave.text: Incendia Agave. Incendia Agave is a rare, spiky aquatic plant native to the Boiling Pool beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. When enchanted by a skilled shaman, its unique properties allow it to kindle the sacred fire of life. Growing beneath and around the waters of the Boiling Pool in Thousand Needles, Incendia Agave thrives directly in the shadow of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Guarded naturally by wandering steam elementals, the plant is difficult to harvest and scarce across Kalimdor. Despite growing submerged in water, it contains potent natural elements that lend themselves directly to rituals of flame.

item:incendia-powder.text: Incendia Powder. Incendia Powder is an enchanted ritual catalyst refined to ignite sacred flames. Carried by Horde emissaries into Thousand Needles, the powder is specifically treated with shamanic incantations to invoke the slumbering spirit-beast Arikara atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Incendia Powder is no mundane explosive or mundane flash powder; it is a purified, ritualistic substance carefully infused with shamanic magic. Enchanted and entrusted to travelers by Magatha Grimtotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise, the mixture is designed to react solely with the dormant sacred fire of life atop the isolated spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Once scattered across the consecrated brazier where the dead are laid to rest, its alchemical and spiritual warding calls forth the vengeful winged serpent Arikara.

item:insane-scribbles.text: Insane Scribbles. Torn from the baffling Twilight Tome, these Insane Scribbles are a fragment of dark literature carried by cultists in Darkshore. Merely looking at the dancing text and distorted scrollwork induces severe dizziness and mental strain. Ancient protectors of the forest study such fragments to decipher the sinister motives of the Twilight's Hammer. Gazing upon the pages of the Twilight Tome proves profoundly hazardous to mortal sanity. The script writhes across the parchment, while graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque, unsettling imagery before the reader's eyes. Tearing loose even a single sheet—these Insane Scribbles—is an ordeal that leaves the bearer lightheaded and disoriented. Despite the chaotic incoherence of the script, the parchment hums with a primal, deeply ancient magic tied directly to dark powers long buried beneath Azeroth.

item:inscribed-bark.text: Inscribed Bark. Inscribed Bark is a living parchment entrusted by the ancient Oracle Tree to carry word of Teldrassil's state to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. It serves as an official report on the boughs of the World Tree and the lingering threats troubling its woods. Carved from the sacred wood of the Oracle Tree, this inscribed bark acts as a direct communique between the ancient guardian and the leadership of the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After adventurers suppress the encroaching harpies in the glades, the Oracle Tree entrusts them with this token, reluctant to risk ordinary couriers through the tainted paths of the boughs. The inscribed message informs Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of both recent victories and the deeper, unsettling blight that continues to grip Teldrassil.

item:intact-raptor-horn.text: Intact Raptor Horn. An intact horn harvested from the predatory raptors stalking the savannas of the Barrens. Kept in pristine condition, it is coveted by an entrepreneurial goblin looking to tap into rumors of raptor intelligence. While common hunters value raptor parts for hides, talons, and trophies, unbroken horns are harder to come by in the field. In the port town of Ratchet, an eccentric goblin alchemist named Mebok Mizzyrix has formulated a wild theory regarding local wildlife: because the raptors of the Barrens display cunning beyond their kin elsewhere, he suspects their intellect resides directly within their headgear. By grinding whole horns down and brewing them into tonic concoctions, Mebok aims to bottle this perceived genius into commercial 'smart drinks.' Pristine horns cannot simply be chipped off any juvenile beast. To yield viable material for brewing, hunters must take them from particularly vicious predators, such as the Sunscale Scytheclaws that prowl the southern plains and the northern borders near Ashenvale. Notable legendary terrors of the veldt, such as Takk the Leaper and the elusive Ishamuhale, also bear horns stout enough to survive the clash of the hunt intact.

item:intrepid-strongbox-key.text: Intrepid Strongbox Key. The Intrepid Strongbox Key is a rusted iron key once guarded jealously by Captain Halyndor, commander of the doomed Alliance vessel Intrepid. Even in undeath, the captain clutches it, keeping locked away the cursed artifact that brought ruin to his crew off the coast of the Wetlands. During the wreck of the Third Fleet off the stormy shores of the Wetlands, the warship Intrepid was cast into ruin, its crew twisted into restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor obsessively watched over a mysterious item stowed inside the vessel's heavy strongbox. In death, his spectral figure continues to prowl the waterlogged deck, refusing to relinquish the rusted key that unlocks the hold's deepest, darkest cargo.

item:invisibility-liquor.text: Invisibility Liquor. Invisibility Liquor is a potent, alchemically infused brew crafted using rare Crystal Kelp Fronds found in Elwynn Forest. Designed to render its drinker unseen for a brief window, it serves as the linchpin in a clandestine plot allowing two star-crossed young lovers to bypass their feuding families. The ongoing feud between the Stonefields and the Maclures makes peaceful contact between their households nearly impossible. When young Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks to meet with Maybell Maclure away from the watchful eyes of their kin, conventional secrecy falls short. Invisibility Liquor provides an uncanny solution: an alcoholic draught that bends sight around the imbiber, granting just enough stealth to slip across disputed farmland undetected.

item:iron-pike.text: Iron Pike. Iron Pikes are sturdy construction materials originally shipped from Stormwind to aid in repairing the Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire.
