The shipment was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short on essential rebuilding supplies. When Lakeshire faced recent attacks from the Blackrock orcs, the town's metal reserves were melted down to forge armor, blades, and ammunition for defense. In response to the shortage, local builders requested a resupply shipment of iron from Stormwind City. Before the materials could reach the town, a pack of Redridge gnolls hijacked the transport caravan along the road. The gnolls dragged crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, halting critical repairs on the Everstill Bridge. Foreman Oslow, charged with overseeing the reconstruction of the Everstill Bridge, relies on adventurers to enter gnoll territory and reclaim the pilfered hardware. Without these heavy iron pikes to reinforce the stone and timber framework, Lakeshire remains partially severed from the northern roadway and vulnerable to further incursions.

item:iron-pommel.text: Iron Pommel. The Iron Pommel is the final missing fragment of Dartol's Rod, a rod created by the long-dead wizard Dartol and sought by the night elves of Astranaar to slow the furbolg attacks on their people. Entrusted to the druids of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den for safekeeping, it was lost when their sanctuary was slaughtered and overrun by oozes. Dartol's Rod was divided and scattered across Ashenvale to protect its mystic power. The Iron Pommel was placed into the care of the night elf druids dwelling near the road winding south toward the Barrens. Tragedy struck the secluded enclave at the Dor'Danil Barrow Den when the circle was massacred, their tranquil shelter falling into ruined silence. The pommel vanished into the aftermath, swallowed by the grotesque, bubbling oozes that now shamble through the defiled glade.

item:iron-rivet.text: Iron Rivet. Iron Rivets are sturdy construction fasteners manufactured in Stormwind to help rebuild the ruined Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire. After a supply caravan was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, these heavy metal components ended up scattered across the gnoll camps in the northern hills. When Lakeshire faced repeated assaults from the Blackrock orcs, the town council was forced to melt down their structural iron reserves to forge urgent weapons, armor, and munitions. Once the immediate crisis subsided, Foreman Oslow requested fresh building supplies from Stormwind to mend the fractured Everstill Bridge. However, the supply caravan ferrying the shipment was ambushed by local Redridge gnolls before reaching the town. The pack beasts and wagons were dragged into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering essential construction materials like iron rivets and pikes among the gnoll packs. Without these heavy iron rivets, structural repairs on the Everstill Bridge cannot proceed safely. The stone and timber framework spanning the lake requires reinforced metal fasteners to withstand the weight of carts and travelers. Recovering the rivets directly from the gnoll camps is essential for restoring Lakeshire's vital link to the western valleys and securing the town's perimeter against further incursions.

item:iron-shaft.text: Iron Shaft. The Iron Shaft is a metallic segment of Dartol's Rod, a relic Raene Wolfrunner's friend Teronis sought in hopes of slowing the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Recovered from a locked chest near the border of Felwood, it serves as a crucial component in restoring the relic for the defenders of Ashenvale. Dartol's Rod was the creation of Dartol, and its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale; one was even given to the druids of Dor'Danil for safekeeping. The Iron Shaft represents the sturdy metal core of the instrument, secured away inside a locked chest in a secluded glade near the northern border of Ashenvale, not far from the tainted realm of Felwood.

item:ironband-s-progress-report.text: Ironband's Progress Report. Ironband's Progress Report is a written dispatch detailing the troubles facing Prospector Ironband's excavation site in eastern Loch Modan. It conveys both an account of slow digging hindered by aggressive troggs and an urgent plea for more blastpowder. Prospector Ironband's excavation in Loch Modan faces continuous disruption from local troggs. To keep the project moving forward, Ironband compiled this progress report to restate his desperate need for blastpowder. Carried first to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar and then forwarded to the Assembly of Explorers in Ironforge, the report documents the site's stalls while requesting heavy munitions. The dispatch quickly raises eyebrows among league leadership, as an ample supply of blastpowder was dispatched to Ironband weeks prior, leaving superiors wondering where the previous shipments vanished.

item:ishamuhale-s-fang.text: Ishamuhale's Fang. Ishamuhale's Fang is a hunting trophy taken from Ishamuhale, the notorious sunscale raptor known as Speartooth in the Barrens. Brought to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the tooth serves as proof of besting one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Ishamuhale is feared across the central savanna as the fiercest sunscale raptor alive, an apex hunter said to kill purely out of predatory passion rather than mere hunger. Lured into the open with fresh zhevra meat beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet, the beast offers no quarter. Severing its massive fang proves to the hunting instructors of the Horde that a traveler has conquered not just a beast, but the sheer savagery of the plains.

item:ivar-s-head.text: Ivar's Head. Ivar's Head is the gruesome proof of the destruction of the ravenous ghoul Ivar the Foul in Silverpine Forest. It is sought by the Deathstalker Rane Yorick to ensure safe recovery for her wounded brother Quinn. While scouting northern Silverpine Forest on the orders of High Executor Hadrec, the Forsaken Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were ambushed at an abandoned farmstead by a feral ghoul known as Ivar the Foul. Though the siblings managed to fend off the fiend, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Stranded at the ruined farm while her brother recovered, Rane could not safely leave Quinn unattended to complete their mission. Severing Ivar's head provides definitive proof that the beast will never terrorize the estate again, granting Quinn the necessary time to recuperate under Rane's watchful eye.

item:iverron-s-antidote-item.text: Iverron's Antidote (item). Iverron's Antidote is a delicate medicinal draught concocted by Dirania Silvershine in Shadowglen. Specially brewed to neutralize the lethal venom of the local Webwood spiders, the mixture is highly unstable and spoils rapidly once prepared. Crafted by Dirania Silvershine in Aldrassil, this antidote is formulated to counteract the potent venom afflicting the young night elf Iverron. Due to the volatile nature of its ingredients and herbal catalysts, the draught possesses an exceptionally short shelf life, remaining viable for only five minutes after brewing. Courier messengers must sprint north toward the Webwood cave without delay to deliver the concoction before it degrades into useless slurry.

item:jade-phial.text: Jade Phial. The Jade Phial is a specially crafted vessel provided by the night elf druid Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It is designed to safely draw and transport sacred water from Teldrassil's moonwells to replenish the druids' central well in Darnassus. Teldrassil is dotted with moonwells that channel lunar and natural energies vital to night elf society and druidic worship. As part of maintaining this harmony, the central moonwell used by the druids in Darnassus must periodically be replenished from the outlying wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts young initiates with the Jade Phial, a receptacle carefully prepared to gather pure waters from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village without disturbing its delicate spiritual potency.

item:jennea-s-flask.text: Jennea's Flask. Jennea's Flask is an empty vessel given to aspiring mages by the wizard Jennea Cannon in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. It is used to collect a water sample from Mirror Lake to study disturbances in the local ley lines. Following the cataclysmic magical struggles across Azeroth, the natural flow of arcane currents has torn loose from its ancient channels. In Stormwind, Jennea Cannon seeks to understand how deeply these mystical shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She provides this simple glass flask to promising apprentices, sending them southwest of the capital's gates to draw fresh water from the base of the waterfall at Mirror Lake. Once filled, the container protects the delicate sample so it can be brought back to the Wizard's Sanctum intact for arcane analysis. The primary concern driving the use of the flask is public safety. If fluctuating ley lines begin to seep magical taint into Mirror Lake, the surrounding ecosystem and anyone drinking from its waters could suffer strange or harmful afflictions. Collecting a pristine sample in Jennea's flask allows the mages of Stormwind to detect invisible magical residue before tainted currents can spread undetected throughout the countryside.

item:jitters-completed-journal.text: Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters' Completed Journal is a handwritten account detailing the grim tragedies of Duskwood, specifically the massacre at Sven Yorgen's farm. Fearing vengeance, the reclusive Jitters surrenders the finished text to clear his name and shed light on the sinister forces haunting the region.

item:johaan-s-findings.text: Johaan's Findings. Johaan's Findings is a bundle of research documents penned by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Entrusted to a courier heading south, these notes convey recent alchemical developments in Tirisfal Glades to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher. The Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from Lady Sylvanas Windrunner to engineer a New Plague capable of destroying both the living and the Scourge. Because researchers are scattered across Lordaeron's contested ruins, maintaining a flow of data between outposts is vital. Apothecary Johaan compiles his local testing notes in Brill and dispatches them southward to Apothecary Renferrel, who directs society efforts from the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. These records represent one small piece of the Society's collective effort to hone their lethal brews.

item:johaan-s-special-drink.text: Johaan's Special Drink. Johaan's Special Drink is a lethal concoction prepared by Apothecary Johaan in the village of Brill. Disguised as a common refreshment, the mixture serves as a field test for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing plague. Brewed in the brewing cauldrons of Brill, Johaan's Special Drink is far from a tavern beverage. Apothecary Johaan concocts the draft by refining various venomous components and local reagents into a single draught, tailored specifically to test virulence against living physiology. Handed over under the guise of slaking a captive's thirst, it represents the Forsaken apothecaries' ongoing ambition to engineer a weapon potent enough to fulfill Sylvanas Windrunner's designs for Azeroth.

item:jordan-s-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Ore Shipment. Jordan's Ore Shipment is a crate of ore that Bailor Stonehand was to turn into his alloy for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Carried by caravan from the Wetlands, the delivery was intercepted and looted by Mo'grosh ogres in the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Meant to be refined by the dwarf Bailor Stonehand into his special alloy, this ore was originally promised to Jordan Stilwell for his metalwork. While crossing south through the mountains from the Wetlands into Loch Modan, the supply caravan was violently ambushed by the Mo'grosh ogres. The shipment was dragged into the ogres' wilderness stronghold, leaving the surviving guards to perish from their wounds and halting Jordan's smithing project until an adventurer can pry it back from the brutes.

item:jordan-s-refined-ore-shipment.text: Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment. Jordan's Refined Ore Shipment is a crate of high-grade metal prepared specifically for the smith Jordan Stilwell. Acquired as part of a paladin's sacred trials, it provides the essential stock needed to forge a holy weapon of virtue. When Jordan Stilwell set out to forge a weapon worthy of a dedicated paladin, ordinary stock would not suffice. The blacksmith required an assortment of rare and exacting components: a Purified Kor Gem, sturdy Whitestone Oak lumber, his own lost smithing hammer, and a specialized shipment of refined ore. This consignment represents the metal foundation for that sacred labor, brought to Ironforge to complete the Test of Righteousness.

item:jordan-s-smithing-hammer.text: Jordan's Smithing Hammer. Jordan's Smithing Hammer is a cherished family heirloom passed down to the human blacksmith Jordan Stilwell by his father. Its recovery from the haunted halls of Shadowfang Keep is essential for forging a holy weapon consecrated to the Light. To an ordinary observer, Jordan's Smithing Hammer might seem like mere smith's iron, but to Jordan Stilwell, it represents both heritage and destiny. Inherited from his father, this tool is central to Jordan's identity as a forge master outside Ironforge. Having somehow wound up within the forsaken stone walls of Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest, it must be reclaimed before Jordan can attempt his masterwork—a sacred weapon fit for a holy champion.

item:kadrak-s-flag.text: Kadrak's Flag. Kadrak's Flag is an emblem of the Horde given by the scout Kadrak at the border between the Barrens and Ashenvale. It serves as an unmistakable warning to the night elves and dryads of Stonetalon Peak, planted directly in the Talon Den after the elimination of Keymaster Rynthariel. Tensions run high along the borders of Kalimdor, where Alliance messengers and sentinels routinely test the boundaries of Horde-held territories. When a decoded scroll reveals communications from the dryad Rynthariel, Keymaster of the Talon Den, Kadrak determines that killing her is not enough. He provides this crimson banner to be planted deep within the Den upon the peak of Stonetalon. By staking the Horde's colors inside one of the night elves' sacred mountain redoubts, Kadrak intends to send a clear message: incursions across the Barrens will be answered with bold retaliation on Alliance soil.

item:keg-of-shindigger-stout.text: Keg of Shindigger Stout. A Keg of Shindigger Stout is a barrel of potent dwarven ale brewed and guarded by the riflemen and soldiers garrisoned within Dun Garok. Desired by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves not as an evening drink, but as a deceitful delivery vehicle for newly synthesized plagues. Dun Garok stands as a formidable dwarven bastion in the southeastern Hillsbrad Foothills, fiercely maintained by the dwarves of Ironforge. Within its entrenched barracks and mess halls, the stout-hearted defenders share barrels of Shindigger Stout to weather the cold and the grinding siege against regional enemies. The brew is robust and plentiful, making it a staple of the garrison's day-to-day survival.

item:ken-zigla-s-draught.text: Ken'zigla's Draught. Ken'zigla's Draught is a potent, foul-tasting medicinal tonic prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains. It is formulated to restore enough strength to critically wounded individuals so they can move without bleeding out. Prepared by Ken'zigla in the Stonetalon Mountains, this potent brew serves as an emergency restorative for those on the verge of death. The tonic is extremely strong and must be measured carefully; drinking more than half a dose at once risks causing the patient to bleed out as their circulation surges. Administering half provides enough raw vigor to move and flee imminent danger, while the remainder must wait until the body stabilizes after a full night's rest.

item:khazgorm-s-journal.text: Khazgorm's Journal. Khazgorm's Journal is a personal field ledger kept by Prospector Khazgorm, the leader of the Ironforge dwarven excavation at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. It details the intrusive activities of the Explorers' League upon lands claimed by the Stonespire tauren tribe. The journal belongs to Prospector Khazgorm, who directs the heavy machinery and blasting operations carving out the southern Barrens hillsides. Far from the idyllic search for knowledge professed by the Explorers' League, the notes reflect a relentless campaign of excavation that displaced the Stonespire tribe. Attempts by the tauren to reach a peaceful resolution were rebuffed, making the journal a prized prize of war for Gann Stonespire as he seeks to understand and dismantle the dwarf presence in his homeland.

item:klaven-mortwake-s-journal.text: Klaven Mortwake's Journal. Klaven Mortwake's Journal is an intelligence report recovered by SI:7 operatives from the Defias tower in northeastern Westfall. Kept secured inside a chest shipped out of Duskwood, it details the Brotherhood's covert attempts to brew alchemical concoctions capable of reanimating the dead. Master Mathias Shaw, leader of Stormwind's intelligence service, prioritized the recovery of Mortwake's journal to piece together the Brotherhood's wider web of alliances. The notes confirm not only dark experiments in reanimation but also the illicit logistical support connecting Duskwood, the Venture Company, and the Defias. For rogue operatives in service to the crown, the recovery of this dark research marks the pivotal transition into mastering the art of poisons.

item:kodo-horn.text: Kodo Horn. Kodo Horns are sturdy natural reagents taken from the beasts that roam the northern reaches of the Barrens. To the Cenarion druids, their dense composition provides the necessary strength and potency for experimental herbal mixtures, most notably in crafting curative salves to treat poisoned wildlife. While kodos are revered throughout the Barrens by the tauren for their endurance and strength, their horns carry practical medicinal value. Tonga Runetotem, working from the Crossroads, employs complete horns to reinforce the potency of his herbal remedies. Chips and fragments do not suffice for refining these salves; only intact horns gathered from the mature kodos wandering the arid plains hold enough strength to anchor the cure.

item:kodo-liver.text: Kodo Liver. A Kodo Liver is a hefty organ harvested from the massive kodos roaming the plains of the Barrens. While hardly standard culinary fare, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet requires it as a vital ingredient for fermenting an unorthodox trogg ale learned from the wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout. The great kodos of the Barrens are primarily hunted by the tauren and wandering predators for their tough hides and nourishing meat. However, a fresh kodo liver serves a much more eccentric purpose in the port town of Ratchet. Brewmaster Drohn uses the organ alongside thunderhawk saliva glands and lightning glands to recreate a potent brew Chen Stormstout taught him: trogg ale. Drohn claims this unusual blend possesses a formidable kick, providing adventurous travelers with a hearty concoction straight from the wilds of central Kalimdor.

item:kodobane-s-head.text: Kodobane's Head. Kodobane's Head is the severed head of Barak Kodobane, a cunning Kolkar centaur chieftain. Taken as proof of his demise, it is brought to the orc warlord Regthar Deathgate to show that the centaur threat near the Forgotten Pools has been broken. The Kolkar centaur of the Barrens have historically been a fractured, disorganized nuisance, yet the rise of ambitious warlords threatens to unite their marauding bands into an army. Barak Kodobane established his encampment at the lush waters of the Forgotten Pools, cutting off vital oasis resources and raiding nearby paths. Regthar Deathgate, stationed in a bunker west of the Crossroads, demands his severed head as undeniable proof that this commander can no longer rally his brutal kin against the Horde.

item:kravel-s-crate.text: Kravel's Crate. Kravel's Crate is a heavy package dispatched by Kravel Koalbeard from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. Destined for the Nesingwary expedition in Stranglethorn Vale, it contains specialized hunting ammunition designed to bring down the jungle's deadliest game. Handed out by the shrewd entrepreneur Kravel Koalbeard at the Mirage Raceway, Kravel's Crate represents an unfinished business transaction across continents. Ordered weeks prior by a wealthy dwarven patron, the shipment was delayed long enough for its buyer to depart Kalimdor entirely. Rather than lose out on the favor of a wealthy customer who already paid for forwarding, Kravel entrusts passing adventurers to haul the crate all the way to northern Stranglethorn Vale. Despite its nondescript appearance and the crust of salt dust it gathers in the Shimmering Flats, the crate carries lethal cargo: heavy, special-gauge ammunition tailored specifically for hunting rifles. When received at the expedition camp north of Grom'gol, the recipient notes that the potent rounds are prized by big-game hunters and vital for survival against the predators roaming the jungle canopy.

item:kreenig-snarlsnout-s-tusk.text: Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk. Kreenig Snarlsnout's Tusk is a gruesome hunting trophy taken from the leader of the Razormane quilboar raiders in the northern Barrens. Severing the tusk serves as indisputable proof for Thork at the Crossroads that the menace targeting Horde supply lines has been put down. The supply caravans traveling west from Durotar into the Barrens face constant harassment, but recent attacks grew increasingly brazen under the orchestration of a fierce Razormane leader named Kreenig Snarlsnout. To cripple the quilboars' coordination, Thork—commander of the Crossroads watch—ordered Snarlsnout eliminated. Taking the chieftain's tusk not only offers concrete proof that the raider has fallen, but serves as a deliberate insult to the Razormane tribe, shattering their resolve and leaving their fighters without central direction.

item:kuz-s-skull.text: Kuz's Skull. Kuz's Skull is the severed head of Kuz, a prominent Razormane quilboar raider in the southern Barrens. Brought forward from Razorfen Kraul, Kuz helped orchestrate violent raids against Horde outposts before being targeted for death by a captive former kin. The plains of the southern Barrens crawl with the Razormane tribe, but their organized aggression stems from specific leaders sent directly out of Razorfen Kraul. Kuz, alongside Nak and their ruthless chieftain Lok Orcbane, coordinated brutal incursions against travelers and settlements like the Crossroads. However, their internal treachery proved their undoing. Having betrayed their fellow quilboar Mangletooth and left him to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo, they made a vengeful enemy. Mangletooth bartered Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to sever the raider's head and end his raids for good.

item:laced-pumpkin.text: Laced Pumpkin. A Laced Pumpkin is an ordinary gourd treated with a lethal concoction developed by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Handed to a starving, imprisoned Scarlet Crusader under the guise of sustenance, it serves as a live field test for the Forsaken's growing arsenal of alchemical weapons. To the untrained eye, the laced pumpkin appears to be ordinary produce salvaged from the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Under the supervision of Apothecary Johaan in Brill, however, the vegetable is treated with experimental toxins designed to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks new weapons to repel both the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south, turning even simple harvest goods into vectors for infection and chemical death.

item:laird-s-response.text: Laird's Response. Laird's Response is a sealed dispatch penned by the fish curer Laird in the coastal port of Auberdine. Written for Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village, the letter details curious ecological differences between mainland marine life and the unusually large fish thriving along Teldrassil's shores. After reviewing catch reports from across the Veiled Sea, Laird of Auberdine noted a striking discrepancy: the fish hauled from Teldrassil's coast are remarkably larger and more plentiful than those taken along the mainland beaches of Darkshore. In this written response addressed to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird shares his working theory—that the unnatural presence and raw vitality of the newly planted World Tree may be warping and stimulating the surrounding marine life. Delivered by travelers returning across the waters, the letter prompts wonder and quiet curiosity among the fisherfolk of Rut'theran Village.

item:lake-creeper-moss.text: Lake Creeper Moss. Lake Creeper Moss is an organic compound harvested from the aquatic creepers dwelling among the Dawning Isles in Lake Lordamere. It serves as a vital reagent sought by the Royal Apothecary Society for their efforts to engineer a lethal new plague. Grown along the hides of the vicious freshwater beasts that prowl the southern Dawning Isles of Lake Lordamere, Lake Creeper Moss carries unique properties shaped by Lordaeron's blighted waters. Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, documented it in his journal, noting that the moss resembled trace materials on the fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. When recovered by Forsaken agents, samples are dispatched directly to the Apothecarium in the Undercity to fuel Master Apothecary Faranell's dark research.

item:lake-skulker-moss.text: Lake Skulker Moss. Lake Skulker Moss is a biological reagent gathered from the bog beasts inhabiting the northern reaches of Lake Lordamere. It was identified by Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, as a key organic component for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into brewing a New Plague. Harvested from the mossy bodies of Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles, this damp aquatic moss possesses properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard meticulously cataloged the flora and fauna of eastern Silverpine Forest, concluding in his journal that both Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could serve as stabilizing or reactive agents. After Berard became a mindless servant of Arugal, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel, who instructed Forsaken champions to gather moss samples alongside a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs, delivering them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

item:large-candle.text: Large Candle. Large Candles are wax tapers prized and carried by kobolds delving into the mines of Elwynn Forest. Mounted atop their heads, these crude lights provide visibility in subterranean tunnels and serve as a reliable source of raw wax for human apothecaries. Kobolds tunneling beneath Elwynn Forest depend upon candle flame to navigate pitch-black subterranean shafts, affixing wax tapers directly to their heads. Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend their candles fiercely against interlopers. Despite their crude manufacture, the large candles carried deep inside Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine contain valuable wax that surface tradesmen cannot easily produce in bulk, turning an everyday monster tool into an alchemical commodity. William Pestle, an apothecary operative hailing from Stormwind City, gathers these oversized candles at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. Seeking rendered wax for the concoctions, balms, and ointments prepared by his family apothecary, Pestle employs passing adventurers to clear the infested mines and strip the candles from the subterranean invaders.

item:large-soran-ruk-fragment.text: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. The Large Soran'ruk Fragment is a sizable remnant of an ancient artifact bound with demonic energy. Originally housing the spirit of a disgraced Burning Legion demon, this shard found its way into the hands of sinister spellcasters within the haunted walls of Shadowfang Keep. When demons of the Burning Legion fall out of favor with their dark masters, their spirits are sometimes condemned to imprisonment within enchanted orbs. These vessels are subsequently distributed among mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion, who draw upon the potent fel forces trapped within. Even when shattered into fragments, the lingering essence of the bound fiend still radiates power, making each piece a prize for ambitious practitioners of shadow magic. The orb of Soran'ruk was long ago cracked into two halves. While one portion was fractured further and dispersed among cultists elsewhere, the larger half was claimed by a sorcerer dwelling within the cursed stronghold of Shadowfang Keep. There, carried among the sinister Shadowfang Darksouls, the Large Soran'ruk Fragment channels demonic power until sought out by those hoping to reforge the ancient vessel.

item:laughing-sister-s-hair.text: Laughing Sister's Hair. Laughing Sister's Hair consists of soft, magical locks harvested from dryads residing in the enchanted forests of Ashenvale. Highly sought after by skilled weavers, these strands possess innate mystical properties ideal for crafting fine robes. Harvested from the dryads known as laughing sisters near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, this hair holds remarkable natural magic. While dryads are sacred woodland protectors linked to Cenarius and the night elves, craftsmen within the Horde value their hair purely as a potent crafting reagent. The troll tailor Kil'hala at the Crossroads spins these gathered locks into enchanted vestments for burgeoning practitioners of the arcane.

item:legacy-of-the-aspects.text: Legacy of the Aspects. Legacy of the Aspects is an ancient tome hidden deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale. Retrieved during a Horde trial of the intellect, the volume contains essential lore concerning the Great Aspects that shaped ancient Azeroth. While earlier trials set forth by tauren elders test physical endurance and resolve, the pursuit of Legacy of the Aspects is designed to challenge the mind. Tasked by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, an aspirant must delve into the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil. Guarded by the restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them, the ancient text rests upon a stone pedestal. Claiming the volume is only the first step; the seeker must commit its contents to memory before relinquishing the book, as they are tested on its historical lessons.

item:letter-to-delgren.text: Letter to Delgren. The Letter to Delgren is an urgent missive penned by Balthule Shadowstrike near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. Addressed to his mentor, the paladin Delgren the Purifier, it details the sinister operations of the demonic Dark Strand cult. Delivering it carries vital intelligence southward to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. As cultists of the Dark Strand gather around the ruins of the Tower of Althalaxx, the night elf Balthule Shadowstrike keeps watch over their escalating malice. Lacking the martial might to eradicate the cult alone, Balthule drafts this dispatch to request aid from his tutor in the Holy Light, Delgren the Purifier. Because the cult's foul rites threaten more than just Darkshore's coastline, the message must be carried the entire length of the region into western Ashenvale, where Delgren works in concert with night elf Sentinels to hunt down demonic and undead threats.

item:letter-to-jin-zil.text: Letter to Jin'Zil. The Letter to Jin'Zil is a piece of correspondence penned by the orc Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads. Entrusted to an adventurer after the defeat of Serena Bloodfeather, it bears word to the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil in the Stonetalon Mountains that the northern Barrens have been purged of the Bloodfeather threat. Following the eradication of the harpy infestation at the Dry Hills and the slaying of Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok Swiftdagger drafts this missive to an old comrade. Recognizing that the harpies of the Barrens originally roosted within the peaks of Stonetalon Mountains, Darsok uses the dispatch to introduce a promising warrior to the wider frontier while notifying the witch doctor Jin'Zil that the harpy matron has fallen.

item:letter-to-jorgen.text: Letter to Jorgen. The Letter to Jorgen is a confidential missive drafted to enlist an old contact in Stormwind City. It serves as an operative's introduction during the early stages of an inquiry into a high-level diplomatic disappearance. When a high-ranking diplomat bound for Theramore failed to arrive for scheduled talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore, royal investigators scrambled to keep the incident quiet. While official agents began scouring the capital, alternative channels were quietly mobilized. This sealed letter was drafted to circumvent standard military bureaucracy, aimed specifically at Jorgen—a gruff veteran passing his days fishing beneath the colossal statues in the Valley of Heroes. The note calls upon old obligations, pulling an unwilling contact into a covert investigation touched by rumors of Defias conspiracy.

item:lewis-note.text: Lewis' Note. Lewis' Note is an urgent supply requisition penned by Quartermaster Lewis at Sentinel Hill. Carried by courier via gryphon flight, it requests vital shipments of protective gear from a private armorer in Stormwind's Old Town. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill operates on a shoestring budget, receiving little official support from the House of Nobles in Stormwind. Facing persistent skirmishes against the Defias Brotherhood, the garrison regularly burns through its meager stocks of gear. To keep the defenders outfitted, Quartermaster Lewis relies on private business arrangements rather than crown logistics. This requisition note bypasses official military channels entirely, tasking an Alliance courier to fly by gryphon to Old Town and present the order directly to Osric Strang, proprietor of the shop Limited Immunity.

item:lightning-gland.text: Lightning Gland. Lightning Glands are harvested from stormhide beasts roaming the plains of the Barrens. Imbued with natural elemental charge, they are sought by Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet to brew a fiery, potent trogg ale learned from the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. The savannas of the Barrens host a variety of elemental-touched predators, including the stormhides. Within their flesh lies the lightning gland, an organ pulsating with latent electrical energy. While hardly suitable for ordinary fare, these volatile glands are prized by eccentric brewers who appreciate a brew with a genuine sting. In the port town of Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn continues the brewing traditions imparted to him by Chen Stormstout. To concoct a potent brew known as trogg ale, Drohn requires five lightning glands alongside a thunderhawk saliva gland and a fresh kodo liver. The resulting draught carries an unmistakable kick that adventurers find both invigorating and potent.

item:logging-rope.text: Logging Rope. Logging Rope is heavy cordage vital to the Warsong clan's ongoing logging operations within Ashenvale. Shipments of this sturdy line were ambushed and stolen by local furbolg tribes who violently resist the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest. Maintaining the goblin-built machinery and lumber mills of the Warsong Lumber Camp requires massive quantities of durable logging line. Rather than reaching the loggers at their encampment, essential shipments were intercepted by the Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolg tribes. Driven mad by corruption and fiercely defensive of their ancestral woods, these furbolgs hoard the stolen ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale. Locke Okarr at Splintertree Post is tasked with recovering the misplaced logistical chain before the Warsong lumber camp grinds to a halt. Reclaiming the heavy rope directly from the furbolg den-mothers and warriors allows the Horde to secure fellable timber, bound logs, and rig saw machinery amidst constant guerrilla resistance from the native forest inhabitants.

item:lok-s-skull.text: Lok's Skull. Lok's Skull is the severed head of Lok Orcbane, a fierce Razormane warrior who led brutal quilboar raids against Horde supply routes in the southern Barrens. Sought after by the imprisoned quilboar Mangletooth as an act of vengeance, the skull serves as undeniable proof that the raiders' chieftain has fallen. Emerging from Razorfen Kraul into the southern Barrens, Lok Orcbane spearheaded aggressive Razormane quilboar assaults on Horde supply lines alongside his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying and abandoning Mangletooth to captivity in Camp Taurajo, Lok earned a grim reputation among orcish defenders who struggled to contain his ruthless raids. Claiming Lok's skull not only avenges the wronged captive who directs Horde champions to Lok's camp, but also shatters the core leadership driving the Razormane offensive.

item:lonebrow-s-journal.text: Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is a weathered diary found clutched in the skeletal remains of the dwarven explorer Henrig Lonebrow at the base of the Great Lift. Its pages detail the final grim journey of Lonebrow through the Barrens and point toward dangers lurking within Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow met an unfortunate end near the base of the Great Lift connecting the Barrens to Thousand Needles. Lying abandoned on a rocky ledge, his skeletal remains still grip this weathered journal. The diary serves as a testament to his final travels and directs whoever discovers it to bring word to the night elf druid Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, the border outpost leading into Feralas. Lonebrow's notes shed critical light on the quilboar menace brewing in the southern barrens.

item:lorgalis-manuscript.text: Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript is an ancient text tied to the worship and lore of the Old Gods, preserved from the fallen night elven ruins beneath Ashenvale. Hidden within the sunken temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps, it holds secrets coveted by dark scholars seeking to awaken ancient, slumbering powers. The Lorgalis Manuscript rests at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken ruins where long-dead elves once dwelt before their city fell. Written by one Lorgalis, it speaks of the Old Gods who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping, and it praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps. Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient entities that sleep deep beneath the world. Stored away in a pitted iron chest amidst the flooded corridors, it has drawn the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

item:lunar-fungus.text: Lunar Fungus. Lunar Fungus is a potent medicinal growth harvested from fungal blooms deep within Darkshore's cavern systems. Druid initiates collect these mushrooms alongside common herbs to brew a restorative salve capable of treating diseased wildlife. Harvested from Lunar Fungal Blooms, this distinctive fungus thrives in dark, subterranean caverns across Darkshore. The Cenarion Circle values it for its amplifying effects; when blended with a soothing water base and common Earthroot, the fungus provides the necessary potency to create an effective counteragent against debilitating afflictions. Because it grows primarily in damp underground spaces frequented by territorial moonkin, obtaining it requires careful navigation of the untamed wilderness. In Auberdine, Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to harvest Lunar Fungus as part of their studies into nature's restorative arts. By witnessing how physical reagents like this fungus counteract virulent poisons in the local deer, initiates learn the underlying principles of herbal remedies before advancing to channel natural antidotes directly through shapeshifting and raw spiritual power.

item:lurker-venom.text: Lurker Venom. Lurker Venom is a potent natural toxin harvested from the predatory spiders that prowl the rocky hills and woods of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders require this caustic venom as a key ingredient to prepare an alchemical neutralizing compound against Dark Iron sabotage. The hills and crags surrounding Loch Modan crawl with predatory arachnids—ranging from common wood lurkers to the infamous matriarch Shanda the Spinner. While their bites pose a constant hazard to mountaineers and travelers, the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk named their virulent poison as one ingredient of a disarming mixture, which Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. Combined with rare minerals and tears harvested from the loch's crocolisks, Lurker Venom forms a reactive solvent capable of disarming complex Dark Iron explosives.

item:lydon-s-toxin.text: Lydon's Toxin. Lydon's Toxin is an alchemical concoction synthesized by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to disrupt the Venture Company's deforestation in the Stonetalon Mountains. Entrusted to Horde adventurers, it is delivered to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff so she can devise an effective delivery mechanism. Developed by Apothecary Lydon in the Hillsbrad Foothills, this virulent compound is designed to combat the invasive Venture Company loggers despoiling the Stonetalon Mountains. According to Lydon, the concoction produces lethal and potentially contagious results upon contact. However, before the substance can be unleashed against the goblins' operations around the Windshear Crag, it must be ferried across continents to Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative in Thunder Bluff. Zamah requires the raw mixture to engineer a wide-dispersal apparatus—the Toxic Fogger—ensuring the brew wipes out the exploitative deforesters without needlessly endangering Horde assets.

item:macgrann-s-dried-meats.text: MacGrann's Dried Meats. MacGrann's Dried Meats are a month's worth of salted provisions prepared by the hunter Tundra MacGrann to survive the harsh Dun Morogh winter. Stored in a reinforced thorium meat locker, the entire cache was snatched by the ferocious yeti known as Old Icebeard. Life in the freezing crags of Dun Morogh demands careful planning. To prepare for the blizzards of the cold season, the dwarf hunter Tundra MacGrann spent weeks hunting game, salting the meat, and securing it inside a sturdy chest. Aware that scavenging bears and prowling predators routinely plague his homestead, MacGrann took no chances and locked his food supply away inside a thorium meat locker. Even with those precautions, he did not anticipate an intruder strong enough to carry away the entire chest rather than trying to pry it open on the spot. While MacGrann was away tracking deer, the notorious yeti Old Icebeard raided the hunter's camp and dragged the heavy chest back to his den in Chill Breeze Valley. Though the beast lacked the means to break through the solid thorium plating, MacGrann's injured leg left him unable to mount a swift rescue into the cavern. Without outside assistance to retrieve the cache before winter sets in, the stranded hunter faced starvation amidst the mountain snows.

item:mackreel-s-moonshine.text: MacKreel's Moonshine. MacKreel's Moonshine is a potent dwarven liquor brewed by Foggy MacKreel, stationed on the broken Thandol Span north of the Wetlands. Strong enough to knock out a sentry on duty, it is prized as far north as Southshore, where Brewmeister Bilger accepts it as payment for debts. Brewed by the guard Foggy MacKreel on the Thandol Span, this moonshine carries an infamous reputation for potency. Even hardened dwarven sentries find themselves laid low by a night with the brew, waking with headaches akin to a brigade of siege engines rolling overhead. Despite its punishing kick, it is highly valued for warming up travelers against the damp chills of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan. Foggy MacKreel ran up an unsettled debt with Brewmeister Bilger, the tavern keeper and master brewer of Southshore. In order to clear his tab, Foggy traded a batch of his moonshine instead of coin. Bilger gladly accepts the liquor in place of gold, eager to add MacKreel's potent brew to his stock for the chilly coastal days of the Hillsbrad Foothills.

item:maggot-eye-s-paw.text: Maggot Eye's Paw. Maggot Eye's Paw is the gruesome trophy taken from the gnoll chieftain Maggot Eye at Garren's Haunt. Carried back to Brill, it serves as physical proof of the beast's execution for grave-robbing on behalf of the Scourge. Maggot Eye earned the harsh wrath of the Forsaken by raiding graves and pillaging the countryside near Garren's Haunt, providing corpses to bolster the ranks of the Lich King's armies. In response, a formal death sentence and bounty were posted in the town of Brill. Because mere rumors of a death are never enough for military administrators like Executor Zygand, bounty hunters must sever the villain's paw and bring it back to town to collect their reward and close the bounty.

item:maggran-s-reserve-letter.text: Maggran's Reserve Letter. Maggran's Reserve Letter is an official dispatch written by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Carried across Kalimdor to the Great Lift, it grants a stationed sentry long-awaited relief so he may return home to visit his family. Maintaining outposts across the rugged expanse of Kalimdor demands vigilance, but the leaders of the Horde recognize that prolonged watch duty takes a heavy toll on morale. Penned by Maggran Earthbinder in the high crags of Sun Rock Retreat, this simple missive serves as official orders notifying Grish Longrunner that a replacement warrior has been dispatched to take over his post at the Great Lift. For a lonely guard watching over the towering wooden winches far to the south, the letter promises something rare in troubled times: an honorable leave of absence to reunite with family.

item:mangy-claw.text: Mangy Claw. The Mangy Claw is a severed claw taken from the great ice claw bear Mangeclaw in Dun Morogh. It serves as grim proof that the deadly beast responsible for killing a stranded dwarven pilot has finally been slain. When Pilot Hildelve's steam tank broke down in the frozen hills of Dun Morogh, he continued his search for ore on foot, only to face the mountain wilderness alone. As recorded in his recovered journal, Hildelve managed to fight off an initial attack by a monstrous ice claw bear named Mangeclaw, though he was savagely mauled in the struggle. The beast later returned to finish off the weakened pilot. Hildelve's final written entry pleaded for vengeance against the predator, a task fulfilled by taking the Mangy Claw from the fallen bear.

item:marshal-haggard-s-badge.text: Marshal Haggard's Badge. Marshal Haggard's Badge is a symbol of rank and authority once carried by Marshal Haggard during his service to the kingdom of Stormwind. After being stolen by the Defias bandit Dead-tooth Jack through trickery, the badge poses a dangerous threat as a tool for impersonating city officials. Though Marshal Haggard has long retired to his small farmstead in the hills of Elwynn Forest, his old Stormwind Marshal's badge still holds official weight. Under the cover of night, a Defias rogue named Dead-tooth Jack donned a Stormwind tabard and posed as Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander. Tricked into believing his former peers required the insignia for official business, the aging Haggard handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before the retired officer realized the ruse. In the hands of the Defias Brotherhood, such an emblem of Stormwind authority could allow outlaws to slip past checkpoints or sow confusion among local patrols.

item:mary-s-looking-glass.text: Mary's Looking Glass. Mary's Looking Glass is a discarded hand mirror once treasured by Blind Mary before tragedy claimed her sight and life. Abandoned in the haunted groves of Duskwood, it was scavenged by a roving ghoul before being sought out to complete Viktori Prism'Antras's telescope. Before her terrible fate, Blind Mary treasured this polished looking glass. After her death and the loss of her eyes, looking upon her reflection became an agonizing reminder of what she had lost. She cast the mirror away behind her barn, leaving it to the encroaching gloom of Duskwood. There it fell into the clutching claws of an Insane Ghoul that wandered the ruined outskirts, carrying the trinket south into the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. In Darkshire, the eccentric stargazer Viktori Prism'Antras dreamed of peering through Duskwood's eternal twilight toward the pristine heavens above. Building his telescope required specialized optical lenses and reflective glass. Learning of his need, Mary directed adventurers to hunt down the feral undead prowling the cemetery's ruined chapel, reclaiming the looking glass to serve as an optical reflector in his grand star-viewing machine.

item:mathystra-relic.text: Mathystra Relic. Mathystra Relics are ancient night elven artifacts scattered among the overgrown ruins of Mathystra in northern Darkshore. Though remnants of a fallen elven bastion, they retain dormant shards of magic that have drawn the interest of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the Great Sundering, Mathystra stood as a proud city and bastion of elven civilization along the Kalimdor coast. Today, its toppled columns and cracked stones sit half-swallowed by brush and sea mist, haunted by restless spirits and lurking beasts. Scattered across the ruins are ancient relics dating back to that golden age. Though worn by ten thousand years of neglect, these artifacts still hold faint traces of elven arcane craft, making them dangerous prizes if left unattended.

item:melenas-head.text: Melenas' Head. Melenas' Head is the severed bounty taken from Lord Melenas, a satyr commander encamped inside Fel Rock. Brought back as absolute proof of his demise, the trophy marks the quiet elimination of a lingering demonic threat on the boughs of Teldrassil. To the night elves guarding Shadowglen and the surrounding reaches of Teldrassil, the mere existence of satyrs upon their new World Tree is a bitter disgrace. Lord Melenas chose to make his lair inside the twisted caverns of Fel Rock, just north of the elven settlements, rallying aggressive grell warriors to his banner. Because the kaldorei prize discretion when handling corruptions so close to their heartlands, this bloody trophy serves as private proof that his scheming has been snuffed out before his influence could spread.

item:menethil-statuette.text: Menethil Statuette. The Menethil Statuette is a rare silvery figurine portraying the late King Terenas Menethil II as a youthful paladin with an upraised warhammer. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of the Wetlands, it is an exceptionally scarce memorial of Lordaeron's fallen sovereign. The statuette depicts King Terenas Menethil II in his early years, portrayed as a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. Terenas was notoriously humble during his reign and disliked personal monuments, meaning few statues or likenesses were ever commissioned in his honor. Following the collapse of the Kingdom of Lordaeron to the Scourge, almost all such relics were obliterated, making this surviving effigy extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance. The statuette was cargo aboard the merchant vessel Blind Princess, bound for the Alliance harbor of Menethil. When the ship came under attack by aggressive Bluegill murlocs off the marshy coast, the cargo was scattered and the statuette ended up trapped in a half-buried barrel on the shore. With local threats like the Dragonmaw orcs hovering nearby, local defenders hurried to send the retrieved icon south to Stormwind City, where Highlord Bolvar Fordragon entrusted it to the Cathedral of Light.

item:merrin-s-letter.text: Merrin's Letter. Merrin's Letter is an urgent message written by Merrin Rockweaver, an archaeologist trapped at the dig site in the Wetlands. It recounts the catastrophic overrun of their archaeological expedition by vicious raptors and assures her loved ones of her immediate survival. While excavating enormous prehistoric fossils and relics at the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands, the dwarven expedition disturbed a nest of ferocious Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, slaughtering several workers and cutting off the surviving researchers from escape. Penning this note amidst the chaos, Merrin Rockweaver wrote to inform her husband Tarrel back at Menethil Harbor that while the dig lies in ruins, she, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid managed to survive behind barricaded shelter.

item:middle-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Middle of Gelkak's Key. The Middle of Gelkak's Key is a broken metal fragment belonging to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel went down off the coast of Darkshore, this central section was snatched away by scavengers among the local Greymist murlocs. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was dragged beneath the waves by wild threshadons, the gnome pirate tumbled ashore with his most precious belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. Among the wreckage was a specialized winding key meant for his mechanical first mate. The key snapped into three distinct fragments during the catastrophe, scattering across the strand. While the tops and bottoms ended up carried off by coastal beasts, the middle section caught the eye of the Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf, who quickly hoarded the shiny metallic piece in their camps and wreckage holdings.

item:milly-s-harvest.text: Milly's Harvest. Milly's Harvest consists of crates and buckets of freshly picked grapes gathered by Milly Osworth in the Northshire Vineyards. When Defias bandits overran the fields, the harvest was abandoned, leaving the fruit at risk of being stolen by thieves or crushed beneath the boots of abbey guards. The fertile soil of the Northshire Valley produces grapes vital for local vintners and the abbey community. When harvesting season arrived, Milly Osworth worked the vines to collect the fresh fruit into storage buckets. Her work was violently interrupted when armed brigands bearing red masks pushed into the vineyards, forcing her to flee back to the abbey grounds with her crop left scattered between the rows. Though Stormwind guards watch the valley entrance, manpower shortages have left Northshire vulnerable. While the garrison promised to drive the Defias out, Milly feared that any drawn-out skirmish between armored guards and ruthless thieves would result in the complete destruction of her work. Retrieving the crates before they are trampled underfoot or carried off as provisions ensures that one of Northshire's few peaceful harvests is not lost.

item:miners-gear.text: Miners' Gear. Miners' Gear consists of sturdy dwarven picks, shovels, and excavation tools stored within the Silver Stream Mine. Following an infestation of vermin, the Miners' League tasked adventurers with retrieving these valuable implements before local guards launched an assault. When the Silver Stream Mine in northern Loch Modan ran out of ore, the Miners' League repurposed the quiet tunnels into a subterranean storage depot for mining equipment. Unfortunately, tunnel-dwelling kobolds quickly overrun the complex, making off with the stored goods and nesting among the crates. Fearing the valuable dwarven gear would either be wrecked in an all-out assault by the Mountaineers or ruined by the scavengers, the league relies on bold adventurers to venture inside and haul the crates back to safety.

item:miners-union-card.text: Miners' Union Card. A Miners' Union Card is an identification credential once carried by laborers working the rich subterranean veins beneath Moonbrook. Following a catastrophic cave-in that sealed a wing of the tunnels, these tokens now remain on the restless skeletal corpses wandering the dark drifts. Long before the Defias Brotherhood took absolute control over Moonbrook, laborers toiled underground under the banner of the miners' guild, extracting valuable ore for the kingdom. That ended in disaster when a severe tunnel collapse crushed a major shaft, trapping and killing dozens of workers beneath tons of rock. Rather than finding a quiet grave, those who perished rose again as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. The union cards clutched in their bony pockets are the sole surviving proof of their identities, sought out by surviving colleagues in Stormwind hoping to bring closure to grieving families.

item:minshina-s-skull.text: Minshina's Skull. Minshina's Skull contains the bound soul of the Darkspear troll Minshina, brother of Master Gadrin. Trapped by the rogue witch doctor Zalazane on the Echo Isles, the skull serves as a grim vessel used to fuel dark ritual magics. When Zalazane seized control of the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear tribe, Minshina was among those captured and slain. Rather than letting his victim pass into death, the traitorous witch doctor bound Minshina's soul to his own severed skull. Placed within a foul circle of power on the southernmost isle, the skull became a tether of magical enslavement. Master Gadrin, guided by tormented visions of his brother calling to him in dreams, seeks out brave travelers to venture into the occupied islands, reclaim the relic, and shatter Zalazane's hold over his brother's spirit.

item:mirror-lake-water-sample.text: Mirror Lake Water Sample. The Mirror Lake Water Sample is a flask of fresh lake water collected from the base of the waterfall in Elwynn Forest. Gathered by novice mages on behalf of Jennea Cannon in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind, it is used to investigate whether altered arcane currents are seeping into local water supplies. Following catastrophic global conflicts that tore the world's mystic channels from their stable courses, the mages of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind have grown deeply concerned about residual arcane disruption. Jennea Cannon tasks promising apprentices with filling a specially prepared flask at the base of the Mirror Lake waterfall, located just southwest of the Stormwind Gate. By analyzing this water sample, the mages seek to detect whether stray magical taints have seeped into the natural waterways relied upon by the surrounding populace.

item:mist-veil-s-lockbox.text: Mist Veil's Lockbox. Mist Veil's Lockbox is a sturdy strongbox resting in the submerged wreckage of the night elven vessel Mist Veil off the coast of Darkshore. It holds the captain's log and personal effects, which were lost when the ship was ambushed and sunk by coastal murlocs. The night elven vessel Mist Veil met its end while sailing the treacherous coastal waters toward Auberdine. Ambushed by hostile murlocs alongside its sister ship, the Silver Dawning, the vessel was overwhelmed and sent to the ocean floor. Its captain perished during the attack, leaving behind their logbook and prized personal belongings sealed inside this lockbox. Resting in the flooded hold, the chest remains a grim trophy surrounded by the very creatures responsible for the catastrophe. For the surviving sailors who managed to reach Auberdine, the loss of their vessel and commander remains an open wound. Gorbold Steelhand seeks the recovery of the Mist Veil's Lockbox so the captain's final effects can be properly honored and laid to rest. Braving the flooded ruins to salvage the chest offers some measure of solace to the grief-stricken survivors stranded on the mainland.

item:mo-grosh-crystal.text: Mo'grosh Crystal. Mo'grosh Crystals are rare mineral formations mined and hoarded by the Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. Prized for their unusual alchemical properties, they serve as a vital component in neutralizing Dark Iron demolition materials. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, the Mo'grosh ogres excavate these distinctive crystals from their stronghold. Though the brute-strength ogres rarely specialize in delicate metallurgy, Mo'grosh Crystals are prized treasures among their clan, carried by common enforcers, mystic shamans, and their towering leaders alike. The crystals are relatively uncommon, making them a heavily guarded possession within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

item:modr-fragment.text: Modr Fragment. The Modr Fragment is one of four missing pieces broken off from the ancient Goaz Stone, a relic unearthed in the Wetlands. Discovered amid relics and loose earth within the Whelgar Excavation Site, it bears ancient Titan script vital to assembling a forgotten prophecy. Before vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from their dig in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone—a massive tablet inscribed with ancient Titan markings. Its translated text abruptly broke off across four distinct gaps, obscuring warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. The Modr Fragment is one of those four lost pieces, left behind among ancient relics and overturned soil when the diggers were forced to flee for their lives.

item:moldy-tome.text: Moldy Tome. The Moldy Tome is a water-damaged, salvaged remnant containing half of the original Tome of the Cabal. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, it holds dark esoteric rituals coveted by warlocks seeking to master demonic summonings. The Tome of the Cabal was a singular, irreplaceable treatise on dark arts once held within the kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point in its murky history, the grimoire was ruthlessly vandalized and split in two. The portion now designated as the Moldy Tome was being transported south by ship toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The vessel never reached its destination, succumbing to the treacherous waters west of Southshore. Swept ashore south of Azurelode Mine, the surviving half lay ruined by damp and surf amidst the scavenging murlocs that stalk the Hillsbrad coast.

item:moonpetal-lily.text: Moonpetal Lily. Moonpetal Lilies are large, luminous flora native to Teldrassil that flourish around freshwater pools. Renowned for their potent restorative qualities, their petals are prized as key ingredients in natural remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow exclusively along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds, particularly favored along the northwestern side of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like much of the plant life flourishing atop the newly grown World Tree, they absorb the unique essence of Teldrassil's sheltered groves. Their broad petals are gentle and radiant, easily spotted hugging the tranquil water's edge where natural moisture allows them to thrive. Night elf healers and herbalists value the Moonpetal Lily for its extraordinary healing properties. When combined with other forest flora, such as Hyacinth Mushrooms, the lily acts as a powerful soothing and stabilizing agent. This restorative quality makes it an essential component when brewing antidotes to counteract lethal toxins, notably the virulent venom produced by the Webwood spiders lurking within Shadowthread Cave.

item:moonstalker-fang.text: Moonstalker Fang. Moonstalker Fangs are sharp canine teeth taken from the predatory moonstalkers roaming the misty woods of Darkshore. They are gathered by travelers assisting Wizbang Cranktoggle with the maintenance of his automated sampling devices. Moonstalkers are stealthy saber cats that haunt the forest fringes of Darkshore, stalking prey between the shadowed pines. Their elongated fangs serve as formidable hunting weapons, capable of shearing flesh and bone. For the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle, however, the teeth serve a very different mechanical purpose. Stationed north of Auberdine near the bridge, his automated contraption known as Buzzbox 323 is calibrated specifically to crush these durable fangs to dust as part of his erratic ecological surveys.

item:moonwell-water-tube.text: Moonwell Water Tube. A vial filled with consecrated water drawn from the moonwell in Auberdine. Its potent, purifying nature magic is used to test and react with a mysterious red crystal embedded along Darkshore's eastern ridges. Drawn directly from the shimmering moonwell resting in Auberdine, the Moonwell Water Tube contains liquid steeped in the blessed energies of Elune. Moonwells serve night elf settlements as sacred reservoirs of restorative magic and purity, rendering even a small phial remarkably potent against corruption or unknown mystical phenomena.

item:mossy-tumor.text: Mossy Tumor. A mossy tumor is a foul, poisonous growth carved from the bark and flesh of corrupted timberlings on Teldrassil. Found primarily around Wellspring Lake, these growths serve as outward signs of an unnerving malevolence spreading through the newly grown World Tree. The timberlings of Teldrassil were created to nurture and tend the boughs of the great tree, but many have turned hostile and diseased. These mossy tumors are physical manifestations of this inner sickness. Heavily laden with toxins, the growths sprout across the bodies of Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings that prowl Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus have tasked travelers with severing the tumors so they may be thoroughly burned, preventing their poison from taking deeper root in the island's soil.

item:mountain-lion-blood.text: Mountain Lion Blood. Mountain Lion Blood is a reagent collected from the prowling predators of the Hillsbrad Foothills and the snowy slopes of Alterac. Apothecary Lydon of Tarren Mill seeks this fresh blood to formulate the Royal Apothecary Society's dreaded Elixir of Pain. The highlands and foothills flanking Hillsbrad and Alterac are prowled by feral and starving mountain lions. While ordinary hunters seek these predators for their pelts and claws, the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society find value in what pumps through their veins. Fresh mountain lion blood possesses specific biological properties that Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes will serve as the base for a potent new toxic brew designed to bring misery to the living. Apothecary Lydon's experiments in Tarren Mill contribute directly to the Royal Apothecary Society's overarching mandate: perfecting the Forsaken's New Plague. By harvesting the blood of vigorous wild beasts, Lydon seeks to refine a concoction he calls the Elixir of Pain, testing how potent local organic compounds can be weaponized against the enemies of the Dark Lady.

item:mudsnout-blossom.text: Mudsnout Blossom. Mudsnout Blossoms are pungent, toxic fungal growths found sprouting in Nethander Stead in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by local gnolls and harvested by the Royal Apothecary Society, these foul mushrooms are used in Apothecary Lydon's elixir research. Despite their floral name, Mudsnout Blossoms are actually large, foul-smelling mushrooms that flourish primarily in the soiled dirt of Nethander Stead, south of Tarren Mill. They grow amidst the camps of the local Mudsnout gnolls, who defend the territory fiercely. To living organisms, the spores and flesh of the mushroom act as a virulent poison, causing agony and rapid biological deterioration.

item:mudsnout-composite.text: Mudsnout Composite. Mudsnout Composite is an alchemical paste prepared by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill from harvested Mudsnout Blossoms. It serves as an essential base ingredient carried to the Undercity for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a new plague. Crafted in the field by Apothecary Lydon, this fine composite is derived directly from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. While noxious on its own, the mash requires a specialized colloid of decay—concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell himself—to activate its more lethal qualities. Once bound, the mixture forms a key chemical component in the development of the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

item:mudsnout-mixture.text: Mudsnout Mixture. Mudsnout Mixture is a toxic alchemical base concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. Created by blending a mudsnout composite with an alchemical colloid of decay, it serves as the foundation for the Royal Apothecary Society's deadly Elixir of Agony. When Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon, he sends a base composite of Mudsnout Blossoms, toxic mushrooms from the gnoll-held Nethander Stead, north to the Undercity. Impressed by the composite's potential, Master Apothecary Faranell introduces his own colloid of decay into the blend, producing the volatile Mudsnout Mixture. The solution stabilizes the mushroom compound while readying its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement back in the foothills.

item:murloc-head.text: Murloc Head. Murloc Heads are grim trophies severed from the amphibious creatures prowling the Western Strand in Hillsbrad Foothills. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle of Southshore requires them as physical proof of culled threats to satisfy his superior, Marshal Redpath. Southshore faces dangers from all directions, but the aggressive murlocs clustering along the Western Strand are an immediate menace to local fishermen and coastal travelers. Although Alliance adventurers frequently sweep the beaches to cull the creatures, Marshal Marcus Redpath demands undeniable verification before signing off on defensive reports. To humor the bureaucracy, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle relies on hired fighters to haul in cold, dripping murloc heads—an unpleasant task Farren himself finds entirely repulsive, especially given how thoroughly the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's local seafood.

item:musquash-root.text: Musquash Root. Musquash Root is a rare botanical specimen found only in the damp soil beneath the massive waterfalls of the Stonewrought Dam in the Wetlands. It serves as a vital component in a concoction brewed by cultists hidden beneath Stormwind. Musquash Root thrives in the perpetually mist-soaked ground where the cascade of the Stonewrought Dam crashes into the Wetlands. Its secluded and damp habitat makes it exceedingly difficult to harvest. While ordinary herbalists rarely seek it out, certain practitioners of the darker arts value the root for its potent chemical and alchemical properties.

item:mysterious-fossil.text: Mysterious Fossil. The Mysterious Fossil is an ancient specimen unearthed along the coast of Darkshore by Prospector Remtravel. Its curious characteristics have drawn the intense curiosity of the dwarven Explorers' League, prompting scholars to shuttle it across the sea to uncover its hidden secrets. While conducting fieldwork among the wild shores of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel uncovered a fossil unlike the common petrified stone scattered across Kalimdor. Deeming it of monumental historical importance, Remtravel arranged for the specimen to be delivered to dwarven scholars rather than let it languish in the wilderness. When brought before Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus, the relic immediately stood out as an extraordinary find.

item:nak-s-skull.text: Nak's Skull. Nak's Skull is a grisly hunting trophy severed from Nak, one of three prominent Razormane quilboar commanders directing warbands in the southern Barrens. Taken as proof of the raider's defeat, it is sought by the captive quilboar Mangletooth to avenge a bitter tribal betrayal. Emerging from Razorfen Kraul, the trio consisting of Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane launched vicious raids targeting Horde settlements and roadways across the Barrens. Unknown to the defenders at the Crossroads, these warlords were orchestrating attacks far more cunning than typical tribal skirmishing. When the Razormane prisoner Mangletooth was abandoned to die in a cage at Camp Taurajo, his thirst for retribution turned against his former brethren. Demanding physical proof of Nak's demise, Mangletooth asks Horde adventurers to deliver the severed skull alongside those of his cohorts to break the back of the southern raiding parties.

item:nek-rosh-s-head.text: Nek'rosh's Head. Nek'rosh's Head is the gruesome proof of the downfall of Chieftain Nek'rosh, leader of the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. Procured by Alliance adventurers, this trophy is delivered to Captain Stoutfist to confirm that the orcish threat menacing Menethil Harbor has been shattered. The Dragonmaw clan poses a persistent danger across the marshlands, massing forces and siege weapons against the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After burning their catapults, the defense of the port hinges on slaying Chieftain Nek'rosh himself. Severing his head provides undeniable proof to Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities that the warlord's grip over the Wetlands is broken.

item:neru-fragment.text: Neru Fragment. The Neru Fragment is one of four ancient carved stone pieces belonging to the Goaz Stone, a relic discovered in the Whelgar's Excavation site within the Wetlands. Unearthed from the disturbed earth, it holds a segment of ancient Titan script detailing the primeval history of Azeroth. Discovered by the dwarven archaeological expedition led by Prospector Whelgar, the Goaz Stone broke apart into four distinct remnants: the Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru fragments. When raptors overrun the dig site, work ground to a halt, leaving the Neru Fragment buried beneath loose soil amid the aggressive beasts. Recovering this fragment is crucial for reassembling the tablet, allowing dwarven scholars to decipher a forgotten record whose surviving words mention a divine plan and a doomed prophecy.

item:nessa-s-collection.text: Nessa's Collection. Nessa's Collection is a package of fish bones and scales gathered from the waters surrounding Rut'theran Village. Prepared for study by fish vendor Laird in Auberdine, it illustrates the unusually massive size of aquatic life thriving around the roots of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong, a fisherwoman residing in Rut'theran Village at the base of Teldrassil, gathered this collection of fish bones and scales to compare the island's marine life with that of the Kalimdor mainland. The waters feeding into the Great Tree yield catches of staggering proportions, prompting Nessa to send physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant operating along the docks of Auberdine. Transferred by way of the village's hippogryph master, Vesprystus, the parcel serves as practical evidence of Teldrassil's burgeoning vitality. Upon inspecting the contents in Darkshore, Laird discovers that the specimens far outstrip their mainland counterparts. The collection contains jawbones nearly twice the size of fish native to the Darkshore coastline, along with individual scales as large as a clenched fist. For coastal night elves, the package provides a clear look at how drastically the waters around Teldrassil differ from the somber shores of northern Kalimdor.

item:nether-gem.text: Nether Gem. The Nether Gem is an enchanted arcane stone entrusted by the reclusive necromancer Gunther Arcanus. Imbued with magical power, it acts as a long-distance conduit allowing Gunther to manifest an arcane projection and communicate directly with his old associate, Bethor Iceshard, in the Undercity. Forged or enchanted by Gunther Arcanus on his solitary island in Brightwater Lake, the Nether Gem serves as a mystical link across Tirisfal Glades. Gunther, having broken free from the Lich King's control through his own sheer willpower, long avoided the fledgling Forsaken nation out of suspicion. After receiving his lost spellbook, he entrusts the gem to an emissary as a gesture of goodwill. Once brought to Bethor Iceshard atop the Magic Quarter in the Undercity, the stone channels Gunther's magical visage directly before the Mage Guild leader, opening the path for the solitary mage to align with Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken.

item:ng-5.text: NG-5. NG-5 is the shorthand designation for Nitromirglyceronium, a notoriously volatile chemical compound. Procured for the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves as the essential catalyst for his explosive engineering schemes. Known formally as Nitromirglyceronium, NG-5 is an exceptionally hazardous chemical solution handled only with extreme caution—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim Rustfizzle, an operative stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, requires the substance as a critical ignition compound. According to Gaxim, NG-5 provides the exact reaction necessary to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, orchestrating a massive explosion meant to serve as a chaotic distraction against his adversaries in the region.

item:nida-s-necklace.text: Hilary's Necklace. Hilary's Necklace is a cherished childhood keepsake lost beneath the surface of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Given to young Hilary by her father, the trinket slipped into the murky waters while the children of Lakeshire were out fishing along the docks. While fishing along the shoreline of Lakeshire with her friend Shawn, young Hilary accidentally dropped her treasured necklace into Lake Everstill. The heirloom holds immense sentimental value, having been a gift from her father. Fear of the fierce beasts and aggressive murlocs inhabiting the depths keeps the local children safely on the docks, leaving the necklace sunken and buried in the silt of the lakebed until an adventurer is willing to dive into the murky water to recover it.

item:nightmare-shard.text: Nightmare Shard. The Nightmare Shard is a crystalline relic handed to couriers by Falla Sagewind after she examines a tainted glowing shard recovered from the Wailing Caverns. Containing the pure, disturbed essence of the Emerald Dream, it carries a troubling vision that prompts immediate warning and secrecy among senior druids in Darnassus and Thunder Bluff. When Falla Sagewind inspects the mysterious glowing shard unearthed deep within the Wailing Caverns, she realizes its energy is far darker than anticipated. Rather than mirroring the serene vitality of the Emerald Dream, the fragment reflects a twisting, unnatural affliction—a waking nightmare. Fearful of what its presence implies, she binds this tainted essence into the Nightmare Shard and commands that it be ferried straight to elder leaders of the Cenarion Circle without delay.

item:nightsaber-fang.text: Nightsaber Fang. A sharp tooth harvested from the predatory nightsabers roaming the wild branches of Teldrassil. While a common trophy of the hunt, these fangs are also sought out as raw reagents by local woodland residents with questionable motives. Nightsabers are among the deadliest natural predators native to northern Kalimdor, revered by the night elves for their agility, ferocity, and deep spiritual connection to Elune. Across the great boughs of Teldrassil, these feline beasts hunt in the shadows beneath the canopy. Striking one down yields sharp fangs that serve as undeniable proof of a hunter's skill, though certain unsavory figures in the forest seek them out for less noble ritual purposes.

item:nissa-s-remains.text: Nissa's Remains. Nissa's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Nissa Agamand, a noblewoman of the once-wealthy Agamand dynasty in northern Tirisfal Glades. Slain and raised as mindless servants of the Scourge during the Third War, she and her family are now hunted down by former laborers seeking vengeance. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the wealthiest and most influential dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, operating prosperous mills across the northern hills. When the Plague of Undeath crept across Lordaeron, the family patriarchs stubbornly refused to evacuate.
