Instead, they fortified their estates and convinced their retainers and laborers to stand their ground. That arrogance cost everyone their lives. The Agamands fell to the Scourge, rising not with their proud independence intact, but as shambling, mindless thralls bound to the Lich King's will. In the town of Brill, survivors who later broke free under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner have not forgotten the family's fatal pride. Coleman Farthing, a former laborer in the Agamand mills, holds a bitter grudge against his former masters for luring their workers into the jaws of undeath. He charges adventurers with putting down the risen Agamands and retrieving their physical remains, such as Nissa's. For Farthing and others among the Forsaken, burning or destroying these relics offers a grim sense of final closure and spiteful revenge.

item:nitroglycerin.text: Nitroglycerin. Nitroglycerin is a volatile chemical substance carried by dwarven soldiers and officers garrisoned at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. It serves as an industrial explosive agent for their excavation operations, though it can also be turned against them. The Bael'dun dwarves tore into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tauren using heavy mechanical drillers and volatile chemistry. To blast holes deep into the ground and tear apart the hills, dwarven personnel at the Bael Modan excavation site and its fortified keep keep stores of raw nitroglycerin close at hand. Both frontline soldiers and officers such as Lord Cyrik Blackforge carry vials of the volatile fluid on their persons to fuel the ongoing, destructive digging.

item:nondescript-letter.text: Nondescript Letter. The Nondescript Letter is a sealed, unmarked missive entrusted to newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell. Handed over by Calvin Montague under the guise of an errand, it directs the bearer down the road to Innkeeper Renee at the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Newly arisen Forsaken looking to venture beyond Deathknell are approached by Calvin Montague, a shifty rogue lingering near the village perimeter. Claiming to be weary from fighting mindless zombies and arachnids, Calvin asks travelers to carry a plain, unmarked envelope along the eastward road to Brill. Addressed casually to an innkeeper named Renee, the letter serves as an excuse to push travelers out of the valley and toward the Gallows' End Tavern, though Calvin's promises of rich compensation ring hollow from the start.

item:nori-s-mug.text: Nori's Mug. Nori's Mug is the personal drinking vessel of Nori Pridedrift, used to deliver scalding mornbrew across the frigid drifts of Dun Morogh. After delivering a warm drink to stave off the biting alpine chill, travelers are tasked with returning the empty cup to its thrifty owner. In the freezing mountain passes of Dun Morogh, a piping hot tankard of mornbrew is one of the few comforts capable of cutting through the bitter cold. Nori Pridedrift entrusts his mug to travelers delivering a fresh, steaming pour to Durnan Furcutter in Anvilmar. Once drained, the sturdy vessel must make the trek back. As Nori notes, mugs do not grow on trees, and keeping track of hard-wearing dwarven dishware is essential business when hospitality meets snowy wilderness.

item:notched-rib.text: Notched Rib. A Notched Rib is a bone trophy harvested from the ranks of mindless undead wandering Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill collects these scarred remains as proof of efforts to break the Scourge's foothold at the Agamand Mills. The Scourge forces massing across the northern fields of Tirisfal Glades consist of reanimated skeletons clad in ruined armor. Among their ranks, Cracked Skull Soldiers and Rattlecage Soldiers throw themselves against any living or free-willed being they encounter. Slicing through their brittle frames leaves their bone structure pitted and scored. To ensure that Forsaken scouts and volunteers actually cull these mindless intruders rather than merely observing them, the Deathguards demand tangible evidence. A notched, battle-marked rib serves as unmistakable proof that another of the Lich King's thralls has been shattered. The Agamand Mills represent a critical strategic position northwest of Brill. Should the Scourge firmly entrench themselves among the ruined farmsteads and windmills, they would possess a direct staging ground to launch assaults deep into the heart of Tirisfal. Deathguard Dillinger monitors the roads leading north, dispatching champions to crush the skeleton cohorts before they can consolidate. Piles of notched ribs returned to Brill demonstrate that the Forsaken lines are holding, slowly grinding down the Scourge vanguard bone by bone.

item:nugget-slug.text: Nugget Slug. Nugget slugs are specialized 17.5-gauge mechanical fasteners used in industrial engineering. Stockpiled in tool buckets by the Venture Company at the Sludge Fen, they are coveted by tinkerers attempting to repair volatile machinery. Nugget slugs are heavy-duty metallic fasteners manufactured for demanding industrial assemblies. Specifically sized at 17.5 gauge, these components are an essential part of the heavy equipment deployed across Venture Company extraction sites. While useless as ordinary trade goods, they are indispensable to tinkerers dealing with customized goblin hardware.

item:ogre-s-monocle.text: Ogre's Monocle. The Ogre's Monocle is an oversized eyeglass worn by Zzarc'Vul, an ogre dwelling in southern Duskwood's Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Its immense glass lens provides the exact dimensions needed by Viktori Prism'Antras in Darkshire to assemble an elaborate stargazing telescope. While ogres are rarely renowned for refined scholarship, Zzarc'Vul somehow came into possession of an enormous monocle tailored to his massive stature. When the Darkshire resident Viktori Prism'Antras set out to build a stargazing instrument using blueprints drafted by the gnome engineer Cog, he found standard lenses far too small. Zzarc'Vul's eyewear proved to be the only piece of polished glass in the region with the curvature and size necessary to focus light through the completed device. Acquiring the monocle requires braving the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound in the shadow of southern Duskwood. Zzarc'Vul resides among his brute brethren, showing little inclination to voluntarily part with his distinctive accessory. Claiming the lens means defeating the brute on his own territory before returning the glass to Darkshire so Viktori can finally turn his gaze to the night skies.

item:okra.text: Okra. Okra is a cultivated vegetable that grows in the tilled plots of Westfall. Highly prized by local homesteaders, it serves as a crucial thickening agent in the region's hearty, improvisational stews. While much of Westfall lies fallow under the threat of Defias outlaws and rogue harvest golem attacks, stubborn farmers like the Saldeans still manage to coax hearty vegetables out of the soil. Okra grows low and green in the tilled dirt around Saldean's Farm. Despite the harsh conditions of the countryside, the crop persists, providing local homesteaders with essential bulk and nourishment when outside trade and supplies from Stormwind run completely dry. Okra is best known as the indispensable base for Salma Saldean's famous Westfall Stew. Combined with whatever meat can be hunted across the dusty plains—such as vulture flesh, goretusk snouts, and coastal murloc eyes—the sliced pods break down under heat to thicken thin broths into a filling, restorative meal. For the struggling settlers clinging to their homesteads, fresh pods of okra turn sparse, wild scavenging into a hot, hearty supper.

item:ordanus-head.text: Ordanus' Head. Ordanus' Head is the grisly trophy taken from Keeper Ordanus at Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale. Claimed on behalf of the blood elf magi Braelyn Firehand, it serves as undeniable proof that one of Cenarius's eldest sons has fallen to arcane vengeance. Keeper Ordanus was an ancient keeper of the grove, one of the elder scions of the forest god Cenarius. When Braelyn Firehand climbed the heights of Stonetalon Mountains on orders from her master, she sought to end the druids' stifling of magic at the peak and exact vengeance on Ordanus. However, the keeper was spirited away to the heart of Ashenvale before she could strike. Using arcane scrying to peer through the forest canopy, Firehand located his sanctuary in the boughs of Raynewood Retreat, demanding his severed head as proof that the wild demigod's arrogance had finally been answered.

item:orendil-s-cure.text: Orendil's Cure. Orendil's Cure is a medicinal draught concocted by the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf in northern Ashenvale. Created using the rare herb Bathran's Hair, it is meant to treat the mysterious, deathly sickness afflicting Relara Whitemoon in Astranaar. When young Relara Whitemoon fell deathly ill in Astranaar, conventional remedies proved useless against her ailment. Her desperate father, Pelturas Whitemoon, turned to Orendil Broadleaf, a hermit and master of natural medicine dwelling along the northern reaches of Ashenvale. Utilizing bundles of the rare plant Bathran's Hair harvested from the haunted ruins of Bathran's Haunt, Orendil brewed this tailored concoction. The arrival of the vial gives Pelturas hope where before he had little, though the cure only slows the disease, and Pelturas must turn to the further remedies Orendil suggested.

item:oslow-s-toolbox.text: Oslow's Toolbox. Oslow's Toolbox contains the vital construction tools needed by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire. En route from Goldshire, the supplies were ferried across Lake Everstill only to be sunk by an orcish catapult bombardment. Maintaining the defenses and infrastructure of Lakeshire is a grueling challenge, particularly with the Blackrock orcs besieging the Redridge Mountains. Foreman Oslow ordered a vital set of construction tools brought in from Goldshire. Because the main bridge leading into Lakeshire had been destroyed by enemy action, the shipment had to be loaded into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill. The crossing was abruptly cut short when Blackrock forces struck the vessel with a catapult blast, plunging the boat and Oslow's heavy chest straight down into the murloc-infested depths.

item:osric-s-crate.text: Osric's Crate. Osric's Crate is a heavy package of freshly crafted armor dispatched from Stormwind to the struggling defenders of Sentinel Hill. Carried aboard a gryphon across the kingdom's flight network, it provides vital equipment to help the People's Militia hold Westfall against outlaw gangs. Westfall suffers under the predations of the Defias Brotherhood and marauding gnolls, while the Stormwind army remains absent. The local defenders, organized as the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill, lack the formal support of the crown and must rely on piecemeal supplies. Osric's Crate contains a fresh batch of protective armor sent from the capital to Quartermaster Lewis, intended to be parceled out directly to volunteer militia fighters on the ground. Transporting gear overland from Stormwind through Elwynn Forest and across the Westfall border is slow and fraught with bandit ambushes. To bypass the roads, the crate is entrusted to an adventurer flying via Dungar Longdrink's gryphon roost in Stormwind's Trade District down to Thor at Sentinel Hill. This swift delivery demonstrates the crucial role gryphons play in keeping frontier garrisons supplied during wartime.

item:package-of-empty-ooze-containers.text: Package of Empty Ooze Containers. This package is a kit of specialized, empty specimen jars supplied by the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge. Intended for dangerous field sampling in the blighted forests of Felwood, it contains jars designed to safely hold tainted and cursed ooze extracts without dissolving. Containing a dozen empty jars—split between containers meant for cursed and tainted oozes—this kit was assembled by Laris Geardawdle for intrepid travelers heading out to Felwood. Because raw ooze specimens are notoriously caustic and prone to digesting ordinary luggage, sturdy, sealed glass is essential for transporting the acidic residues across continents back to the tinker's workbench in Ironforge. Geardawdle's interest in ooze is far from a simple eccentric hobby. Noticing that Forsaken researchers from the Royal Apothecary Society routinely harvest these bizarre organisms across Azeroth, he suspects oozes may hold profound secrets about the world's origin. Geardawdle theorizes that slimes might be primordial secretions connected to the planet's very creation, and he relies on field agents using this kit to collect the evidence he needs to win acclaim within the Explorers' League.

item:painted-gnoll-armband.text: Painted Gnoll Armband. Painted Gnoll Armbands are crude adornments worn by the Riverpaw gnolls prowling the outskirts of Elwynn Forest. Westbrook Garrison collects these marked bands as physical proof of bounties fulfilled against the encroaching packs. The Riverpaw pack marks its warriors and scavengers with rough armbands painted in crude tribal patterns. The painted bands are collected from the Riverpaw gnolls along the wilderness borders of Elwynn Forest. To the defenders of Stormwind, however, they represent a growing territorial menace encroaching near Stone Cairn Lake and the woods south of Westbrook Garrison. With the Stormwind Army stretched thin across the kingdom, Westbrook Garrison struggles to keep the western border secure against encroaching threats. Deputy Rainer placed a standing bounty on the invading packs, directing adventurers to slay Riverpaw outrunners and runts. The painted armbands serve as undeniable proof of the kill, allowing garrison deputies to tally bounties and thin the gnoll population encroaching on nearby farmlands.

item:panther-cage-key.text: Panther Cage Key. The Panther Cage Key is a small metal key held by Wizlo Bearingshiner at Whitereach Post. It unlocks a reinforced cage holding an enraged, captive predator within the wreckage of an ambushed caravan in Thousand Needles. When a traveling caravan was attacked and ransacked by centaur raiders north of Whitereach Post, the goblin tinker Wizlo Bearingshiner barely escaped with his life. Amid the ruins of wagons and plundered cargo, the marauders left one thing entirely untouched: a sturdy cage housing a ferocious, rare panther. Around the predator's neck hung Wizlo's prized invention, a hypercapacitor gizmo. Unwilling to approach the snarling beast, the centaur gave the cage a wide berth, leaving Wizlo's key as the only way to open the door and retrieve the device.

item:parker-s-lunch.text: Parker's Lunch. Parker's Lunch is a freshly prepared meal packed by Darcy in Lakeshire. Intended for Guard Parker on patrol, it offers a simple glimpse into the daily bonds and modest comforts of Redridge's defenders. While Redridge Mountains reels under attacks from gnolls and Blackrock orcs, the small gestures of daily life persist. Darcy, a waitress at the inn in Lakeshire, packs this wholesome meal for Guard Parker, who patrols the exposed road leading south toward Duskwood. Redridge's garrison is stretched thin and isolated from Stormwind's aid, leaving individual guards to maintain long, lonely watches. Delivering this bundle not only keeps a sentry fed, but also sparks an enduring, bashful courtship between the two townspeople.

item:partially-filled-vessel.text: Partially Filled Vessel. The Partially Filled Vessel is an enchanted container used to transport blessed moonwell water across Teldrassil. Given to young night elf initiates by Tenaron Stormgrip in Aldrassil, it carries water drawn from Shadowglen toward the settlement of Dolanaar. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, initiates of the kaldorei collect blessed waters from the secluded moonwell of Shadowglen. Tenaron Stormgrip pours that pure sample into this specialized vessel, preparing it for travel across the World Tree. The vessel remains only partially filled because its journey has merely begun; more sacred waters from across Teldrassil must eventually be gathered to tend to the island's health. Carrying the vessel requires traveling south through the valley's gates and following the cobblestone roads west to Dolanaar. The journey marks a young adventurer's departure from the protected nursery of Shadowglen out into the broader wilds of Teldrassil. At Dolanaar's central moonwell, Corithras Moonrage takes custody of the vessel to direct the next phase of the ritual.

item:pendant-of-shadow.text: Pendant of Shadow. The Pendant of Shadow is a dark talisman worn by the renegade warlock Morganth atop the Tower of Ilgalar in the Redridge Mountains. Brought to the mage Theocritus at the Tower of Azora, it serves as undeniable proof that the rogue spellcaster has been eliminated before his sinister ambitions could bear fruit. Held by the rogue warlock Morganth within his perch at the Tower of Ilgalar, the Pendant of Shadow is steeped in dark sorcery. Morganth sought to unravel the mysteries of the Scythe of Elune, an ancient relic of immense and volatile power. Fearing the havoc the warlock could unleash upon the Redridge Mountains and the kingdom of Stormwind, the mage Theocritus tasked adventurers with infiltrating Ilgalar, ending Morganth's plotting, and wresting the talisman from his grasp as proof of his demise.

item:pendant-of-the-sea-lion.text: Pendant of the Sea Lion. The Pendant of the Sea Lion is a sacred druidic talisman representing the union of aquatic agility and endurance. Assembled at the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, it serves as proof that an initiate is ready to master their aquatic form. To claim the aquatic aspect of the sea lion, a druid must prove mastery over the water's greatest hazards. The pendant is created by recovering two distinct halves: one embodying the agility needed to slip past aquatic predators, and the other granting the endurance required to withstand prolonged submersion. Brought before the Shrine of Remulos in Moonglade, the two pieces are joined into a single whole. Once forged, the completed pendant is brought before elder mentors—such as Turak Runetotem on the towering rises of Thunder Bluff or Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus. The talisman provides undeniable proof of the initiate's trials under Dendrite Starblaze, permitting the elders to bestow the secrets of shifting into an aquatic form.

item:perenolde-tiara.text: Perenolde Tiara. The Perenolde Tiara is an emerald-studded heirloom of Alterac's fallen royal house, originally fashioned by dwarven craftsmen of Ironforge. Lost amidst the destruction of the kingdom, it eventually fell into the greedy hands of an ogre wandering the ruins before drawing the interest of collectors in Stormwind. Before the mountainous realm of Alterac collapsed in infamy and rubble during the Second War, its ruling house was the Perenolde family. Among their treasures was this delicate tiara, commissioned from master jewelers in Ironforge and set with brilliant emeralds. When Alterac fell to ruin following King Aiden Perenolde's treachery, the crown jewel vanished into the chaotic devastation of the high crags. Rather than being buried forever beneath the snow, the tiara was unearthed by Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage who rummages through the ruins of Alterac searching for abandoned wealth. News of the surviving relic reached Count Remington Ridgewell, a wealthy noble in Stormwind eager to acquire famous relics for his family museum, prompting a search to prise the tiara from the ogre's grasping hands.

item:phial-of-scrying.text: Phial of Scrying. The Phial of Scrying is an enchanted vessel provided by the ancient of lore Onu in Darkshore. When used, it manifests a scrying bowl that allows distant communion across the corrupted woodlands. Entrusted to scouts investigating deep within Darkshore, the Phial of Scrying contains mystical waters that conjures a temporary scrying bowl upon the earth. This tool enables long-distance divination, allowing travelers venturing into perilous reaches like the Master's Glaive to commune directly with Onu without immediately journeying back to his grove.

item:piece-of-krom-zar-s-banner.text: Piece of Krom'zar's Banner. A torn strip of cloth taken from the standards of Warlord Krom'zar, commander of the Kolkar retaliatory force. It serves as tangible proof to Regthar Deathgate that the centaur invasion from Desolace has been broken. Following the systematic defeat of Kolkar chieftains across the Barrens, a furious warband marched east from Desolace intent on revenge. Led by Warlord Krom'zar, these invaders assaulted the defensive bunkers west of the Crossroads. Slicing a remnant from the warlord's fallen battle standard provides undeniable proof to Regthar Deathgate that the assault was crushed and the southern trade routes preserved for the Horde.

item:plainstrider-beak.text: Plainstrider Beak. Plainstrider Beaks are harvested from the tall, flightless birds roaming the scrublands of the Barrens. Huntmasters at the Crossroads collect these beaks as physical proof that a hunter has culled local birds threatening the settlement's provisions. The vast savannahs surrounding the Crossroads are populated by various breeds of plainstrider, including greater, fleeting, and ornery varieties. While relatively simple prey compared to the fiercer beasts of central Kalimdor, their aggressive foraging makes them a constant pest around settlements. Sergra Darkthorn tasks arriving hunters with bringing back Plainstrider Beaks to confirm the flock has been culled away from essential supply lines and storehouses.

item:plainstrider-feather.text: Plainstrider Feather. Plucked from the swift birds roaming the plains of Mulgore, Plainstrider Feathers are essential materials gathered by young hunters on Red Cloud Mesa. The tauren of Camp Narache use them primarily for crafting clothing and tribal adornments, while honoring the creatures that provide for the village. On Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren learn early that survival relies on keen tracking and hunting. Plainstriders run wild across the grassy plateau, offering both sustenance and practical materials. Plucking their sturdy feathers allows the camp to craft traditional garments and gear. Presenting these feathers alongside fresh meat to Grull Hawkwind demonstrates respect for the tribe's needs and serves as the very first test toward being recognized by Chief Hawkwind and welcomed in Thunder Bluff.

item:plainstrider-kidney.text: Plainstrider Kidney. A harvested organ taken from the swift-footed plainstriders roaming the arid plains of the Barrens. Though unappetizing to most travelers, it serves as a bizarre yet essential component in exotic Kalimdor brewing traditions. The vast expanses of the Barrens are populated by tall, flightless birds known as plainstriders. While their feathers and meat are often claimed by hunters for tools and simple rations, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks their internal organs for an entirely different purpose. According to the eccentric brewer, plainstrider kidneys are a necessary ingredient to replicate Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale, imparting a unique kick passed down through an unconventional lineage of brewmasters.

item:plainstrider-meat.text: Plainstrider Meat. Plainstrider Meat is freshly harvested game taken from the flightless birds that wander the plains of Mulgore. For the young tauren coming of age on Red Cloud Mesa, gathering this sustenance serves as both vital winter provisions and a core rite of passage. Tauren life is inextricably bound to the land, balancing respect for nature with the practical necessity of survival. On Red Cloud Mesa, the settlement of Camp Narache depends heavily on game hunted from the surrounding grasslands. Plainstrider meat provides essential food reserves for the village when stocks run lean, while the birds' plumage offers material for clothing and ceremonial adornments. Hunting plainstriders is one of the initial tests given to youth seeking to earn the tribe's respect. Grull Hawkwind directs hopeful hunters to stalk the swift birds across the mesa, gathering meat and feathers to prove their tracking skills and self-reliance before appearing before his father, Chief Hawkwind.

item:plainstrider-scale.text: Plainstrider Scale. A tough scale harvested from the tallstriders roaming the sweeping plains of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller to counter a virulent infection. While plainstriders are best known for their soft feathers and lean meat, their powerful legs are covered in tough, protective scales. These scales are resilient against the harsh scrubland terrain and predator claws. Finding one intact and suitable for medicine requires patience, as only select plainstriders across Mulgore yield scales firm enough to be ground and prepared for folk remedies.

item:plainstrider-talon.text: Plainstrider Talon. A Plainstrider Talon is a sharp claw harvested from the large, flightless plainstriders native to Mulgore. Tauren shamans use these talons alongside other natural reagents to craft sacred cleansing totems when the land's water sources are corrupted. The large, flightless plainstriders roam the open grasses of Mulgore, relying on powerful legs and sharp claws to defend against predators and forage through the tough prairie earth. To the tauren of Bloodhoof Village, every part of a hunted beast carries spiritual resonance. When goblin ventures tainted sacred sources like the Winterhoof Water Well, shaman Mull Thunderhorn sought plainstrider talons alongside prairie wolf paws. In tauren ritual crafting, gathering reagents from native predators and foragers allows the spiritual essence of the land to be channeled into totems capable of purging unnatural poisons.

item:podrig-s-order.text: Podrig's Order. Podrig's Order is a written military requisition penned by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher. It requests a fresh shipment of weapons from Undercity merchant Gordon Wendham to keep Silverpine's Forsaken garrison properly armed. Silverpine Forest is a precarious frontier for the Forsaken, caught between encroaching Scourge, feral beasts, and other lurking threats. After an equipment inventory conducted by Deathguard Podrig on the orders of Executor Hadrec, the Sepulcher's stores were found mostly adequate but desperately low on replacement weapons. This official dispatch details the needed blades and arms to sustain the Deathguards holding the outpost. Because weapons cannot be forged easily amidst the damp crypts of Silverpine, the request is directed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer located in the bustling Trade Quarter of the Undercity. To expedite the order, couriers carry the document directly to bat master Karos Razok, taking advantage of Forsaken flight paths to secure a swift resupply from the capital.

item:pork-belly-pie.text: Pork Belly Pie. Pork Belly Pie is a savory, homemade dish baked by 'Auntie' Bernice Stonefield in Elwynn Forest. Despite the bitter, long-running feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families, young Billy Maclure cannot resist Auntie Bernice's cooking, demanding a pie as a bribe to reveal information about a lost family heirloom. The Stonefield and Maclure families have nursed a bitter rivalry for years, quarreling over land and pride in the heart of Elwynn Forest. Despite this hostility, young Billy Maclure harbors a glaring weakness: he loves Auntie Bernice's famous pork belly pie. When a valuable family necklace goes missing, Billy refuses to share what he knows until an adventurer delivers him a warm slice. Bernice bakes it with great reluctance—and a pointed wish that the greedy boy chokes on it—proving that culinary reputation can sometimes breach even the stubbornest family feuds.

item:powdered-azurite.text: Powdered Azurite. Powdered Azurite is a crushed mineral reagent harvested from the Azurelode Mine in Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought by the master armorer Thun'grim Firegaze to temper and forge brutal armor for rising Horde warriors. Powdered Azurite is a refined dust derived from the mineral veins beneath Hillsbrad Foothills. The human workers of Azurelode Mine delve into the earth to extract this distinctive blue stone, pulverizing and packing it for trade and metallurgy. In the hands of a skilled smith, the dust acts as a crucial flux or additive when working dense metals, enhancing durability and lending unique resilience to finished armor. Though native to human-held tunnels across the Great Sea, Powdered Azurite is recognized by veteran Horde blacksmiths for its exceptional metallurgical properties. Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc armorer residing in the Barrens, demands small quantities of the powdered stone alongside refined iron and fiery reagents. Mixed into the smelt, the powder allows him to hammer out the heavy, punishing plating that characterizes his masterwork battle armor.

item:powers-of-the-void.text: Powers of the Void. Powers of the Void is a rare magical tome originally kept in a restricted wing of Northshire Abbey's library. After an errant novice stole it while defecting to the Defias Brotherhood, the warlock mentor Drusilla La Salle seeks its recovery to further her own study of dark magic. The Northshire Abbey archives hold far more than holy scripture and clerical records. Tucked away in a protected wing of the abbey's library was Powers of the Void, a scholarly work regarding shadow and nether energies, presumably penned by the archmage Khadgar. Given the dangerous nature of such research, abbey authorities kept the book heavily guarded and strictly off-limits to casual visitors. This kept it out of the hands of Northshire's local warlock mentor, Drusilla La Salle, who could not loiter near the restricted shelves without drawing unwanted suspicion from the priesthood. The tome finally left the abbey's walls not by Drusilla's hand, but through betrayal from within. A novice studying at Northshire abandoned his vows to join the Defias Brotherhood, looting several valuable volumes as he fled into the neighboring vineyards. Taking advantage of the thief's opportunism, Drusilla sends promising warlock initiates directly into the Defias bandit camp to seize the tome from their tents. Retrieving the text serves a double purpose: it places dark knowledge into the trainer's grasp and tests whether a novice possess the nerve required to bind otherworldly demons.

item:prairie-alpha-tooth.text: Prairie Alpha Tooth. A Prairie Alpha Tooth is taken from the fierce pack leaders roaming the plains around Thunder Bluff. In tauren tradition, these teeth serve as a potent offering to cleanse and honor the land's precious water sources. The water wells of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren, and maintaining their spiritual purity demands rites of respect and sacrifice. To cleanse the Wildmane Well, Mull Thunderhorn of Bloodhoof Village requires teeth gathered from the prairie wolf alphas that stalk the shadow of Thunder Bluff. As apex predators of the rolling grassy plains, these alphas represent the raw strength of the wild. Offering their teeth honors the balance between hunter, prey, and the spirits of the earth.

item:prairie-wolf-heart.text: Prairie Wolf Heart. A Prairie Wolf Heart is a vital organ harvested from the wolves roaming the grasslands of Mulgore. It serves as an essential ingredient in an urgent folk remedy prepared by Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village to counteract venomous infection. The wolves of the plains are fierce predators, hardy and persistent across the sweeping grasses of Mulgore. Their hearts are sought out by Maur Raincaller, a tauren residing in Bloodhoof Village who fell victim to the legendary plainstrider known as Mazzranache. Struck by the creature's virulent, fever-inducing venom, Maur relies on traditional plains medicine to halt the spreading poison. Alongside other potent reagents like cougar bone and bird gizzard, the vital essence of a freshly slain prairie wolf provides the cleansing properties needed to concoct a cure before delirium proves fatal.

item:prairie-wolf-paw.text: Prairie Wolf Paw. Prairie Wolf Paws are harvested from the predators roaming the plains of Mulgore. Shamanic practitioners, such as Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, use them as organic components to bind the natural power of the land into cleansing totems. Prairie wolves stalk the rolling grasses across Mulgore, hunting in packs alongside prairie stalkers and their pack alphas. While dangerous to young hunters and local livestock, the creatures are deeply intertwined with the spiritual balance of the plains. Tauren shamans view the wolf's paws not merely as trophies, but as vital conduits of the earth's innate vitality. When goblin ventures tainted Mulgore's sacred water reserves, shaman Mull Thunderhorn required the physical aid of the land itself to counteract the pollution. Bound together with plainstrider talons, the wolf paws provide the raw spiritual resonance necessary to fashion cleansing totems, beginning the vital work of purifying the Winterhoof Water Well.

item:pridewing-venom-sac.text: Pridewing Venom Sac. Pridewing Venom Sacs are harvested from the lethal wyverns nesting around Mirkfallon Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. The night elves of Astranaar seek to stockpile and destroy these sacs after intelligence suggests Horde operatives harvest the potent poison for covert assassinations. The pridewings of Stonetalon are dangerous, airborne predators native to the peaks south of Ashenvale, particularly around Mirkfallon Lake. While wild wyverns are naturally venomous, Alliance intelligence out of Theramore suggests that Horde assassins have begun milking them for poison to coat blades used in covert raids against night elf settlements. To safeguard their kin and disrupt enemy supplies, the Sentinels in Astranaar hire scouts to hunt down the beasts and collect the venom glands before the Horde can secure them.

item:prismatic-punch-card.text: Prismatic Punch Card. The Prismatic Punch Card is the highest security clearance data card found within the fallen city of Gnomeregan. Upgraded sequentially through a series of Matrix Punchograph terminals, it holds data desperately sought by gnome refugees in Ironforge. When the gnomes fled the trogg invasion and toxic irradiation of Gnomeregan, massive troves of research and civic records were abandoned in the depths. To safeguard high-level systems, the gnomes utilized an escalating security protocol. Accessing the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminal in the lower Engineering Labs requires working through a progression of punch cards: starting from a basic White Punch Card and advancing through Yellow, Blue, and Red clearances at dedicated terminals before stamping the final Prismatic Punch Card. Its encoded clearance level is whimsically noted as pending the invention of an entirely new number.

item:pristine-spider-silk.text: Pristine Spider Silk. Pristine Spider Silk is an exceptionally fine thread gathered from the venomous arachnids of Duskwood. Mages of Stormwind commission this rare material to weave durable, enchanted robes worthy of recognized practitioners of the arcane arts. Not just any thread can hold the enchantments and wear demanded by a practicing mage. While ordinary spider silk is common enough among tailors, only the immaculate strands taken from carrion recluses and black widow hatchlings in the shadowed groves of Duskwood possess the necessary resilience. The mages of Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum send their rising adepts into these perilous woods to harvest pristine spools, tasking local master tailor Wynne Larson with fashioning the material into a garment fit for an adept.

item:prowler-claws.text: Prowler Claws. Prowler Claws are severed trophies collected from the savannah prowlers that stalk the sun-baked plains of the Barrens. Brought to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads, they serve as tangible proof that a hunter can stalk and overpower Kalimdor's deadliest stealth predators. The tall grasses of the Barrens conceal Savannah Prowlers, large feline predators known for their patience, cunning, and lethal strikes. Hunting them is a vital proving ground for rising Horde warriors and scouts. Unlike herbivorous quarry like the plainstrider or the zhevra, prowlers actively ambush anything entering their hunting grounds. Taking their sharp, curved claws requires besting a creature that relies on absolute stealth and territorial aggression, proving to the camp's huntress that the stalker has become the prey. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn demands these claws to measure an initiate's readiness for greater trials. Bringing back a handful of claws demonstrates that a hunter has mastered tracking among the golden savannah grass and can withstand claws capable of tearing leather and flesh. Those who return with their prize show they possess the awareness needed to survive even deadlier beasts lurking across the plains.

item:pure-hearts.text: Pure Hearts. Pure Hearts are ritual reagents provided to Forsaken warlocks by Carendin Halgar in the Undercity. They are used to lure and manifest a succubus across the Twisting Nether so the practitioner can defeat and bind the demon. Demonology relies on exploiting base desires and spiritual vulnerabilities. To summon a succubus into the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Carendin Halgar provides warlocks with Pure Hearts. When placed upon the summoning circle, these untainted spiritual essences act as potent bait, drawing the seductive demon across the Twisting Nether into the mortal realm. Once the demon manifests, the warlock must resist her enthralling mind-charms and strike her down in combat. Overcoming the succubus asserts mystical dominance, banishing her back to the Twisting Nether until Carendin teaches the warlock the spell to summon her forth at will.

item:purified-kor-gem.text: Purified Kor Gem. A Purified Kor Gem is a rare, consecrated crystal required by the weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell outside Ironforge. Once tainted by dark energies, it must be reclaimed from the depths of Kalimdor and cleansed by elven magic before it can be forged into a holy arm of the Light. The stone begins its journey as a Corrupted Kor Gem in the possession of the vile naga lurking within Blackfathom Deeps, deep beneath the coast of Ashenvale. To cleanse the stone of its aquatic, shadowy taint, a paladin must seek out the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Drawing upon arcane and natural arts, Thundris purges the corruption from the stone, transforming it into the radiant Purified Kor Gem. Only in this pristine state is it fit to serve as a conduit for holy power. Outside Ironforge in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh, the human weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell requires the gem as a key component for forging a masterwork weapon. Having long possessed designs for an armament worthy of the Silver Hand, Stilwell lacked the exotic materials to realize his plans. The Purified Kor Gem, alongside Whitestone Oak Lumber and rare ore, provides the spiritual core necessary to channel the paladin's righteous wrath.

item:putrid-claw.text: Putrid Claw. Putrid Claws are the decaying hands severed from mindless undead prowling the woods west of Brill. Deathguard Dillinger collects them as definitive proof that the encroaching Scourge threat near the old bridge is being held at bay. Even in their own homeland, the Forsaken are not entirely safe from the Lich King's reach. Pockets of mindless Scourge—rotting dead and ravaged corpses—regularly wander across the eastern borders into Tirisfal Glades, clustering along roads and near the old bridge west of Brill. To ensure the safety of travelers and garrison supply lines, the Deathguards place bounties on these wandering horrors. A severed putrid claw serves as unmistakable, physical evidence that one more shambling corpse has been put down for good.

item:pyrewood-shackle.text: Pyrewood Shackle. Pyrewood Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by the beleaguered inhabitants of Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest. Imbued with the strange magic of Archmage Arugal, these bands are linked to the eerie curse that transforms ordinary townsfolk into ravenous worgen once night falls. The cursed village of Pyrewood holds an unsettling secret: by day, its residents carry on ordinary lives appearing as typical humans, but the setting sun twists them into feral Moonrage worgen. Archmage Arugal bound these villagers in enchanted shackles as part of his twisted experiments with worgen sorcery. Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane researcher stationed at the Sepulcher for the Forsaken, studies these shackles to decode the enchantments driving this dual existence. By gathering and analyzing the lingering energy on the bands, Dawnweaver seeks a deeper understanding of Arugal's magic in hopes of unraveling the mad archmage's hold over the region.

item:quinn-s-potion.text: Quinn's Potion. Quinn's Potion is a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel in the Sepulcher. It is brewed to stabilize and revitalize the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick following a disastrous scouting patrol in Silverpine Forest. After Deathstalker Quinn Yorick was severely battered and incapacitated near the Ivar Patch, word reached the Royal Apothecary Society at the Sepulcher. Apothecary Renferrel hastily compounded this specialized draught to facilitate Quinn's recovery. While Renferrel rarely lets minor field casualties distract him from his grander, more sinister research for Lady Sylvanas, he provided the restorative to get the injured scout back on his feet and capable of travel.

item:ran-bloodtooth-s-skull.text: Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. Ran Bloodtooth's Skull is a grisly trophy taken from the chieftain of the corrupted furbolgs in Ashenvale. Brought back to the night elves of Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that a ferocious threat to the woodland realm has been ended. The forests of Ashenvale have suffered immensely from demonic taint and wilderness corruption, driving once-peaceful furbolg tribes into murderous madness. Among the fiercest of these hostile chieftains was Ran Bloodtooth. Recovering his skull provides the night elf Sentinels with definite proof that the brute has fallen, breaking his hold over the local furbolgs and offering a small measure of respite to the beleaguered town of Astranaar.

item:raptor-head.text: Raptor Head. A severed raptor head serves as bloody proof of a beast slain in the Barrens. Gazrog of the Crossroads demands these macabre trophies to purge the local packs after an improbable theft of guard payroll. Life in the arid plains of the Barrens is harsh enough without local wildlife raiding settlement towers. When a chest containing guard payroll vanished from the Crossroads watchtower, the defenders caught an improbable culprit red-handed: a wild raptor. Perplexed and furious, Gazrog placed an immediate bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the savannah. Bringing severed raptor heads back to the outpost proves that these predatory pests are being culled before they can pilfer any more Horde supplies.

item:rare-earth.text: Rare Earth. Rare Earth is a specialized package of mineral-rich soil procured from Darnassus for botanic experiments on Teldrassil. It is sent via courier from Dolanaar to the herbalist researcher Denalan at his lakeside camp near Lake Al'Ameth. Teldrassil's newly grown ecosystem requires careful observation and nurturing, prompting herbalists across the island to study how various plants respond to foreign or enriched soils. This particular parcel of rare earth was requisitioned directly from Darnassus by Denalan, an eccentric botanist stationed along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. After languishing in transit and turning up late in Dolanaar, herbalist Syral Bladeleaf entrusts travelers passing south to deliver the perishable soil to Denalan before its potency fades.

item:rattlecage-skull.text: Rattlecage Skull. Rattlecage Skulls are the shattered remnants of mindless undead roaming the ruined outskirts of Deathknell. Novice Forsaken warlocks must gather these calcified trophies for Venya Marthand to demonstrate their emerging will and qualify for the dark arts of summoning. Within the sunless bounds of Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken with an affinity for dark magic are guided by Venya Marthand. To prove that a fledgling practitioner has the fortitude to bend extraplanar creatures to their command, Venya tasks them with subduing the lingering Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy. Striking down these lesser undead and retrieving their severed skulls serves as both a practical test of discipline and a ritual foundation before learning to breach the void and enslave a first demonic minion.

item:raven-claw-talisman.text: Raven Claw Talisman. The Raven Claw Talisman is a sacred night elf relic tied to the Druids of the Talon. Kept deep within Ban'ethil Barrow Den on Teldrassil, it is one of the four essential Relics of Wakening required to safely guide slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman is preserved within a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the subterranean sanctuary where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered their deep meditative slumbers. Druidic hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. If a druid's link to the waking world is shattered without the proper ceremonial focus, their spirit risks being stranded within the Emerald Dream indefinitely. Alongside the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting, the talisman is required by Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to conduct the ritual of awakening and bring the slumberers back safely. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the sacred chests and the sleeping druids fell into immediate peril. The furbolg desecration severed the sanctum from outside aid and put the relics in danger of being lost or destroyed. Athridas Bearmantle tasks defenders of Teldrassil with braving the winding earthen corridors of the den to secure the Raven Claw Talisman before the displaced druids are lost to the Dream forever.

item:razorflank-s-medallion.text: Razorflank's Medallion. Razorflank's Medallion is a personal token carried by Charlga Razorflank, the crone ruling over Razorfen Kraul. Recovered from the heart of the quilboar stronghold, it serves as undeniable proof that the matriarch has been brought down. Carried by Charlga Razorflank herself, this medallion represents the authority of the crone who leads the Razorfen quilboar. When Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar learns of the fates of fallen explorers like Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, he tasks Alliance adventurers with striking directly at the quilboar leader. Presenting the crone's medallion confirms her death, reassuring the night elf sentinels guarding the borders of Feralas that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

item:reagent-pouch-shaman.text: Reagent Pouch (shaman). A reagent pouch carried by Burning Blade cultists lurking in the crags of Durotar. Shaman seeking to communing with fire require these gathered spell components to distill their initial fire sapta. To forge a fire sapta and attune a young shaman to the spirits of flame, specific ritual catalysts are vital. Cultists of the Burning Blade carry small satchels stocked with reagents tailored for demonic fire conjurations. The hermit Telf Joolam uses these gathered powders and oils, combined with the fire tar of Razormane quilboar, to craft the draught needed to grant sight into the realm of fire. Though the Burning Blade perverts flame for destruction and fel sorcery, the physical elements within their pouches remain bound to the primal nature of heat and combustion. Shamanic philosophy maintains that all elemental forces exist in tension: fire is both creator and destroyer. By taking the cultists' stolen tools, a shaman reclaims the elemental medium to awaken genuine communion with the spirits.

item:reconstructed-tome.text: Reconstructed Tome. The Reconstructed Tome is a pieced-together grimoire of dark cabal lore, compiled for warlocks seeking to expand their mastery of demonic servants. It contains the arcane knowledge and rituals necessary to summon and bind a predatory felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Recovered in fragments and painstakingly pieced back together, the Reconstructed Tome represents an elusive collection of cabal teachings known formally as the Tome of the Cabal. Warlocks of both the Alliance and the Horde go to great lengths to restore its frayed leaves, consulting occult scholars eager for a mere glimpse of its esoteric contents before surrendering the completed manuscript.

item:recruitment-letter.text: Recruitment Letter. The Recruitment Letter is an official dispatch handed to promising adventurers departing Durotar for duty in the Barrens. Issued by scout Takrin Pathseeker, it directs able-bodied volunteers to report to the border outpost overseen by Kargal Battlescar. As young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill, the Horde's gaze turns west toward the vast, untamed expanse of the Barrens. Takrin Pathseeker identifies promising recruits who appear strong enough to handle frontline service and provides them with this letter. Crossing the Southfury River bridge marks a rite of passage: leaving the sheltered red dirt of Durotar behind to join the ranks of the Horde standing guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts. The letter's intended recipient is Kargal Battlescar, the grizzled veteran managing the outpost just across the river. Kargal evaluates each conscript before formally signing off on their enlistment. Yet holding this letter is only the first step; frontier outposts are perpetually stretched thin, and any signed recruit is swiftly redirected further west to the strategic hub of the Crossroads.

item:red-burlap-bandana.text: Red Burlap Bandana. Red Burlap Bandanas are the crude, dyed cloth masks worn by low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Defias Brotherhood. In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem collects these pieces of cloth as proof of slain thieves encroaching near the abbey vineyards. Worn across the lower face, the red burlap bandana serves as the identifying badge of the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Made from cheap, rough fabric and soaked in red dye, the cloth conceals a thief's features while signaling allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards, unaware that the local guards use the striking red fabric as a grim bounty marker.

item:red-leather-bandana.text: Red Leather Bandana. A signature piece of attire worn by members of the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall. Crafted from dyed crimson leather, it serves as both a practical face covering and an unmistakable symbol of defiance against the Crown of Stormwind. Across the dusty fields and abandoned farms of Westfall, these crimson bandanas conceal the faces of highwaymen, looters, and rebellious laborers. To the People's Militia stationed at Sentinel Hill, the headwear is more than simple cloth—it is concrete proof of allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. Scout Galiaan collects these bandanas from passing adventurers to monitor the shifting movements and dwindling numbers of the brotherhood throughout the region.

item:red-linen-bandana.text: Red Linen Bandana. A red linen bandana is the distinctive facial mask worn by members of the Defias Brotherhood across Elwynn Forest. Beyond concealing a bandit's identity, the cloth is woven from quality linen that resourceful locals often repurpose into useful garments. While lower-ranking initiates and common thugs in Northshire Valley make do with coarse burlap face masks, full-fledged Defias operatives throughout Elwynn Forest wear woven red linen bandanas. The bright crimson fabric serves as both a uniform and a statement of allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity, disguising faces while signaling insurrection against the crown of Stormwind. Despite their violent associations, the bandanas are cut from respectable yardage. Pragmatic settlers like Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp routinely ask travelers to collect them from outlaw encampments. With a bit of washing and needlework, the contraband cloth is transformed into sturdy clothing and bandages for the working folk of the forest.

item:red-wool-bandana.text: Red Wool Bandana. Red Wool Bandanas are makeshift symbols fashioned by imprisoned Defias cutthroats inside the Stormwind Stockade. Torn from jailhouse wool blankets, they serve as defiant emblems of brotherhood even behind bars. Even locked deep within the high stone walls of the Stormwind Stockade, members of the Defias Brotherhood refuse to surrender their identity. Using scraps torn from prison wool blankets, inmates secretly craft red bandanas to wear as identifying colors. To the guards, these scarves are contraband that spark fatal mutinies; to the prisoners, they are a statement that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains. The bandanas gained a bitter notoriety after fourteen-year-old prison guard Mac Raskol caught inmates shredding blankets to make them. When he attempted to discipline the prisoners, the Defias convicts stabbed him in the back. In the wake of his death, his grieving grandmother Nikova seeks out adventurers to venture into the rioting dungeon, cull the rioters, and retrieve the crimson cloth as proof of vengeance.

item:remaining-drops-of-purest-water.text: Remaining Drops of Purest Water. The Remaining Drops of Purest Water are the final residue of a specialized draught prepared by the water seer Brine. Shaman carrying these potent drops travel across kingdoms to cleanse a sacred water shrine corrupted by the Scourge's undead plague. Forged through ritual gathering across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, this concentrated elixir retains the purest essence of clean water, prepared by the hermit Brine in the Barrens. While part of the draught is consumed to grant shaman vision of distant elements, the remaining drops are safeguarded for a far more perilous task. Carried to the plague-choked shores of Silverpine Forest near the Sepulcher, the drops serve as the vital purifying catalyst atop the Brazier of Everfount. Consumed in ritual flames alongside the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental, this pure water cuts through the necrotic corruption, calling forth an untainted spirit of water to commune with the shaman and complete their communion with the element.

item:remedy-of-arugal.text: Remedy of Arugal. The Remedy of Arugal is an incantation penned by the mage Arugal during his early experiments with worgen magic. Left behind in a dilapidated farmhouse in Silverpine Forest, the spell is sought by Dalar Dawnweaver to unravel the sorcerer's dark work. Before seizing Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal took refuge at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. There, amidst forgotten farm tools and rotting floorboards, he documented his strange arts in a set of dusty spellbooks. The scroll titled the Remedy of Arugal is among these notes, outlining early methods and magical formulations he devised while dabbling in the dangerous transmutations that cursed the local populace. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished Forsaken spellcaster operating from the Sepulcher, holds little respect for Arugal's pedigree, dismissing the former Dalaran wizard's intellect as fragile and transparent. Even so, Dawnweaver recognizes the urgent need to understand the exact mechanics behind the worgen curse. By recovering the Remedy of Arugal, Forsaken agents provide Dawnweaver with the foundational arcana required to counter Arugal's spreading menace and secure Silverpine for Lady Sylvanas.

item:rendered-spores.text: Rendered Spores. Rendered Spores are a volatile emulsion prepared from fungal samples gathered across the Barrens. Created by Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads, the mixture decays rapidly unless swiftly delivered to Apothecary Zamah beneath Thunder Bluff for stabilizing. After acquiring strange fungal spores from mushrooms near the damp oases of the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim processes them into an active chemical emulsion known as Rendered Spores. The delicate extraction suspends the potent compounds of the fungal growths in a liquid medium, but the solution is chemically unstable. It maintains its vital potency for only forty-five minutes before breaking down and becoming completely useless for scientific study. Because Helbrim lacks the necessary facilities or time at his remote outpost to complete the refining process, the emulsion must be rushed directly to his Forsaken colleague, Apothecary Zamah. Hidden away in the subterranean Pools of Vision beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff, Zamah possesses the specialized equipment and reagents needed to reseal and finish processing the spores for the Royal Apothecary Society.

item:renferrel-s-findings.text: Renferrel's Findings. Renferrel's Findings is a collection of research notes compiled by Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Entrusted to Horde couriers, these documents carry vital data southward to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to assist in brewing the Forsaken's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society labours tirelessly under direct orders from the Dark Lady, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, to engineer a New Plague. Achieving this breakthrough requires constant collaboration among researchers scattered across Lordaeron. Stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel compiles these findings to document his progress and experiments, sending the gathered intelligence south to Tarren Mill so fellow researchers can build upon his results. Carrying these papers across the border from Silverpine into the Hillsbrad Foothills represents a vital link in the Forsaken's alchemical network. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon eagerly awaits Renferrel's notes to cross-reference and advance his own concoctions against the living and the Scourge. Without reliable couriers running the contested roads of Hillsbrad, the Society's decentralized research would quickly stall.

item:report-on-the-defias-brotherhood.text: Report on the Defias Brotherhood. The Report on the Defias Brotherhood is an official document compiled by City Architect Baros Alexston, detailing the activities and threat posed by Edwin VanCleef's conspirators. Intended to inform the royal court, it is entrusted to the adventurer who uncovered the Deadmines plot for personal delivery to Stormwind Keep. Following the long investigation into the unrest plaguing Westfall and the surrounding territories, City Architect Baros Alexston prepared this formal report to alert the leadership of Stormwind to the full scope of the Defias threat. Rather than sending a standard royal messenger, Alexston entrusted the document to the very hero who untangled the conspiracy. Delivered directly to Stormwind Keep, the report is meant to accompany a personal audience detailing Edwin VanCleef's schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

item:resonite-crystal.text: Resonite Crystal. Resonite Crystals are rare mineral samples mined by kobolds inside Boulderslide Cavern in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their frantic digging has drawn the concern of Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat.

item:restabilization-cog.text: Restabilization Cog. Restabilization Cogs are precision mechanical components salvaged from the leper gnomes wandering outside the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. In Kharanos, gnomish tinkerers require these intact parts to construct the Recombobulator, an ambitious machine intended to reverse leper mutation. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a disastrous attempt to wipe out the invading troggs, countless gnomes were twisted into sick, hostile leper gnomes. Despite their madness, these afflicted exiles still carry intricate gnomish machinery and salvageable fittings. Tinkers Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the horrific transformation can be systematically undone. To finish their prototype Recombobulation Device, they rely on adventurers to recover vital parts directly from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates, including intact Restabilization Cogs to balance the machine's inner combustion systems.

item:ring-of-zoram.text: Ring of Zoram. The Ring of Zoram is an ancient Kaldorei heirloom dating back to the glory days of the sunken city of Zoram before the Great Sundering. Once worn by the city's rulers and the key to the ancient lock of a sunken statuette, it recently fell into the hands of the encroaching coastal naga. Before the Well of Eternity collapsed and the oceans swallowed the western reaches of Kalimdor, Zoram was a coastal jewel of the night elven empire. The Ring of Zoram belonged to the rulers of the city, and a strange code is written upon its inner band in the language of the night elves. When the Great Sundering shattered the continent ten thousand years ago, the ring sank along with the city, lost beneath the crashing tides of what is now the Zoram Strand. For millennia, the ring remained buried beneath silt and ruins until the naga began scouring the coastline of Ashenvale. Ruuzel, a naga leader dwelling on an islet off the northern strand, uncovered the artifact among the sunken debris. Scholars like the night elf Talen seek the ring not merely for its antiquity, but because it functions as the only key capable of unlocking other relics salvaged from the depths, including sealed ancient statuettes recovered from the sea floor.

item:robo-mechanical-guts.text: Robo-Mechanical Guts. Robo-Mechanical Guts are salvagable gearworks, conduits, and machine innards harvested from the malfunctioning constructs roaming the ruins of Gnomeregan. Gnomish engineers in Stormwind require these specific components to repair heavy tunneling vehicles meant to aid in the reclamation of Gnomeregan in Dun Morogh. When High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and the surviving gnomes evacuated Gnomeregan, thousands of automated mechanisms, clockwork sentries, and industrial robots were abandoned inside. In the city's radioactive aftermath, these machines continue to roam the corridors autonomously. In Stormwind City, the tinker Shoni seeks to assemble a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators to pierce the defenses of Gnomeregan and reclaim the lost city. Lacking fresh raw materials, she tasks bold adventurers with braving the contaminated halls of Gnomeregan to carve out functional robot viscera—springs, wires, and gyro-components—to refit the excavation machinery.

item:rocket-car-parts.text: Rocket Car Parts. Rocket Car Parts are the scattered, twisted metal remains of high-speed collisions across the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Constantly generated by reckless gnome and goblin racers pushing experimental speeders past their limits, these salvaged scraps are harvested by opportunists looking to turn racetrack accidents into quick coin. The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is the staging ground for an unending, combustible rivalry between goblin and gnome engineering. In their pursuit of unmatched land speed, racers regularly suffer catastrophic breakdowns, explosive misfires, and high-velocity crashes that scatter metal across the salt flats. These discarded remnants—ranging from bent cylinders and burnt gears to crushed sheet metal—do not stay abandoned for long. Scavengers and merchants, most notably the opportunistic dwarf Kravel Koalbeard, hire passing adventurers to comb the blinding white expanse and collect the debris. Because both racing teams are perpetually desperate for spare machinery to patch together their next prototype, scavenged wreckage can easily be resold directly back to the very teams that wrecked it.

item:rod-of-channeling.text: Rod of Channeling. A Rod of Channeling is an arcane focus carried by spellcasters of the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. Warlocks seeking to master the summoning of a felhunter must gather several of these rods for Strahad Farsan's acolytes to safely anchor the ritual circle in Ratchet. When a warlock seeks to bind a predator as volatile as a felhunter, raw willpower is rarely enough. Strahad Farsan requires three matched rods to allow his acolytes to channel their magic in concert, stabilizing the summoning circle while the practitioner undertakes the binding. The Dragonmaw clan's darkcasters, including the bonewarders and shadowwarders haunting the Angerfang Encampment and surrounding ruins in the Wetlands, carry these implements for their own fell workings. Though typically worn and nicked from combat, the rods remain potent focuses capable of directing chaotic nether energy.

item:rot-blossom.text: Rot Blossom. Rot Blossoms are foul, necrotic flora found growing among the desecrated graves of Duskwood. Fed by the blighted soil and undead remains, they are sought after for their potent, unwholesome alchemical properties. Duskwood's unnatural corruption breeds bizarre and disturbing plant life, none more unsettling than the Rot Blossom. Rooted in the defiled earth of graveyards such as the Tranquil Gardens Cemetery, these morbid blooms thrive in proximity to death. Local rumors claim they can even take root within the cracked skulls of the walking dead, particularly Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends that stalk the barrows. To the locals in Darkshire, harvesting them is both a grim chore and a dangerous necessity, as disturbing their soil means braving the unrested dead. Despite their repulsive nature, Rot Blossoms serve a specialized purpose in local concoctions. The blooms contain dark essences required to brew Zombie Juice, a foul draft tied to Duskwood's macabre survival efforts. Those dispatched to gather the blossoms often find themselves inadvertently aiding the Night Watch, culling the restless skeletons that wander the haunted gravesites in the process.

item:rot-hide-ichor.text: Rot Hide Ichor. Rot Hide Ichor is a foul bodily fluid harvested from the undead Rot Hide gnolls infesting Fenris Isle in Lordamere Lake. Apothecary Renferrel collects samples of the substance at the Sepulcher to uncover the origin of the gnolls' corruption and devise a strategy against them. The Rot Hide gnolls of Fenris Isle are not ordinary wild beasts; they are visibly decomposed and twisted by unnatural blight. Rather than normal blood, their veins pump a noxious ichor that sustains their animated flesh. The Royal Apothecary Society suspects that this fluid holds the secret to how the pack was corrupted and who commands them from within the ruined keep of Fenris Isle. Apothecary Renferrel gathers vials of this ichor to analyze its properties at the Sepulcher. By isolating the chemical and magical components fueling the gnolls, the Forsaken hope to pinpoint vulnerabilities before committing troops to a full-scale assault across Lordamere Lake.

item:rough-quartz.text: Rough Quartz. Rough Quartz is a humble elemental stone gifted to novice shaman by a Minor Manifestation of Earth. Though small and unrefined, it serves as the vital spiritual core needed to craft a shaman's first Earth Totem. To the untrained eye, rough quartz appears to be nothing more than an ordinary desert pebble. Yet to a shaman communing with the spirits in Durotar or Mulgore, it is an elemental gift offered directly by a Minor Manifestation of Earth. The stone represents endurance, patience, and unwavering strength. When presented to an elder such as Canaga Earthcaller in the Valley of Trials, the quartz is bound into the carved wood of an Earth Totem, acting as the spiritual focus that links the fledgling shaman directly to the living soil of Azeroth.

item:rumbleshot-s-ammo.text: Rumbleshot's Ammo. Rumbleshot's Ammo is a mislaid crate of munitions bound for the gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot in Dun Morogh. Lost when a frightened courier fled from hungry wendigos, the heavy crate sits abandoned in the snow near the Grizzled Den. Hegnar Rumbleshot operates a roadside arms shop along the mountain path leading down from Coldridge Pass toward Anvilmar. With Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar teams constantly drilling in the snowy heights, his supplies burn away almost as fast as powder catches flame. This particular shipment of shot was dispatched by Loslor from Kharanos, but never reached the shelves. The courier tasked with transporting it pitched camp too close to the predatory wendigos of the Grizzled Den, panicked when attacked, and fled for his life, leaving the heavy supply crate sitting deep within the beast's hunting grounds.

item:rune-inscribed-parchment.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. A written missive delivered to aspiring orc shamans in the Valley of Trials. Penned by the trainer Shikrik and handed out by Gornek, it calls initiates to embrace their role as spiritual leaders and conduits for the elemental spirits. Within the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, new orc shamans begin their training under the watchful gaze of veteran overseers. While performing initial trials for Gornek, an initiate is handed this rune-covered document. Sent directly by Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor, the parchment serves as a formal summons into the deeper mysteries of elemental communion. Orcish culture regards the shaman not merely as a battlefield spellcaster, but as an essential mediator between the living and the ancestors. This brief writ marks the transition from simple brute strength to the disciplined path of ancestral reverence.

item:rune-inscribed-pendant.text: Rune-Inscribed Pendant. The Rune-Inscribed Pendant is a magical trinket recovered from Dalaran supply shipments destined for Ambermill. Prized by the Kirin Tor, these pendants serve as conduits for channeling potent arcane energies. Discovered among crates of cartographic supplies bound for the Dalaran enclave at Ambermill, this pendant bears intricate arcane inscriptions. High-ranking wizards of the Kirin Tor frequently employ such artifacts to focus and amplify their spellcasting. The presence of numerous channeled pendants moving into the region immediately draws the suspicion of the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, signaling an impending project of immense magical power.

item:rune-inscribed-tablet.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. A Rune-Inscribed Tablet is a stone message delivered to young Darkspear troll shamans in the Valley of Trials. Handed over by Gornek, it directs promising mystics to begin formal communion with the elements under the tutelage of the orc trainer Shikrik. Carved with elemental runes, this tablet serves as a formal invitation for burgeoning troll shamans taking their first steps in Durotar. When an initiate demonstrates their mettle in the Valley of Trials, the overseer Gornek presents the stone, sent by the troll shaman Ishi-yo to direct the initiate to the shaman trainer Shikrik. For the Darkspear trolls—who hold deep spiritual traditions of their own—the tablet marks the beginning of their shared path with the orcs, bridging ancient troll mysticism with the revitalized shamanic heritage championed by Warchief Thrall.

item:rune-of-nesting.text: Rune of Nesting. The Rune of Nesting is one of the four sacred Relics of Wakening kept within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den on Teldrassil. It is an essential component in the delicate druidic ritual required to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druids undergo deep, cyclical hibernations within underground barrow dens to commune with nature through the Emerald Dream. Waking from this profound trance is not simply a matter of stirring; it requires a precise ritual guided by sacred instruments. The Rune of Nesting, kept safely within the Chest of Nesting deep in the winding chambers of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, anchors this process. Alongside the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, and the Sapphire of Sky, the rune serves as a conduit to call the Druids of the Talon back to the waking world. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the barrow's slumbering defenders were placed in immediate peril. Without access to their relics, the druids risked being trapped within the Emerald Dream indefinitely while invaders desecrated their sanctuary. Recovering the Rune of Nesting and its companion artifacts allows Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to prepare the ritual necessary to safely awaken the endangered druids.

item:runes-of-summoning.text: Runes of Summoning. The Runes of Summoning are a ritual item provided by the warlock trainer Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. They are used to call forth an unbound voidwalker into a summoning circle so that an aspiring warlock may bend it to their will. Within the dark recesses of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners of the dark arts study the manipulation of the Nether. Carendin Halgar entrusts the Runes of Summoning only to warlocks who have prepared themselves to take command of a voidwalker. By casting the runes within the active summoning circle below Halgar's station, the practitioner tears through the fabric of the Void, drawing forth a creature that must be overpowered and bound into servitude.

item:sack-of-murloc-heads.text: Sack of Murloc Heads. The Sack of Murloc Heads is a gruesome bundle collected along the beaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assembled as proof of military action against local shore pests, it is pawned off by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle onto passing adventurers for delivery to Marshal Redpath in Southshore. Southshore stands under constant siege from Syndicate outlaws, Forsaken skirmishers, and wild murlocs crowding the coast. To secure funding and favor from town leadership, local officers must demonstrate that coastal threats are actively being culled. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gathers proof in the form of severed heads, but the distasteful nature of the cargo—and his own squeamishness—prompts him to hand the dripping sack off to travelers rather than deliver the grisly evidence to Marshal Redpath himself.

item:sack-of-supplies.text: Sack of Supplies. These supply sacks belong to a caravan shipment intended for the goblin engineer Rezlak outside Orgrimmar. Transported across Durotar, the goods were intercepted by the Dustwind harpies roosting in the crags of Razorwind Canyon. Rezlak, an engineer contracted out of Ratchet by Gazlowe, relies on regular caravans through Durotar to supply his construction efforts for the Horde. Durotar's wilderness, however, is far from tame. When a promised shipment passed near the canyon road south of Orgrimmar, it was ambushed and pillaged by the local Dustwind harpies. The vicious creatures hauled the cargo deep into their roosts within Razorwind Canyon, scattering the sacks among the dirt and scree alongside harpy nesting sites.

item:salty-scorpid-venom.text: Salty Scorpid Venom. Salty Scorpid Venom is a caustic fluid harvested from the scorpids stalking the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Packed with natural salts from the desert floor, it is prized by gnomish rocket racers attempting to engineer volatile, ultra-hot fuel. The scorpids crawling the arid expanse of the Shimmering Flats have adapted to an intensely mineral-rich environment. Over generations, the venom of beasts like the Scorpid Reavers and Scorpid Terrors has absorbed enormous quantities of local salt. Rather than brewing antidotes or standard poisons, gnomish tinkers like Fizzle Brassbolts prize this caustic compound as a prospective additive for high-combustion engine fuel. Out at the Mirage Raceway, the engineering competition between gnomes and goblins drives inventors to test increasingly dangerous materials in their rocket cars. Fizzle Brassbolts believes boiling down the salted venom, treating it with specialized catalysts, and mixing it into propellant tanks will deliver the blazing heat necessary to outrun goblin racers on the salt pans.

item:samophlange-item.text: Samophlange (item). The samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical component recovered from the deep interior of an automated control console in the Barrens. Despite its complex appearance, its precise function remains an engineering mystery even to the goblin mechanics who sought it. Tucked away behind a labyrinth of superfluous wiring and hollow tubing within a Barrens control console lies the samophlange. It takes some rooting through deliberately confounding machinery just to unseat it from its housing. To the untrained eye, it appears to be an essential nexus of clockwork and steam-driven technology. To goblin tinkerers, it is an irresistible mechanical puzzle intended for shipment to the Tinkers' Union in Undermine—though its fragile build means it rarely survives casual handling long enough to be understood.

item:samophlange-manual.text: Samophlange Manual. The Samophlange Manual is a technical operating guide detailing the inner workings of the elusive samophlange. Kept under tight lock and key by the Venture Company, its scattered pages hold the instructions needed by goblin engineers to repair and operate the bizarre contraption. Engineering schematics and operating handbooks are guarded like gold among goblin enterprises, and the Samophlange Manual is no exception. While working within the Venture Company, an ambitious overseer named Boss Copperplug jealously hoarded knowledge regarding the device, distributing only scattered pages to his most loyal subordinates to retain control over the machinery. When the device fell out of Venture Company clutches, repairing it proved impossible without assembling the torn, distributed documentation from the overseer and his crew at the Boulder Lode Mine. After breaking ties with the Venture Company, the goblin engineer Rilli Greasygob took up residence in Orgrimmar with hopes of mastering the samophlange's construction. Lacking Copperplug's favor during his former employment, Rilli relies on enterprising travelers to retrieve the handbook's cover and loose leaves. Reconstructing the handbook offers goblin tinkerers working alongside the Horde a rare window into proprietary Venture Company engineering.

item:sample-ichor.text: Sample Ichor. This vial contains a refined extract of the foul fluid that sustains the rot hide gnolls of Silverpine Forest. Distilled down to its base components by Apothecary Renferrel, the substance carries lingering traces of both necromancy and warlock sorcery. The Rot Hide gnolls that prowl Silverpine Forest are no ordinary beasts. After recovering samples from the creatures and their lingering remnants, Apothecary Renferrel of the Royal Apothecary Society reduced the vile liquid into its constituent elements. His chemical breakdown revealed that the ichor was artificially manufactured through a convergence of dark schools: necromantic rites woven together with warlock magics. Because the craft behind it borders on arcane disciplines outside simple alchemy, Renferrel packaged this sample and dispatched it to the Undercity for Bethor Iceshard to examine with divination.

item:sample-of-zanzil-s-altered-mixture.text: Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. This vial contains a potent specimen of a concoction brewed by the witch doctor Zanzil, recovered during a covert infiltration in the Barrens. Carried by an operative suffering from its debilitating effects, the sample is sent across the sea to Tarren Mill in hopes of unlocking both an antidote and the lethal secrets of poisoncraft.
