After infiltrating the Venture Company's tower near the Sludge Fen and looting the cache of Zanzil's mixture from Gallywix's lockbox, an operative ends up afflicted by Zanzil's foul touch. Shenthul orders the stricken agent across the Great Sea with a sample of the brew in hand. Finding a cure means locating Serge Hinott, an apothecary stationed at Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills, who possesses the rare expertise required to isolate the toxin and decipher its components.

item:sample-snapjaw-shell.text: Sample Snapjaw Shell. A Sample Snapjaw Shell is a durable tortoise carapace harvested from the freshwater oases of the Barrens. Remarkable for its lingering vitality, it is sent across the Great Sea to aid druidic research into rejuvenating the blighted woodlands of Silverpine Forest. The snapping turtles that dwell in the lush, anomaly-tinged oases of the Barrens possess shells of surprising vigor. Unlike common shell matter, a fresh Sample Snapjaw Shell retains a faint inner radiance and an energetic pulse long after being separated from the creature. To the tauren druids observing the land's rapid ecological shifts, these carapaces embody the resilient, adaptive spark of Kalimdor's wilderness, suggesting that nature can flourish even amidst harsh arid surroundings. Recognizing the latent vitality within the shell, tauren naturalists dispatch couriers across the sea to deliver specimens to Mura Runetotem at the Sepulcher. Stationed within the blighted expanses of Silverpine Forest, Mura seeks to aid the Forsaken by finding ways to heal the afflicted northlands. By examining the enduring life-force preserved inside the snapjaw's armor, she hopes to isolate secrets that can revitalize an ailing forest and encourage new growth in dying soil.

item:samuel-s-remains.text: Samuel's Remains. Samuel's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Samuel Fipps, a former resident of Tirisfal Glades who fell to the Scourge. Gathered by adventurers near Deathknell, they are laid to rest beside his wife Marla to fulfill her dying wish. Before the plague of undeath swept across Lordaeron, Samuel Fipps lived peacefully with his wife, Marla. When the contagion struck, Samuel succumbed and was bound into mindless service to the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath only to be struck down by the very husband she loved. Despite this brutal end, her final wish was not vengeance, but eternity together: she pleaded to be interred beside Samuel once his cursed form was put to rest. Novice Elreth in Deathknell enlists newly awoken Forsaken to track down Samuel's wandering form northeast of the settlement, recover his bones, and bury them in the front row of the local cemetery.

item:sapphire-of-aku-mai.text: Sapphire of Aku'Mai. Sapphires of Aku'Mai are glowing, water-infused mineral clusters growing along the subterranean tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps. The encroaching naga have begun harvesting these gems, prompting the Earthen Ring to seek them out before their potent arcane power can be exploited. Discovered within the watery cavern entrances of Blackfathom Deeps along Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Sapphires of Aku'Mai are crystalline formations rich in elemental energy. The spirits of water cling tightly to them, making them exceptional catalysts for magical workings. When scouts reported that the subterranean naga had begun actively quarrying these clusters from the cavern walls, the Shaman Je'neu Sancrea sought adventuring assistance to confiscate them. Left in the serpent peoples' clutches, the stones could easily fuel devastating arcane rites.

item:sapphire-of-sky.text: Sapphire of Sky. The Sapphire of Sky is one of four sacred Relics of Wakening kept by the night elves within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. It is an essential focus used to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Deep within the roots of Teldrassil, Druids of the Talon commune with the wilds while resting in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Awakening from such deep trance-states into the waking world is a fragile, perilous process. To safeguard the transition, the druids rely on four consecrated artifacts known as the Relics of Wakening: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. Without this resonant gem, the harmony required to call sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream remains incomplete, leaving them vulnerable to eternal entrapment. When corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the barrow den, the sacred artifacts were left behind in their ornate repositories. The Sapphire of Sky resides secured inside the Chest of the Sky amidst the winding subterranean corridors. With the druids still slumbering as the furbolgs rampage around them, retrieving this jewel alongside its companion relics is an urgent matter for Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the sleepers are permanently lost.

item:sara-balloo-s-plea.text: Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a handwritten missive penned by a grieving widow in Ironforge. Unable to face the monarch directly in her sorrow, she entrusts this letter to a trusted champion of the Alliance to carry before King Magni Bronzebeard. Written in the shadow of deep personal tragedy, Sara Balloo's Plea represents a humble appeal directly to Ironforge's throne. Rather than braving the High Seat herself in her grief-stricken condition, Sara seeks an adventurer who has demonstrated loyalty and valor to the Alliance to deliver her words. The message asks for the attention of King Magni Bronzebeard, drawing the sovereign's gaze toward the private mourning and sacrifices made by ordinary dwarven families serving the kingdom.

item:sarilus-foulborne-s-head.text: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Sarilus Foulborne's Head is a gruesome trophy claimed from an undead sorcerer who defiled the waters of northern Kalimdor. Carried back across the border from the Barrens into Ashenvale, it serves as undeniable proof that the meddling mage has met his end at the hands of the Sentinels. Perched high atop Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens, the Forsaken spellcaster Sarilus Foulborne drew the wrath of the night elves by corrupting and binding swarms of water elementals. From her post at Silverwind Refuge, Sentinel Velene Starstrike recognized his foul handiwork and dispatched champions across the frontier into Horde territory to end his reckless experiments. Severing the mage's head was the only proof Starstrike would accept to verify that his mocking grin was wiped away forever, securing a measure of peace for the troubled waters of Ashenvale.

item:sarkoth-s-mangled-claw.text: Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Sarkoth's Mangled Claw is the severed pincer of Sarkoth, a monstrous scorpid stalking the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Heavily scarred by the badly wounded troll Hana'zua, the trophy serves as both proof of the beast's death and a final consolation for a wounded hunter's pride. While hunting in the Valley of Trials, a young Darkspear troll named Hana'zua engaged a massive scorpid known as Sarkoth. Before Sarkoth's venomous stinger pierced his chest and left him bleeding under a nearby tree, Hana'zua landed a crushing blow against the creature's massive pincer. Severing this battered limb offers undeniable proof that the monstrous scorpid has been slain. For Hana'zua, holding the mangled claw confirms that his desperate strike left a lasting mark, providing a fleeting spark of warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

item:sarltooth-s-talon.text: Sarltooth's Talon. Sarltooth's Talon is a severed claw taken from the alpha raptor lurking above Whelgar's Excavation Site in the Wetlands. It serves as tangible proof for the dwarf Ormer Ironbraid that the vicious beast responsible for overrunning the archaeological dig has been slain. When raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition, Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge above, unable to prevent the slaughter. He singled out one massive, menacing raptor—Sarltooth—as the likely pack leader behind the assault. Seeking retribution for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and requested one of its vicious talons as proof of the deed. Severing this claw marks the end of Sarltooth's reign of terror over the ancient dwarven ruins.

item:sathrah-s-sacrifice.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. Sathrah's Sacrifice consists of the silvery spinnerets taken from Lady Sathrah, a mighty spider dwelling in Teldrassil. Entrusted to adventurers by Priestess A'moora, this offering is presented at the fountain of the Temple of the Moon to cleanse the creature's corruption and lay her spirit to rest. Lady Sathrah was once a venerable creature of Teldrassil who fell prey to the creeping madness and corruption afflicting the boughs of the great tree. Tasked by the Sisterhood of Elune, adventurers retrieve her silvery spinnerets not as mere trophies, but as a consecrated offering. By bathing these remains within the sacred fountain of the Temple of the Moon, the foul taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind is washed away. The rite frees her troubled soul, allowing her spirit to manifest peacefully within the sanctuary and granting her the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

item:satyr-horns.text: Satyr Horns. Satyr Horns are grim trophies harvested from the corrupted satyrs that plague the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Coveted both by grieving forest dwellers seeking retribution and opportunistic merchants trading out of Ratchet, they serve as undeniable proof that another servant of the Burning Legion has fallen. The curled horns of Ashenvale's satyrs are stark symbols of demonic corruption taken root in the sacred forest. For the dryad Illiyana at the Shrine of Aessina, gathering these severed horns is a matter of grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. To outside traders like the traveling goblin Pixel resting at Splintertree Post, however, the horns represent raw opportunity. Demand for satyr horns has surged in the neutral port of Ratchet, transforming these macabre remnants of slain demons into lucrative trade goods for anyone daring enough to hunt their bearers. Satyr Horns cannot be bought from ordinary suppliers; they must be cut directly from the beasts lurking in the dark corners of the woodland. The satyrs maintain strongholds across Ashenvale, most notoriously in the corrupted groves of Xavian, the shadowed hollows of Satyrnaar, and the ruins of Night Run. Clearing these enclaves rids the land of lingering demonic taint while keeping both grieving guardians and eager merchants supplied with proof of the cull.

item:savannah-lion-tusk.text: Savannah Lion Tusk. Savannah Lion Tusks are hefty fangs taken from the predatory big cats roaming the arid plains of the Barrens. While common hunting trophies for travelers, they serve an exotic purpose as a brewing ingredient for Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. The great cats of the Barrens—from prowlers and huntresses to majestic prides ruled by patriarchs and beasts like Humar the Pridelord—are armed with sharp, heavy tusks. While most who fell these predators take their teeth as simple proof of prowess, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks them out for a far more spirited craft. Drohn uses the tusks alongside plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous namesake brew, imparting a legendary kick that few mortal gullets can easily withstand.

item:scaber-stalk.text: Scaber Stalk. Scaber Stalks are rare mushrooms that flourish in the damp, secluded cavern hidden behind Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore. Prized by herbalists and alchemists for their unusual properties, they are sought by Barithras Moonshade for his concoctions. Scaber Stalks are obscure mushrooms found deep within the cavern nestled behind Cliffspring Falls, situated along the northeastern mountains of Darkshore. Unlike ordinary forest flora, these pale stalks thrive strictly in the secluded dampness of the subterranean cave network. Their remote and hazardous habitat makes gathering them exceedingly rare, leading alchemists like Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine to commission daring scouts willing to brave the dark.

item:scale-of-old-murk-eye.text: Scale of Old Murk-Eye. The Scale of Old Murk-Eye is taken from the infamous murloc leader who terrorizes the coastline of Westfall. Severed from the beast's hide, it serves as undeniable proof of his demise for Captain Grayson, the ghost who haunts the Westfall Lighthouse. The coast of Westfall is perilous enough between hidden shoals and relentless storms, but the presence of Old Murk-Eye elevated the danger from navigational hazard to outright massacre. According to Captain Grayson, the ghost bound to the Westfall Lighthouse, this particular murloc possessed a cunning beyond his feral kin, rallying weaker-minded murlocs to raid the shore. Murk-Eye scared off the keeper's family, leaving the beacon dark the night Grayson's ship smashed against the rocks, and when the family returned to relight the flame he raided again and slaughtered them. Taking a scale from the creature is the only way to satisfy the vengeful spirit and prove that the shore has been cleansed of its fiercest predator.

item:scarlet-armband.text: Scarlet Armband. Scarlet Armbands are insignia worn by members of the Scarlet Crusade, marking their fanatic allegiance to the eradication of all undead. In Deathknell, Executor Arren demands them as proof that fledgling Forsaken have struck back against the zealots encroaching on their territory. Worn on the sleeves of Scarlet Initiates and fresh converts alike, the Scarlet Armband is the unmistakable mark of the Scarlet Crusade. To the newly risen Forsaken emerging from Deathknell, these strips of red cloth represent a lethal threat right on their doorstep. The Crusade makes no distinction between the mindless minions of the Scourge and the free-willed subjects of the Dark Lady; in their eyes, any walking corpse must be put to the torch. Executor Arren uses the collection of these armbands as a grim rite of passage, confirming the deaths of enemy scouts southeast of the settlement and proving that new Forsaken can defend their fledgling nation.

item:scarlet-crusade-documents.text: Scarlet Crusade Documents. These intercepted papers were carried by a Scarlet Crusade messenger at the Crusade's camp near Deathknell. Containing orders for the Crusade's field commanders across Tirisfal Glades, they provide the Forsaken with the exact military intelligence needed to target the Crusade's regional leadership. The courier Meven Korgal carried these documents at the Crusade's encampment southeast of Deathknell. Issued by order of the Highlord, the directives are addressed to the captains of the Crusade's Tirisfal Regional Command: Captain Perrine is to further fortify the southwest tower and gather information on the undead in Brill, Captain Vachon to crush undead movement near the northern tower, and Captain Melrose to watch the borders of the Plaguelands. The documents reveal the names, posts, and orders of Scarlet field officers stationed across Tirisfal Glades, turning an otherwise routine courier run into a catastrophic intelligence breach for the zealots. Executor Arren swiftly recognized that local forces in Deathknell could not exploit the full breadth of the intelligence. Instead, the captured dossier serves as a newly awakened Forsaken's passport out of Deathknell. Carried northeast past Cold Hearth Manor into Brill, the documents are handed directly to Executor Zygand outside the Brill Town Hall. With these orders in hand, the Forsaken military leadership plans swift decapitation strikes against Scarlet commanders entrenched across the Glades.

item:scarlet-insignia-ring.text: Scarlet Insignia Ring. A Scarlet Insignia Ring is a signet band worn by members of the Scarlet Crusade garrisoned throughout Tirisfal Glades. For the Forsaken defenders of Brill, these rings serve as gruesome proof that another zealot has been eliminated from Lordaeron's soil. Every fighting member of the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades—from fresh neophytes and zealous friars to seasoned captains like Melrache and Perrine—carries an insignia ring. Marked with the Crusade's fiery sigil, the rings identify brother and sister within an organization consumed by paranoia. To outsiders and enemies, however, these trinkets serve entirely different purposes: they are unmistakable identifiers of Lordaeron's most fanatical human remnant. Under the direct mandate of Varimathras, Lady Sylvanas's dreadlord lieutenant, Deathguard Burgess in Brill actively collects these rings. The Forsaken consider the Scarlet Crusade an intolerable pestilence crawling across their newly claimed homeland. For Forsaken recruits, bringing stacks of these rings back to Brill is treated as undeniable proof of demise and a direct affirmation of loyalty to the throne of the Undercity.

item:scavenged-goods.text: Scavenged Goods. Scavenged Goods are miscellaneous pieces of discarded gear and supplies packed into equipment boxes around Deathknell. Newly risen Forsaken recover them to ensure the endless stream of fresh recruits can be armed and clothed. When new Forsaken pull themselves out of the earth in Deathknell's graveyard, they awaken with little more than rotting burial shrouds. Surrounding settlements and kingdoms offer no aid to the undead, leaving them entirely dependent on what they can salvage. Deathguard Saltain coordinates the collection of discarded weapons, tools, and garments cached in supply crates across the village, distributing them directly to the next batch of risen recruits.

item:scavenger-paw.text: Scavenger Paw. Scavenger Paws are severed limbs gathered from the young and ragged wolves roaming the hills of Deathknell. Newly awakened Forsaken collect them for local caretakers to stitch together into crude, protective gear. Resources are scarce for the newly returned in Deathknell. With the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade pressing against Tirisfal, every scrap of hide and bone is put to practical use. Novice Elreth, assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis, collects paws from the local scavenger wolves alongside bat wings to fashion serviceable garments and armor for disoriented Forsaken stepping fresh from their graves.

item:scorched-spider-fang.text: Scorched Spider Fang. Scorched Spider Fangs are specialized crafting materials harvested from predatory arachnids lurking in the sodden caverns of the Wetlands. The dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard requires a substantial bulk of these heat-tempered fangs to forge resilient fire-hardened mail for seasoned warriors. Forging armor capable of turning blades and resisting violent trauma requires more than standard iron. In Stormwind's busy district, the skilled blacksmith Furen Longbeard uses obscure metallurgical techniques that blend beast parts with rare reagents. Furen demands fifty scorched fangs from the giant arachnids of the marshlands, utilizing their dense, venomous, and naturally toughened composition to reinforce mail links during the tempering process. These fangs are harvested directly from the lethal arachnids inhabiting the sunken valleys and burrows of the Wetlands, notably Cave Stalkers and Leech Stalkers. Despite the damp, rotting environment of the marsh, these predators possess peculiarly hardened, scorched mandibles. Gathering them in the quantities Furen demands requires venturing into deep hollows and clearing out entire swarms of monstrous vermin.

item:scroll-of-messaging.text: Scroll of Messaging. The Scroll of Messaging is an enchanted parchment carrying a specific magical sending spell. Acquired for the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves an unusual purpose: providing the magical trigger needed to detonate remote explosives. While ostensibly an arcane script meant for long-distance communication, Gaxim Rustfizzle has a far more disruptive application in mind for the Scroll of Messaging. By combining its transmission incantation with volatile NG-5 charges, the gnome plans to create a remotely detonated explosive. The resulting blast is intended to trigger a massive distraction at the Venture Company's logging operation in Stonetalon, granting operatives a window to slip past guards and pilfer proprietary engineering schematics and confidential correspondence.

item:sea-creature-bones.text: Sea Creature Bones. Sea Creature Bones are skeletal samples gathered from the massive marine carcasses washing ashore along the mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore. Sent directly to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, these remains are central to an ongoing investigation into what is driving these great beasts to strand themselves upon the beaches. The fog-blanketed beaches of Darkshore have recently witnessed an alarming surge of massive sea creatures—including giant threshers far larger than those native to the local shallows—flinging themselves onto the shallows until they perish. The sight is viewed as an ominous portent by the night elves. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, an investigator dispatched by the Temple of the Moon to Auberdine, collects bone specimens from these beached leviathans to ship by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. Recovering these bones is fraught with danger, as the immense carcasses inevitably attract local scavengers. The coastal Greymist murlocs frequently swarm the dead and dying leviathans, feeding on the remains and defending the feeding grounds aggressively. Although the murlocs are far too weak to hunt such colossal creatures on their own, their opportunistic presence along Mist's Edge forces investigators and adventurers to fight through the scavenging packs to secure viable bone fragments for study.

item:sea-turtle-remains.text: Sea Turtle Remains. Sea Turtle Remains are skeletal samples salvaged from the carcasses of giant sea turtles along the coast of Darkshore. They serve as vital specimens for night elf researchers in Auberdine investigating an alarming surge of marine strandings. Giant sea creatures have begun beaching themselves all along Darkshore's mist-shrouded shores, while others lie submerged just off the coast near sunken wrecks. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, stationed in Auberdine, oversees the collection of skeletal fragments and tissue from these corpses. The Temple of the Moon in Darnassus urgently requests these samples, concerned by theories that the beasts may be fleeing an unnatural disturbance in the waters surrounding the newly grown world tree, Teldrassil. Recovering these remains is perilous work. Coastal tribes of murlocs routinely congregate around the massive carcasses, picking the bones clean and nesting beside them. Scholars require fresh bone fragments and tissue before the scavengers destroy any surviving evidence that might explain the creatures' fatal migration.

item:sealed-description-of-thredd-s-visi.text: Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor. The Sealed Description of Thredd's Visitor is a confidential report penned by Warden Thelwater regarding an enigmatic man who visited the imprisoned Defias leader, Bazil Thredd, inside the Stormwind Stockade. Its contents help track down a covert operative moving unseen through Stormwind's political and criminal spheres. For years inside the Stockade, prisoner Bazil Thredd sat in his cell with no visitors. That routine shifted when an uncommunicative man began stopping by once or twice a week with completely valid identification papers. Taking note of these unusual arrivals, Warden Thelwater composed a physical account of the man, who carried identification marking him as 'Maelik'. The warden sealed the profile to prevent any meddling eyes from reading it before proper investigators could act.

item:sealed-envelope.text: Sealed Envelope. This tightly sealed packet contains confidential Venture Company technical documents and stolen schematics. Assembled by the exiled goblin engineer Fizziks, it holds proprietary designs meant for delivery to Sputtervalve in Ratchet. When the goblin engineer Fizziks was abruptly ejected from the Venture Company's logging operations in the Stonetalon Mountains, he did not leave empty-handed. Stuffing internal manuals, operating procedures, and technical specifications into this envelope, he managed to smuggle out company secrets under the noses of his former overseers. Most prized among these stolen records are the technical schematics for the Super Reaper 6000, a devastating piece of industrial clear-cutting machinery. Rather than keeping the dangerous trade secrets buried, Fizziks sends the packet south to Sputtervalve, an engineer residing in the neutral goblin port of Ratchet. While business rivals in the Steamwheedle Cartel have little personal love or trust for Fizziks, the engineering value of the designs inside the envelope is undeniable. The documents provide a clear window into Venture Company mechanical ingenuity and give independent engineers a chance to exploit the Venture Company's advanced logging technologies.

item:sealed-note-to-elling.text: Sealed Note to Elling. The Sealed Note to Elling is a confidential dispatch penned by the Stormwind fisherman Jorgen. Intended for Elling Trias, the proprietor of Trias' Cheese, it serves as an early link in the discreet investigation surrounding a vanished diplomat. Carrying a sealed note through the bustling avenues of Stormwind might seem mundane, but Jorgen's strict instructions make the stakes clear: deliver the parchment into Elling Trias's hands and keep silent. While Trias outwardly presents himself as a mild-mannered cheese merchant in the Trade District, this clandestine message directs the investigation of the missing diplomat straight to his counter, hinting at networks far deeper than dairy trade.

item:sealed-note-to-watcher-backus.text: Sealed Note to Watcher Backus. The Sealed Note to Watcher Backus is a confidential dispatch written by master cheese merchant and informant Elling Trias. Addressed to a member of the Night Watch patrolling the road outside Darkshire, it calls in a personal favor to gather intelligence on Defias activity in Duskwood. When Jorgen's sealed note drags him into the hunt for the missing diplomat, cheese monger Elling Trias grudgingly agrees to put his own contacts to work. He pens this wax-sealed missive to Watcher Backus, a Night Watch guard stationed in Duskwood. Trias sends an adventurer south through the gloomy forest to deliver it by hand, using his longstanding rapport with Backus to secure any reports of Defias presence wandering near Darkshire.

item:searing-collar.text: Searing Collar. Searing Collars are ritual torcs worn by members of the Burning Blade cult hiding within Skull Rock in Durotar. Heated to burn the wearer's flesh, they are used by the cultists to attune themselves to demonic powers. Within the shadowy cavern of Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar, the Burning Blade gathers to perform dark rituals. Cultists, neophytes, and thugs of the cult don Searing Collars around their necks, willingly subjecting themselves to scorching heat that brands and sears their skin. The hermit Margoz studies these cruel devices, theorizing that the burning sensation and dark enchantments bound to the metal serve to attune the wearers directly to demonic energies. Investigating the collars reveals that they are a significant conduit of demonic corruption creeping into orc society right under the Horde's nose.

item:searing-coral.text: Searing Coral. Searing Coral is a rare, resilient mineral substance harvested from living iron corals off the coast of the Wetlands. Prized by tinkerers and smiths, it possesses remarkable thermal properties that allow it to be smelted and forged into protective armor. Searing Coral grows exclusively in the chilly ocean waters along the coast south of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Despite thriving in cold saltwater, this unique marine organism yields a mineral-rich material capable of enduring extreme heat. Harvesters brave the Wetlands' treacherous surf and coastal predators to pry the hardened formations loose. While traditionally outside standard dwarven metallurgy, Searing Coral caught the attention of inquisitive minds in Ironforge. Gnome craftsmen such as Klockmort Spannerspan adapt the techniques of veteran armorsmith Furen Longbeard, smelting and hammering the coral directly into metal alloys to produce lightweight, exceptionally durable armor for aspiring warriors.

item:secure-crate.text: Secure Crate. The Secure Crate is a tightly packed parcel filled with potions, alchemical reagents, and other miscellaneous goods destined for the Eastern Kingdoms. Entrusted to travelers in the Barrens, it must be carried to the bustling port of Ratchet to catch the outgoing tide. Trade routes between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms rely on a fragile chain of couriers, desert caravans, and goblin merchant vessels. When land caravans across the Barrens miss their scheduled departures, fragile shipments like this Secure Crate must be hauled by independent travelers down to the coast. Inside are alchemical goods, potions, and various reagents earmarked for associates across the Great Sea. Given the delicate and valuable nature of the contents, the crate is firmly sealed to ensure it survives both the arid trails of the Barrens and the salty spray of oceanic transit. The destination of the crate's land leg is the dock at Ratchet, overseen by Wharfmaster Dizzywig. Ratchet's harbor serves as the primary neutral funnel through which supplies cross the sea toward destinations like Blackwater Cove. Operating under the ledger of the Steamwheedle Cartel, Dizzywig ensures that small parcels and heavy freight alike are properly manifested and loaded aboard the next departing vessel, providing a vital commercial link between the Old World and the frontier.

item:senir-s-report.text: Senir's Report. Senir's Report is a dispatched document penned by Mountaineer Senir Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll threat in Dun Morogh. It carries findings commissioned under royal directive and is destined for Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Drafted after scouting missions against the Frostmane trolls nestled in the crags of Dun Morogh, this field report contains mountaineer observations intended for the dwarf Senate. Senir Whitebeard, stationed out in the cold foothills, penned the document and enclosed his brother Grelin's report on Coldridge Valley, which states that Grelin acted under a sanction from King Magni Bronzebeard. Senir tasks adventurers with hauling the findings straight to Senator Barin Redstone in the High Seat of Ironforge—cautiously advising couriers to omit just how much outside help he required to compile it.

item:serena-s-head.text: Serena's Head. Serena's Head is the grisly trophy taken from the matriarch of the Dry Hills harpies in the northern Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger of the Crossroads demanded it as proof of her demise, intending to display it upon Horde supply wagons as a harsh deterrent against further aerial raids. The Witchwing harpies of the Dry Hills have long plagued trade moving through the northern Barrens, but under Serena Bloodfeather their assaults turned particularly vicious. Her raids against Horde supply lines were driven by personal vengeance for her sister, who fell to the beastmaster Rexxar. To permanently break the morale of the flock, the orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger ordered Serena hunted down. Rather than letting her death go unnoticed, he sought her severed head so it could be mounted upon the next outbound caravan—serving as a stark, bloody warning to any harpy watching from the crags above.

item:serpentbloom.text: Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a rare, subterranean herb found growing only in the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Its potent natural properties have drawn the keen interest of the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society. Serpentbloom grows exclusively within the damp, shadowy tunnels of the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens. Rooted in an ecosystem warped by unrestrained Emerald Dream energies, the plant thrives far from sunlight and often harbors venomous serpents nesting among its stems. Because the cave system is overrun with hostile beasts and corrupted druids, few who venture inside ever return with viable specimens. Operating from the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah collects Serpentbloom on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society of Undercity. The Forsaken continuously seek out virulent, strange, and chemically potent vegetation across Kalimdor to fuel their research for the Dark Lady. Zamah believes that harvesting Serpentbloom in significant quantities could yield valuable breakthroughs for Forsaken alchemy.

item:sethir-s-journal.text: Sethir's Journal. Sethir's Journal is a personal record carried by the elusive satyr Sethir the Ancient in Teldrassil. Recovered through stealth, its contents confirm the alarming spread of corruption from mainland Kalimdor onto the World Tree.

item:sevren-s-orders.text: Sevren's Orders. Sevren's Orders are written dispatches penned by Magistrate Sevren of Brill. They direct a proven Forsaken agent to report to Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage stationed in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. As the Forsaken solidify their grip on the ruins of Lordaeron, skilled agents who have proven their worth against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south to the capital. Issued by Magistrate Sevren, these written orders serve as official introduction and credentials to Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost practitioners of the arcane in the Magic Quarter. While Sevren knows little beyond the fact that the assignment involves reaching out to an errant lich, the summons carries the absolute authority of the Undercity's high mages.

item:shadowhide-pendant.text: Shadowhide Pendant. Shadowhide Pendants are crude ornamental charms carried by the Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains. Collected as legal proof of bounty enforcement, they signify that local defenders have enacted Lakeshire's law against gnolls collaborating with the rogue mage Morganth. Carried by warriors, brutes, and spellcasters of the Shadowhide clan, these pendants serve as crude personal totems or rank insignias. Deep in the hills of Redridge, the clan has rallied under Lieutenant Fangore and fallen under the sway of Morganth, a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To the townspeople of Lakeshire, these charms are not mere primitive jewelry; they are identifying marks of an organized menace harassing settlements across the region on behalf of an enemy of the Crown. Under the authority of Magistrate Solomon and the laws of Stormwind, actively aiding a known criminal of the realm carries a sentence of death. Lacking sufficient royal reinforcements, Bailiff Conacher in the Lakeshire Town Hall relies on independent adventurers to uphold the peace. Presenting ten Shadowhide Pendants provides tangible proof that gnolls obeying Morganth's orders have faced frontier justice.

item:shaman-voodoo-charm.text: Shaman Voodoo Charm. The Shaman Voodoo Charm is a dark ritual trinket carried by Gnarlpine furbolg shamans deep within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Emanating a vile aura, this charm channels an unnatural magic capable of severing a slumbering druid's spirit from their physical flesh. The Gnarlpine tribe of Teldrassil has fallen into madness and corruption, but within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, their shamans wield powers far beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Utilizing these strange voodoo charms, the shamans discovered a way to rip a sleeping druid's consciousness away from the mortal realm and trap it helplessly within the Emerald Dream. By severing the soul from the vessel, the furbolgs are able to animate the empty physical form, turning venerable night elf protectors into mindless guardians that slaughter anyone venturing into the barrows.

item:shard-of-water.text: Shard of Water. The Shard of Water is an elemental remnant gathered during a shaman's communion with the spirits of water. Delivered to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast, it serves as tangible proof that an initiate has understood water's life-giving nature and conquered its corruption. For shamans seeking mastery over the elements, communing with water demands a deep understanding of balance, life, and preservation. In the trials of the Call of Water, shamans are directed to confront corruption seeped into natural springs—even journeying across the sea to blighted lands like Silverpine Forest. The Shard of Water is granted upon purifying these corrupted waters. Returning this crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky shores of the Barrens proves the initiate's worth, providing the final key needed to forge their Water Totem.

item:shaw-s-report.text: Shaw's Report. Shaw's Report is a confidential dispatch written by Master Mathias Shaw of SI:7 for Gryan Stoutmantle in Westfall. It outlines the intelligence agency's knowledge regarding the Stonemasons Guild, its leader Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown following the rebuilding of Stormwind.

item:shimmering-frond.text: Shimmering Frond. A Shimmering Frond is a specimen harvested from a strange, glowing plant growing within the Oracle Glade of Teldrassil. Its unusual luminescence and twisting aura reveal it to be an exotic species entirely alien to the boughs of the World Tree. While wandering the verdant canopies around the Oracle Glade, travelers may come across strange vegetation boasting a pulsing, radiant aura. The fronds plucked from this plant catch the filtered woodland light in unnatural ways, shimmering with vibrant vitality. Denalan, a botanist tending to his planters by Lake Al'Ameth, recognizes the foliage immediately as a species native to the distant Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from a marsh so far across the Great Sea managed to take root and flourish upon the newly raised Teldrassil remains an intriguing mystery, prompting Denalan to sprout and study specimens in his own soil.

item:shimmerweed.text: Shimmerweed. Shimmerweed is a distinct herb cultivated by the Frostmane trolls on Shimmer Ridge in the snowy heights of Dun Morogh. While the trolls harvest it for their own tribal rituals, local dwarven brewers covet its sharp, unique flavor for experimental ales. High above the lowlands of Dun Morogh, the Frostmane trolls tend patches of shimmerweed along the icy crags of Shimmer Ridge. The trolls harvest and store the plant in woven baskets scattered throughout their camps, relying on it to fuel their sacred and enigmatic rituals. Outside of troll society, few mountaineers pay the weed much mind, though its potent properties have drawn the gaze of inventive outsiders. In nearby Brewnall Village, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew has taken a keen interest in the herb. Believing that brewing is in his blood, Rejold seeks to craft the ultimate dwarven stout and suspects that the pungent, unmistakable flavor of shimmerweed might be the missing piece. He frequently hires adventurous travelers to slip into the Frostmane encampments, dodge the hostile trolls, and haul back bushels to dump into his fermenting vats.

item:shindrell-s-note.text: Shindrell's Note. Shindrell's Note is a written missive detailing recent observations of corruption around Astranaar and the Ashenvale coastline. Penned by the night elf Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, it serves as an intelligence report dispatched east across the forest to the druid Kayneth Stillwind. As unrest spreads throughout Ashenvale, night elf sentinels and druids coordinate to monitor the woodland's borders. Penned by Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar, this report details troubling disturbances spotted along the western coast and through the central canopies. It is addressed to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid stationed at the shrine of Forest Song within the Nightsong Woods to the east. By dispatching couriers with her firsthand observations, Shindrell aids Kayneth's investigation into the subtle corruption creeping through the sacred groves.

item:shipment-of-boots.text: Shipment of Boots. A crate of footwear dispatched from Booty Bay by the merchant Drizzlik, intended for Gazlowe's trade network in Ratchet. It was intercepted off the coast by Southsea Freebooters and stashed away in their encampment south of the port. Running a goblin trade port requires endless supplies, and Gazlowe arranged for a fresh delivery of boots from Drizzlik, a purveyor of apparel based out of Booty Bay. The consignment never reached Ratchet's docks. Southsea Freebooters prowling the Merchant Coast ambushed the transport vessel, carrying the crates off to their beach encampments south of the harbor. The pirates scattered the stolen freight throughout their tents and shanties, leaving Gazlowe without his expected wares until adventurous mercenaries could be hired to scour the shoreline.

item:shipment-of-iron.text: Shipment of Iron. A crate of raw metal stored at the human smithy in Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as vital stock for local armament production, making it a priority target for Forsaken forces seeking to cut off the supply lines arming the Hillsbrad townsfolk. In the ongoing struggle across the Hillsbrad Foothills, the human peasantry has mounted surprisingly stiff resistance against Tarren Mill. Much of this fighting capability stems directly from the smithy at the southwestern edge of the Hillsbrad Fields, where Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices work round the clock churning out weapons and armor from heavy shipments of iron. To break the farmers' resolve, Forsaken commanders ordered the forge extinguished, its smiths eliminated, and its stockpiled metal seized for the Horde war effort.

item:shipping-schedule.text: Shipping Schedule. The Shipping Schedule is a logistical document held by the Defias Brotherhood's dockmaster at Jerod's Landing. It outlines illicit cargo shipments flowing through Elwynn Forest between Redridge and Westfall, drawing the close attention of Stormwind's intelligence agency. South of Goldshire on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River, the Defias Brotherhood seized control of Jerod's Landing to serve as a hub for their river traffic. Through this covert dock, the Brotherhood moves large quantities of contraband between Redridge and Westfall, slipping through waterways right under the nose of the Stormwind Guard. The Shipping Schedule records these clandestine movements, kept under close guard on the dockmaster's person. Master Mathias Shaw, leader of SI:7, commissioned the theft of the schedule to map Defias supply chains and test fledgling operatives. Infiltrating the dock house and lifting the document from the dockmaster's pockets serves both as actionable intelligence for the crown and as an initiation trial. If the operative is caught, SI:7 disavows all connection, leaving no trail back to the barracks in Stormwind.

item:sida-s-bag.text: Sida's Bag. Sida's Bag is the personal satchel of Sida, a resident of Menethil Harbor. Swallowed whole by a creeping ooze during her excursion to Ironbeard's Tomb, the bag and its mysterious contents require a thorough hunt through the acidic slimes of the Wetlands to recover. While paying her regular weekly visit to Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr, Sida found herself ambushed by the dreadful, dripping oozes that infest the area. Panicking in the face of the encroaching sludge, she flung her personal satchel directly at one of the creatures. Rather than driving the beast off, the ooze simply absorbed the bag into its gelatinous body. The distraction bought Sida enough precious moments to flee with her life back to the safety of Menethil Harbor, leaving her possessions trapped inside an unknown slime. Because the undulating oozes prowling Ironbeard's Tomb—ranging from crimson to monstrous varieties—look largely identical, finding the bag requires cutting down the marsh slimes until the swallowed satchel emerges intact. Despite soaking within acidic digestive muck, the durable sack preserves its contents. Once returned to Sida, she eagerly reclaims her belongings and discards the ruined, slime-coated exterior, offering the washed-out container to whoever braved the marsh on her behalf.

item:signed-recruitment-letter.text: Signed Recruitment Letter. The Signed Recruitment Letter is an official dispatch issued by Kargal Battlescar at the Far Watch Post. Bearing Kargal's mark, it transfers new recruits deeper into the arid interior of the Barrens to report for duty at the Crossroads. Standing as the eastern threshold of the Barrens, the Far Watch Post evaluates newcomers crossing over the Southfury River from Durotar. Once a conscript proves their readiness to Kargal Battlescar, he stamps and signs this letter of introduction. It serves as military orders directing recruits west down the road to the Crossroads, where Sergra Darkthorn coordinates logistical operations and territorial defense across the dry plains. While the letter is an official document of the Horde, Kargal does not hide his personal contempt for the officer awaiting the recruit. He views Sergra Darkthorn as an abrasive shaman who talks circles around soldiers, openly questioning Warchief Thrall's high opinion of her. Despite his misgivings, the dispatch must be delivered directly into Sergra's hands before any further assignments in the Crossroads are granted.

item:silithid-egg-the-barrens.text: Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Silithid Eggs are the developing brood of the insectoid creatures nesting in the southern Barrens. Found buried within earth mounds around the Field of Giants, these clutches are gathered by Horde researchers seeking to uncover the origins and intelligence of the encroaching swarm. In the arid basin of the Field of Giants, bizarre insect-like beings have begun churning the earth into towering mounds. Deep within these nests lie their eggs, buried beneath hardened soil and watched over by territorial broods. The Horde knows remarkably little about the silithid, but scouts stationed at the Crossroads have noted signs of coordinated behavior and uncanny intellect far exceeding ordinary wild beasts. Gathering unhatched eggs offers scholars in Orgrimmar their best chance to study the lifecycle and nature of this emerging menace. Reaching the eggs requires prying into silithid mounds with specialized digging claws. Disturbing these clutches is perilous work; the silithid react fiercely to intrusions near their subterranean nurseries, swarming any who threaten their unhatched young. For researchers like the troll Korran, securing intact, unbroken specimens is critical for analysis before the swarm spreads further across Kalimdor.

item:silixiz-s-tower-key.text: Silixiz's Tower Key. Silixiz's Tower Key is a small key carried by Foreman Silixiz outside the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Horde operatives belonging to the Shattered Hand are tasked with lifting it directly from the foreman's pockets as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. The Venture Company operation north of the Sludge Fen runs under tight security, centered on an isolated lookout tower supervised by Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix. Outside the compound patrolled by goblin mercenaries, Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key that the Shattered Hand operative is instructed to steal and keep. For the rogue network of the Shattered Hand operating out of Orgrimmar, obtaining this key is not a matter of blunt force; field operatives must slip into the compound undetected and pick the foreman's pockets cleanly, proving their mastery of stealth before climbing into the toxic upper levels.

item:silver-dawning-s-lockbox.text: Silver Dawning's Lockbox. The Silver Dawning's Lockbox is a sturdy chest resting within the sunken wreckage of the vessel Silver Dawning off the coast of Darkshore. It holds the personal effects and ship log of the vessel's fallen captain, lost during an ambush by coastal murlocs. The ship Silver Dawning was en route across the sea toward the port of Auberdine when disaster struck. Coastal murlocs swarmed the vessel, driving it down into the dark surf north of the harbor. The captain perished in the assault, leaving the wreckage submerged beneath the waves as a grim monument claimed by the creatures. Inside the flooded hull remains the captain's personal lockbox, holding the ship's log and private belongings. Recovering these effects offers a final measure of peace to the surviving crew members ashore.

item:silvery-spinnerets.text: Silvery Spinnerets. Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from the great spider Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Once used to weave webs that captured healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon, they are sought by the Priestesses of Elune to honor the fallen creature's soul through a sacred ritual of rebirth. Lady Sathrah was once counted among the favored creatures of Elune, renowned for spinning shimmering webs through the moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered the evening mist, forming healing dews prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. Unfortunately, the corruption creeping through the boughs of Teldrassil did not spare her. Falling into violent madness, Sathrah became a danger to her own brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end the spider's suffering and recover her spinnerets as an act of mercy, bringing closure to a revered resident of the great boughs.

item:simple-memorandum.text: Simple Memorandum. The Simple Memorandum is an official notice delivered to novice gnome warriors training in Coldridge Valley. A terse gnomish directive, it instructs fledglings to report to the warrior trainer Thran Khorman in Anvilmar to prepare for the war to take back Gnomeregan. Novice adventurers in Coldridge Valley frequently find themselves entrusted with letters of introduction as they demonstrate their mettle against the local wildlife and trogg threats. For young gnome fighters, this memorandum serves as a formal order to report to Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer within Anvilmar. Dwarven veterans recognize that while gnomes may rely on intellect and contraptions, retaking Gnomeregan will demand pure physical resolve and martial discipline. The memorandum directs the bearer to put aside preliminary tasks and seek personalized instruction in the art of war.

item:simple-rune.text: Simple Rune. A Simple Rune is an inscribed stone token passed to fledgling dwarven warriors training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as a summons from the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, directing recruits to seek instruction inside Anvilmar. Carved with basic martial marks, the Simple Rune is handed to promising recruits who have begun clearing out the threats around Coldridge Valley. Rather than a magical charm, it acts as a formal calling stone from Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer at Anvilmar. Upon reading its inscribed guidance, a young fighter is expected to report directly to Thran to learn basic combat techniques and hear practical advice on surviving Dun Morogh's hostile wilds.

item:simple-sigil.text: Simple Sigil. A Simple Sigil is a modest training token presented to novice night elf warriors in Shadowglen. Carried as a summons from the warrior trainer Alyissia, it marks a young fighter's formal introduction into the martial defense of Teldrassil. Within the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen, young night elves are guided by Conservator Ilthalaine to find their calling. For fledgling warriors, Ilthalaine delivers a Simple Sigil sent by a runner from the warrior trainer Alyissia. Bearing an inscription that directs the recruit to report for instruction, this token represents the start of disciplined martial training amidst troubling times for the World Tree. When brought to Alyissia, the sigil opens a dialogue on the pressing state of the kaldorei. The recent growth of Teldrassil, the creeping corruption tainting forest beasts, and the rediscovery of distant lands like Feralas have stretched night elven protectors thin. The sigil is not an artifact of power, but a practical credential welcoming the recruit into the fold of guardians tasked with shielding their people from emerging threats.

item:simple-tablet.text: Simple Tablet. The Simple Tablet is a written missive handed to novice troll warriors arriving in the Valley of Trials. Delivered by Gornek, it directs the fledgling combatant to present themselves to Frang, the local warrior trainer. Within the harsh red bounds of the Valley of Trials, new recruits are quickly set to work. For young trolls seeking the path of the warrior, Gornek passes along this simple slate or parchment. Written by the troll Tar'sere and addressed to Frang, the master-at-arms resting near the Den, it serves as an official introduction to martial training in Durotar. It urges the recruit to step forward, present themselves, and prove their willingness to swing weapons under the banner of the Horde.

item:singed-scale.text: Singed Scale. Singed Scales are the charred, shock-hardened plates harvested from the electrified thunder lizards of Durotar. Procuring them serves as a rite of passage for young Horde warriors striving to master defensive battle arts. To the veterans of the Horde, a true warrior is not measured solely by the blood drawn by their axe, but by the blows they can absorb to shield their allies. In the arid canyon of Thunder Ridge in western Durotar, lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with volatile storm energies. Hunting these beasts requires a warrior to endure relentless electrical shocks and crushing physical strikes. The blackened, scorched scales torn from their hides offer undeniable proof of a fighter's ability to weather punishing assaults and stand firm where lesser soldiers would fall. At the Far Watch Post on the border between Durotar and the Barrens, the veteran warrior Uzzek demands five of these scales from initiates before imparting his knowledge. In Uzzek's eyes, an initiate must possess inherent physical toughness before they can comprehend the subtle discipline of stances and tactical defense. Presenting the scales demonstrates that a warrior has the fortitude needed to combine thick hide, heavy armor, and calculated footwork into an unyielding wall against the enemies of the Horde.

item:skeleton-finger.text: Skeleton Finger. A severed, bony digit scavenged from the walking dead prowling the cursed groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire collects these macabre remnants alongside ghoul fangs and spider venom to craft protective talismans. The cursed woods of Duskwood are overrun by the restless remains of the dead, ranging from skeletal raiders and warriors to necrotic mages and fiends. While ordinary travelers avoid touching the foul remains of the risen dead, fortune tellers and mystics value their cold essence. Madame Eva, the resident seer of Darkshire, gathers these bony fingers to bind their lingering necrotic energies into a ward of retaliatory magic known as the Totem of Infliction.

item:skin-of-sweet-rum.text: Skin of Sweet Rum. A Skin of Sweet Rum is a specialized liquor sourced from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. It is sought after by Barkeep Daniels in Lakeshire, who is desperate to keep his tavern stocked while Blackrock orcs cut off Redridge from regular trade routes. In the war-weary town of Lakeshire, tavern supplies are running dangerously low. The Blackrock orc invasion has choked the supply roads leading into the Redridge Mountains, leaving Barkeep Daniels scrambling to quench the thirst of beleaguered town guards and refugees. To restock his depleted shelves, Daniels sends travelers across the kingdom to gather regional specialties, including a waterskin filled with the distinctive sweet rum brewed and served in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn.

item:skittering-blood.text: Skittering Blood. Skittering Blood is an alchemical reagent harvested from the arachnids dwelling within the Skittering Dark of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital toxic ingredient for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a New Plague designed to eradicate both Scourge and humanity. Harvested from Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner, this venomous hemolymph possesses virulent properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Apothecary Renferrel discovered that when refined alongside toxins extracted from grizzled bear hearts, the blood forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. The compounds within the fluid demonstrate severe contaminating agents, making it an ideal biological catalyst for the Apothecarium's chemical experiments. Under the direction of Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity, the Royal Apothecary Society gathers reagents like Skittering Blood to engineer a devastating New Plague. Faced with overwhelming Scourge hordes and hostile human remnants, the Forsaken pursue biological warfare as an equalizer. Faranell analyzes the blood's toxic potency to devise a contagion potent enough to snuff out unlife and living flesh alike.

item:sleepers-key.text: Sleepers' Key. The Sleepers' Key is one of three enchanted keys crafted by night elf druids to seal their sacred vault within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Kept safe inside a hidden cache opened with the Gatekeeper's Key, it is one of the three keys needed to open the druids' hoard. Carved into the heights of Stonetalon Peak, the Talon Den serves as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. Aware that their sacred relics and potent treasures might draw unwanted attention, the night elf keepers devised an intricate system of locks and hidden caches to protect their hoard. The Sleepers' Key is one third of that protective ward. Placed within a secluded cache in the den's depths, it can only be retrieved using the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. Alongside the Claw Key and the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key must be set into the stone locks of the Talon Den Hoard to disperse the ward and reveal the ancient items held within.

item:smoky-iron-ingot.text: Smoky Iron Ingot. Smoky Iron Ingots are roughly processed metal bars smelted by the kobolds of the Windshear dig sites in the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize these ingots as raw material for forging sturdy mail gear fit for Horde warriors. Within the soot-stained tunnels of the Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains, kobolds excavate deep into the rocky earth, pulling unrefined ore from the slopes and smelting it over crude, smoking fires. The resulting Smoky Iron Ingots are far from pristine—thick with residue and charcoal—yet dense enough to retain substantial tensile strength. The near-blind orc armorer Thun'grim Firegaze, working out of a rugged camp overlooking the Barrens, specifically requests these ingots when crafting armor for proven warriors of the Horde. Combined with refined iron bars, powdered azurite, and volatile phlogiston, the smoky metal serves as a resilient core for crafting Brutal Hauberks.

item:smoldering-embers.text: Smoldering Embers. Smoldering Embers are the glowing, heat-baked remnants retrieved from the raging fire elementals of the Charred Vale. Night elf Sentinels track these cinders as physical proof that the fiery terrors overrunning the devastated woodland are being subdued. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting and industrial devastation tore through the Charred Vale, setting the forest ablaze and unleashing destructive fury from deep within the earth. In their wake, elementals of living fire—Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and wandering Rogue Flame Spirits—surged across the scorched basin. These Smoldering Embers are the lingering, ash-covered cores left behind when an elemental is extinguished, serving as proof that the rampant fires of the vale are being systematically suppressed.

item:snellig-s-snuffbox.text: Snellig's Snuffbox. Snellig's Snuffbox is a personal keepsake recovered from the restless undead First Mate Snellig among the wreckage of the Lost Fleet. Bringing this trinket back to First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor serves as proof that his cursed former crewmate has finally been put to rest. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground along the northern shores of the Wetlands, its sailors and officers did not find peaceful deaths. Bound by a mysterious and dark power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead. Among them was First Mate Snellig, who still haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. Even in death, he clung to his snuffbox—a small, mundane reminder of his mortal life at sea. For the sole living survivor of the disaster, First Mate Fitzsimmons, recovering this small possession provides tangible proof that at least one of his lost shipmates has been released from an eternity of torment.

item:snufflenose-command-stick.text: Snufflenose Command Stick. The Snufflenose Command Stick is a training rod provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It is used to direct trained snufflenose gophers to locate and unearth valuable blueleaf tubers buried deep within Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted delicacies across Azeroth, but finding them is nearly impossible without specialized help. Buried in the thorny underground depths of Razorfen Kraul, the roots are entirely hidden from sight. To exploit this lucrative market without braving the quilboar dens himself, the Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix conditioned keen-scented snufflenose gophers to dig up the tubers. The Snufflenose Command Stick is the tool adventurers use to direct these trained critters, prodding them to sniff out and expose root nodes from up to fifty paces away.

item:snufflenose-owner-s-manual.text: Snufflenose Owner's Manual. The Snufflenose Owner's Manual is an instructional booklet from Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc., kept beside the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It outlines how to deploy and direct a trained Snufflenose Gopher to locate rare Blueleaf Tubers buried in Razorfen Kraul. Written by Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., this short guide details how to work with the company's trained snufflenose gophers. These beasts possess a keen sense of smell capable of detecting subterranean Blueleaf Tubers from fifty paces away. The manual instructs prospectors to release a gopher using a ventilated crate and guide its rooting instincts with a command stick, directing the creature through the hostile thorns and quilboar tunnels of Razorfen Kraul to secure the prized culinary delicacies.

item:sodium-nitrate.text: Sodium Nitrate. Sodium Nitrate is a volatile chemical reagent carried by the dwarven excavators and garrison stationed at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Though imported by the Ironforge expedition to blast through ancient stone, the exiled tauren Gann Stonespire seeks to reclaim it to assemble an explosive charge against the invaders. The Bael'dun expedition tore into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tribe armed with heavy earthmovers and blasting reagents. To crack open the stubborn rockbeds of the southern Barrens, the dwarves relied on volatile chemical compounds. Sodium Nitrate forms a crucial stabilizing and oxidizing agent in high-grade explosives, carried routinely by Bael'dun riflemen, soldiers, and officers inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-darkshire.text: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Solomon's Plea to Darkshire is an urgent missive penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire addressed to Lord Ello Ebonlocke. In the face of mounting Blackrock orc and gnoll threats, the letter begs the leadership of Darkshire to send their elite militia, the Night Watch, to bolster Lakeshire's strained defenses. Lakeshire stands on the brink of being overwhelmed by invading Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, with virtually no official reinforcements arriving from Stormwind. In desperation, Magistrate Solomon drafted this formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke of Darkshire, petitioning him to dispatch members of the Night Watch northward into Redridge. The document reflects the severe breakdown of central military support across southern Azeroth, forcing individual human settlements to look to one another for mutual survival.

item:solomon-s-plea-to-westfall.text: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. Solomon's Plea to Westfall is an urgent written appeal penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire. Desperate for reinforcements against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Solomon sends this dispatch to Gryan Stoutmantle in Westfall hoping the newly formed People's Militia can lend aid while Stormwind's royal army fails to respond. As the threat of the Blackrock clan and hostile gnolls looms large over Redridge, Magistrate Solomon finds himself dangerously isolated in Lakeshire. The royal army from Stormwind has inexplicably failed to arrive in force to defend the region's borders. Unable to wait for official support from the kingdom's capital, Solomon pens this plea in a desperate bid to recruit assistance from outside the regular military structure. Having caught word of a volunteer defense force coalescing across Elwynn to the west, he turns directly to the People's Militia. The message is addressed directly to Gryan Stoutmantle, a veteran warrior organizing the frontier defense of Westfall. Solomon hopes Stoutmantle can spare fighters to reinforce Lakeshire until Stormwind's crown finally sends regular reserves. Entrusted to an adventurer acting as courier, the document reflects the fracturing administrative coordination across Stormwind's outlying territories, where local magistrates are left to negotiate mutual aid agreements on their own initiative.

item:soran-ruk-fragment.text: Soran'ruk Fragment. A Soran'ruk Fragment is a shattered shard of a demonic prison orb once bound to the spirit of a disgraced servant of the Burning Legion. Though split and dispersed among cultists deep beneath Ashenvale, each shard still radiates residual fel energy. When demons of the Burning Legion fall out of favor with their masters, their spirits are sometimes condemned to imprisonment inside specialized orbs and distributed to fel spellcasters as conduits of raw power. The orb of Soran'ruk met this fate, yet somewhere in its history, it was cracked apart. One half was broken into smaller shards and fell into the hands of the Twilight's Hammer cultists lurking within the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, who draw upon the lingering demonic essence for their own dark workings.

item:southsea-treasure.text: Southsea Treasure. The Southsea Treasure is a valuable hoard kept deep within the hold of the Southsea Freebooter vessel, the Tide Razor. Sought by Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet, retrieving it tests the lockpicking and infiltration skills of fledgling thieves. Anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, the pirate vessel Tide Razor serves as a forward base and training ground for the Southsea Freebooters. Stashed deep in its lowest hold lies a coveted stash of plunder known as the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel operating out of Ratchet, considers it the ultimate test for aspiring pickpockets. According to Wrenix, the last five operatives sent to filch the chest returned in pieces, owing to the alert pirates aboard and a surprisingly ferocious guardian guarding the hold.

item:spectral-comb.text: Spectral Comb. The Spectral Comb is an ethereal grooming tool used to interact with the restless dead of Duskwood. Fashioned to pass through intangible forms, it is brought to the sorrowful spirit Blind Mary to harvest strands of ghost hair. Normal implements cannot touch or groom a spirit, making gathering ethereal materials nearly impossible for mortal craftsmen. The Spectral Comb is specially suited to interact with ghostly forms, gliding through otherwise intangible tresses. It is carried south of Darkshire to the ruined farmstead where the weeping ghost Blind Mary wails in isolation. Finding solace in the familiar act of grooming her ruined hair, Mary willingly uses the comb, leaving behind the spectral fibers needed to weave Ghost Hair Thread.

item:spells-of-shadow.text: Spells of Shadow. Spells of Shadow is a dark grimoire carried by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar in Ragefire Chasm. Filled with fel magic granted by the Burning Legion, it is targeted for recovery by the Forsaken leadership in the Undercity. Hidden deep in the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm, members of the Searing Blade—a splinter cult tied to the Shadow Council—wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. Among their most guarded treasures is the Spells of Shadow, a text containing insidious shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks of the sect keep this book close at hand as they plot beneath the very feet of the Horde in Durotar. Word of the Searing Blade's demonic gifts reached the royal quarters of the Undercity. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, determined that such powerful relics were wasted on cultists with lesser vision. Varimathras tasks Horde adventurers with venturing into the chasm to seize the Spells of Shadow alongside its companion tome, Incantations from the Nether, directing their power toward the Forsaken cause against the Scourge and the Lich King.

item:spotted-sunfish.text: Spotted Sunfish. Spotted Sunfish are freshwater fish native to Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Renowned locally for their flavor, they are a staple commodity for Lakeshire's docks, though the growing murloc infestation makes procuring them hazardous. Lake Everstill has long been celebrated for its spotted sunfish, which fetch a dependable price among local merchants and visitors alike. Dockmaster Baren keeps a steady trade in them at the Lakeshire piers, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. However, the aggressive murloc tribes prowling the shallows have disrupted routine fishing, often stockpiling catches of their own that adventurers must recover by force.

item:stalker-claws.text: Stalker Claws. Stalker Claws are the talons harvested from the prairie stalkers roaming the rolling plains of Mulgore. Tauren shamans use them as vital components in carving traditional cleansing totems to purify tainted water wells. The grassy steppes of Mulgore are home to deadly natural predators, among them the stealthy prairie stalkers. These beasts survive through raw instinct and lethal precision, an essential balance within the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn, seeking to heal the blighted land, requires these claws not out of malice toward the animals, but because the pure, natural ferocity with which they hunt holds the spiritual resonance necessary to counteract artificial corruption. When goblin ventures began drilling and mining across central Kalimdor, chemical poisons seeped deep into the subterranean waters feeding the ancestral tauren wells. The Thunderhorn Water Well in particular fell prey to vile taint. By binding Stalker Claws and Cougar Claws into a Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem, tribal shamans create a spiritual conduit capable of scouring the muck and unnatural sludge out of the earth's natural springs.

item:steelgrill-s-tools.text: Steelgrill's Tools. Steelgrill's Tools are a specialized set of mechanic implements requisitioned for Beldin Steelgrill, the master technician of Steelgrill's Depot. Renowned for pushing siege engines—and his own equipment—to their limits, Beldin frequently breaks gear and relies on shipments from nearby Kharanos to keep his workshop running. Beldin Steelgrill is widely regarded as one of the finest siege engine technicians in Dun Morogh, but his aggressive repair style is infamous among local merchants. Working tirelessly on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, Beldin tends to destroy delicate equipment almost as fast as it can be forged. Between snapping arclight spanners and stripping fang-ratchets, the mechanic is constantly placing fresh orders in Kharanos to keep his repair benches stocked. This particular delivery of tools is vital for keeping Ironforge's war machines operational. At his depot northeast of Kharanos, Beldin is actively servicing combat vehicles for seasoned drivers like Pilot Stonegear. Without freshly supplied wrenches and ratchets, critical siege engines would sit half-assembled in the snow, leaving both the depot and local defenses stalled.

item:steelsnap-s-rib.text: Steelsnap's Rib. Steelsnap's Rib is a grim trophy taken from the carcass of the ferocious hyena Steelsnap in Thousand Needles. Brought back to Thunder Bluff, it serves as physical proof that a creature deemed outside the Earthmother's blessing has been put down. Most tauren hunts are undertaken for sustenance, for honor, or to seek harmony with nature. Steelsnap, however, represents a different kind of quarry. Roaming the canyon floor of Thousand Needles south of Camp E'thok, this vicious alpha hyena terrorizes peaceful wildlife and rallies packs of lesser predators to senseless bloodshed. When the hunt master Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise marks Steelsnap for death, he demands a heavy bone—Steelsnap's rib—as undeniable confirmation that the tyrant has been slain and the canyon cleansed of its blight.

item:stolen-silver.text: Stolen Silver. The Stolen Silver is a recovered strongbox of Horde coin meant for the Crossroads guard garrison. It was bizarrely carried off into the wilderness by the ferocious raptors of the Barrens, leading to disbelief among the outpost's overseers. The vast wilds of the Barrens present constant threats to supply lines, but few expected the local Sunscale raptors to target strongboxes of metal currency. When a shipment of silver meant as payroll for the Crossroads garrison was stolen from the guard tower, the raptors dragged the lockbox back to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. To overseers like Gazrog, the theft reveals an unsettling degree of cunning in the predators, who apparently value shiny trinkets or possess intelligence far beyond that of ordinary wild beasts.

item:stone-of-relu.text: Stone of Relu. The Stone of Relu is an ancient archaeological relic recovered from the Wetlands. Believed by Archaeologist Flagongut to be the key to unlocking latent powers within primordial fossils, it was briefly lost when local raptors ambushed the scholar on the road. Discovered during Explorers' League operations, the Stone of Relu is believed to hold the deciphering power needed to unlock prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Archaeologist Flagongut identified the artifact as the catalyst required to unleash secrets within both his own Wetlands specimens and the fossil unearthed by Prospector Remtravel in Darkshore. While Flagongut was traveling along the Wetland roads to rendezvous with Prospector Whelgar, a pack of mottled raptors ambushed him. During the scramble, the relic was lost and swallowed by one of the ravenous beasts, forcing the League to enlist adventurers to hunt the marsh raptors and cut the ancient stone from their gullets.

item:stonetalon-sap.text: Stonetalon Sap. Stonetalon Sap is a sticky, potent substance harvested directly from the lumbering sap beasts that roam the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a key reagent for the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses its raw woodland properties to concoct a spiteful brew.

item:stormpike-banner.text: Stormpike Banner. The Stormpike Banner is a military standard hidden deep within the treacherous Icewing Cavern in Alterac Valley. Alliance recruits must brave wild harpies to recover it as an initiation trial, proving they are worthy to wear the Stormpike insignia. To officially join the ranks of the Stormpike expedition in Alterac Valley, prospective recruits must prove their mettle before they ever clash with the Frostwolf orcs. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends newly arrived Alliance soldiers into the Icewing Caverns, situated southwest of Dun Baldar. Planted deep inside this frozen subterranean den, the Stormpike Banner serves as a testing ground: anyone brave enough to brave the native harpies, seize the standard, and bring it back alive earns the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.

item:stormpike-s-request.text: Stormpike's Request. Stormpike's Request is a written commission dispatched by Mountaineer Stormpike from the hills of Loch Modan to Stormwind City. The letter petitions master armorsmith Furen Longbeard to craft a custom shield of unmatched dwarven quality. While stationed far to the north in Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike requires a sturdy new shield to weather the dangers of the dwarven frontier. Rather than trusting an ordinary smith, he insists on commissioning Furen Longbeard, an armorsmith whose legendary craftsmanship he holds in the highest regard. Because Furen now resides far to the south among the humans of Stormwind's Dwarven District—lured away from Ironforge by what Stormpike assumes must be a king's ransom—the mountaineer relies on traveling adventurers to deliver his formal request across the kingdoms. Delivering the letter into the bustling Dwarven District of Stormwind places the order directly into Furen Longbeard's capable hands. As a proud and established dwarven clan known across Khaz Modan for both martial grit and substantial wealth, a Stormpike commission carries weight. Pleased to receive word and business from his ancestral northern homelands, Furen agrees to fulfill the order and set to work hammering out the mountaineer's shield.

item:stormwind-armor-marker.text: Stormwind Armor Marker. A Stormwind Armor Marker is an official military requisition token issued to adventurers who have aided the realm. It can be redeemed with sanctioned artisans, such as Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp, in exchange for freshly crafted gear. Maintaining law and order across Elwynn Forest stretches the resources of the realm thin. Rather than distributing standard gear directly from military outposts, commanders sometimes issue official tokens known as armor markers. These requisition slips verify that the bearer has performed valorous service for Stormwind and authorize local contracted craftsmen to supply them with tailored armor. One key destination for these markers is the Eastvale Logging Camp, situated on the eastern frontier of Elwynn. There, artisans like Sara Timberlain operate under commission from the Stormwind Army, turning local materials into protective cloth and leather garments. Presenting a marker grants recruits custom-fitted defense to aid them in safeguarding the surrounding woodlands.

item:stoutmantle-s-response-to-solomon.text: Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon is a written dispatch carried from Sentinel Hill to Lakeshire. In it, Gryan Stoutmantle grimly informs Magistrate Solomon that the embattled People's Militia cannot spare a single soldier to defend Redridge Mountains. Facing relentless pressure from Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire reached out to Sentinel Hill hoping Westfall's local forces could send reinforcements. Gryan Stoutmantle's written reply brings bitter news. Mourning Lakeshire's losses, Stoutmantle explains that Westfall is plagued with its own war. The People's Militia was formed out of desperation precisely because the Crown withdrew its garrison, leaving farmers and volunteers to battle the Defias Brotherhood alone.
