Stoutmantle explains that his own forces are bleeding and stretched thin, unable to sacrifice men to bail out another abandoned frontier.

item:strange-smelling-powder.text: Strange Smelling Powder. Strange Smelling Powder is an enigmatic residue uncovered during investigations into suspicious sabotage around Loch Modan. Feared to be an unstable demolition agent, it prompts Chief Engineer Hinderweir to send an urgent courier north to seek out a demolition expert. Discovered amid signs of sabotage threatening Loch Modan's infrastructure, this peculiar powder immediately raised alarm for Chief Engineer Hinderweir. Its pungent odor and fine consistency suggest an engineered demolition compound rather than standard mining blast powder. Unsure of the mixture's chemical nature or origin, Hinderweir refuses to tamper with it himself, knowing that even a slight spark could trigger disaster.

item:strangely-marked-box.text: Strangely Marked Box. A Strangely Marked Box is a piece of cargo discovered inside the harnesses strapped to dead sea turtles along the Darkshore coastline. Its mysterious exterior bears the runic script of the serpentine naga, offering night elf scholars proof that these sea creatures did not strand themselves by accident. While several giant sea turtles and sea creatures simply wash ashore along Darkshore's mist-veiled beaches, others tell a far more ominous tale. Scattered carcasses bear the splintered remnants of riding harnesses and abandoned carriages bound straight to their shells. Within the ruins of these buckled contraptions lie sealed containers covered in foreign, sinuous runes. Scavenging Greymist murlocs frequently take up residence in the hollow ribcages and broken wagons, picking at the carrion and guarding whatever remnants were left behind.

item:strigid-owl-feather.text: Strigid Owl Feather. Strigid Owl Feathers are gathered from the wild strigid owls nesting within the boughs of Teldrassil. While natural forest plumage, they are sought after by questionable figures seeking raw materials for their covert dealings.

item:sturdy-dragonmaw-shinbone.text: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbones are durable skeletal trophies gathered from the renegade Dragonmaw orcs in the Wetlands. Required by armor crafter Velora Nitely in the Undercity, they serve as reinforcement struts for bespoke warrior armor. When forging brutal leg guards for frontline warriors, smiths require raw components that can endure severe punishment. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely prizes the skeletal density of the renegade Dragonmaw orcs entrenched at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands. Dragonmaw orcs are known for their thick, sturdy frames, making their shins well suited to serve as structural bracers. However, not every collected bone can withstand the strain; warriors must test each piece with their bare hands, discarding those that snap under pressure.

item:sully-balloo-s-letter.text: Sully Balloo's Letter. Sully Balloo's Letter is a waterlogged, tender missive recovered from the sunken remains of a dwarven soldier beneath the Thandol Span. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it represents the quiet personal tragedies lingering beneath the grand conflicts of Khaz Modan. Beneath the massive stone pillars of the Thandol Span, connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands, lies the skeletal remains of a dwarf pinned deep under the rushing water. Clutched in his grasp is a fragile, waterlogged envelope containing this letter. Written with painstaking care in his final days or hours, it begins with the poignant words, 'My dear Sara....' Though the parchment has suffered from prolonged submersion, the ink still holds the enduring love of a dwarven defender who never made it back home to the city of Ironforge.

item:sunscorched-shell.text: Sunscorched Shell. Sunscorched Shells are the sturdy remnants of wyvern eggs gathered beneath the roosts of Highperch in Thousand Needles. Hardened by the harsh desert heat, they are prized by skilled armorcrafters who can render them into a protective lacquer for mail links. Perched high upon the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor, Highperch wyverns lay eggs that endure relentless desert sun and searing winds. The discarded shell fragments accumulate beneath their roosts, baked to remarkable hardness by the arid climate. While seemingly little more than brittle refuse to a casual wanderer, these sunscorched remains possess natural structural resilience that makes them an intriguing reagent for specialized artisans. In Darnassus, the armorer Mathiel studies crafting methods pioneered by his colleague, the dwarf smith Furen Longbeard. Intrigued by Furen's discoveries, Mathiel uses these shells to create a fine lacquer capable of reinforcing mail armor. When properly processed and applied, the mineral-rich coating bonds to metallic links, adding substantial resilience without overburdening the wearer.

item:super-reaper-6000-blueprints.text: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. The Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints are the technical schematics for an enormous mechanized woodcutter deployed by the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains. Designed under the supervision of the gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the plans are heavily coveted by his disgruntled goblin rivals. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting operation in Windshear Crag relies on massive mechanized lumber harvesters known as Super Reapers. To the utter dismay of traditional goblin engineers, the company placed a gnome named Gerenzo in charge of designing the Super Reaper 6000 model. These blueprints contain the schematics for the contraption, carried by Venture Co. operators working the machinery across the crag. When the goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was ousted from the operation, he was quickly hired by Sputtervalve to steal the designs. However, deciphering Gerenzo's dense, eccentric gnomish technical notations proves to be almost as difficult as taking the blueprints by force.

item:supplies-for-sven.text: Supplies for Sven. Supplies for Sven is a bundle of vital provisions packaged in Darkshire and destined for Sven Yorgen's secluded camp. Surrounded by the horrors of Duskwood, Sven and his small band rely on sympathetic townspeople like the Carevin family to sustain their vigil against the shadows. Carrying survival gear and basic necessities through Duskwood is no simple chore. Sven Yorgen and his handful of followers camp in the northwestern wilderness of the woods, far from the safety of Darkshire. Their numbers are so depleted and their watch so demanding that they cannot spare a single fighter to make the trek into town. This parcel represents a lifeline sent by the Carevin family, ensuring that the isolated camp has the food, bandages, and materials needed to hold their ground.

item:surena-s-choker.text: Surena's Choker. Surena's Choker is an enchanted bloodstone necklace gifted by Gakin the Darkbinder to his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. After Surena betrayed Gakin and fled to join the Defias Brotherhood, the warlock master sent aspiring acolytes to reclaim the piece by force. Gakin the Darkbinder, operating quietly from beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, took Surena Caledon on as a promising student in the dark arts. Taken by her youthful charm and magical aptitude, Gakin presented her with a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. However, Surena abandoned her training and absconded with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood. Unwilling to let such a potent artifact remain in the hands of a traitor, Gakin task initiates seeking mastery over the void to track Surena down to the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, reclaim the necklace, and demonstrate where true loyalty lies.

item:swoop-gizzard.text: Swoop Gizzard. A swoop gizzard is an organ harvested from the predatory birds soaring over Mulgore. Highly sought after for traditional folk remedies, it serves as a crucial ingredient for cleansing deadly toxins. Swoops are predatory avian hunters native to the plains and mesas of Mulgore, known for their keen eyesight and scavenging nature. While their feathers and meat serve everyday uses for the tauren, their internal organs—particularly the gizzard—are prized by herbalists and healers. When combined with other potent animal remnants like cougar bones and wolf hearts, the dense muscular organ aids in neutralizing venomous animal bites and halting festering systemic infections. In Bloodhoof Village, the medicine worker Maur Raincaller fell prey to the legendary plainstrider Mazzranache, suffering a vicious, venomous wound to his shoulder. Falling into delirium from the creeping poison, Maur relies on a swoop gizzard alongside a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, and a plainstrider scale to concoct a curative poultice capable of expelling the beast's lethal venom.

item:tablet-of-verga.text: Tablet of Verga. The Tablet of Verga is an arcane stone inscribed with demonic runes essential for binding dark entities. Stolen by the sinister Burning Blade cult, it was taken deep into their lair within Skull Rock. Recovering the artifact allows dark practitioners in Orgrimmar to decipher the rituals needed to bind a voidwalker. The Tablet of Verga holds specific ritual runes required to summon and bend creatures of the Nether to a master's will. When the Burning Blade cult managed to steal the tablet, they concealed it within a hidden chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. For the warlocks working discreetly in the shadows of the Cleft of Shadow, regaining the relic is crucial—not only to study its ancient markings for summoning a voidwalker, but also to deny the fanatical cultists their own dark advantage.

item:tainted-heart.text: Tainted Heart. The Tainted Heart is a blighted floral core extracted from the corrupt flora of Teldrassil. Given to adventurers by the botanist Denalan, it requires magical and nutritive cleansing to rid it of lingering foul energies. Teldrassil's natural balance suffers from an unnatural malady, warping its native plants and beasts. After stripping away foul moss that clung to a blighted growth, Denalan presents this lingering core: the Tainted Heart. Though freed of its outer rot, darkness still permeates the tissue. Denalan seeks to discover whether specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counteract the lingering taint and restore life to what was corrupted.

item:tainted-keg.text: Tainted Keg. The Tainted Keg is a barrel of stolen dwarven stout laced with a lethal Forsaken brew concocted by Apothecary Lydon. Delivered under the guise of refreshments to imprisoned human farmers in Tarren Mill, it serves as a gruesome field test for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing poisons. The keg began its existence as a barrel of Shindigger Stout, plundered from the dwarven riflemen entrenched at Dun Garok. Rather than drinking it, Apothecary Lydon contaminated the hearty ale with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. By lacing an ordinary beverage, the Forsaken crafted an insidious vector designed to slip past suspicion, turning a familiar comforts of the living into a swift death sentence.

item:tainted-letter.text: Tainted Letter. The Tainted Letter is a discreetly delivered summons bearing the seal of Drusilla La Salle, a warlock trainer lurking on the outskirts of Northshire Abbey. It directs aspiring human practitioners of the dark arts to report to her for specialized tutelage away from watchful eyes. While priests, paladins, and standard soldiers train openly across the manicured lawns of Northshire Abbey, practitioners of fel magic must operate with far greater discretion. Handed to initiates returning from the nearby kobold camps, this letter carries the personal insignia of Drusilla La Salle. Bearing subtle traces of dark artifice, the missive instructs novice warlocks to seek out their mentor discreetly near the abbey's grounds before the local town guards and clerics become suspicious of their forbidden path. Meeting Drusilla reveals the necessity for such secretive measures. Warlocks are viewed with deep distrust by the mundane populace of Elwynn, forcing mentors to linger on the fringes and avoid prying sentries. Drusilla uses the delivered letter to initiate a critical lesson in discipline: arcane and nether magic invite relentless corruption, requiring practitioners to temper their surging ambition with patient self-control while communing with denizens of the Twisting Nether.

item:tainted-memorandum.text: Tainted Memorandum. The Tainted Memorandum is a discreet note handed to novice gnome warlocks starting out in Coldridge Valley. Penned by the warlock trainer Alamar Grimm, it urges the reader to cast aside traditional paths and seek out the true power offered by the dark arts. In the chilly dwarven outpost of Anvilmar, practitioners of fel magic are neither celebrated nor widely trusted. For young gnomes dabbling in forbidden arts, the Tainted Memorandum serves as an invitation from Alamar Grimm. The message rejects reliance on the Holy Light or mundane martial steel, pointing instead to the fall of Gnomeregan as proof that conventional methods and tinkering have failed their people. To Grimm, relying on dwarven charity is a dead end; gnomes must seize undeniable power and summon unquestioning minions if they ever hope to secure their own future.

item:talisman-of-corruption.text: Talisman of Corruption. The Talisman of Corruption is a vile demonic trinket used by the satyr Xabraxxis to poison the minds of Darkshore's Blackwood furbolgs. Carried within the satyr's personal pouch, it serves as a magical conduit that binds the tribe to fel madness. The night elves of Auberdine have long struggled to understand why the Blackwood furbolgs turned so aggressively upon their former allies. Thundris Windweaver discovered that the tribe's downfall was not a natural descent, but deliberate sabotage orchestrated by the satyrs. Using talismans like this one, demonic agents project corrupting sorcery across the wilderness, tainting food supplies and twisting peaceful forest spirits into frenzied beasts. By channeling fell magics directly through these devices, the satyrs hold an unbroken grip over the minds and wills of the local tribes.

item:tallonkai-s-jewel.text: Tallonkai's Jewel. Tallonkai's Jewel is a luminous emerald stolen from an enchanted druidic talisman on Teldrassil. Prized by the furbolg mystic Ferocitas the Dream Eater, it serves as the crucial centerpiece required to mend the Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot was given the Emerald Dreamcatcher by Gaerolas Talvethen, warden of the druids in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, as a potent focus that siphons energy from the Emerald Dream. When his talisman was damaged, the central radiant emerald was pried loose and carried off into the wilds of eastern Teldrassil. The jewel fell into the paws of Ferocitas the Dream Eater, a corrupted Gnarlpine leader who fashioned the gleaming stone into a personal necklace. While the green stone cast an eerie glow in the forest gloom, its true harmonious resonance was entirely useless to the furbolg, serving merely as a trophy until retrieved.

item:taming-rod.text: Taming Rod. A Taming Rod is an instructional tool entrusted to novice hunters by their trainers. Infused with simple binding magic, it allows a student to temporarily pacify and command local wildlife to master the fundamentals of beast handling. Novice hunters cannot immediately exert the mental force required to bind a wild creature to their will permanently. To bridge that gap, veteran trainers issue specialized Taming Rods. In places like Razor Hill, mentors such as Thotar give aspiring orc and troll hunters these enchanted implements to subdue regional predators—such as dire mottled boars and armored scorpids. The rod temporarily pacifies the beast, allowing the handler to practice issuing commands and fighting alongside an animal companion without the danger of an unbreakable primal bond forming prematurely. The control granted by a Taming Rod is fleeting, typically lasting only a short while before the magic fades. Each rod is attuned to specific types of wild beasts, serving as a stepping stone through successive trials. Once a novice has proved they can command various wild temperaments—from docile foragers to aggressive venomous hunters—the rod is returned to the trainer. Having demonstrated proper technique, the student is finally taught the innate art of taming, calling, and dismissing lifelong companions without needing an artifact.

item:tattered-manuscript.text: Tattered Manuscript. The Tattered Manuscript consists of loose, vandalized pages torn from the singular copy of the Tome of the Cabal. Hidden away in the dusty depths of southern Kalimdor, this battered portion of the text holds arcane secrets vital to warlocks seeking mastery over felhunters. The Tome of the Cabal was once an intact, unique volume safeguarded within the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, an unknown defiler ripped almost half of the treatise directly from its binding. While the surviving spine and remainder of the book—now known as the Moldy Tome—were shipped south toward Khaz Modan and lost at sea, these torn parchment leaves drifted far across the Great Sea into Kalimdor, ultimately falling into the hands of the Galak centaur inside Splithoof Hold. Kept within a battered chest deep within the labyrinthine caverns of Splithoof Hold, the manuscript survived the harsh arid winds of Thousand Needles. Despite its fragile, tattered state, practitioners of the dark arts—both Alliance warlocks working with Krom Stoutarm in Ironforge and Horde practitioners aiding Jorah Annison in the Undercity—brave the aggressive centaur to reunite these lost leaves with the Moldy Tome. Once combined, the completed treatise contains the dark rituals necessary to summon and bind a demonic felhunter.

item:tazan-s-satchel.text: Tazan's Satchel. Tazan's Satchel is a locked pouch carried by the troll Tazan, who operates alongside pirates near Ratchet. It holds secret information coveted by the Shattered Hand, the covert guild of rogues based beneath Orgrimmar. Within the sun-baked wastes of the Barrens, a troll named Tazan carries on illicit dealings with the pirates encamped along the coast near Ratchet. These under-the-table arrangements drew the keen eyes of Therzok, a guild master of the Shattered Hand situated in the subterranean gloom of the Cleft of Shadow. Seeking to build covert power away from Warchief Thrall's cautious diplomacy, the Shattered Hand marked Tazan for elimination to seize the valuable intelligence bound within his satchel.

item:tear-of-the-moons.text: Tear of the Moons. The Tear of the Moons is a mysterious, radiant crystal unearthed by dwarven excavators at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Though prized by the dwarven expedition, it carries a volatile and corruptive power that led directly to obsession, exile, and bloodshed. Discovered during the initial excavations of Bael Modan, the crystal was celebrated as the dig site's first major triumph. Its strange radiance captivated the miners, but none more intensely than Feegly. Claiming the relic gifted him profound strength, Feegly fell under its sway. Fearing the artifact's dark influence—and alarmed by Feegly's increasingly unstable behavior toward his comrades—expedition commander General Twinbraid declared the stone cursed. Twinbraid confiscated the relic, sealed it securely inside his personal strongbox within Bael'dun Keep, and cast Feegly out into the Barrens wasteland.

item:tear-of-tilloa.text: Tear of Tilloa. The Tear of Tilloa is a delicate, pale blossom found in the shadows of Duskwood. Desired for its potent alchemical properties, it grows quietly in the overgrown grounds of the Mistmantle estate near Darkshire. Growing amidst the encroaching blighted woods outside Darkshire, the Tear of Tilloa takes root within the estate grounds of Stalvan Mistmantle. Though Duskwood's soil has turned hostile to wholesome vegetation, this small white flower persists among the shadowed plots. Its scarce growth and secluded location make it an object of interest for those seeking rare reagents not easily discovered in lawful markets.

item:techbot-s-memory-core.text: Techbot's Memory Core. Techbot's Memory Core is the polarized central repository of Tinkmaster Overspark's mechanical assistant, Techbot. Recovered from the malfunctioning automaton within the corrupted depths of Gnomeregan, it contains the critical data Overspark hopes to use to reverse the machine's reversed, negatronic behavior. Before the catastrophe that forced the gnomes into exile, Techbot served Tinkmaster Overspark and his fellow inventors as an indispensable assistant, packed with gizmos and encyclopedic data. When Gnomeregan fell, an errant electrical discharge jolted the automaton, inverting its positronic brain into a hostile negatronic state. Driven mad by the reversal, Techbot now wanders the tainted halls of the city attacking anyone in sight. Recovering its memory core is Overspark's only hope for analyzing the malfunction and restoring his prized creation to its senses.

item:telescopic-lens.text: Telescopic Lens. The Telescopic Lens is a precision optical component imported by Gazlowe to complete the construction of the Ratchet observatory. Intercepted along the coast by Southsea pirates, the fragile glass must be recovered from their encampment south of town before the port's grand telescope can scan the skies. Ratchet is known primarily as a port of ruthless commerce, but its chief engineer and overseer, Gazlowe, harbors grander mechanical ambitions. Prominently perched over the harbor, his observatory was built to house a powerful telescope to monitor maritime traffic and astronomical phenomena. While the larger lens arrived safely via an overland caravan from Durotar, the vital smaller lens was routed by sea—making it easy prey for the Southsea Freebooters who plague the merchant lanes off the Barrens coastline. When the Freebooters raided the transport ship, they hauled off anything of value, packing the delicate optics into a crate marked 'Fragile - Do Not Drop.' Unable to appreciate the fine craftsmanship or simply unsure how to pawn it, the buccaneers left the lens stashed amidst the clutter of their beachside camp south of Ratchet. Gazlowe relies on daring adventurers to brave the cutthroats, secure the unblemished glass, and finally bring his observation deck into focus.

item:teronis-journal.text: Teronis' Journal. Teronis' Journal is a field notebook recovered from the remains of a night elf scout in Ashenvale. Found alongside the slain investigator, it documents his search for a mysterious gem and serves as vital evidence for the Sentinels in Astranaar. A longtime friend of Raene Wolfrunner aiding the Sentinels, Teronis ventured into the wilds of Ashenvale seeking a gem for a rod he believed could slow the furbolg attacks on his people. His mission ended abruptly when he fell in the field, surrounded by aggressive creatures near the shore. Recovered from his personal effects, this journal remains in remarkably good condition despite the violence of his demise. It outlines his findings regarding a radiant gem that once formed part of that rod, providing Astranaar's defenders with the vital trail needed to see his unfinished mission through.

item:tharil-zun-s-head.text: Tharil'zun's Head. This grizzly trophy is the severed head of Tharil'zun, leader of the Blackrock orc Outrunners occupying Stonewatch. Marshal Marris demands it as irrefutable proof that the commander terrorizing the Redridge approaches has been slain. The Blackrock orcs entrenched within Stonewatch Keep have exerted ruthless pressure on Lakeshire, raiding farms and ambushing travelers along the roads. At the vanguard of these raiding parties were the Blackrock Outrunners, orchestrated by Tharil'zun. Because the garrison in Lakeshire cannot afford to act on rumors or partial victories, Marshal Marris demands concrete proof of the leader's demise. Bringing him Tharil'zun's severed head demonstrates that the coordinated ambushes from the keep have suffered a major blow.

item:tharnariun-s-hope.text: Tharnariun's Hope. Tharnariun's Hope is a specialized trap crafted by the night elf Tharnariun Treetender in Darkshore. Designed to pacify diseased wildlife rather than harm it, the device projects a calming light intended to tame rabid thistle bears so they can be examined for a cure. As a mysterious affliction spreads through Darkshore, the local thistle bears have grown increasingly frenzied and violent. Rather than sanctioning a cull of the afflicted wildlife, the druid Tharnariun Treetender crafted this unique trap in the hope of studying and curing the illness. When laid upon the ground, Tharnariun's Hope emits a soothing radiance. Any rabid thistle bear that steps across the trap's light has its frenzy temporarily broken, rendering the beast docile enough to follow an adventurer back to Tharnariun's camp for treatment.

item:the-book-of-ur.text: The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a scholarly magical treatise penned by the late Dalaran wizard Ur, detailing his research into strange extradimensional entities. Left behind in Shadowfang Keep, it fell into the hands of Archmage Arugal before drawing the keen interest of Forsaken researchers in the Undercity. Before Dalaran fell to the Scourge, Ur was renowned among the Kirin Tor for his esoteric investigations into other planes of existence and otherworldly creatures. Despite his fascination with extraplanar magic, Ur was guided by caution and ethical restraint, choosing to record his discoveries rather than recklessly breach the veil between worlds. Tragically, when the Scourge assaulted the violet city, his magical prowess and moral hesitations were not enough to save him.

item:the-collector-s-schedule.text: The Collector's Schedule. The Collector's Schedule is a handwritten itinerary detailing dates and times for illicit gold shipments extracted from the mines of Elwynn Forest. Recovered from local gnolls, the document reveals that an elusive figure known only as 'The Collector' is coordinating the operation from near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. The schedule provides alarming evidence of organized activity right under the nose of Stormwind's garrison. Although the kingdom has not formally operated Elwynn's mines for months due to banditry and creature incursions, ore is still being systematically extracted and moved. The note lists specific days and times when someone titled 'The Collector' receives shipments, pointing toward a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. When presented with the document, Marshal Dughan recognizes the name of the Collector, though the true mastermind paying for the stolen gold remains hidden.

item:the-embalmer-s-heart.text: The Embalmer's Heart. The Embalmer's Heart is an unholy relic beating within the undead corpse of Eliza, buried deep in Duskwood. Once belonging to a grief-stricken alchemist known as the Embalmer, it was transplanted through dark magic to revive his deceased wife, becoming the primary anchor of his twisted power. According to the folklore of Darkshire, the Embalmer was once a gentle alchemist whose mind shattered upon the passing of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to reclaim her from the grave, he turned to foul sorceries and cut out his own heart, placing it inside Eliza's lifeless chest. While the unholy transfusion successfully stirred her corpse back to unlife, the resurrection twisted her into a ravenous creature consumed by an insatiable hunger for living human flesh, forcing the horror-stricken alchemist to inter her once more within the earth.

item:the-general-s-response.text: The General's Response. The General's Response is an official military dispatch written by General Marcus Jonathan, commander of the Stormwind city guard. Intended for Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire, the missive acknowledges Redridge's plea for aid while revealing that the capital cannot—or will not—immediately send royal reinforcements. When Magistrate Solomon reaches out to Stormwind City desperately seeking troops to fend off the gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands in Redridge, he sends his plea straight to the high command. General Marcus Jonathan's written response delivers cold comfort: while the plea has been forwarded upward to the throne, no soldiers are currently dispatched. Caught between protocol and politics, the General orders the letter delivered back to Lakeshire, leaving Solomon troubled and suspicious that a deeper sickness paralyzes the capital's leadership.

item:the-lich-s-spellbook.text: The Lich's Spellbook. The Lich's Spellbook is a volume of necromantic lore kept within a chest on the island in Brightwater Lake. Recovered for Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, the tome reveals the true identity and immense magical power of a reclusive undead lich dwelling just north of the Forsaken capital. On an isolated island in Brightwater Lake stands an enigmatic lich surrounded by skeletal guardians. Though free-willed, this sorcerer distrusts the outside world, mistaking all other undead for thralls of the Scourge and ordering his minions to destroy any who approach. Bethor Iceshard, seeking gifted necromancers to bolster the Forsaken ranks beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked an emissary with infiltrating the island camp to retrieve the lich's spellbook. Through its study, Bethor hoped to discern the master's magical aptitude and uncover who he was before death took Lordaeron.

item:the-state-of-lakeshire.text: The State of Lakeshire. The State of Lakeshire is an urgent written report penned by Magistrate Solomon detailing the desperate military crisis gripping the town of Lakeshire. Intended directly for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind, the document pleads for the capital to deploy royal army reinforcements before the Redridge settlement falls. Penned by Magistrate Solomon amid relentless attacks on Redridge, 'The State of Lakeshire' outlines the dire circumstances threatening the township. Besieged by hostile Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Lakeshire lacks the local manpower to hold its borders indefinitely. Entrusted to trusted couriers traveling the road west to Elwynn Forest, this dispatch carries Solomon's formal request for the Stormwind Army to intervene and preserve the eastern reach of the kingdom. Upon delivery to General Marcus Jonathan at Stormwind's gates, the general acknowledges Solomon's noble standing and the gravity of the report. However, Jonathan cannot mobilize the army unilaterally. Military deployments require the explicit consent of the crown, forcing Lakeshire's urgent plea to wait upon high-level council with the young King and the regent Bolvar Fordragon.

item:theramore-medal.text: Theramore Medal. A Theramore Medal is a military insignia carried by the Alliance garrison stationed at Northwatch Hold. Emblazoned with the mark of Theramore, these tokens serve as identifying proof of service among the marines and officers defending the outpost along the Merchant Coast. Carried by marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving out of Northwatch Hold, these stamped medals signify military allegiance to Lady Jaina Proudmoore's realm of Theramore. To the human soldiers perched on the cliffs overlooking the Barrens, they represent legitimate service and sovereign authority in a hostile frontier. To outsiders, however, the medals are trophies of an overzealous foreign garrison that treats every approaching vessel along the coast as a mortal threat. Northwatch Hold's gun batteries pose a deadly hazard to maritime traffic navigating the Merchant Coast, frequently bombarding privateers and merchantmen alike. In response to lost vessels, Ratchet privateer Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun seeks these medals as proof that Northwatch's trigger-happy ranks have paid in blood for sinking his ships.

item:thick-bear-fur.text: Thick Bear Fur. Thick Bear Fur is a prized pelt gathered from the cold-hardened bears roaming the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh. Coveted for its heat retention, it is commonly used by traveling scouts and soldiers to craft insulation and warm bedding against the bitter alpine freeze. The bears prowling the ridges of Dun Morogh endure some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick, resilient coats provide vital protection from blizzards, making the pelt an invaluable resource for locals and travelers alike. Rather than being discarded as scrap, these heavy pelts are regularly harvested by hunters and used to line clothes, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls. When Pilot Bellowfiz began outfitting his siege tank, Jetsteam, at Steelgrill's Depot, he faced the harsh prospect of spending a full month in the field on a long mission for the Siege Brigade. Because cold iron offers little comfort in high-altitude snowbanks, he commissioned local scouts to gather thick bear furs from the snow fields south of the Grizzled Den to fashion warm bedding for his cabin quarters.

item:thistlenettle-s-badge.text: Thistlenettle's Badge. Thistlenettle's Badge is an official insignia of the dwarven Explorers' League, once carried proudly by Foreman Thistlenettle into the depths of the Deadmines. Following a catastrophic cave-in and an invasion of thieves, the token is all that remains to confirm the foreman's tragic fate to his surviving brother in Stormwind. Before the Defias Brotherhood locked down Moonbrook and the cavernous tunnels beneath it, dwarven prospectors affiliated with Ironforge's Explorers' League delved into the old gold mines of Westfall. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew worked deep underground until a sudden tunnel collapse separated the team. While his brother Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind City, the foreman and several laborers remained trapped in the subterranean dark.

item:thresher-eye.text: Thresher Eye. Thresher Eyes are organic harvesting samples taken from the threshers prowling the coastal waters of Darkshore. They are sought by the eccentric gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle to service his automated field devices known as Buzzboxes. Off the misty shores of Darkshore, aquatic predators known as Darkshore Threshers hunt along the surf and outer shallows. While dangerous to local fishermen and travelers, these beasts possess large ocular organs that have drawn the peculiar interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. Stationed nearby and deeply fond of crawler wine, the gnomish engineer demands these eyes as essential components to repair Buzzbox 411, one of his far-speaking communication machines, positioned on the beach north of Auberdine. Wizbang never fully elaborates on how slimy sea-creature eyes repair delicate mechanical apparatuses, whether functioning as crude optical lenses, chemical agents, or esoteric biological gears. Regardless of the questionable engineering logic, feeding three of these harvested eyes into Buzzbox 411's maintenance hatch successfully restores the machine's comms link, allowing Wizbang to dispense rewards through static-choked transmissions.

item:thule-s-head.text: Thule's Head. Thule's Head is the grisly proof demanded by the Forsaken to confirm the demise of Thule Ravenclaw, commander of the Scourge forces on Fenris Isle. Bringing this macabre trophy back to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher solidifies the Forsaken's hold on Silverpine Forest. Fenris Isle serves as the primary bastion of the Lich King's Scourge within Silverpine Forest. From deep inside Fenris Keep, the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw directs his legions of rot hides and undead minions, directly threatening Forsaken outposts like the Sepulcher. High Executor Hadrec requires absolute certainty that this dark commander has fallen, refusing to accept any testimony short of Thule's severed head. The violent release of dark magic upon Ravenclaw's death was felt across the woods, but his head remains the physical proof Hadrec requires to declare Fenris Isle broken.

item:thunder-lizard-blood.text: Thunder Lizard Blood. Thunder Lizard Blood is a vital fluid taken from the massive thunder lizards wandering the southern Barrens. It serves as martial proof of survival against some of Kalimdor's most crushing terrestrial beasts. Thunder lizards, known across the plains as Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads, are colossal beasts whose heavy strides shake the earth. Hunting them is an exercise in perilous footing, as their crushing weight easily flattens unwary stalkers. Bringing back their blood demonstrates not just hunting prowess, but the sheer endurance needed to survive a bout beneath their thundering feet.

item:thunder-lizard-horn.text: Thunder Lizard Horn. A thunder lizard horn is a hardy trophy harvested from the massive, lightning-attuned thunder lizards wandering the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks this unusual reagent to recreate a legendary beverage originally concocted by Chen Stormstout. Thunder lizards roam the arid flats of the Barrens, crackling with raw, localized lightning that arcs from their crested bodies. While hunters occasionally seek their thick hides, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet values their horns for a very different purpose. Handed down from a mentor who learned it from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout, the recipe for Stormstout ale calls for unusual, potent local ingredients. The horn of a thunder lizard provides the electrifying kick that gives the legendary draught its fiery, unforgettable bite.

item:thunderhawk-saliva-gland.text: Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. A Thunderhawk Saliva Gland is a potent biological reagent harvested from the greater thunderhawks that soar over the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet prizes it as an essential ingredient for recreating Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. The arid savannas of the Barrens are home to thunderhawks—winged serpents renowned for harnessing the storm itself. Among their population, the older and more dangerous greater thunderhawks produce a saliva gland charged with raw, natural potency. While ordinary travelers steer clear of these deadly beasts, skilled brewmasters recognize the organ's rare properties as an extraordinary base for exotic concoctions. Following the legendary wandering brewmaster Chen Stormstout's travels through Kalimdor, Brewmaster Drohn settled outside Ratchet to master the pandaren's remarkable fermentation techniques. Drohn requires a fresh thunderhawk saliva gland alongside stormhide lightning glands and kodo liver to brew Trogg Ale, a fiery spirit with an unmistakable kick intended to fortify hardy adventurers.

item:thunderhawk-wings.text: Thunderhawk Wings. Thunderhawk Wings are feathered trophies taken from the fierce wind serpents soaring above the central and southern Barrens. Presented to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, they serve as definitive proof of a hunter's strength, cunning, and endurance in tracking down one of the savanna's most majestic predators. Wind serpents, known to local hunters as thunderhawks, are formidable winged reptiles capable of striking swiftly from above. For the hunters stationed at Camp Taurajo, harvesting a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings is far more than collecting biological scraps; it represents the culmination of grueling hunting trials in the Barrens. By tracking the aerial predators across the open plains and claiming their wings in combat, an initiate proves their readiness to walk the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

item:thunderhorn-cleansing-totem.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. The Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. It is imbued with ancestral magic to purify the corrupted waters of the Thunderhorn Water Well. Across the rolling plains of Mulgore, the lifeblood of the earth is being fouled by unseen corruption. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes provide vital nourishment to the herds and hunting grounds, but foul agents have tainted the water. Entrusted by the elder Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers carry this prepared totem north of Bloodhoof Village to drive out the pollution settling over the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the disturbed spirits of the water and cleanses the ancestral site.

item:thurman-s-remains.text: Thurman's Remains. Thurman's Remains are the corporeal remnants of Thurman Agamand, recovered from the family's ruined mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a wealthy mill owner who persuaded his workers to stand against the Scourge, Thurman succumbed to the Plague and wanders his former estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the most prosperous landowners in Tirisfal Glades, operating extensive mills and employing dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate rather than fleeing. Convinced that their wealth and fortified mills could weather the onslaught, they persuaded their loyal laborers to take up arms beside them. The defense failed utterly. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and transformed into mindless servants of the Lich King. Today, Coleman Farthing—a former employee risen as Forsaken—demands the destruction of his former masters, seeking Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch has paid for dooming his household.

item:thurman-s-sewing-kit.text: Thurman's Sewing Kit. Thurman's Sewing Kit is a small pouch containing the needles and shears required by an apprentice tailor in Stormwind City. Belonging to Thurman Schneider, it was conveniently left behind at his family's canal home in an attempt to dodge a long day of tedious tailoring work. The sewing kit holds the everyday tools of an apprentice tailor: needles, shears, and thread. It belongs to young Thurman Schneider, who studies tailoring at Larson Clothiers deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. Knowing her son cannot perform his duties without his equipment, his mother, Rema Schneider, asks sympathetic passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. Thurman's reaction upon receiving it reveals that leaving his shears and needles behind was no accident, but rather a failed plot to skip out on stitching garments in favor of leisure.

item:timberling-seed.text: Timberling Seed. Timberling Seeds are botanical kernels harvested from the agitated plant elementals inhabiting Teldrassil. Naturalists and druids study these seeds to understand why the forest's plant life has grown unusually aggressive. The timberlings of Teldrassil are nature elementals whose temperament reflects the balance of the World Tree. Recently, these creatures have turned hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists like Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth believe the issue lies rooted in the soil, collecting seeds from wild timberlings in hopes that nurturing them under controlled, purified conditions might sprout docile offspring.

item:timberling-sprout.text: Timberling Sprout. Timberling Sprouts are young, nascent plant elementals taking root near the shores of Lake Al'Ameth in Teldrassil. Even in their earliest growth, these sprouts show signs of corruption, prompting night elf wardens to pull them before they mature into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits closely tied to the natural vitality of Teldrassil, but the seedlings sprouting along Lake Al'Ameth have worried the local night elves. Rather than emerging healthy and in harmony with the wild, they sprout already tainted and aggressive. Because these infant sprouts appear beyond cleansing or natural healing, caretakers at Lake Al'Ameth must gather and destroy them to prevent an uncontrolled spread of hostile timberlings across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

item:tirisfal-pumpkin.text: Tirisfal Pumpkin. Tirisfal Pumpkins grow in the tilled plots of the Solliden Farmstead, tended by surviving living humans struggling to survive in the blighted glades. The Forsaken routinely raid these fields to supply the Royal Apothecary Society with organic matter for their ongoing chemical concoctions. Despite the corruption settling over Lordaeron, crops still somehow sprout in the fields west of Brill. At the Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers cling to their soil, cultivating massive orange squash under the watchful guard of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. For these mortals, the harvest is vital sustenance. For the nearby Forsaken of Brill, however, the pumpkins represent both a spiteful target of sabotage and a bounty of raw organic reagents needed by Apothecary Johaan. Deathguard Simmer directs young Forsaken out into the contested fields to pilfer the pumpkins directly from beneath the farmers' noses. Rather than feeding the dead, these vegetables find their way into the boiling cauldrons of the Royal Apothecary Society. The apothecaries frequently test how natural flora reacts to their plagues and experimental mixtures, turning Lordaeron's remaining agriculture against the living.

item:token-of-thievery.text: Token of Thievery. The Token of Thievery is a proof of skill recovered by novice rogues during their training in the Redridge Mountains. Placed inside a locked footlocker at the orc-threatened Alther's Mill, it serves as the final test set by the seasoned thief Lucius to demonstrate mastery over lockpicking. Not every scoundrel possesses an innate knack for working tumblers and slipping catches unnoticed. In Lakeshire, the roguish instructor Lucius puts promising operatives through their paces by testing their wits and tools in the field. Rather than keeping his trials confined to quiet alleys, Lucius stashes the Token of Thievery inside a sturdy lockbox hidden among the ruins of Alther's Mill, directly in the path of encroaching Blackrock orcs. Retrieving the token proves that an initiate can pick a secure mechanism under the pressure of mortal danger, earning them their formal Certificate of Thievery.

item:tome-of-the-cabal-quest-item.text: Tome of the Cabal (quest item). The Tome of the Cabal is a grimoire entrusted to warlocks by Strahad Farsan on the bluffs overlooking Ratchet. It holds the perilous incantations necessary to pull a ravenous felhunter across the Twisting Nether and bind it to the summoner's will. Felhunters are vicious, mana-devouring beasts native to the chaotic expanse of the Twisting Nether. Subduing one is a rite of passage for seasoned warlocks, and the rituals required to tear open a pathway for such a beast are contained within the pages of the Tome of the Cabal. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer operating out of Ratchet, provides the tome only after an aspirant has proven capable of gathering the rare and hazardous components needed to fuel its magics. Summoning from the tome is far from a solo endeavor. Strahad establishes a primary summoning circle within his sanctum, while his acolytes employ rods of channeling to construct a greater protective boundary. The warlock must then recite the tome's exact incantations to drag the felhunter into our world, immediately battling and subduing the ravenous demon to cement their dominion over it.

item:top-of-gelkak-s-key.text: Top of Gelkak's Key. The Top of Gelkak's Key is one of three shattered fragments of a mechanical key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel was lost off the coast of Darkshore, this jagged brass section was snatched up by a giant foreststrider roaming the nearby woods. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was attacked and sunk by ravenous threshadons off the coast of Darkshore, the gnome washed ashore clutching the winding key meant for his mechanical first mate. The impact against the coastal rocks broke the instrument into three pieces. Before the dizzy pirate could gather his wits, the indigenous beasts scavenged the wreckage, with a giant foreststrider making off with this ornate upper portion into the misty forest.

item:torch-of-the-dormant-flame.text: Torch of the Dormant Flame. The Torch of the Dormant Flame is a ritual implement carried by young Horde shaman during their communion with fire in Durotar. Awaiting the defeat of a flame manifestation atop the mountain, it serves as a vessel meant to capture primal elemental fire upon the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. A shaman seeking the favor of fire is entrusted with the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame before ascending the peaks above Durotar. After drinking a spirit-revealing fire sapta, the shaman sees and challenges a Minor Manifestation of Fire upon the mountaintop. Slaying this elemental spirit yields a glowing ember, which is deposited into the weathered brazier of the Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Touching the head of the dormant torch to the resulting white-hot conflagration awakens the wood, transforming it into a burning emblem of elemental mastery.

item:torn-fin-eye.text: Torn Fin Eye. Torn Fin Eyes are ocular organs harvested from the Torn Fin murlocs prowling the shores of Hillsbrad Foothills. They serve as a crucial reactive ingredient for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim alchemical research into new plagues. The Royal Apothecary Society rarely lets any vile biological component go to waste in their quest to develop the Forsaken's New Plague. Torn Fin Eyes, harvested from the salt-crusted murlocs prowling the Western Strand of Hillsbrad Foothills, possess specialized organic properties needed to activate volatile alchemical compounds. When combined with Daggerspine naga scales, restorative troll elixirs, and gnoll-derived sludge, the optic tissues help stabilize and trigger toxic mixtures formulated to sow death across enemy territories.

item:torn-murloc-fin.text: Torn Murloc Fin. Torn Murloc Fins serve as proof of work for the Stormwind Army's standing bounty on hostile amphibians in eastern Elwynn Forest. Harvested from foragers and lurkers along the riverbanks, they demonstrate that local waterways are being systematically cleared. As the murloc population along eastern Elwynn's streams and lakes surged, the Stormwind Army authorized a direct bounty to cull their numbers. Guard Thomas, stationed at the bridge spanning the eastern river, collects these severed fins to verify kills. With Stormwind's military stretched thin defending against internal unrest and regional threats, local authorities rely heavily on traveling adventurers to bring in physical proof of cleared encampments.

item:totem-of-hawkwind.text: Totem of Hawkwind. The Totem of Hawkwind is a carved token carried by young tauren departing Camp Narache. Presented to Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, it serves as proof that the bearer has completed their initial trials and is prepared to undergo the remainder of the Rites of the Earthmother. Carved by the hand of Chief Hawkwind atop the Red Cloud Mesa, this wooden totem acts as an introduction and proof of passage for youth coming of age. In tauren tradition, formal writ is rarely used; instead, meaningful symbols and familiar tribal craft carry a leader's intent. When an aspiring youth completes their preliminary trials at Camp Narache, Hawkwind crafts this icon to send them forward along the road into the wider expanse of Mulgore. The distinctive carvings identify the bearer to Baine Bloodhoof, signaling that they possess the spirit and strength required to face the next trials and seek the eventual blessing of Thunder Bluff.

item:tough-wolf-meat.text: Tough Wolf Meat. Tough Wolf Meat is raw game meat harvested from the predatory timber wolves and young wolves prowling Northshire Valley and Coldridge Valley. Though coarse and stringy, it serves as a staple ration for hungry locals like Eagan Peltskinner in Elwynn Forest and dwarven outfitters in Dun Morogh. The wolves roaming the outskirts of Northshire Valley and Dun Morogh pose a constant menace to local settlements, but they also offer a gritty source of sustenance. Tough Wolf Meat is notoriously sinewy and chewy compared to prime game, yet resource-strapped frontiersmen prize it all the same. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner despises the beasts for their viciousness but happily cooks their meat into rustic steaks, eagerly trading basic supplies and gear to anyone willing to cull the packs.

item:tourmaline-phial.text: Tourmaline Phial. The Tourmaline Phial is a specialized gem-crafted vessel given to travelers in Teldrassil by Corithras Moonrage. It is used to draw blessed waters from the moonwell beside the Pools of Arlithrien as part of ongoing rituals to monitor and soothe the boughs of the World Tree. Corithras Moonrage provides the Tourmaline Phial to aid in the rituals surrounding the World Tree. The druids in Dolanaar use such dedicated gemstone vials to safely collect pure moonwell waters from across Teldrassil. This particular phial is designated for the moonwell on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien, southeast of the road leading to Darnassus, an area increasingly beleaguered by hostile Gnarlpine furbolgs.

item:toxic-fogger.text: Toxic Fogger. The Toxic Fogger is a specialized dispersal device filled with lethal poison, concocted by the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. It is designed to contaminate the Venture Company's air transit operations in the Stonetalon Mountains. Carrying a toxin brewed by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill and dispatched by Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, the Toxic Fogger serves as biological sabotage aimed directly at the Venture Company's strip-mining efforts. Suspecting that the goblins rely on courier flying machines to shuttle messages and light cargo between Stonetalon and their headquarters, Zamah sends the fogger to release its poison right where machines land and refuel. Rather than engaging in prolonged skirmishes with endless mercenary crews, the Forsaken method strikes at the logistical spine of the operation, ensuring that the poison travels directly back to corporate leadership.

item:treshala-s-pendant.text: Treshala's Pendant. Treshala's Pendant is an intimate heirloom of bonding belonging to Treshala Fallowbrook, a night elf dwelling in Darnassus. Carried into southern Kalimdor by her husband, Heralath, it was ripped away by the quilboar in Razorfen Kraul as he lay dying. The pendant serves as a symbol of deep marital devotion between Treshala and Heralath Fallowbrook. Before embarking on perilous journeys away from Teldrassil, Heralath carried the bonding necklace close as a reminder of his home and his beloved.

item:trogg-stone-tooth.text: Trogg Stone Tooth. A Trogg Stone Tooth is a rugged, mineralized tooth taken from the Stonesplinter troggs infesting the hills of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders use these teeth as physical proof that wandering adventurers are thinning the trogg numbers around the southern frontier. With the Ironforge Reserve committed to the Alliance Front, local dwarven garrisons are stretched thin across Khaz Modan. At the southern gate guard tower in Loch Modan, Captain Rugelfuss cannot spare his soldiers from their posts to mount offensive patrols against the lurking Stonesplinter troggs. Instead, he issues a standing call for volunteers to hunt the creatures in the nearby hills. To confirm that the menace is being driven back, Rugelfuss demands Trogg Stone Teeth as crude, undeniable evidence of every beast slain.

item:troll-charm.text: Troll Charm. Troll Charms are sacred spiritual amulets carried by the Darkspear trolls. A collection of them was recently looted by hostile Thistlefur furbolgs after an ambush along the northern reaches of Ashenvale. To the trolls of the Horde, spiritual charms are far more than mere ornamentation. As the scout Mitsuwa explains, a troll without their charm is considered as diminished as an orc without battle scars. When a party of Darkspear kin journeyed toward Zoram'gar Outpost through the dense canopy of Ashenvale, they were ambushed and slaughtered by the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. While their spirits were commended to the afterlife, the furbolgs looted the dead and carried off their sacred charms as trophies, stashing them in chests deep within Thistlefur Hold.

item:trophy-swoop-quill.text: Trophy Swoop Quill. A Trophy Swoop Quill is a prized hunting token plucked from the large birds of prey that circle over the plains of Mulgore. Among the tauren, gathering these feathers demonstrates keen eyesight, patience, and hunting skill. Swoops are cunning avian predators indigenous to Mulgore, known for riding high thermals and remaining difficult to track across the grasslands. For young tauren hunters and travelers striving to prove themselves in Bloodhoof Village, claiming a trophy quill from these birds is a traditional rite of cleverness and determination. Presenting these quills to elders such as Harken Windtotem honors the hunter's clan and signifies that one possesses the sharp senses needed to thrive upon the plains.

item:twilight-pendant.text: Twilight Pendant. A Twilight Pendant is an insignia worn by cultists of the Twilight's Hammer deep within Blackfathom Deeps. To the Argent Dawn, these dark talismans serve as definitive proof of the cult's subversive operations on the coast of Ashenvale. Within the drowned ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, members of the Twilight's Hammer gather alongside the naga to conduct foul rites in veneration of the chaotic Old Gods. Cultists—ranging from shadowmages and aquamancers to reavers and loreseekers—wear these pendants as emblems of devotion to their shadowy patrons. Because the cult operates in secrecy beneath the former night elf temple, retrieving these ornaments is one of the few ways outside observers can gauge the cult's numbers and thwart their machinations. Argent Guard Manados in Darnassus actively seeks these pendants as evidence of a successful purge against the encroaching darkness. Blackfathom Deeps once housed a pristine moonwell, and its desecration by malevolent void-worshipers poses a severe threat to Kalimdor. Gathering the pendants confirms that the cultists' foothold in Ashenvale is being dismantled before their dark patrons can unleash greater terror.

item:twilight-whisker.text: Twilight Whisker. Twilight Whiskers are harvested from twilight runners prowling the northern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. In the settlement of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil covets them as an ingredient in a cruel, venomous concoction he mockingly names forest magic. The high crags near Stonetalon Peak are home to twilight runners, predatory felines attuned to the deep shadows of the ancient groves. While hunters prize their pelts, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil of Malaka'jin seeks their stiff whiskers for a far darker purpose. Seeking vengeance upon captured night elves who once defended these woodlands, Jin'Zil gathers components of the forest—resinous sap, countless eyes, fey dragon scales, and twilight whiskers—to brew a lethal draught intended to mock and poison his captives.

item:twitching-antenna.text: Twitching Antenna. Twitching Antennae are severed sensory appendages gathered from the invasive silithid swarming the southern Barrens. Sought by the tauren warrior Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo, they serve as proof of a young warrior's swiftness and combat prowess before their lingering nerve twitches fade. Carved directly from the heads of silithid grubs, swarmers, and harvesters, these antennae retain residual nervous reflex even after detachment. Their violent spasming does not last long once severed from the insectoid host. Because of this brief window of vitality, bringing back still-twitching antennae serves as a strict test of speed, requiring an aspirant to hunt the beasts in the southern wastes and dash back across the scrublands before the twitching goes still. Beyond serving as a rite of passage, these antennae are troubling harbingers. Silithid are not native to the Barrens, and their recent burrowing mounds at the Field of Giants deeply unsettle the hunters of Camp Taurajo. Ruga Ragetotem demands these specimens to study the new threat while simultaneously steeling Horde warriors against an encroaching, alien menace.

item:ukor-s-burden.text: Ukor's Burden. Ukor's Burden is a heavy bundle of rations hauled out of Razor Hill by a well-meaning orc peon. Intended to feed hungry novices in the Valley of Trials, the unwanted provisions must be hauled back before the wilderness scorpids and raptors pick up the scent. Orc peons rarely act on their own initiative, which makes Ukor's errand unusual. Packing a heavy load of provisions from the inn in Razor Hill, he braved the red dust and aggressive wildlife of Durotar to aid young recruits training in the Valley of Trials. To his dismay, the overseers and instructors turned him away—believing that hardship and lean bellies forge true warriors. Trapped outside the canyon's mouth and terrified of the beasts stalking the trail back, Ukor entrusted the sack to passing travelers to return it to Innkeeper Grosk.

item:uncloven-satyr-hoof.text: Uncloven Satyr Hoof. An Uncloven Satyr Hoof is a swollen, solid hoof harvested from the satyrs lurking in Ashenvale. Saturated with corrupt magical energy leeched from the ancient forest, these grim trophies serve as potent crafting components for Darkspear troll armorers. Satyrs haunt the corrupted groves of northeastern Ashenvale, feeding directly upon the ancient forest's magical purity. As they gorge themselves on this essence, the corruption distorts their demonic physiology, causing their hooves to swell and lose their natural cleft. These solid, uncloven hooves become dense reservoirs of absorbed energy, holding volatile power that can be harvested by skilled shamans and leatherworkers. Down on the coast of Durotar in Sen'jin Village, the troll armorer Ula'elek knows how to turn demonic corruption into strength for Horde champions. By taking the hooves of these sated satyrs, he leeches out the trapped woodland magic, channeling the stolen power into the forging of brutal gauntlets designed to protect young warriors facing the rigors of Kalimdor.

item:underbelly-whelp-scale.text: Underbelly Whelp Scale. Underbelly Whelp Scales are harvested from the younger broods of the Black Dragonflight found roaming the Redridge Mountains. Valued by craftsmen for their resilient yet pliable texture, they serve as precious barter material among local artisans. Dragonhide and scales possess legendary durability, but full-grown black dragons are lethal beyond measure to ordinary folk. Instead, resourceful frontiersmen and craftsmen look toward the skies south of Lake Everstill, where young black dragon whelps nest among the crags. While the dorsal plating of a whelp is brittle or coarse, the scales running along its softer underbelly strike an ideal balance between flexibility and protection. As a result, these underbelly scales command substantial value in regional trade, functioning as high-end crafting material and dependable collateral for debts. In Lakeshire, the magistrate's craftsmen must often rely on barter when coin is scarce or trade routes are strained. Verner Osgood, the local blacksmith, found himself heavily indebted to the blacksmith Argus over a shipment of shoes brought in from Goldshire. Knowing Argus's fondness for rare trade goods, Verner relies on passing adventurers to harvest underbelly whelp scales to satisfy the debt and keep his workshop in good standing.

item:unidentified-ore.text: Unidentified Ore. Unidentified Ore is a peculiar mineral sample unearthed by Venture Company operations in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered by the disgruntled laborer Piznik, it was smuggled away to be analyzed by goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks and forwarded to engineers in Undermine. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting and strip mining in Windshear Crag tore deep into the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, exposing unusual mineral strata. The site's new boss, Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, ordered large amounts of a strange gold-green ore mined, and the demoted goblin worker Piznik, still loyal to his fired former boss Ziz Fizziks, secured a sample of it while plotting his exit from the outfit. Handed off to a traveler bound for the western ridge of the crag, the sample made its way into the hands of Ziz Fizziks, who planned to ship the prize back to Undermine for study, keeping a pocket-sized cut for personal profit.

item:unrefined-ore-sample.text: Unrefined Ore Sample. An Unrefined Ore Sample is a piece of unusual raw mineral mined by the Gravelsnout kobolds dwelling in Thousand Needles. Camp Taurajo's master weaponsmith, Tatternack Steelforge, seeks it out to evaluate whether the metal can be forged into superior weapons for Warchief Thrall's armies. South of the Barrens, within the canyon walls of Thousand Needles, a clan of kobolds known as the Gravelsnout burrow endlessly through stone and earth. Travelers returning north through the Barrens brought word of a curious mineral discovered among the slain vermin—an unrefined ore unlike the standard veins found across Kalimdor. While the travelers refused to surrender their prize to the Horde, the subterranean diggers and surveyors of Thousand Needles carry raw chunks of the stone straight from their excavations. In Camp Taurajo, the weaponsmith Tatternack Steelforge labours directly under orders from Warchief Thrall to develop stronger armaments for the Horde. Tatternack was infuriated by travelers who hoarded knowledge of the deposit, deeming it an insult to the Horde's war effort. By securing a raw sample of the mineral, Steelforge aims to test its tensile strength and temper, hoping to smelt it down and fashion a prototype blade worthy of Orgrimmar's approval.

item:ur-s-treatise-on-shadow-magic.text: Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic. Ur's Treatise on Shadow Magic is a perilous arcane tome penned by the renowned wizard Ur of Dalaran. Originally safeguarded by the mages of Stormwind, the enchanted book was stolen by the renegade sorcerer Morganth and hidden away in the Tower of Ilgalar. Penned by the Dalaran scholar Ur, this treatise delves into the subtle and corruptive nature of shadow magic. Because delving into such arts invites doom and ruin for the unwary, the mages of the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind placed protective seals upon the volume to bar anyone from reading its contents. However, when the sorcerer Morganth surrendered to dark arts and was exiled from the city's magical circle, he made off with the tome, carrying it eastward into the Redridge Mountains to his stronghold at the Tower of Ilgalar.

item:urgent-message.text: Urgent Message. The Urgent Message is a sealed dispatch penned by Brave Moonhorn warning Freewind Post of escalating centaur violence across Thousand Needles. Carried by travelers descending into the canyon, the letter alerts the tauren garrison that their supply lines and scouting parties are under immediate threat. Penned by Brave Moonhorn near the great lift that descends from the Barrens into Thousand Needles, the Urgent Message represents the first line of defense for travelers crossing the border. Moonhorn monitors the jagged canyons below, where aggressive centaur tribes have renewed their relentless raids against Horde travel. Addressed to Cliffwatcher Longhorn atop Freewind Post, the missive sounds the alarm about emboldened attackers striking dangerously close to crucial roadways, urging the local garrison to brace for sustained conflict and guard against secondary threats like the unpredictable Grimtotem clan.

item:valdred-s-hands.text: Valdred's Hands. Valdred's Hands are the severed limbs of Valdred Moray, claimed after his death in southern Silverpine Forest. They are sought by Raleigh Andrean in the Undercity as a morbid trophy and proof of vengeance for the murder of his wife. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, Valdred Moray and Raleigh Andrean were close friends. That bond was shattered when Valdred murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. Though Raleigh succumbed to death and arose as one of the Forsaken—professing an inability to genuinely grieve—the lingering hunger for retribution never left him. When Valdred attempted to flee southward past the Greymane Wall into Gilneas, Raleigh dispatched an emissary to end his former friend's flight, demanding his severed hands as definitive proof that the deed was done.

item:velinde-s-journal.text: Velinde's Journal. Velinde's Journal is a personal record kept by the Night Elf priestess Velinde Starsong, stored away in the Sentinel bunkhouse in Darnassus. It holds crucial accounts of her duties and the mysterious circumstances surrounding her departure from the city. When Priestess Velinde Starsong departed Darnassus, her personal belongings were locked away in a footlocker within the Sentinels' bunkhouse in the Tradesmen's Terrace. Among her stored effects rests her personal journal, documenting her responsibilities and duties before she slipped away. While the Sentinels hold Velinde in high regard and assumed she simply had private matters to attend to, the contents of her journal suggest her unexplained absence is far more troubling than first believed.

item:velinde-s-key.text: Velinde's Key. Velinde's Key is a small key entrusted to adventurers by Thyn'tel Bladeweaver in Darnassus. It unlocks a personal storage locker within the Sentinel bunkhouse, containing the writings left behind by Priestess Velinde Starsong before her mysterious disappearance. Held in Darnassus by Thyn'tel Bladeweaver, this simple key secures the personal belongings of Priestess Velinde Starsong. Stored safely inside a footlocker in the Sentinel bunkhouse above the Tradesmen's Terrace, Velinde's worldly possessions were put aside after she departed night elf lands without warning. Bladeweaver only surrenders the key to those who present legitimate evidence—such as revelations uncovered in the Tome of Mel'Thandris—proving their genuine interest in discovering the priestess's fate.

item:venomtail-antidote.text: Venomtail Antidote. Venomtail Antidote is a specialized concoction brewed to neutralize the lethal toxins of Durotar's venomtail scorpids. Prepared by Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar, it serves as an urgent remedy for Rhinag, an afflicted troll scout stranded near the northwestern border of Durotar. The arid expanse of Durotar crawls with dangerous wildlife, none more hazardous to careless wanderers than the local scorpids. A deep sting from a venomtail delivers a virulent poison capable of killing an adult warrior within an hour. When the troll Rhinag found himself envenomed far from aid near the northwestern border, his only survival lay in obtaining a specialized remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary sequestered deep within Orgrimmar's subterranean Cleft of Shadow. Securing the antidote requires navigating the underbelly of Orgrimmar to locate Kor'ghan. Knowledgeable in desert toxins and harsh remedies, Kor'ghan prepares the vial to purge the venom before it turns fatal. Once delivered, the draught halts the venom's progression, sparing Rhinag a humiliating death in the wilderness—though Kor'ghan demands further trials and hunts from the scout to atone for his carelessness.

item:venomtail-poison-sac.text: Venomtail Poison Sac. A Venomtail Poison Sac is a biological organ harvested from scorpids native to the arid expanses of Durotar. While containing a virulent toxin capable of incapacitating an unwary hunter, it is also the vital ingredient required to brew an effective counter-agent. The scorpids prowling the red rocks of Durotar—chiefly the Venomtail Scorpid, alongside mutated varieties like the Corrupted Scorpid and the notorious Death Flayer—produce a fast-acting, debilitating venom. Stored within specialized tail sacs, this poison can quickly overwhelm even seasoned warriors if left untreated. Ironically, the very sacs that deliver this lethal sting contain the primary compounds necessary to synthesize an antidote. When the hunter Rhinag fell victim to a sting outside Orgrimmar, local alchemists required four fresh poison sacs to concoct the remedy needed to neutralize the venom coursing through his veins.

item:venture-co-documents.text: Venture Co. Documents. These tightly bound papers were recovered from a crate amidst a ruined caravan in eastern Mulgore. They detail the operations of the Venture Company, confirming the predatory cartel's illegal strip-mining ventures within the tauren homeland. Discovered packed atop mined ore and minerals in the remnants of a ransacked wagon, these documents expose the scale of the Venture Company's intrusion into Mulgore. Known across Kalimdor for ruthless deforestation and uncontrolled excavation, the goblin-led cartel has quietly set up drilling and mining outposts in the eastern foothills. Morin Cloudstalker and the tauren Outrunners rely on these seized ledgers to gauge the threat to their sacred ancestral plains and rally hunters to drive the trespassers out.

item:venture-co-engineering-plans.text: Venture Co. Engineering Plans. The Venture Co. Engineering Plans are mechanical schematics kept inside the goblin logging mill in Windshear Crag. Recovered by Alliance operatives, they detail the inner workings of the heavy machinery devastating the Stonetalon Mountains. Windshear Crag is choked with smoke and logging machinery as the Venture Company strips the forests of Stonetalon. Hidden inside their lumber mill south of Cragpool Lake, these engineering blueprints lay out the exact construction, strengths, and flaws of their specialized timber-harvesting contraptions.

item:venture-co-letters.text: Venture Co. Letters. The Venture Co. Letters are internal correspondence recovered from Windshear Mine in Stonetalon Mountains. Stolen under the cover of explosive distractions, they provide the night elf Sentinels with crucial intelligence on goblin industrial operations in the region. Windshear Crag has been overrun by the Venture Company, whose logging machines and strip-mining operations tear through the ancient woodland. To uncover the full scope of the cartel's ambitions, Alliance operatives deployed covert sabotage to create distractions and infiltrate Windshear Mine. These retrieved letters contain private communications and logistical records detailing the company's local activities, giving Sentinel leadership insight into how the defilers organize their workforce and supply lines.

item:verdant-note.text: Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a summons delivered to novice tauren druids in Camp Narache. Sent on behalf of the druid mentor Gart Mistrunner, it instructs young initiates to report for training and begin learning the rites of the Earthmother. Young tauren who demonstrate a spiritual affinity for nature receive the Verdant Note shortly after beginning their trials in the Red Cloud Mesa. Carried by a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner, the brief missive directs the initiate to present themselves to the mentor at Camp Narache. Restless spirits and shifting elements have begun troubling Mulgore, making the instruction of new druids an urgent duty for the elders. Upon answering the note, initiates are inducted into the deeper mysteries of nature communion. Gart Mistrunner cautions young druids that although night elves share a common bond with the wild, their ancient pride keeps them distant and unwelcoming. Tauren druidism focuses strictly on reverence for the Earthmother, guiding initiates to listen to the land's restless ancestral voices and serve as her living instruments.

item:verdant-sigil.text: Verdant Sigil. The Verdant Sigil is an inscribed druidic token presented to fledgling night elf druids beginning their training in Shadowglen. Carried as a summons from the druid mentor Mardant Strongoak, it marks a novice's formal entry into the Cenarion teachings under the branches of Aldrassil. In the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen, young night elves who feel the call of the wild receive the Verdant Sigil from Conservator Ilthalaine. Sent via messenger from the trainer Mardant Strongoak, the token directs novices to climb into the boughs of the great tree Aldrassil. Carrying the sigil serves as a formal invitation to leave basic chores behind and commence serious training in communion with nature spirits and the deep mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak initiates the young druid into their lifelong craft. While novices are not yet prepared to walk the sleeping trance of the Emerald Dream, acknowledging the sigil marks the start of their mentorship. Under Mardant's instruction, initiates learn to interpret the whispers of the wilderness and master early shapeshifting and healing arts in service of Teldrassil.

item:verna-s-westfall-stew-recipe.text: Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe is a handwritten culinary guide penned by Verna Furlbrow as she prepares to flee Westfall. Entrusted to travelers bound for Salma Saldean, it preserves a hearty regional staple amidst the collapse of the countryside. As the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems run rampant across Westfall, longtime homesteaders like Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have been forced to abandon their land. While waiting for their wagon to be repaired so they can escape toward Stormwind, Verna scribbles down her beloved formula for Westfall Stew. Rather than letting the recipe vanish with their departure, she entrusts it to passing travelers to deliver to her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean, ensuring that a warm, familiar comfort endures for those remaining behind.

item:verner-s-note.text: Verner's Note. Verner's Note is a written requisition penned by Lakeshire's blacksmith, Verner Osgood, and carried to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It details a critical shortage of iron in Redridge, asking the Elwynn smith for emergency horseshoes. Maintaining the defense of Lakeshire demands a heavy toll in worked metal. With the Stormwind Guard stationed in town stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils, Verner Osgood has consumed nearly all his iron reserves keeping soldiers armed and armored. As a result, Lakeshire's stables have fallen into neglect, lacking even basic horseshoes for their mounts. This letter represents Verner swallowing his pride to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for an external shipment of prepared shoes to keep the town's horses mobile.

item:verog-s-head.text: Verog's Head. Verog's Head is the grisly trophy claimed from Verog the Dervish, a prominent Kolkar centaur leader who oversees forces around the Stagnant Oasis. It is sought by the orc Regthar Deathgate as proof of the chieftain's demise and to demoralize the aggressive Kolkar tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar centaur pose a relentless threat to Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish, known for his nomadic habits, leaves his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable while roaming the arid scrubland. To bring him out into the open, Horde operatives attack his forces around his pavilion until an alarm is raised. Once Verog rushes back to defend his camp, he is slain and decapitated. Delivering his severed head to Regthar Deathgate serves as vital evidence that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has been dismantled, joining the head of Barak Kodobane on display.

item:vial-of-innocent-blood.text: Vial of Innocent Blood. A Vial of Innocent Blood is a grim alchemical reagent gathered by Syndicate shadow mages lurking in the ruins of Durnholde Keep.
